en: The Amoghapāśakalparāja Sūtra, Scroll One.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Bodhiruci of India during the Great Tang Dynasty.
Chapter One: The Introduction to the Mātṛ-dhāraṇī-mantra. Chapter One: The Introduction to the Mātṛ-dhāraṇī-mantra.
Thus have I heard.
At one time, the Bhagavat was dwelling on Mount Potalaka, within the great palace of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara.
That palace was composed entirely of immeasurable great jewels and exquisite, rare treasures,
interspersed and ornamented together;
these various gems interpenetrated one another, emitting a great blaze of light.
Half-moon and full-moon shaped jeweled bells and golden chimes,
as well as precious pearls and necklaces, were suspended everywhere;
when stirred by a gentle breeze, they all produced the sounds of the Dharma.
It was adorned with precious canopies, banners, and streamers,
as well as various wonderful flowers and fly-whisks, all spread throughout and draped with nets of pearls.
Surrounding the hall were many jeweled towers and pavilions,
with precious canopies clustered together;
rows upon rows of various jewel trees were laden with flowers.
That is to say: the flowers of the precious sāla trees, the flowers of the precious tāla trees,
the flowers of the precious tamāla trees, the flowers of the precious campaka trees,
the flowers of the precious aśoka trees, and the flowers of the precious atimuktaka trees.
Furthermore, there were countless hundreds of thousands of millions of varieties of precious incense trees,
their fragrances intermingling in sweet perfume as they surrounded and adorned the area.
There were also immeasurable jeweled ponds, springs, and marshes.
The eight qualities of water fill it to the brim;
fragrant flowers and soft grasses are found everywhere,
and the various blossoms provide such exquisite adornment that it is most delightful.
That mountain abounds with all manner of diverse birds and beasts;
their forms and appearances are exquisite and beautiful, and they all possess hearts of compassion.
They emit various wonderful sounds, calling to one another in harmony as they frolic and enjoy themselves.
All the mantra-vidyādhara sages of the bodhisattvas,
together with the gods of the Thirty-three Heavens, enjoy themselves there;
the Tathāgata dwells therein together with a great assembly of eight thousand bhikṣus.
They were all arhats,
dwelling in great wisdom that was exhaustive and perfectly clear;
their renown surpassed that of the world and reached far and wide.
Possessing great supernormal powers, sovereignty, and unimpeded mastery,
he prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, circumambulated him three times to the right, and sat in the assembly.
He was accompanied by nine hundred and ninety billion *koṭi-nayuta* hundreds of thousands of great bodhisattvas.
Their holy life was entirely pure;
they had thoroughly mastered immeasurable and boundless dharanis, mantras, and samadhi gates,
and were likewise endowed with all profound and wondrous wisdom.
Each of these bodhisattvas was endowed with immeasurable and sublime merits that could not be fully extolled even in hundreds of millions of eons.
They prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, circumambulated him three times to the right, and took their seats in the assembly.
Furthermore, there were immeasurable hundreds of thousands of kings of the Śuddhāvāsa heavens, including King Īśvara,
King Maheśvara, King Mahābrahmā, and King Śakra.
They all gave rise to vast vows, deeply delighting in the Mahāyāna,
and vowed to inherit and protect the Buddha-dharma so that it would never be interrupted.
Each of them held precious banners, streamers, canopies, jeweled beads, necklaces, and exquisite celestial flowers.
They all went together to the place where the Buddha was, prostrated at his feet,
circumambulated him three times to the right, made extensive offerings,
and sat together in the assembly while singing praises in unison.
Furthermore, there were immeasurable mahāvidyādharas, mantra-vidyādhara sages,
hosts of ascetic sages, Yama, Varuṇa, Vāyu, and Agni.
The Sun Deity, the Moon Deity, the Star Deities,
the planetary deities presiding over the twenty-eight lunar mansions,
and the female seers who uphold mantras and vidyās.
Together with the remaining hosts of devas,
they all, with profound resolve, vowed to make great aspirations and collectively venerated, upheld, and protected the Mahāyāna.
Together they went to the place where the Buddha was, prostrated at his feet,
circumambulated him three times to the right, and gazed upon the Tathāgata;
filled with joy and serene composure, they sat down in their respective seats.
Furthermore, there were immeasurable great nāga spirits,
yakṣas, rākṣasas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas.
They made great vows and sang praises of the Mahāyāna;
together they protected the gateway of the unsurpassed *dhāraṇī* mantras,
and all went to where the Buddha was to prostrate at his feet.
Having circumambulated [the Buddha] three times to the right and gazed up at the Tathāgata,
he sat down upon his seat in the assembly without looking away.
At that time, the Venerable Bhagavan...
He was specifically for the sake of the Śuddhāvāsa deities, Īśvara, Maheśvara, Mahābrahmā,
Śakra, and the hosts of devas,
preaching the Great Dharma while seated upon a lion throne of precious lotuses.
Surpassing the light of all the suns, it illuminated everything.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara,
with joy and a smile, rose from his seat.
Baring his right shoulder, he joined his palms in reverence,
prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, adjusted his robes,
knelt with hands clasped before him, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One, I possess a dhāraṇī called the *Amoghapāśahṛdayarāja-dhāraṇī-mantra-samaya*.
This dharma was [revealed] ninety-one kalpas ago.”
In that final kalpa,

there shall be a Buddha named Lokêśvararāja Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed Leader of Men to be Tamed, Teacher of Gods and Humans, Buddha, Bhagavān.
Out of compassion for me, that Buddha, the World-Honored One,
bestowed this dhāraṇī mantra and all the gateways to the Dharma.
That buddha-world is named Supreme Contemplative Wisdom.
"Bhagavān, from that time forth, I have constantly upheld this dhāraṇī-mantra and all its teachings,

guiding and transforming immeasurable hundreds of thousands of kings of the Śuddhāvāsa heavens, King Īśvara, King Maheśvara, King Mahābrahmā, King Śakra, and all other heavenly kings, each together with their retinues."
They shall all be reverently honored, served, respected, and praised,
and be established in the stage of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*,
all adorned with the wisdom that is free from delusion.
"Bhagavān, when I first attained this dharani-dharma,
I realized the samadhi-door called 'The Adorned Head of Hundred-Thousandfold Non-empty and Unerring Wisdom.'"
And all [these] appear before me.
World-Honored One, you should know that this is due to the power of this mantra.
I clearly behold the assemblies of all the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, in the infinite and countless various lands throughout the ten directions,
all of whom are making offerings and listening to the profound Dharma.
Through successive rounds of teaching and transformation,
immeasurable sentient beings shall all attain the resolve for unsurpassed bodhi;
therefore, practitioners should receive and uphold this in its entirety.
World-Honored One,
wherever this sutra may abide,
one should know that in that place there will be immeasurable hundreds of thousands of kings of the Śuddhāvāsa heavens, King Īśvara, King Maheśvara, King Mahābrahmā, and King Śakra.
Furthermore, World-Honored One, twelve million hundred thousand celestial kings, together with their retinues,
constantly surround, revere, and protect you all at once.
In whatever place this sūtra may abide, should there be those who,
in accordance with the Dharma, transcribe it with purity,
read, recite, uphold, and praise it;
One should know that such a place is a *caitya* containing the relics of all the Buddhas.
Blessed One, if there are sentient beings who are able,
even for a moment, to read, recite, hear, or circulate this mantra-samaya of the Heart-King Dhāraṇī of the Amoghapāśa, [they shall obtain these benefits].
It should be known that such a person has approached,
honored, and made offerings to immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Buddhas,
and has planted various roots of goodness.
Why is this? World-Honored One,
this Dharma is the great mass of radiant jewels of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
If there are sentient beings who commit extremely evil deeds,
slandering all Buddhas, bodhisattvas, pratyekabuddhas, and śrāvakas,
as well as slandering the True Dharma by claiming that no goodness exists;
Furthermore, if one destroys the images, stūpas, temples, sūtras, śāstras, or the teachings of the Buddhas, bodhisattvas, pratyekabuddhas, or śrāvakas,
such a person should fall into the Avīci hell.
For incalculable eons, they undergo uninterrupted suffering;
even though the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Pratyekabuddhas,
and Śrāvakas possess supernormal powers, they cannot save them.
World-Honored One, if such sentient beings can give rise to a mind of repentance, bathe themselves until clean,
anoint their bodies with fragrant scents, and put on fresh,
pure garments before the Buddha in accordance with the Dharma.
With utmost sincerity, repent for the grave offenses committed in past and present lives;
vow never to commit them again,
and maintain the precepts of fasting and purification of the mind.
Having refrained from speech and discourse for seven days and seven nights,
one who recites this dhāraṇī mantra one hundred and eight times every day before the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara of Amoghapāśa—

It should be known that all the ten evil deeds, the five heinous crimes, and the four grave offenses committed by such a person in past and present lives will be completely extinguished without remainder, and they shall not fall into hell.
Except for those who have committed the five heinous crimes and undergo retribution lightly in the present life, how can this be known?
It is by observing [the symptoms] for one day, two days, three days, or four days.
Even for those suffering from malarial fevers or infectious fevers lasting up to seven days,
or those afflicted with ailments of the eyes, ears, nose, tongue, gums, palate, teeth, head, back,
both shoulders, heart, stomach, abdomen, ribs, waist, or thighs.
Diseases of the two arms and two knees, hemorrhoids, dysentery, and cholera;
afflictions of the hands and feet such as painful itching, white leprosy, wind-tumors, and carbuncles;
scabies, ringworm, abscesses, shifting swellings, and boils.
Boils, carbuncles, toxic swellings, jaundice, hemorrhoids, ulcers, blisters,
itching, insanity, scabies, and diseases caused by *gū* (poisoned food),
or being tormented and disturbed by ghosts and spirits.
Or they may be subjected to various kinds of slander by the people,
receiving baseless insults, flogging,
and imprisonment, thereby undergoing all manner of suffering and affliction.
Should they encounter other misfortunes or have inauspicious dreams,
the World-Honored One declares that such a person will undergo these lightly;
they shall be able to avert all the grave retributions of the intense sufferings of hell.
How much less could a sentient being with pure faith fail to achieve accomplishment when upholding this dhāraṇī mantra, even if they have committed minor offenses?
If there is a sentient being whose body and mind are not at peace, [they should recite it].
For those who, in order to eliminate various calamities, fears, evil dreams, and inauspicious omens,
daily cleanse themselves, recite, uphold,
and offer incense in worship, these shall be extinguished.
Blessed One, if there are sons or daughters of good family who,
in accordance with the Dharma, copy, receive, uphold, read, recite, hear,
and for the sake of others preach and praise this Dharma in accordance with the Dharma.
Instruct others to transcribe, receive, uphold, read, and recite it,
so that all sentient beings born from wombs, eggs, moisture,
or transformation may widely hear this dharani mantra-samaya.
All shall attain liberation from all karmic obstacles of sin.
These sons and daughters of good family should purify their minds.
One reflects according to reality by means of the wisdom of non-apprehension, the wisdom of directionlessness,
the wisdom of no-self, no person, and no experiencer, and the wisdom of non-conceptualization.
The wisdom of neither arising nor ceasing; the wisdom of non-delayed action;
the wisdom of non-action and non-defilement; the wisdom of the nature of equality;
and the wisdom of diligence that is free from the five aggregates—form, sound, smell, taste, touch, and phenomena—and characterized by neither grasping nor rejecting.
By means of these various skillful wisdoms regarding suchness,
one controls the mind as a skillful means; through contemplation,
one constantly perceives all Buddhas as being ever-present before one's eyes.
Before long, you shall behold all the hundreds of thousands of Buddhas of the ten directions appearing before you simultaneously;
they will touch your head with their hands, praise you, and act as witnesses.
Alternatively, you may perceive auspicious signs in dreams or upon waking.
Or they may encounter Buddhas who manifest as śramaṇas to bestow upon them the superior precepts of a bodhisattva,
causing them to extinguish all grave sins accumulated over immeasurable hundreds of thousands of kalpas, as numerous as atoms of dust.
Even to the point of transcribing this sutra according to the Dharma,
placing it within one's home, and making offerings, honoring, and prostrating to it with various incenses and flowers according to one's inclination.
The merit thus obtained is likewise so.
World-Honored One, you have now merely briefly explained a small portion of it.
If there are sentient beings who, for the sake of surpassing others, harbor jealousy, flattery, and deceit;
Whether out of fear, for the sake of wealth and profit, or with a frivolous mind dependent on others,
those who read, recite, hear, or listen to this dharani-mantra samaya shall all obtain supreme benefit.
Furthermore, even those who, having heard it, slander and disparage it,
and fail to show reverence, will still obtain a great benefit.
O World-Honored One, this benefit is known only by those of great wisdom.
This is due to the majestic spiritual power of the Tathāgata Lokeśvararāja and the great compassionate power of Avalokiteśvara,
which causes all sentient beings of an evil nature to—
"Once it has entered the ear, one shall immediately plant immeasurable roots of goodness.
Why is this? World-Honored One, it is as if there were a person who, with a deluded and evil mind..."
He goes to groves of camphor, white sandalwood, aloeswood, or various other fragrant trees; with a mind of delusion,
he reviles the fragrance in various ways,
and further giving rise to a heart of malice, he slanders the fragrance, saying, "Fragrance has no scent," and he plucks the fragrant wood, cuts it, chops it into pieces, and grinds it into powder.
If one drinks it with water or consumes it, or applies it to the body,
this incense has no intentionality regarding whether or not it gives its fragrance to others;
yet by the nature of its fragrance, it can permeate all odorless things so that they all become fragrant.
World-Honored One, this Samaya of the Heart-King Mother Dhāraṇī Mantra of the Amoghapāśa is likewise so.
If there are sentient beings who deny cause and effect, [they shall be transformed].
Various slanders, false accusations, faults, and evils,
or the calamities of envy, flattery, and the pursuit of wealth and food— all such misfortunes shall be averted by upholding,
reciting, and making offerings [to this scripture].
By reason of these causes and conditions, one attains great roots of goodness.
From this life onward, in whatever place one is born,
one will always obtain the fragrance of morality, the fragrance of concentration, the fragrance of wisdom, and the fragrance of liberation.
The incense of majestic power, fearlessness, and the provisions of merit;
the incense of the mass of merit that is firm, indestructible, and dedicated to all-enlightenment;
the incense of the perfection of noble lineage and clan.
One should bring about benefit.
World-Honored One, if any sons or daughters of good family receive,
uphold, read, and recite this dhāraṇī mantra, [they shall obtain such benefits].
One should always, on the eighth day of the waxing moon,
or on the fourteenth or fifteenth day of the waxing moon,
bathe thoroughly and anoint the body with fragrant scents.
Wearing clean garments and eating the three white foods,
or else fasting and ceasing all speech,
one should sit according to the ritual rules before the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara of the Amoghapāśa.
Burning incense as an offering, one should gaze upon the face of the Bodhisattva and recite [the mantra] seven times seven or one hundred and eight times.
World-Honored One, you should know that such a person, in this present life...
One will then obtain twenty meritorious benefits of praise.
What are these twenty?
First, the body is free from various ailments.
First, if any illnesses arising from past karma occur, they will be swiftly cured.
Second, the skin of the body will be fine, soft, beautiful, pleasing, and exquisite.
Third, one will always be gazed upon and cherished by the multitude, never being met with weariness or distaste.
Fourth, their six sense faculties will be constantly settled and their wealth and treasures will appear spontaneously.
Fifth, their clothing and treasures will not be plundered by bandits.
Sixth, all their wealth and treasures will not be consumed by fire or swept away by water.
Seventh, one shall not cause others to be robbed, assaulted, killed, or forcibly deprived of their wealth and treasures, thereby causing them to die of starvation.
Eighth, one shall not cause others to fall from cliffs or mountains to their deaths.
Ninth, one shall empower pure ashes and pure water with mantras.
It scatters upon all fruits and crops,
so that evil winds, frost, hail, insects, and beasts cause no calamity;
the crops flourish and grow luxuriantly.
Tenth, they do not die from being killed in the turmoil of military arrays and battles.
Eleventh, they do not die from having their vital essence sucked and devoured by various evil spirits and ghosts of the world, nor from being harmed as retribution for grudges.
Twelfth, they are constantly praised and extolled by the multitude;
they cherish one another and do not meet with death during an evil age.
Thirteenth, when they see any non-Buddhists or wicked people, these naturally become harmonious and conciliatory.
Fourteenth, one shall not be slandered or harmed by any evil persons;
should such occurrences arise, they will quickly extinguish themselves.
Fifteenth, one shall always be free from fear toward all humans and non-humans.
Sixteenth, one will not die at the hands of those who employ worldly sorcery, spells, curses, or *ḍākinī* spirits.
Seventeenth, all evil latent tendencies (*anuśaya*) and afflictions (*kleśa*) will naturally diminish and fade away.
Eighteenth, they shall not be burned by fire or swept away by water,
nor shall their bodies perish through the calamities of swords, arrows, poisons,
or venomous insects. Nineteenth, all the devas shall constantly provide them with protection.
"Twenty: wherever one is born, one shall possess great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity, as well as the four kinds of unhindered minds.
World-Honored One, there are furthermore eight dharmas; what are these eight?"
First, at the time of death,
Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva will personally manifest his body in the form of a śramaṇa;
through skillful means he will exhort and guide them to the Buddha-field.
Second, at the time of death, their body will not experience pain;
they will be free and at ease in going and staying, as if entering meditative absorption.
Third, at the time of death, their eyes will not wander restlessly, nor will they die with the manifestation of evil signs.
Fourth, at the time of death, his hands and feet will be peaceful and steady as he dies lying on his right side.
Fifth, at the time of death, he will not lose control of his excrement or urine, nor will he die from foul diarrhea or hemorrhaging.
Sixth, at the time of death, one does not lose right mindfulness, but dies sitting upright rather than lying face down.
Seventh, at the time of death, one possesses various skillful eloquences.
They preach the profound and wondrous Dharma until their lives end in death.
Eighth, at the time of their passing, they vow to be reborn in a Buddha-field;
according to that vow, they are reborn in the pure lands of all Buddhas.
Born by transformation from a lotus flower,
they constantly behold all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Mahāsattvas,
and never regress.
Bhagavān, if there are sentient beings who deeply delight in this Dharma, you should preach it for them;
or if there are those who have resolved their minds to seek this Dharma exhaustively.
One should uphold, recite, and chant it without stinginess,
and explain it extensively according to the Dharma. Why is this?
A bodhisattva constantly gives rise to compassion and wisdom toward all sentient beings;
being free from the mind of stinginess, parsimony, and jealousy,
they are thus able to cultivate and refine the unsurpassed Dharma.
Furthermore, a bodhisattva constantly and diligently cultivates wholesome dharmas for the sake of sentient beings;
for this reason, they are truly named a bodhisattva.
What is meant by the term "bodhisattva"?
"Bodhi" is named wisdom, and "sattva" is named compassion;
together they extensively demonstrate the manifold meanings of skillful means.
By means of these two dharmas, one takes up the burden of delivering sentient beings.
Thus one is named a Bodhisattva.
World-Honored One, if you would grant me permission,
I shall act for the benefit of all good sons and good daughters.
Furthermore, for those sentient beings with wrong views, nihilistic views,
or evil wisdom who recite this mantra of the Samaya of the Heart-King Dharani of Amoghapasha before the Tathagata:
"I pray that you will graciously accept it.
At that time, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, saying:
You should now speak it, for this is the very time;
the Tathāgata rejoices in and empowers you.
I, too, do so now for the benefit of all sentient beings in this degenerate age who are burdened by heavy defilements and possess little merit.
Furthermore, for the sake of newly initiated bodhisattvas dwelling in the Mahāyāna,
he extensively performs acts of benefit and happiness as a Buddha-activity.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara...
Having received the Buddha’s permission, he smiled with joy,
joined his palms in reverence, gazed up at the Tathāgata without averting his eyes for a moment, and addressed him, saying: "World-Honored One..."
Since the Tathāgata has now granted me permission to speak this *Amoghapāśahṛdaya-mātṛ-dhāraṇī-mantra-samaya*,
this teaching belongs to all Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
It is that which has been jointly cultivated and purified, which is to be venerated with prostration, and which is the locus for attaining liberation;
it is compassionate toward the world and brings benefit, welfare, and happiness to immeasurable sentient beings.
If one upholds it:
One should first pay homage to all Buddhas of the three times and to the great Bodhisattvas, Pratyekabuddhas, and Śrāvakas.
Next, one should pay homage to the assembly of Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas, such as Maitreya, who have attained the right destination and practice the right conduct.
Next, one should pay homage to the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Suvarṇavarṇaprabhāsavikrīḍitaśvarāja;
and pay homage to the Tathāgata Siṃhavikrīḍitarāja.
Homage to the Tathāgata Amitābha. According to the Sanskrit original,
if one recites otherwise,
one may briefly perform homage to the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and so forth.
When the Bodhisattva Maitreya descends,

he briefly proceeds from paying homage to the Tathāgata Amitābha, and from the Tathāgata Amitābha he briefly proceeds to pay homage to the Triple Gem of the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha, and so forth, up to paying homage to the Tathāgata Supratiṣṭhita-maṇiratna-śikhara-rāja.
Homage to the Tathāgata Samantaprabhāstutaguṇasaṃcayarāja.
Homage to the Tathāgata Vairocana.
Homage to the Tathāgata Ratnaśikhin.
Homage to the Tathāgata Lokeśvararāja. Homage to the Tathāgata Skandhakṣayavivarjita.
Homage to the Tathāgata Kanakavarṇaśānta.
Homage to the Tathāgata Kāśyapa.
Homage to the Tathāgata Śāntamati. Homage to the Tathāgata Yaśasvi.
Homage to the Tathāgata Samantaprabhājitārivaśavartin.
Homage to the Tathāgata Indraketudhvajaśrī. Homage to the Tathāgata Ratnārciḥsvarāj.
Homage to the Tathāgata Unobstructed King of Medicine.
Homage to the Tathāgata Valiant Striding.
Homage to the Tathāgata Well-Abiding Fearless.
Homage to the Buddha Jewel, the Dharma Jewel, and the Bhikṣu Saṅgha Jewel.
Homage to the Noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the Greatly Compassionate One.
Having thus paid homage to these noble beings:
Recite the mantra of the Mother Dhāraṇī of the Heart-King of the Amoghapāśa of the Noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara.
At that time, one should contemplate the syllables and phrases of the Mother Dhāraṇī mantra of the Noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara.
All were suffused with a golden light that shone through them clearly.
Then he spoke the Heart-King Mother Dhāraṇī Mantra of Amoghapāśa, saying:
Namaḥ sarva-tathāgatebhyaḥ. (Namaḥ saṃkṣipta-ṛte) [Note: The phonetic transcription provided in the source text appears to be a transliteration of a specific recitation sequence.]
The syllable *Āḥ* (㘑): those who pronounce it from the side of the mouth all roll their tongues; it is pronounced as *zhèng yě* (正野) [the latter character is read as *yě* hereafter].
Pronounce *tí néng* (特能) [the latter character is read as *néng* in the following examples]. Pronounce *bó* (縛) lightly [the same applies to subsequent examples].
Pronounce *ǎ* (誐) as *yín jiā* (銀迦) or as *jiā jīn luó* (迦斤攞). Pronounce *diǎo* (嚲) as *dōu wǒ* (都我). One phrase: *pǒ* (跛) [the latter character is read as *pǒ* hereafter].

The character *ra* (囉) and the character *va* (凡) are pronounced with the upper tone (shǎngshēng) when placed beside the mouth radical; they are pronounced with the retroflex (dànshé) articulation as the correct form.
*Ti* (底), *shi* (瑟), *chi* (恥), *di* (帝), *piao* (瓢)—the latter is pronounced with the *yào* rhyme, and the same applies to those below. [These constitute] two phrases. *Sabbuddhān* (薩縛勃陀):

the first syllable is pronounced with the upper tone, and subsequent examples follow this pattern. *Bodhisattvānām* (菩地薩得): the same applies below. *Pai-mi-ji* (廢微計): the same applies below. *Piao* (瓢) enters the [appropriate rhyme category].

The three phrases of Sound: *Namaḥ sarvabuddhādhyeṣaka-pratibuddha-vaśī*. (Note: For all words containing the letter *ṛ* with a dot above it [ṛ], they should be pronounced with the tongue curled back;
this is the correct method. The four phrases of Power: *Śrī-vajra-saṃjñi-pāṇi*. (Note: *Śrī* is pronounced with the retroflex *ṛ*; *vajra* is pronounced with the retroflex *ṛ*;
*saṃ* is pronounced with an aspirated *s*; *jñi* is pronounced with the retroflex *ṛ*. *Pāṇi*. (Note: *pā* is pronounced with the labial *p*.)
6. *Namo ratnatrayāya*. 7. *Namo samyaksambuddhānām*. 8. *Namo samyakpradipānām*.

Hṛ-hṛ (76), hā-he hūṃ phaṭ (77), svāhā (278). Regarding the term *svāhā* as translated by various scholars of past and present,
none have meticulously examined the clarity or obscurity of the Sanskrit phonemes,
resulting in variations and discrepancies across different versions of the text.
Some say *satsaṃbhāha*; some say *saḥpāha*; some say *saboha*; and some say *sabhāha*.
Some say "svāhā," some say "suṣvāhā," and some say "saha."
Some say "Saha," while others say "Sa-su-he" (with the final "he" pronounced as a retroflex *cha*). These Sanskrit pronunciations are all devoid of the original meaning.
This is not because the Indian monks who transmitted them failed to pronounce them correctly.
This was merely an error on the part of those who took up the pen. Therefore, it is now definitively established that:

where [the character] was borrowed for the pronunciation *shā* (with the tone of *sāngyì*), it should instead be the character pronounced *shā*; where it was borrowed for the pronunciation *fú* (with no tonal mark), it should instead be the character pronounced *wúkě*; and where it was borrowed for the pronunciation *hē* (with the tone of *hūgè*), it should instead be the character pronounced *hē*. By doing so, one will correctly grasp the phonetic intent of the Holy One.
Therefore, there are no sounds in the Chinese and Sanskrit scriptures that are not permissible;
all *dhāraṇīs* hereafter should be recited according to this principle.

In the midst of the sky,

If one burns aloeswood incense at different times each day and recites [the mantra] twenty-one times,

This applies whether one is traveling on a road or staying overnight at a lodging place.
Whether in cities, towns, villages, mountains, marshes,

Alternatively, one may empower pure water and pure ashes to sprinkle as a boundary-delineation;
empower khaṭvāṅga-wood vajra-stakes;
and empower five-colored threads.
By driving stakes into the ground and nailing them around the four directions,

The mantra-vidyā deities will rejoice;

If all people place it on their arms, wrists, heads, or waists,
those who wear it shall have their illnesses cured and their fears stilled.
If one consecrates cow’s ghee or black sesame oil and has someone suffering from a fevering illness consume it on an empty stomach, it will cause the illness to be immediately cured.
If others have cast curses, spells, or malevolent charms, [the same shall apply].

Using one mantra-sword,

do this daily for seven days, and it will then be cured.
If one suffers from abdominal pain,
by reciting the mantra over red salt water and having it drunk, the ailment will be immediately cured.
If one has been stung by any venomous insect, [the same applies].
Repeatedly smear the poisoned location with mantra-empowered yellow clay;
or, after repeated empowerment, drink cow’s milk on an empty stomach;
or, empower boiled bean juice.
If one warms it and applies it as a poultice to the area poisoned by insects, the affliction will be cured.
If one suffers from eye pain,
one should recite the mantra over a white thread and tie it to the ear ornament.

or alternatively, one may use *pāṭala* water while reciting the mantra.
If one washes with it daily, one will immediately be cured.
If suffering from earache, tinnitus, or heat-wind disorders,
one should recite the mantra over castor oil or clarified butter (ghṛta).
If one repeatedly drips [the liquid] into the ears, the affliction will be eliminated before long.

If one consecrates a cord of five-colored threads and causes it to be worn, the illness will be immediately cured.
This applies even to cases of poisoning, wounds from blades or staves, throat swellings, carbuncles, malignant sores, or other evil ulcers.
Having finished the mantra, one should have [the patient] consume and apply cow’s milk and rock honey; thus, they will immediately be cured.
If there is a dispute about to arise or one that has already arisen, every morning at dawn, one should face the sun.
If one washes the face and rinses the mouth with water purified by mantras, [the afflictions] will be immediately dispelled.
Should a land fall into chaos, high ministers plot rebellion, foreign armies invade,
or pestilence and epidemics arise— [in these times, this shall likewise bring relief].
First, having purified oneself through bathing and wearing new, clean garments, one should partake of the three white foods for twenty-one days while strictly maintaining the ritual site (*maṇḍala*).
At the four corners and the center, place jars of scented water.
On the day of the prayer, one should maintain internal and external purity and perform offerings according to the Dharma.
To the west and north of the mandala, burn incense and scatter flowers;
then sit according to the prescribed manner.
Recite this dhāraṇī mantra with a voice that never falters.
By performing this rite for the elimination of calamities for twenty-one days,
all the people of the land will immediately attain great peace and security.
Every day, empower the water in the jar within the mandala and sprinkle it over all people; thus,
they will once again be protected.
Calamities, karmic obstacles, and transgressions will naturally be extinguished.
If one suffers from sudden afflictions caused by ghosts or spirits, or has lost their voice,
one should empower white sandalwood incense paste with mantras.
Once it has been smeared over the heart, it immediately returns to its original state.
If one lacks wealth, food, drink, incense, or flowers for constant offerings,
one should simply recite and maintain this practice, never allowing it to be interrupted or abandoned.
Furthermore, one shall eliminate all karmic obstacles and hindrances.
If one desires that the household deities provide protection so that no calamities or illnesses occur,
one should daily take one hundred and eight lotus stalks.
Smear [the area] all over with ghee and honey,
scatter white sandalwood powder, and perform the consecrated homa one hundred and eight times for each of the three sessions every day.
When seven days have passed,
it will immediately provide protection and eliminate all calamities.
If one wishes for the multitude to rejoice, [one should recite it].
Consecrate ghee, honey, and white sandalwood incense.
Perform one hundred and eight *homa* offerings, and then recite the verse according to one's wishes:
"The mantra-verse of the medicinal *mudrā* is able to eliminate all manner of calamities, obstacles, and suffering."
The number of these should be pacified by *mriyaya*, *nākulī*, *yaṣṭimadhu*, *nirguṇḍī*, *nākulī*,
*elā*, *agaru*, *campaka*, *indranīla*, *pravālaka*, *gandhabhṛṅgarāja*.
Tagara-yakṣakardama, mahā-kakola-śīra-piśāca-karada-yakṣa,
soma-rāji-sunandana— these pure and refined ingredients should be compounded with rainwater to form pills the size of jujube fruits.
Mark the boundaries at the beginning and end, and maintain the protection.
Recite the mantra over it one thousand and eight times for universal empowerment, then dry it in the shade. When wearing it, empower it seven times;
wear it according to the three grades—superior, middling, or inferior. For the superior grade, wear it upon the crown of the head.
Those of middle capacity shall constantly wear it upon their arms; those of lower capacity shall always wear it upon their necks.

All shall be able to eliminate every calamity and misfortune—disasters of water, fire, and poison, as well as various forms of sorcery, bewitchment, and curses—none of which shall be able to cause harm.
No malevolent spirits or ghosts shall cause harm; bathing with harmonized fragrant water will cleanse all obstacles.
If fierce winds, thunder, hail, and lightning should arise repeatedly, one should empower white mustard seeds and water.
Facing the place where it arises, recite one mantra for each scattering of [the substance] one hundred and eight times;
then it will be eliminated.
Alternatively, empower a branch of pomegranate.
If one visualizes the mantra at the place where [the affliction] arises and applies it even once, it shall be dispelled.
World-Honored One, this Mother Dhāraṇī mantra is the most supreme dharma;
one need only constantly recite and maintain it.
One may achieve accomplishment even without constructing a mandala, forming mudrās, or performing offerings according to the ritual rules.
If one wishes to achieve accomplishment in this dharani-mantra samaya, [one should proceed as follows].
Paint an image of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara with the Amoghapāśa according to the Dharma,
like Maheśvara, with a jeweled crown upon his head,
and within the crown, the emanation of Amitābha Buddha.
Wearing garments of deer skin,
yet adorned with robes of the seven precious gems, pearl necklaces,
and jeweled bracelets; they carried various weapons and implements.
Using pure yellow earth, *gomaya* cow dung, and fragrant mud,
smear the altar according to the ritual rules and cleanse it with colorful paintings;
place the image in the center, adorned with banners and flowers.
In the center of the four corners, place a vase of incense.
Arrange and present offerings of the three white foods, various fruits, and other edibles;
however, exclude all remnants, impure food, food touched by those of improper discipline, food from families of evil precepts, the hundred flavors of food, the five pungent roots, alcohol, and meat.
Without making offerings to others, one should universally invite and worship them all, burning aloeswood incense.
The practitioner of mantras should diligently apply themselves day and night, serving according to the Dharma.
Always remain pure and clean, bathe, and wear clean garments.
At each session, face east, burn incense, scatter flowers, and sit in the lotus posture according to the ritual rules to gaze upon the Bodhisattva.
Recite and maintain the mantra according to the Dharma without missing even a single count.
On the eighth day of every waning moon, one should observe a fast and diligently perform recitation.
At that time, Avalokiteśvara will manifest within the maṇḍala;
the practitioner shall behold him, gaze upon him, and prostrate.
One's requested aspirations shall all be fulfilled.
Furthermore, place realgar or *añjana* within the maṇḍala;
through empowerment by mantra, cause the three signs to appear.
First is the sign of heat;
second is the sign of smoke;
third is the sign of light.
Dotting the forehead, dotting the eyes,
dotting the two palms of the hands, and dotting the two soles of the feet,
one immediately realizes the Samādhi of the King of Ābhāsvara Adorned with Supernatural Wisdom.
There is no undertaking whatsoever that will not be accomplished.
At that time, the Tathāgata praised the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, saying:
Excellent, excellent, son of good family! You are able,
amidst this great assembly of devas and humans,
to kindle the torch of the Great Dharma, create a mass of various jewels, and draw forth all sentient beings from the root of all suffering.
At that time, the celestial kings of the Śuddhāvāsa heaven—King Īśvara, King Maheśvara, Great Brahmā King, and Śakra King—as well as all the other celestial kings, [were present].
Upon hearing this teaching, they were all filled with great joy.
With palms joined in reverence, they rose from their seats together and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, in the future final age..."
Wherever there may be in any land— whether in mountains, forests, cities, towns, or villages—
if there are sentient beings who,
in accordance with the Dharma, write down, read, recite, and uphold this *Amoghapāśahṛdaya-mātṛ-dhāraṇī-mantra-samaya*, [they shall obtain these benefits].
"We, the Heavenly Kings, together with our respective retinues,
shall assemble day and night to constantly protect them.
At that time, the Tathāgata addressed the various heavenly kings:
Excellent, excellent, you gods among kings!
You have seen those sons and daughters of good family in various regions who read,
recite, receive, and uphold this dharani-mantra samaya.
One should guard them and not let them go,
causing them to practice and train,
thereby increasing and nurturing all roots of goodness and the accumulations of merit for enlightenment.
May they attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

At that time, the various devas, hearing the Buddha’s praise and exhortation, were filled with joy and leaped for gladness; they paid homage with deep respect, receiving his words upon the crowns of their heads.

The Amoghapāśakalparāja Sūtra, Scroll One. Oṃ amoghapāśahṛdaya svāhā. Namaḥ sarvatathāgatānām amoghapāśapratyarthisamudghātanakarāṇāṃ tadyathā | oṃ kaṇakaṇa khana khana cina cina vīra vīra mahāvīrya hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. *The Amoghapāśa-kalparāja-sūtra, Scroll One.* *Namo sarva-tathāgatānām amoghapāśa-pratyarthi-samudghātana-karāṇām | tadyathā | oṃ kaṇa-kaṇa khana-khana cina-cina vīra-vīra mahā-vīrya hūṃ phaṭ svāhā.*

The Amoghapāśakalparāja Sūtra, Scroll Two. Translated by the Tripitaka Master Bodhiruci of India during the Great Tang Dynasty.
Chapter Two: The Secret Heart Mantra. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara rose again from his seat and adjusted his robes.
With his right knee touching the ground, he joined his palms and gazed upon the Buddha;
his countenance was serene and joyful, his mind possessed immeasurable great kindness and great compassion,
and from his entire body he universally radiated the light of a billion suns, like a king.
It illuminated the Buddha-worlds of the trichiliocosm throughout the ten directions,

With the bodhicitta, one clearly contemplates the five aggregates as being by nature empty and quiescent, free from the marks of self and what belongs to self, free from the mark of a sentient being, free from the mark of an experiencer, and free from all marks. Why is this so? Because all phenomena...
By nature, it is empty and quiescent; there is no self and no agent.
It is devoid of self and other, transcending the five aggregates, the elements, and the sense bases.
Because these aggregates, bases, and elements cannot be found when observed with true insight, and because there is no self-consciousness, they cannot be grasped or maintained.
Why is this so? Because all dharmas are from the very beginning without color, without form, and without marks; they are free from all defilements and attachments.
The mind, likewise, does not abide within, without, or between the two. The fundamental nature of dharmas is itself empty, quiescent, and pure.
Equal and non-dual, unstained and unattached. Why is this so?
Because the mind is fundamentally without marks. One who performs this contemplation is practicing right contemplation;
its measure is equal to the Dharma-realm, coexisting with samādhi—the contemplation of the Dharma within the Dharma-realm.
Contemplate clearly the syllable *kaṅkha* (pronounced as *kāṅkhā*): it signifies that all phenomena are devoid of agency.

The mantra for combing the hair is: Oṃ āmukha pāṭhamaśrīkṛtu ru tu ru tiṣṭha vadhramante svāhā. This is the empowerment of the hair for combing and binding it.
And as for the empowerment of placing the hand upon the recipient to bestow the dharma:
the mantra for the flask and the cord is *oṃ āmukha pādma jvaloccha pa vili vili hūṃ*. This is the empowerment of the flask and the cord.
