Having consecrated it once more, place it within the maṇḍala and perform the empowerment with this auspicious mantra:
Oṃ āmukha pūjaya pūjaya pracaṇḍe mṛḍi mṛḍi kāmaḷe svāhā. This is the method for binding the boundary by forming the mudrā.
Burn incense, scatter flowers, hang banners, drive in stakes, kindle fires, and provide food offerings.
If one holds a rosary,
one should put on or take off one's clothes.
When performing any ritual procedures related to the altar,
as well as when reading or reciting scriptures,
one must always empower the hands before proceeding with the task.
This is because it is for the purpose of praising all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and celestial deities.

The Mantra for Purifying the Mouth is: Oṃ ā-mogha-mī-male-īśvara-ra-saṃskṛta-ni-pāṭoma-kumara-īśvara-saṃskṛta-ya-dhara-dhara-su-mīmaṃ svāhā. If one wishes to recite this Dharma for the sake of repentance, [one should do so].
When prostrating to and praising the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas,
one should first empower water to cleanse the mouth and teeth, whereby they will become pure and clean. Thus,
the faculty of the tongue shall become purified, supple, and in color like a lotus flower.
Regarding these mantra-samayas, one should take twelve portions each of the following seven substances:
high-quality white sandalwood, nalana incense, red lotus,
bhṛṅgarāja incense, saffron, kuṅkuma incense, and lotus filaments.
Take two measures each of kakkola and tagara, weighing four parts in total;

grind them and mix with stone honey (*śarkarā*). Whenever one recites mantras, by consecrating it and holding it in the mouth, one’s breath will become fragrant and pure, like the scent of the *utpala* flower.
One shall always be beheld by all Buddhas, who will joyfully protect and praise one.
For those with ailments such as phlegm, drinking disorders, or vomiting, these shall be dissolved and cured.
When the gods of the Thirty-three Heavens hear the sound of this dhāraṇī being chanted, they will rejoice, revere, and protect them.
When sentient beings hear the voice of this person, all their obstacles and afflictions are removed, and they come to love one another.
Constantly abiding in accordance with the Dharma and imbued with fragrance, the Great Goddess of Eloquence enters the tip of the tongue through her secret supernatural powers,
bestowing unimpeded eloquence and causing them to remember what was previously forgotten.
Uttering the great sound of the syllable HŪṂ, each sound fills the seven sounds of the mantra-deities, celestial beings, and hosts of immortals;
they immediately gather within the maṇḍala and provide protection.
Furthermore, with a voice of intense wrath, one utters the syllable PHAṬ; each sound fills the seven sounds.
All malevolent vināyakas, ghosts, spirits, and demons shall flee in terror and scatter;
those who constantly hold this incense and recite [this mantra] will naturally manifest all auspicious signs,
while defilements, obstructions, and karmic burdens will all be extinguished, and non-human beings shall never again cause interference or harassment.
Regarding the samaya of these mantras, one should employ nāgapuṣpa, clove bark, uśīra, tagara,
white sandalwood, lotus filaments, tagara, white kakkola, dāruharidrā, and saffron.
Parpaṭaka herb, śyāmāka herb, clove flowers, and ugragandhika herb—
taking equal parts of each of these, purify them thoroughly and mix them with rainwater.
At the time of bathing, one should empower [the mixture] for use.
Bathing with decoctions according to the ritual, the skin and body become radiant and fragrant;
calamities and misfortunes are dispelled, and filth and impurities are washed away. Being pure and acting according to the Dharma, one recites and contemplates;
whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, there is no fear of any evil gods, nāgas, or spirits.
The Vināyakas and their vengeful cohorts shall naturally depart; one will be joyful and free from obstacles.
By constantly bathing with this medicine mixed in warm water, know that such a person will swiftly achieve realization.
All Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and celestial deities will look upon them with joy and protection, granting their supreme vows.
Regarding this mantra-samaya: take one part each of realgar and ox-gall, and twelve parts each of powdered blue utpala flowers and sea-foam.
Thoroughly refine and grind these substances together with rock honey, then mix them with clear water; empower the mixture through recitation and use it.
Applying collyrium to the eyes clears away eye-secretions and cataracts; all Buddhas and Avalokiteśvaras will be delighted, and malevolent spirits and ghosts shall not create obstacles.
One’s dreams will always be auspicious and the faculty of the eyes will be purified.
Such is the samaya of this mantra; furthermore, it is empowered with ox-gallstone.
Using the Mātṛ-dhāraṇī mantra, as well as the mantra of the Furenu-wang (Krodharāja),
and also employing the Guhyahṛdaya-mantra, one performs the rite of empowerment by marking the forehead;
this immediately causes all evil spirits, ghosts, and demons, such as the Vināyakas and their like, [to be subdued].
All are terrified and submit, fleeing in fear; Just as when birds and beasts see a mass of fire at night, they all become afraid and scatter in haste.
May the fears of those who remove all obstacles be dispelled;
Should there be śramaṇas or brāhmaṇas, Or any people who behold [him], they shall all pay him reverence.

The deities of all *dhāraṇī* mantras who dwell within the maṇḍala rejoice at the sight [of the practitioner] and increase their protective guardianship without weariness. Whether traveling on roads, through wildernesses, mountains,
marshes, streams, ravines, or any such place, one need not fear robbers, sorcery, or poisons.
The perils of evil winds, thunder, hail, and lightning; the perils of lions, tigers, wolves, and other fierce beasts;

and the various calamities of vipers, snakes, adders, and scorpions—if a practitioner of mantras applies this medicine and, with a mind free from distraction, recollects me while chanting the *Amogha-mantra*, [they shall be protected].

I shall come before you and bestow my protective empowerment. Thus, through this *Amoghapāśahṛdaya-mātṛ-dhāraṇī-mantra-vidhi*, and by the power of the bodhicitta vows and the samaya, may all the Buddhas protect me;
may they grant their protection through the truth of their compassionate speech.
This is also the heart-mantra of Amoghapāśa, the power of the mudrās, dhāraṇīs, true mantras, secret maṇḍalas, and samādhis;
it is further the power of the practitioner’s sincere aspiration for bodhi. For this reason, I have advanced this person.
May all the aspirations of my heart be fulfilled. If there are sentient beings who do not rely on the Dharma but act with deceit and hypocrisy merely for the sake of livelihood;
or those who deceive others, destroy [the teachings], violate the pure conduct (*brahmacarya*), or dwell in impurity—I shall not manifest myself before them.
Why is this so? Because one has attained suchness by practicing the Dharma in accordance with the Dharma.
For this reason, those who uphold the Dharma should govern their minds according to the Dharma;
being pure both internally and externally, they cultivate and refine the Dharma, thereby definitively accomplishing all dharma-gates.
The *Avalokiteśvara* mantra: Oṃ ā-mogha-siddhe svāhā | Hrīḥ svāhā | Hrīḥ phaṭ | This rite consecrates white thread.
One should have a young girl join them together,
like sinews and so forth, into two thighs and three strands;
these are the three strands of rope.
The two ends and the center are tied together as a single knot.
Recite the respective mantras for each knot;
finally, tie all three knots together and join the two ends.
The mantra practitioner should always wear ornaments draped over the shoulders.

To empower the clothing with this samaya, one should don it while reciting the mantra: *Oṃ āmoghapāśa mūla-mūlare hūṃ haḥ kaṣi kaṣa vaśaṃkara tara tara svāhā*. Thus, one should thread and wear the garment, empowered by this samaya.
The mantra for shedding the robes is: Oṃ āmukhāvatāraṇīkṣipamudrāṇi pātum iha svāhā. This rite is for entering and exiting the maṇḍala.
When eating, walking, sitting, or lying down,
one should empower one's hands, remove one's garments,
place them in a clean location, and empower them once again.
The Mantra for Bathing: Oṃ na-kha-puṭa-mukha-sapāruṇa-vare viśodhaya hūṃ. With this dharma, empower scented bathing water and sprinkle it over the body to cleanse it.
The Mantra for Washing Hands and Face: Oṃ āmṛte mudgabhāṣmani vārīśodhani julu julu svāhā. This samaya empowers the pure water.
Wash your hands, face, and rinse your mouth and teeth.
Recite this mantra for protecting the body: Oṃ āmukāvaliśani kuru kuru svāhā. With this dharma, empower white mustard seeds and water.
If sprinkled upon one's body,
no non-human beings will be able to find an opportunity [to cause harm].
It is the same for protecting others.
The mantra for conferring the dharma is: Oṃ ā-mogha-sādhya mahā-padma tiṣṭha tiṣṭha hūṃ. When one who is to receive this dharma enters the gate of the maṇḍala, [this mantra is recited].
The Ācārya takes [the disciple’s] hand, performs the empowerment (*adhiṣṭhāna*), and leads them through the gate of the maṇḍala.
The mantra for protecting the companions is: Oṃ sarvatrā-mogha-vati tiṣṭha rakṣa tu hūṃ. This rite empowers the purified ashes.
Having applied [the substance] to the foreheads of one's companions and disciples, they will be protected.
The mantra for rectifying one’s deportment is: Oṃ trile rucye padma moghākaraṇi miri miri svāhā. This is the mantra of this rite.
Regarding those who perform the ritual within the maṇḍala and make offerings:
having empowered themselves and entered the boundary of the site,
they must not further touch or disturb the images of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, nor their mantra-seats.
One should properly arrange and perform all ritual activities according to the Dharma.

For the mantra of the Jewel Cord (*ratnasūtra*), recite: *Oṃ pratyavekṣaṇamahāpratyavekṣaṇa sara sara samantitanapariṣṭhāpayamoghaprabhāsana dhuru dhuru svāhā*. With this rite, one consecrates a cord of five-colored threads.
The outer boundary of the encircled altar is the gateway.

The mantra for suspending the banner is: Oṃ miñjitra-mogha-vāse-tarodana-lagna-ga miśuddhaya kṣiṇi kṣiṇi hūṃ. Regarding this rite, when suspending the banner or when drawing the banner-seal (dhvajamudrā):
One should empower all of them and immediately suspend them.
To perform the mantra for the arrow, recite: Oṃ āmukhaśara vajraduṇḍa trātrātra svāhā. By this rite, one empowers the arrow.
Insert and hold [the arrow].
The painted arrow is treated in the same way.

The mantra for opening the gate of the maṇḍala is: Oṃ (1) mīpuramogha (2) mahā-ṭaṅkavajra-miśrite (3) siri siri (4) svāhā (5). When a recipient of the dharma enters the gate of the maṇḍala by means of this rite...
Furthermore, at the moment of one's own entry,
by consecrating the gate of the maṇḍala, one immediately enters the maṇḍala;
this is equivalent to entering all the celestial palaces within all Buddha-fields.
The Mantra for Purifying Flowers: Oṃ nana-mi-citra-mogha puṣpa-phala-ratna-prayā prapara hūṃ. With this dharma, empower various branches, flowers, and leaves.
Insert [the vessel] into the mouth of the vase.
Tie five-colored threads around the neck of the vase.
Furthermore, empower it and place it within the altar cloth.
The Mantra of the Incense Burner: Oṃ āmogharatnābhimukhacintābhūte hūṃ jvala saṃpārana samantadīpane jvala jvala svāhā. This rite consecrates the incense burner.
Place it within the maṇḍala and offer incense as an offering.
The mantra for the precious flask is: Oṃ jvalati ratnagaṭṭa śarini dume dume svāhā. This rite consecrates the precious flask.
Arrange offerings of abundant ghee, milk, curd, and rice, and recite this mantra for the precious vessel: Oṃ hūṃ bhojanamudgāpātama-vare pura-pura hūṃ. This is the samaya.
One should use consecrated ceramic vessels for offerings.
The *arghya* mantra is: Oṃ āryāvalokiteśvara nātha vati svāhā. This method of consecrating *arghya* water should be used for making offerings.
The Amoghapāśakalparāja Sūtra, Scroll Second; The Amoghapāśakalparāja Sūtra, Scroll Third.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Bodhiruci of India during the Great Tang Dynasty.
The Third Chapter on the Mantras for Secret Accomplishment, Part Two:
The Kuntī Mantra. Oṃ śrāṇi śrāya āmukha-pūjani māta-mātani hūṃ. This samaya-consecrated Kuntī should be used for making offerings.

The Boundary-Delimiting Mantra: Oṃ (1) vaḥ (2) vāruṇi (3) vibhajāya tu (4) samantānāṃ (5) sara-sama (6) vāsariṇi (7) svāhā. This rite establishes the positions for the altar, the streets, and the boundaries.
Consecrate the site of the mandala,
then demarcate the boundaries of the streets and positions,
and draw them according to the ritual rules.
The mantra for the painted image is: Oṃ nana-pāra-haṇa āmukha-mudrā-āveśaya āveśaya svāhā. When painting the various images within this dharma-maṇḍala, [recite this].
When the painting is completed, perform the general empowerment for all its constituent parts.
The mantra for the cord-boundary is: Oṃ ā-mogha-ratna-sūtra-vare jñi jñi svāhā. By this rite, empower the five-colored threads.
One should use this thread mixed with vermilion to outline and measure all the positions and boundaries around the altar;
likewise, when one intends to paint an image upon a white cotton cloth or silk on a wall,
one should always use this same thread mixed with vermilion for the outlining and measurement.
This is praised for its meritorious qualities by all the noble ones (ārya).
The mantra for the gateway is: Oṃ 1. Mipura-vare 2. Para-vaiśraye 3. Āmogha-patme 4. Hūṃ 5. When performing this rite, one should draw the gateway of the maṇḍala at this time.
The ground of the empowerment gate (*adhiṣṭhāna-mukha*) is the drawing of the maṇḍala gate.
The mantra for the golden vessel is: Oṃ (1) vaṃ vajra-mudgara-ghaṭa-vare (2) jili-jiri (3) hūṃ (4). This samaya empowerment of the golden vessel should be used for making offerings.
The mantra for the silver vessel is: Oṃ pracura-lūṣa-lūha-vajre āmukha pātrami svāhā. This samaya-mantra is used to consecrate the silver vessel for the purpose of making offerings.

The mantra for food and drink is: Oṃ (1) mimita (2) rūpāhāra-prakaraṇa (3) tsara-tsara (4) āmukha-vati (5) svāhā (6). By this samaya-consecration, various kinds of sweet delicacies and food and drink are empowered.
Make abundant offerings.
The Mantra for Floating Flowers is: Oṃ, kaṃ, khaṃ, gandhe, nū-sa-r-i-ṇi, ā-mu-ga-ja-re, dhara dhara, svāhā. By means of this rite, empower various flowers and float them upon the water.
One should use this for making offerings.
The incense mantra is: Oṃ khaṇḍarohā-saṃpūjani svāhā. This dharma should be empowered with incense at every session.
Burn this as an offering to all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Vajras, and devas.
The mantra for smearing the altar is: Oṃ amala-kāya-śuddhe amṛte gandha-prabhāvani pravarapravara hūṃ. This dharma empowers the fragrant mud and scented water.
Perform the offering upon the maṇḍala.
The mantra for powdered incense is: Oṃ khandarohaṇi purabhedani julu julu svāhā. By this rite, the powdered incense is consecrated.
Distribute it within the maṇḍala and offer it as an offering.
The mantra for the unguent is: Oṃ sāmāsamantitanirmale gandhottame svāhā. This is the consecration of the unguent through the samaya.
When the bathing of the body is completed, one should rub and anoint it upon the body.
The Consecration Mantra is: Oṃ hūṃ khaṇḍa-parāpūraṇi sagarājñe hūṃ dhiṣṭhitakaraśūnari prāṇapravarya jayasiddhe svāhā. By this rite, the incense water flask is empowered.
When the ācārya and the person receiving the dharma have finished washing, they should use [this mantra] for the consecration (abhiṣeka).
The mantra for offering food is: Oṃ raśaraśa gharavati sarvabhūtiṣṭhe sambhāraya hūṃ. This is the samaya for when offering food.
Recite this while holding the abundant food.
The mantra for offering the food is: Oṃ hūṃ hūṃ bhūrjaṇa puraya mibhura-parāpi svāhā. This is the consecration of the food and drink through the *samaya*.
One should hold these as offerings.
The mantra for the three white foods is: Oṃ tilasarṣapāḥ | yavān | varmiśrāḥ | rājacandrāvatī | sūraprasūrasū | hūṃ. By this samaya-consecration, [one consecrates] the ghee, milk, and curd.
Hold it to perform the offering.
The mantra for the fruit is: Oṃ (1) phalavati (2) sāravaṭi (3) hūṃ phaṭ vaṇase (4) tara tara tu (5) svāhā (6). With this samaya-mantra, empower the fruit and hold it to perform the offering.
The Mantra of Pure Flowers: Oṃ hūṃ ku-supuṣpā nana puṣpa parāvāsani bho bho svāhā. With this, empower all the flowers through the samaya-consecration and scatter them as an offering.

The Mantra for Gathering Flowers: Oṃ (1) mi-mi-dha-ra-ta (2) pu-ṣpa-baddho-dhi-ta (3) va-na-se-pa-ti (4) ā-hā-ra (5) saṃpu-raṇa-kiṃ-bī (6) svāhā (7). When gathering flowers, branches, or leaves, this rite [should be performed].
First, empower it;
then, collect it and offer it as an oblation.
The incense mantra is: Oṃ mahā-dūṣya-megha-pratara-sañcintyānāṃ svamantrīṇāṃ hūṃ hūṃ svāhā. When performing this rite of homa, [recite this].
Empower incense and burn it as an offering to all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and devas.
The mantra for inviting the Fire God (Agni) is: Oṃ agnaye jvala jvala nirmukte svāhā. By this rite, one invites the Fire God and immediately performs the offering.

The Mantra of Adornment: Oṃ (1) mi-mi-dha-maṇi (2) kānaka (3) ratna-īśvara (4) puṣpaṇa (5) maṇi maṇi (6) āmogha-maṇi (7) svāhā (8). By this rite, all jewels, bracelets, armlets, necklaces, banners, and parasols are consecrated.
Zhuangzi and Liezi made offerings to their various images.
If one uses rings, bracelets, or necklaces to adorn oneself, these too should be consecrated.

The mantra for offering is: Oṃ (1) padmakaṇṭha (2) mibhuraṇakārya (3) sarma sarma (4) sarvatathāgata (5) tiṣṭhati (6) svāhā (7). When performing this rite, whether during praise or recitation, [one should do so].
First, recite three times the mantra for praise and offering.
The mantra for prostration is: Oṃ sarvabuddhabodhisattvaśrīpraṇāmatāṃ namasyāmi tathāgatam iḥ miḥ miḥ dhūrṇi svāhā. When performing this rite while prostrating to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas:
First, recite this three times.
With palms joined, prostrate and pay homage to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, who will joyfully praise you.
The mantra for walking the path is: Oṃ naśani śahaḥ (śa is pronounced with a retroflex *ṣ*) vipaṇḍana prasaratu hūṃ. When practicing this rite of walking the path:
First, recite [the mantra] three times while performing the circumambulation with palms joined.
This is for all devas and humans to praise simultaneously.
The Weapon Mantra is: Oṃ mi-mi-dha-yu-dha (1) jvalita-prabhe (2) prajvala (3) prajvala-sphura hūṃ (5). By this rite, one empowers the weapon-seal (*āyudha-mudrā*) that has been drawn.
All mantra-deities and vidyā-deities will be delighted.
The mantra of the vajra-bell is: Oṃ hūṃ mukuṭa-mi-bhura-śvare samatūra-khuśaruṭi raṇa-raṇa hūṃ. Within this maṇḍala, [recite it].
When reciting praises, walking the path, invoking deities, chanting mantras, or performing homa,
one should empower the bell and ring it; thus,
all worthy sages will be awakened and joyfully assemble at the gathering.
The Mantra of Lamp-Light: Oṃ raśmijvala mantidhana vāsaya mahāmaṇi ratnākṣite svāhā. With this dharma, empower the lamp-light offering.
Then, cause all the celestial beings, mantra-deities, vidyā-deities, and messengers to behold the offering of the jewel-lamp’s radiant flame.
The invocation mantra is: Oṃ (1) dūru dūru (2) āvaha ākarṣaya (3) āgaccha bhīḥ (4). When this rite is bestowed upon others, [one should recite it].
Burn consecrated guggulu incense to invoke all Buddhas,
Bodhisattvas, mantras, vidyās, and deities, so that they may bestow their supernatural powers and blessings.
The mantra for removing obstacles is: Oṃ ṭaṭa sattvamīmudraṇi sama-sama vāre svāhā. Recite this mantra seven times with a vigorous voice.
It subdues all enemies, calamities, spirits, and deities, causing them all to submit and their minds to become joyful.
The mantra for the rosary is: Oṃ miñjitra maṇi mibhura paravāradani hūṃ. When visualizing this method regarding the rosary:

Furthermore, when taking up the beads, one should empower them by performing the *mudrā* and reciting the mantra for the flower garland: Oṃ miñjitra-labdha-nirvāra-ṣma-vare-puṣpa-vati svāhā. This method empowers the flower garland for offering.
If it is wrapped around the head, neck, arms, or wrists, it likewise provides empowerment.
Recite this mantra of accomplishment: Oṃ, hūṃ, rocani, āmukhīye, parāvarai, sarvam icchatiṣṭha, siddhiśuddham locite, svāhā. One should pray for its protective grace at every session of this rite.
First, recite [the mantra] three times to request empowerment and bring about the manifestation of accomplishment.
Then, the mantra for dismissal is: Oṃ ā-mogha-pratimā-samantāpavane tara-tara gaccha-cchinda-saṃvara-vān svāhā. When this ritual procedure and the making of prayers are completed:
Recite this three times. Then,
address the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, devas, and bright spirits, requesting them to each return to their respective palaces.
The mantra of the mendicant’s staff (khakkhara) is: Oṃ khaṃ purani nāgamilocani hūṃ. Upon this maṇḍala empowered by this samaya, one should draw the seal (mudrā) of the mendicant’s staff.
The mantra of the Precious Alms Bowl is: Oṃ pratara-praṇi prāya āmukha-vati samantapāra-bhe svāhā. This rite involves consecrating the drawing of the seal of the Precious Alms Bowl.
The mantra of the auspicious *kuśa* grass: Oṃ nara-pavite miṣṭi-ṣṭite para-sare sara-sare riṣi-burte svāhā. With this dharma, one consecrates the *kuśa* grass.
Scatter [the materials] clockwise around the four sides of the fire altar;
perform the homa upon the ritual seat according to the dharma, executing the rites in accordance with the respective directions.
The homa mantra is: Oṃ jvala jvala śikhi raśmijvāle svāhā. With this dharma, empower the clarified butter, honey, and various incenses.
Perform the homa offering to all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and celestial deities.
The mantra for bathing in the river is: Oṃ bhrūmi bhrūmasane varapradare nāgabandhani svāhā. This samaya is for when entering the river to bathe.
One should recite this five times.
One should also empower the drawing of the River and Ocean Seals with it.
The mantra for shoes is: Oṃ kha-ga-ja-li-ni ga-ma-ga-ma-ya pa-na-bha-ra-ca-li-ni hūṃ. If one enters the maṇḍala or the Buddha hall by means of this method, [one shall be protected].
Consecrate new, clean shoes by reciting the mantra three times and then put them on.
One should also consecrate the drawing of the shoe seal in the same manner.
The Consecration Mantra: Oṃ sarvatrāmoghapāśamahāsthāmaprāptābhiṣekāya padmarāgaprabhāya padmatrāṇāya svāhā. This rite should be performed within the consecration maṇḍala.
Holding a flask in the left hand and pressing the crown of the head with the right,
perform the empowerment seven times by forming the mudrā and making this vow:
"World-Honored One, if there be anyone who reads, recites, receives, or upholds the mantra-samaya of the Mother Dhāraṇī of the Heart-King Amoghapāśa..."
One must fully rely upon these samayas of the wondrous verses of these mantras;
for within each and every mantra,
there exists immeasurable, boundless, and ineffable, vast majesty and supernatural power.
They are all able to exercise mastery over the production of hundreds of thousands of koṭis of wondrous and marvelous jewels from the Buddha-fields,
including all kinds of precious incense, precious flowers, precious vessels, precious pearls, and jeweled necklaces.
All exquisite jewel palaces, towers, and pavilions, with precious lion thrones;
all wondrous and marvelous jewel banners, pennants, canopies, hanging pearls, necklaces, and nets;
and all the ambrosial food and drink of the various devas.
The jewel palaces, jewel lion thrones, and jewel lotus thrones of all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the ten directions;
and all the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, and gandharvas.
The palaces, food, and drink of the asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras,
and mahoragas appear in such infinite varieties;
all of these are the samaya of the mantra of the Mother Dhāraṇī, the Heart-King of Amoghapāśa.
All things manifest;
therefore, the holder should,
with a truly pure mind, [practice].
Receive and uphold according to the Dharma;
empower each object three or five times,
and do not allow it to be forgotten or neglected.
I shall behold this with immeasurable joy;
thus I will manifest a truly wondrous form-body and purify all karmic obstacles of the ten evil deeds and the five heinous crimes.
He causes all to become completely pure,
so that their aspirations are entirely fulfilled.
Furthermore, he grants them the most supreme and vast liberation-lotus of King Amogha.
He also bestows the samaya of the seals of all great maṇḍalas,
as well as the empowerment-samaya of the vidyādhara of the vast and unerring mantra, so that one may attain the true accomplishment of all mundane and supramundane dharmas.
They shall all quickly reach fulfillment.
Furthermore, they will attain all worldly fearlessnesses,
becoming noble, wealthy, and prosperous, and being loved, respected, praised, and honored by others.
If one upholds this samaya,
one should not give rise to a mind of doubt;
I now declare with certainty that such is the case.
One should always be diligent and sincere, giving rise to the mind of great compassion.
With this mind of true compassion and words of loving-kindness,
whether walking or staying, one should act accordingly.
One should read, recite, receive, uphold, maintain mindfulness of, and contemplate this samaya.
One should constantly keep in mind all the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Vajras of the ten directions,
reverently prostrating to, praising, and making offerings to them without ever ceasing or forgetting.
Whenever the time comes, one should sit cross-legged upon white *śara* grass before Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva and recite this Mother Dhāraṇī mantra and the Secret Heart Mantra.
May I be able to fulfill the aspirations of all beings;
may they increase day by day without even momentary regression,
and may they realize bodhi.
Chapter Four: The Samaya of Secret Mudrās, Part One. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara...
By means of this Amoghapāśahṛdaya-mātṛ-dhāraṇī-mantra-samaya, the reality of the most supreme, vast liberation-lotus maṇḍala-mudrā-samaya.
He addressed the Venerable Blessed One,
speaking these verses:
"Revealing this unfailing dharma of liberation, Pure and perfect like a lotus flower."
With compassion to rescue all sentient beings, may all the Buddhas of the ten directions bestow their blessings upon the assembly of all devas,
nāgas, and the eight classes of beings; upon the great mantra-siddhas,
the ascetic siddhas, the goddess Gaurī, the Śuddhāvāsa devas, Īśvara, and Maheśvara.
Mahābrahmā, Śakra-devendra, Maheśvara, Nārāyaṇa,
and the Trāyastriṃśa gods; Kumāra, the deities of the Trāyastriṃśa palace,
the Cāturmahārājika gods, Yama-rāja, Varuṇa, Vāyu, Agni, and the others.
The Sun-god, the Moon-god, and the celestial deities of the constellations, seeing this *Amogha-mantra-sūtra*,
gathered together at once to respectfully protect the pure place of practice in every direction—
the Great Lord Maheśvara, and the hosts of goddesses Jaya and Vijayā.
The deity Śaṅkara, the deity Maheśvara, the deity Bhṛkuṭī, Aṅgiras, Brahmā, Vibhāvasu,
the Great Virtuous Deity (Mahāguṇadeva), the Goddess of Eloquence (Sarasvatī),
the deity Mahāpadma-kiṭi, the messenger Duti, and Utpalī.
The Flower-tooth Deity Supoṣa, the deity dwelling on Mount Kīlaśa,
the Great Mother of Ghosts Hārītī, the Ten Great Vajradharas,
the Great Vajradharas, and the Vidyārāja; upon seeing this *Amogha-mantra-sūtra*, [they all rejoice].
In a pure place of practice according to the direction, All gathered together at once, joyfully guarding [him],
The Thousand-Armed and Thousand-Eyed Avalokiteśvara, With hands forming a thousand mudrās, stands before him. Furthermore,
all the Buddhas of the ten directions, Each accompanied by their respective Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas, [appear].
The Blue-Necked Mother of the Avalokiteśvara Family; the assembly of Bodhisattvas of the Ten Pāramitās;
the Amoghapāśa Avalokiteśvara; the one who manifests in the form of Mahābrahmā, Niṣpaṇḍita Avalokiteśvara; and the Great Vidyārājñī Hayagrīva Avalokiteśvara.
Paṇamukha Avalokiteśvara; Eleven-faced Avalokiteśvara; Four-faced Great Compassionate Avalokiteśvara;
the Immortal Avalokiteśvara who removes the eight hardships—all of whom uphold the Amogha-dhāraṇī; the most supreme, vast, and great liberation.
The Lotus Family Maṇḍala: All methods of illusory transformations and miraculous displays each manifest various wondrous physical forms.
Whether in dreams or upon waking, beholding this assembly, they all dwell before me as the Western Realm of Ultimate Bliss is revealed— A great radiance of every exquisite color.
Amitābha Buddha sits upon a precious throne, surrounded by an immeasurable assembly of bodhisattvas,
preaching the Dharma of eternal bliss to the multitude; in a mere instant,
they all behold him appearing once more throughout the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, in hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of worlds.
The Tathāgatas of all buddha-fields as numerous as atoms,
each surrounded by assemblies of hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of bodhisattvas, all appear simultaneously upon awakening from the dream;
they further manifest various great signs at the site of enlightenment, the adamantine throne.
At the place where the Wheel of Dharma was turned, at the place where Māra was subdued, and at the place where Perfect Enlightenment was attained by Vairocana—
if there are sentient beings who are stubborn and dull-witted, who disparage what I have spoken and give rise to suspicion,
then even though they may read, recite, and uphold [the teachings], they shall not perceive such auspicious signs.
If there are sentient beings with perverse and evil wisdom who harm the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha and destroy the Path,
or those who have committed the five heinous crimes, all the worthy and holy ones will abandon them;
they shall fall into the great Avīci Hell and undergo intense suffering for ten million kalpas.
For sentient beings burdened by such karmic offenses, who give rise to a heart of fear and repent for their many sins—
if they are able to see or hear this sutra and receive and uphold it from a teacher for seven days—
then even such retribution as that of the Avīci Hell will be completely consumed and extinguished in a single moment.
If there be anyone who even momentarily beholds this sutra,
it is as if they have truly seen Avalokiteśvara within the palace of Mount Potalaka, amidst his various and subtle forms.
If there be one whose devotion is peerless and sincere, who constantly upholds this sutra of all dharmas—

Then one will behold all the Tathāgatas within hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of world-systems as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in the ten directions, appearing simultaneously before one’s presence;
some will offer exhaustive praise and gaze upon one, while others will secretly bestow the gates of great wisdom.
By this power of non-emptiness, this person’s body is moistened and nourished by the pure, wondrous Dharma;
they will soon become equal to a Tathāgata sitting at the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa).

Through the merit of turning the wheel of the true Dharma, their blessings and lifespan increase beyond measure, doubling and extending far; free from all premature death and illness, they shall be like the devas.
Those who thus read, recite, receive, and uphold [this teaching] should always bathe and cleanse themselves in a pure,
secluded, and excellent place, anointing their bodies with incense; they should constantly wear fragrant-smoked garments that are perpetually clean,
sever all worldly discourse, remain ever tranquil and silent, and practice by making various kinds of offerings.
Anointing the hands with fragrant ointment and forming the mudrā of retention, one should call to mind all the World-Honored Ones of the ten directions,
taking refuge in them day and night, praising and prostrating before them. Contemplating the Greatly Compassionate One, Avalokiteśvara,
one should give rise to a mind of great compassion and equanimity, practicing with diligence, sincerity, and reverence for the Dharma.

Not for the sake of fame or profit, they practice flattery or deceit; rather, they give rise to compassion toward all sentient beings and toward those who share their same karma and serve them. All together they practice the Dharma that is unfailing.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara...
Having recited these verses,
the treatise explains the mudrās for all supernatural powers (*abhijñā*) and the *samaya* seal:
the root mudrā consists of joining the two hands in *añjali* with the palms hollowed.
Bend the tips of the two index fingers so that they rest against the upper joint of the middle fingers.
Extend the two thumbs side by side and straight.
This mudrā can compile all the bodhi-dharma-gates of all Buddhas,
and it can also summon and invoke Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva to come and bestow protection and mindfulness.
The mantra for this mudrā is: Oṃ ā-mogha-mi-kuṭe mite svā-dhā-rū-kaya-maṃ sthiraya dhitiṣṭha mogha-pratime jvara-mijvara-saṃjvara hūṃ hūṃ. This is the mantra for this mudrā.
It is named the "Lotus Light Supernatural Power and Majestic Virtue of the Illumination that Contemplates the Three Times as Not Empty.
If one truly possesses a mind of great compassion and recites while forming this mudrā, [the goal will be attained].
At that time, one shall cause the Buddha-fields as numerous as the atoms of the three periods of time to tremble all at once;
all the Tathāgatas within these Buddha-fields will be filled with joy and emit great rays of light.
He reached out his hand and stroked [his] head,
bestowing the supreme divine transformations of the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya-mātṛ-dhāraṇī-mantra*,
which removes all veils, hindrances, the eight difficulties, and great terrors.
The Śuddhāvāsa deities, Īśvara, Maheśvara, Mahābrahmā, Śakra, and all the other devas,
shall joyfully protect this Maudgalyāyana.
Within this Dharma, it is the most supreme:
join the wrists with the lotus mudrā, open both palms wide,
and bend the two middle fingers so that their tips are half an inch apart.
Bend the tips of the two index fingers and the two ring fingers so that they are each two inches apart.
Bend the two thumbs and the two little fingers, likewise [two inches apart], with the middle fingers half an inch apart; this is the mudrā for the mantra.
Oṃ āmukha-mukha-samaya jvala hūṃ hrīḥ kṣi hrīḥ kṣi tara tara mahāsattva hūṃ. If one binds and maintains this seal and mantra:
The Buddhas of the three periods of time joyfully praise and bestow their empowerment upon the holder of this [mantra].
Through the heart of great compassion, supreme efficacy is accomplished and various auspicious signs appear.
One shall thereby fully realize all Tathāgatas’ dhāraṇī-mantras, liberation-maṇḍalas, mudrās, and samayas.
The mantras, maṇḍalas, and mudrās of the entire family of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattvas shall likewise manifest before them,
and they will always be joyfully beheld by the mind of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.
Add the supreme vow.
For the Lotus Request for Protection mudrā, join the palms at the heart;
within the great hollow of the palms, [place the fingers].
With the two middle fingers and the two ring fingers,
join them together vertically with their tips touching;
then, with the two index fingers, pinch the first joints on the backs of the two middle fingers.
The two thumbs are slightly extended upward as if about to touch one another;
the two little fingers are stretched straight out,
splayed apart at a distance of two cun.
Form this mudrā.
This is the mudrā and mantra for all flowers, incense, food and drink, perfumed water, all vessels, robes, and offering implements.
Oṃ āmukha pūjaye mahāsattvāyatu eka-maṇḍale dhiri dhiri mīra mīra pūjāpūje svāhā. This is the mudrā and mantra.
Invoke all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Vajras, devas, nāgas, spirits, and vidyā-deities to assemble for protection and blessing.
Form the boundary-sealing mudrā by joining the palms with the hollows of the hands held open.
With the two index fingers and the two ring fingers,
extend them upright and join their tips together;
then bend the tips of the two middle fingers.
On the first joint of the side of the ring finger;
the tips of the two middle fingers are two *aṅgula* apart;
[and] the tips of the two thumbs.
Place each thumb on the side of the first joint of the index finger.
Spread the two little fingers apart at a distance of two inches and seal with this mantra:
Oṃ ā-mogha-vajra-jvalita-pradīpte mahā-siṃha-kṣe-pakṣa-siṃha jvala jvala hūṃ phaṭ. This is the mantra for this mudrā.
One binds the boundaries of the ten directions and uses them for self-protection.
Within the ten directions of the mandala, a great protection extending seven yojanas is established.
The mudrā of the Supreme Lotus follows the first mudrā described above.
Change the tips of the two index fingers so that each rests on the upper side of the middle joint of the middle finger,
with a distance of six fen between them.
Spread apart the two thumbs and the two little fingers,
with the tips of each separated by two inches.
This mudrā is the samaya of the Great Maṇḍala Mudrā for accomplishing all liberations.
One will also be able to harmonize and master all maṇḍalas, mudrās, and samayas, swiftly attaining supreme efficacy.

The mantra for this mudrā is: Oṃ (1) vaśire (2) vaśiradhiṣṭhita (3) pratyamīśvaropadeśe (4) dhara dhara hūṃ (5) parāmṛśaya tu (6) tiryagatrabodgata (7) dṛṣṭiṃ dehi (8) svāhā (9). One who holds and binds this mudrā with a mind of great compassion—
May the gates of all the palaces in every buddha-field throughout the ten directions be opened,
and may they tremble in six ways;
likewise, may the gates of all the palaces of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven also be opened.
Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva gazes upon them with joy;
emitting light that touches them, he causes them to attain purity and extinguishes their past and present five sins of immediate retribution.
After passing away from this life, one will be born in the palaces of the Buddha-fields of the ten directions;
the gates of the sixteen great hells will be closed,
and having transcended the evil destinies, one will attain great liberation.
For the mudrā of the Supreme Fist (*jyeṣṭhamuṣṭi*), with the right hand,
use the tip of the thumb to press against the first joint at the base of the ring finger;
tightly clench the four fingers around the thumb to form a fist.
One who binds this mudrā shall enter the samaya of the mudrā of the vast maṇḍala of liberation and attain great accomplishment.
Use the previous mudrā and mantra.
For the Lotus-Head Mudrā, follow the fifth mudrā,
with the modification that the two thumbs are changed.
Bend the head [of the right hand] into the palm; with the right thumb,
press down specifically upon the left thumb.
The mantra for the seal upon the first part of the fingernail is:
Oṃ āmukha-bhūta-mārjani viśodhaya hūṃ dīri dīri mimāre svāhā. This seal and mantra are used at the time of the consecration bath.
Form the incense flask mudrā. Then,
having bound this mudrā and placed it upon the crown of the head,
one person should be made to hold the incense flask.
One should perform the empowerment by sprinkling water upon the crown of the head and further bathe the body; thereby,
all heavy sins and obscurations from the past shall be completely eliminated and extinguished.
One attains purity of body, and the accumulation of merit becomes full;
one accomplishes all dharmas, which increase more and more,
and is joyfully protected by all the devas.
Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva protects and bestows his grace.
This is the mantra of the Heart-King Dhāraṇī of Amoghapāśa, the most supreme accomplishment of the samaya-siddhi.
Forming the seal of the Great Samādhi, sit in the full lotus posture.
Join the two hands in *añjali* and bend the two index fingers.
On the upper side of the middle joint of the middle finger,
the tips should not touch one another;
the remaining eight fingers are all extended and pressed tightly together.
Place the mudrā at the heart and extend it straight downward;
this is the mantra for the inverted-hanging mudrā: Oṃ āmukha-vajra jṛṃta pātami śvabhra hūṃ. When binding and maintaining this mudrā with this mantra:
Just as when entering meditative absorption,
his body is as firm and solid as the Vajra Sumeru King of Mountains;
furthermore, he is clad in the armor of vajra-mail.
There shall be no harm from others;
all vināyakas will flee in terror, unable to cause any affliction or injury.
The Seal of Mastery follows the seventh seal;
however, change the two index fingers so that they press upon the middle phalanges on the backs of the middle fingers.
Slightly open the palms.
Then, extend the two thumbs outward,
with a distance of three inches between them.
Place the mudrā at the heart and recite the mantra:
Oṃ padmīśvara āmokṣa-parāna vīra vīra svāhā. If one employs this mudrā and mantra with a mind of pure great compassion, [the desired result will be attained].
When one performs the ritual of binding the mudrā and making offerings before Avalokiteśvara,

one shall obtain [the presence of] all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the three times throughout all the Buddha-fields of the ten directions, numbering as many as the sands of the Ganges, koṭis, nayutas, and hundreds of thousands.
Beholding and praising them,
he simultaneously emitted light that illuminated and brought comfort.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara...
It is also manifested before one;
through this, one shall attain correspondence with the merits of the ten pāramitās.
If a practitioner of mantras recites [this] every eighth day of the waxing moon.
If one fasts and maintains silence for one day,
and recites the Mother Dhāraṇī Mantra and the Secret Heart Mantra one hundred and eight times while forming the mudrās,
one will swiftly cause the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara to manifest his body, place his hand upon one’s head, and speak these words.
"Excellent, excellent, son of good family!
What you have now done is the most supreme and sublime Dharma for King Ajātaśatru.
What wish do you require?"
I shall fulfill your wishes.
You are now my son within the *Āmogha-rāja-samādhi*.
You have now attained the *Amoghapāśa-hṛdaya-rāja-mātṛ-dhāraṇī-mantra*, as well as the liberation, the maṇḍala, the mudrās, and the samaya.
Do not be anxious or fearful.
Generate a heart of great compassion toward all sentient beings;
with this mind, you should constantly cultivate your own body and abide securely within my Dharma.
This present body of yours is your final incarnation;
after casting off this life,
you shall go directly to the Land of Ultimate Bliss in the west to sit upon a lotus throne.
Adorning their own bodies with all the primary and secondary marks,
they were equal to all those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas,
hearing and learning all dharmas that are eternal, blissful, and pure.
From this present life until reaching enlightenment,
they shall never again suffer premature death or illness, and shall never regress;
such is the realization of those who attain it.
One should serve and make offerings to Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva in accordance with the Dharma;
one should always remain serene and silent, not engaging in debate with others,
and give rise to great compassion toward all sentient beings.
Sitting according to the ritual rules, one forms the mudrās and recites the Mother Dhāraṇī Mantra and the Secret Heart Mantra;
furthermore, one realizes the Samaya of the Great Mantra-Sages of the Maṇḍala of Vast and Unfailing Great Spiritual Powers.
Eighteen koṭi-nayuta-hundred-thousand mantra-vidyādhara-sages accompanied one another as companions, sporting in the realm of space,
having attained great mastery and an exceedingly long lifespan.
Furthermore, he realized the Samaya of the Great Supernatural Power of the Vast and Radiant Crown of Non-Emptiness,
whereby he traveled to all worlds throughout the trichiliocosm in the ten directions and returned to his original place in the time it takes to extend one's arm.
Furthermore, he realized the Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva’s Samaya of the Great Illusory Transformation of the King of Non-Emptiness and the Samaya of the Pure Celestial Eye of Non-Emptiness;
by the power of this illusory transformation samaya, he...
He manifests in forms identical to sentient beings,
appearing as those such as the Śuddhāvāsakāyika devas and Īśvara.
Maheśvara Deva, Mahābrahmā Deva, Śakra Deva, Nārāyaṇa Deva,
Kumāra Deva, and the Four Great Kings.
The deities of water, wind, sun, and moon; King Yama;
the eight classes of nāgas and spirits, humans and non-humans alike;
and all sentient beings, including those of the water and land among the animals.
All those of similar kind are manifested to gather, transform, and deliver them,
causing them all to submit in accordance with the Dharma and attain great liberation.
World-Honored One, this dharma is named the Heart-King Mother Dhāraṇī Mantra of the Unfailing Lasso, the Samaya for the accomplishment of worldly goals and the subduing of sentient beings.
Furthermore, one shall behold all the buddha-fields of the ten directions,
with all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas,
manifesting their bodies simultaneously.
He bestows upon them the prophecy of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*,
such that they shall never again fall back from enlightenment.
In this way, he gives rise to great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*) toward all sentient beings.
One should sit according to the ritual rules before Avalokiteśvara;
however, those who perform the mudrās and recitations need not sit according to the ritual rules.
Without forming mudrās, one should recite [the mantra] one hundred thousand times or ten million times.
One will receive the consolation and prophetic assurance (vyākaraṇa) of all Tathāgatas;
all wisdom and understanding, as well as the six pāramitās, will be spontaneously accomplished.
Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva will manifest his form before them,
thereby fulfilling all their aspirations;
all evil karmic obstructions and all illnesses will simultaneously be extinguished.
Therefore, the practitioner should constantly keep all Buddhas in mind without allowing the mind to become distracted or disordered;
this will cause one to attain the most supreme accomplishment.
*Amoghapāśakalparāja Sūtra*, Scroll Three.
The Amoghapāśakalparāja Sūtra, Scroll Four, translated by the Tripitaka Master Bodhiruci of India during the Great Tang Dynasty;
Chapter Four: Secret Mudrās and Samayas, Part Two.
To perform the seal of accomplishment, join the two hands in *añjali* with the palms hollowed out;
extend the two index fingers and the two ring fingers,
bending them flat so that their tips touch one another.
The two middle fingers are slightly curved and held upright with their tips joined.
The tips of the two index fingers and the first joints of the two ring fingers are extended upward.
The two thumbs are placed side by side, slightly bent, and held upright.
From the head [of the hand], measure one inch and four *fen* toward the side of the second fingers.
Extend both little fingers upright.
Press against the sides of the ring fingers, which are two inches apart, while reciting the seal-mantra (*mudrā-mantra*).
Oṃ tura-tura pāthami āmukhasiddhi hūṃ. This is the seal of samādhi; by binding it, one attains mastery.
May the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara swiftly bestow his grace.
May all the supramundane dharmas of King Amogha be accomplished;
may his merit and virtue increase and flourish, and may he be joyfully praised by all people.
All the celestial deities shall protect and guard him.
Form the Vajra-Lotus Heart Seal by covering the palm of the right hand with the upturned palm of the left hand.
The backs of the two hands are joined together.
The right little finger is inserted between the joints of the left thumb,
and the right thumb is inserted between the joints of the left little finger.
Bend the index fingers of both hands sharply into the palms;
place the middle and ring fingers of both hands side by side and extend them onto the backs of the hands.
Place the mudrā at the heart, sit upright with the body straight, and with a mind like a vajra, maintain pure mindfulness and recite the Mudrā-mantra:
Oṃ ārya-mogha-hṛdaya pratīhāriṇi dhāraya dhāraya pratīhāramudrā mahāmaṇḍala-hṛdaya hūṃ. For those who bind and maintain this seal-samādhi, [the benefits shall follow].
One who recites the Secret Heart Mantra seventeen times will achieve success in all ritual activities.
[Then,] form the noose mudrā (pāśamudrā) and place the palm of the left hand over the heart.
The thumb is bent toward the palm,
its tip remaining one cun from the palm;
as for the index, middle, ring, and little fingers:
Each [finger] is slightly bent;
the space between each of the four fingers is one cun apart,
resembling the petals of a lotus flower.
The right hand is turned upward,
its palm resting upon the back of the left hand at a distance of seven inches.
The thumb is bent toward the palm;
its tip is one inch from the palm. The middle finger is bent at its tip so that it aligns with the thumb.
The thumbs are separated by one cun on the back of the hands;
the index, ring, and little fingers are slightly bent toward the palms.

The mantra for this mudrā is: Oṃ 1. *paśupa* (vocative), *pati-paśyata-ra* 2. *śānta-svāhā-sara* 3. *raśmi* 4. *parātimantrita-kaya* 5. *ākariṣaṇi* 6. *buddhe buddhe* 7. *puru puru* 8. *amogha-tyaja-siddhe* 9. *hūṃ* 10. Whoever binds this mudrā and samādhi, [it shall be accomplished].
Recite the mantra of the Mother Dhāraṇī once;
perform the empowerment mudrā once,
extending the right hand outward.
Cast [the substances] three times until they are full,
holding them steady with the left hand.
Then, recite the Secret Heart Mantra seven times.
Thereupon, one dissolves the seal.
By this means, one gathers the samādhi of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi and the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñatā),
abiding within the mental consciousness.
In whatever place they are born, they shall obtain the marks of a Great Man;
all devas will protect and gaze upon them with affection,
and the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the ten directions will joyfully and attentively behold them.
Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva will touch their head with his hand and offer praise and exhortation;
all the sins of slandering the True Dharma and holding great false views throughout beginningless kalpas shall be extinguished,
and the merit and blessings they obtain will be as if they had seen my own body.
It is like Mount Sumeru.
With the seal of the great jewel banner, join the palms so that the two ring fingers and the two little fingers are within the hollow of the great palms.
The hands are held straight up, side by side,
with the tips joined. The two middle fingers are each bent at their tips to press upon the first joint on the side of the two ring fingers.
Let the tips of the two index fingers be separated by two *aṅgula*.
Bend the two index fingers so that their tips touch each other.
Place the two thumbs against the sides of the index fingers.
Extend the arms straight upward with the mudrā placed upon the crown of the head.

The mantra for this mudrā is: Oṃ jvala-vinardita-bhagavan bhīṣaṇa-saṃtrāsaya sarvajvalita-bhayāpaha-susuparvita-abhyudgata-sarvatathāgata-tejodhipate hūṃ. For those who bind this samādhi-mudrā, [it shall be effective].
Then, one receives the empowerment conferred by the hands of all the Tathāgatas of the ten directions.

Furthermore, it is asked: "By receiving the empowerment conferred by the hand of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, one shall, in whatever place one is born, realize the samaya of the Great Universal Wheel-Turning King of the Mantra-Siddhas."
When this King of Non-Void Samādhi manifests before one,
the veils and hindrances of afflictions are crushed, extinguished, and liberated;
one’s birth within the world shall be endowed with limitless merit and longevity.
For the mudrā of the Wrathful King (Krodharāja), join the wrists with palms facing upward and extend the fingers.
The two middle fingers, the two ring fingers,
and the two little fingers have their tips joined together and are slightly bent.
The two hands are separated by half an inch.
Each index finger grasps the middle joint on the side of the middle finger,
bending upward like a hook.
Extend both thumbs upward, keeping them half an inch apart,
and place the seal upon the crown of the head.
Knitting his brows and glaring with eyes wide open,
he manifested great wrath,
looking from left to right.
The seal-mantra is: Oṃ krodharāja mahāmudgara ghnāghna sarvaduṣṭān hūṃ. This samādhi-seal can destroy all evil devas, nāgas, spirits, and all wicked people.
It can subdue and suppress evil minds,
and it can also destroy the King of Mountains, Sumeru,
as well as all the malevolent Vināyakas.
All their retinues were naturally submissive;
all devas, śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, vaiśyas, and śūdras rejoiced and paid homage, accomplishing all dharmas.
For the mudrā of Bodhisattva Tārā, join the palms with the hollows of the hands empty;
the ten fingers of both hands are slightly bent and held upright,
with their tips touching one another.
The mantra for this seal is: Oṃ padmamate dṛḍha dṛḍha hūṃ. This seal-samādhi can also accomplish all activities.
For the mudrā of the Great White Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, join the palms with the space between them opened by one cun.
The two index fingers, two middle fingers, and two ring fingers are each held upright,
side-by-side, with their tips joined together.
Both thumbs are held upright,
each striking the side of the index finger at a distance of one cun above it;
both little fingers are held upright and slightly bent.
The distance between the two thumbs is eight *aṅgula*.
The seal-mantra is: Oṃ mahāpātmi śveta-nyai hulu hulu svāhā. This seal-samādhi can gather all dharmas and swiftly realize accomplishment.

For the mudrā of the Bodhisattva Bhṛkuṭī, join the palms; extend the two middle fingers, the two ring fingers, and the two little fingers so that they stand upright, side by side, with their tips joined.
Extend the two index fingers and place them respectively between the gaps of the middle and ring fingers.
The heads [of the thumbs] touch one another;
the two great thumbs are extended side by side,
pressing down upon the middle joints of the two middle fingers.
Pressing the lips together, gnashing the teeth, knitting the brows, and staring with bulging eyes, one gazes with wrathful anger.
The mudrā and mantra are: Oṃ bhrūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā. This mudrā-samādhi subdues all and fulfills every wish.
The mudrā of the White-Body Avalokiteśvarī Bodhisattvā is the same as the mudrā of the Great White Avalokiteśvara described previously.
The mantra for this mudrā is: Oṃ bhaṭṭāra-paṇḍaravāsini kuru kuru svāhā. For the mudrā of all devas, join the wrists together.
The two middle fingers are bent flat with their tips touching one another;
the remaining eight fingers are each spread apart,
with a distance of one cun between the gaps.
In general, slightly bend the head so that the heads do not touch one another.
The mudrā and mantra are: Oṃ āmukhībhava avalokite svāhā. This mudrā and samādhi summon all the celestial deities.
Abiding within the assembly altar, they joyfully maintain [the practice].
All the messengers join their palms with the hollows of the hands facing outward,
like an unopened lotus flower.
The mudrā-mantra is: Oṃ sarvatrāgame ni āvāhayā ruruṇi hūṃ. This mudrā-samādhi summons all the goddesses, yakṣas, and messengers.
All come to assemble and abide [there].
For the seal of the Seven Tārā goddesses, join the wrists so they touch,
and bend both thumbs into the palms.
Each person should correctly grasp the first joint at the base of the ring finger;
then, with the index, ring, and little fingers,
firmly clench the thumb to form a fist.
The middle fingers of both hands are each slightly bent at the tips, with a distance of half an inch between them.
The seal-mantra is: Oṃ ajamukhi jvalini dāridrya-pratimardani hūṃ. This seal-samādhi can subdue all malevolent celestial deities.
The mudrā for the Rite of Protection:
For the Hayagrīva Avalokiteśvara, join the palms with the hollows empty;
bend the two index fingers and insert them into the palms.
Have the backs of the hands joined together.
Extend both thumbs side by side and press them against the middle joints of the two index fingers.
The mantra of this mudrā is: Oṃ dharu dharala pratimī ajamukhi jrau hūṃ. This mudrā-samādhi is the most extraordinary and supreme among all dharmas.
For the Bhaṇḍamukha mudrā, join the palms with the hollows facing upward;
draw back the two middle fingers and press them down upon the first joints of the index fingers.
The tips of the two index fingers touch each other. Each tip of the two index fingers rests upon the upper sides of the two ring fingers.
The two thumbs are placed side by side, slightly extended and held upright, pointing upward.
The mudrā-mantra is: Oṃ (1) vaṇa-vamukhi (2) nikṣiptāya (3) ṭhaḥ hūṃ (4). This mudrā-samādhi is able to accord with all Vidyā-dharmas of the Vajras.
The *Sarvasattvānugrāhaka* Samādhi manifests swiftly.
For the seal of Avalokiteśvara with the Blue Neck (*Nīlakaṇṭha*), join the palms with the hollows empty;
bend both thumbs and insert them into the palms.
The two index fingers each grasp the upper joint of the thumbs.
The two middle fingers, the two ring fingers, and the two little fingers are slightly bent with their tips touching one another.
The seal-mantra is: Oṃ pratyamitārajaṭini śvābharaṇa phuru phuru hūṃ. This seal-samādhi can assist in accomplishing all samādhis.
For the mudrā of Eleven-faced Avalokiteśvara, join the wrists together.
Bend each of the two thumbs across within the palms.
Then, with the index, middle, ring, and little fingers of each hand...
Form a fist by grasping the thumb;
join the surfaces of the two fists together.
With a serene and joyful countenance, arouse the mind of great compassion.
The mudrā-mantra is: Oṃ sva-prabhā-nidhe pratisaṃdeśaya hūṃ. This samādhi-mudrā is able to bring all vidyā-dharmas to accomplishment.
The Seal of the Unobstructed Īśvara Deva:
Join the palms with the hollows empty;
[extend] the two middle fingers, the two ring fingers, and the two little fingers.
Join the two palms together with the heads of the fingers aligned;
bend both index fingers and hook them over the middle joints of the sides of the middle fingers.
The two thumbs are four *aṅgula* apart and slightly tilted upward;
their tips are eight *aṅgula* from the tips of the two index fingers.
The mudrā-mantra is: Oṃ bhaṭṭārikāśvare hūṃ. With this mudrā and samādhi, one summons all the Īśvaras.
They all come to the assembly and abide there to provide protection.
For the seal of the deity Maheśvara, follow the previous seal but change the left index finger to be upright and slightly bent,
and change the tips of the two middle fingers so they touch one another.
Press the first joint on the side of the second ring fingers.
The seal-mantra is: Oṃ ā-mu-khi śvāri hūṃ. This seal-samādhi subdues all wicked and evil spirits and deities.
The seal of King Yama (formerly and erroneously called King Yanluo) is formed with the eight fingers of both hands:
the right hand presses down upon the left, the fingers interlace and hook together,
and the finger pads touch one another.
Both thumbs should be held upright and spread apart,
slightly bent with a distance of half an inch between them;
first, one should quickly direct them toward the top of the head.
Next, place it upon the heart.
Move the thumbs up and down.
The mudrā and mantra are: Oṃ sāmari dharidhari hūṃ. With this mudrā and samādhi, one summons King Yama.
Come to attend this assembly and sit with joy to provide protection and blessing.
The Seal of Varuṇa (Water Deity) has the left hand with the palm facing upward beneath the left breast;
the five fingers are slightly bent like the petals of a lotus flower.
Place the right hand over the heart with the palm facing downward.
Extend the thumb and little finger, each bent within the palm;
extend the index, middle, and ring fingers, spreading them apart.
With the heads separated by one inch and slightly bent, the seal-mantra is: Oṃ nāgapratimanyai hūṃ. With this seal and samādhi, one summons all the great nāga kings.
All shall come to the ritual assembly with joy to provide protection and assistance.
King Vaiśravaṇa’s staff mudrā is formed by joining the backs of both hands together;
the two index fingers, the two middle fingers, the two ring fingers, and the two little fingers [are interlaced].
Each hook the fingers back-to-back with the palms facing each other;
extend the two thumbs straight upward and splay them outward.
First rotate quickly to the right, then place [the hands] at the heart.
The mudrā and mantra are: Oṃ bhaiṣajyabuddhi sru sru hūṃ. This seal and samādhi crush and destroy the evil intentions of all yakṣas, bhūtas, and spirits, dispersing and shattering them.
The seal of Mahābrahmādeva: the left hand is as described above for the seal of Varuṇa;
the right hand is bent at the elbow, held level with the shoulder.
The thumb is slightly bent toward the palm;
the index finger is also slightly bent,
positioned one inch away from the tip of the thumb.
The middle, ring, and little fingers are held upright and pressed together.
The mudrā-mantra is: Oṃ ā-mukhi-mūla-rūpe hūṃ. This seal-samādhi can manifest all the dharmas of the Brahmā heavens and all the celestial deities.
The mudrā of the Ascetic Rishi follows the mudrā of Brahmādeva;
however, one modifies it by joining the index finger and thumb of the right hand and extending the middle finger upright.
The little finger is bent like a hook.
The seal-mantra is: Oṃ riṣivara-de ajamukha-sapūṇe hūṃ. With this seal and samādhi, one summons all the vidyā-siddhas who practice asceticism.
Joining the palms in homage, one praises and prostrates with joy.
Regarding the wheel mudrā of Viṣṇu (formerly called Nārāyaṇa): join the palms and extend each of the five fingers of the right hand apart.
Insert the index, middle, ring, and little fingers of the left hand between the middle joints of the index, middle, ring, and little fingers of the right hand.
When going out,
grasp the four fingers of the right hand with the tips of the four fingers of the left.
Place the five fingers of the right hand with their intervals open;
press the left thumb upon the joint of the right index finger, and extend the right thumb straight upward.
The seal-mantra is: Oṃ ajamukhi miśrara pāṭumanaḍi sarvasamudra-pūjani svāhā. This seal-samādhi can crush all asura hosts, causing them to bow in reverence, flee, and disperse.
The seal of Maheśvara has the left hand bent at the elbow with the palm facing upward and forward;
the five fingers form the gesture of grasping a large fruit.
The right hand is bent at the elbow so that it is level with the shoulder;
the thumb presses upon the nail of the little finger,
while the index, middle, and ring fingers [are held straight].
Each [finger] is extended upward and spread apart.
The seal-mantra is: Oṃ rudra tuṃ miri svāhā. This seal-samādhi can destroy all malarial spirits and spirits that consume vital essence; they will all flee in terror and scatter.
For the mudrā of Maheśvaraputra, extend the index finger of the right hand straight upward;
bend the thumb across within the palm,
while the middle, ring, and little fingers remain [extended].
Quickly clench the hands into fists;
the left hand is done in the same manner as the right.
The side of the right fist is to rest against the waist.
The index finger points forward.
His left hand is clenched into a fist and placed at the side of his heart.
Point the head of the hand outward.
With eyes wide and full of wrath, perform the mudrā and recite the mantra: Oṃ ślokitāre āmukhābandhe svāhā. This mudrā and samādhi subjugate all obstructing spirits and ghosts.
The Seal of the Sun Deity (*Āditya*) is as follows: in Sanskrit it is called *Āditya*. With both hands palms facing upward, the sides of the palms are pressed together.
Both thumbs are placed crosswise within the palms;
both index fingers are bent and press down upon the upper joints of the thumbs.
The middle fingers, the two ring fingers, and the two little fingers are each placed side by side and slightly bent toward the palms.
The seal-mantra is: Oṃ sahakāralanike hūṃ duli svāhā. This seal-samādhi can emit hundreds of thousands of rays of light and is protected by the Sun Deity.
The seal of the Moon Devaputra (*Somadevaputra*): as before, the palms face upward with the fingers side-by-side and touching;
both thumbs are held upright and extended.
The two index fingers are each held upright and slightly bent;
the two middle fingers, the two ring fingers, and the two little fingers are each bent to form fists.
The mantra of this seal is: Oṃ sumāraḍi hūṃ. This seal-samaya provides protection for all the luminous stellar deities.
World-Honored One, such is this seal-samaya.
Each and every one is capable of accomplishing all activities,
extinguishing all calamities, misfortunes,
and karmic obstructions, and extensively adorning the samaya of the vast liberation lotus maṇḍala of King Ajamukha.
This practitioner should always bathe so that the body is pure, wear fragrant and clean garments,
and consume pure food.
He gives rise to great compassion for all sentient beings;
he reveres his preceptors and ācāryas;
and his mind is constantly respectful, honoring, and making offerings to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara.
Uphold this Dharma and seek the Bodhi of a Buddha.
Furthermore, do not associate with those of different karmic paths,
nor with anyone other than your own ācārya.
Furthermore, those who do not understand the nature of phenomena,
and those who do not seek awakening,
present and explain their states of realization through the practice of mingling with others.
Always remaining in silent seclusion, he diligently practiced and studied;
with powdered incense and unguents rubbed upon his hands,
he burned incense as an offering and bound the wheel-seal mudrā.
Maintain them without revealing them, lest you violate the samaya;
as each seal is applied, visualize its samaya-mark appearing in accordance with it.
Recite this three times.
By performing the ritual procedures, reciting the mantras, repenting, making vows, practicing the path, and offering praise,
one will daily obtain hundreds of thousands of koṭis of times more merit than before, a vast accumulation of great blessings.
He shall be conferred the office and the prophetic decree by all the Tathāgatas and great Bodhisattvas of the ten directions;
and all the devas shall joyfully provide him with protection and guardianship.
One shall receive the greatest offerings in the world;
one will fully accomplish all dharanis, mantras, mandalas, mudras, and samayas;
and in whatever place one is born, one’s life shall not meet with calamity or untimely death.
Having attained the samaya of the Great Mantra-Vidyādhara Wheel-King of Unfailing Siddhi,
possessing great wisdom and eloquence,
he expounded this Dharma to the entire assembly of celestial beings and sages.
Attaining great fearlessness, they will be respected by others and shall be born within the assembly of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.
At the time of their death, their body and mind will be tranquil, as if entering meditative absorption.
Thereupon, all the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Mahāsattvas were simultaneously addressed by them, saying: "True sons of the Buddha,
come into my land!"
My land is the place where you were born, grew,
and dwelt. From this life until you reach enlightenment,
you shall never again fall into the three miserable realms or the evil paths.
In every birth, they shall not undergo birth from a womb, an egg, moisture, or transformation;
their lifespan shall never diminish,
and they shall travel from one buddha-field to another.
Born by transformation from a lotus, he possesses the knowledge of past lives.
Chapter Five: The Adornment of the Secret Seal of the Dharma Realm. World-Honored One, these various hand-seals (*mudrā*) of the samaya of the vast liberation lotus maṇḍala—
The seals of all weapons are vast and immeasurable,
like the great earth,
which serves as the basis for the birth, growth, and dwelling of all sentient beings.
Just as all sentient beings rely upon and find fulfillment in the Tathāgata’s knowledge of all modes,
so it is for those who rejoice.
One should know that such a person shall extinguish all sins and attain accomplishment in this samādhi;
if they practice it while abiding in a mind of great compassion.
One who fully maintains the mantra and the pure discipline of the precepts,
and who seeks unexcelled, perfect enlightenment by receiving, upholding, reading, and reciting the Samaya of the Heart-King Mother Dharani Mantra of Amoghapāśa;
If one can, according to the Dharma,
depict the vast liberation lotus maṇḍala mudrā-samaya and maintain it with offerings.
One who practices with diligence while contemplating all samādhis along with their signs should be known as being like a great wheel-turning monarch.
Endowed with the seven treasures and immeasurable majesty,
he guides and transforms the four continents;
wherever he goes, all sentient beings [are influenced].
There was none who did not bow in reverence and come to hold him in high esteem;
all the vināyakas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, and malevolent spirits and ghosts spontaneously submitted as his subjects and gave rise to hearts of joy.
Either they will perish or flee;
the thieves' plots and the resentment of enemies shall all be resolved.
All grave sins from beginningless time and every affliction of illness shall likewise be destroyed and extinguished.
The Blessed One spoke this Dharma in this way for the sake of bringing peace and happiness to all sentient beings,
and for the sake of attaining the accomplishment of all samādhis.
It is taught for the sake of eliminating all karmic obstacles;
it is taught for the sake of subduing all malevolent spirits and deities;
it is taught for the sake of attaining all-encompassing enlightenment.
This is taught so that all mantra-holders may give rise to various forms of samādhi, wisdom, contemplation, and corresponding insight;
and so that they may attain the universal reliance upon the vast maṇḍala of the lotus of liberation, its mudrās, all samayas, and all their characteristic marks.
One should depict the vast maṇḍala of the lotus of liberation;
upon the blossoming lotus pedestal,
one should depict all mudrās of hand gestures, all implements and weapon mudrās, and all mudrās of precious flowers and fruits.
All around the seal, there is blazing firelight with flickering flames;
the various lotus branches, stalks, and leaves are distributed with their respective colors and forms.
All the mudrās resemble the forms of living beings;
they are fresh, radiant, and exquisite.
These include, for example, the mudrā of grasping all jewel fruits and the mudrā of grasping all vajra fruits.
He holds the seal of the three-pronged vajra, the seal of the precious arrow,
the seal of maṇḍali, the seal of the vajra-lotus,
the seal of the lotus garland, and the seal of varaṅga.
The Vajrapāśa mudrā, the Vajraśṛṅkhalā mudrā, the Abhayapradāna mudrā,
the Aṅguliparāmarśana mudrā, the Muṣṭi mudrā, and the Samaya mudrā.
The Unfailing One holds the *pāśa* (lasso) mudrā; the one with palms joined holds the *aṅkuśa* (hook) mudrā;
the one with the prison seal holds the *śṛṅkhalā* (chain) mudrā;
and the one with the contemplation seal holds the jewel-in-hand mudrā.
Holding the seal of the excellent vajra, holding the seal of the unerring lotus,
holding the seal of the vajra bell, holding the seal of the sword,
holding the seal of the trident, and holding the seal of the mallet.
The mudrā of holding the precious staff, the mudrā of holding the flower mace,
the mudrā of holding the noose, the mudrā of holding the great fish,
the mudrā of holding the precious wheel, and the mudrā of holding the precious conch.
He holds the seal of the unconditioned fruit; he holds the seal of the pomegranate fruit;
he holds the seal of the moon; he holds the seal of the sun;
he holds the seal of the hammer; and he holds the seal of the tooth-stick.
The mudrā of holding a precious flower; the mudrā of holding a rosary;
the mudrā of holding a five-pronged vajra; the mudrā of the Amoghapāśa hand;
and the Amoghasiddhi mudrā.
These hand gestures all feature the wrists adorned with various ornaments,
such as rings and bracelets made of the seven precious gems.
Perform the mudrā with the hand. The mantra is: Oṃ āmukha-mañjari mili mili hūṃ | Oṃ āśvāsaya kṣaṇamigati.

1. *Sarvatrāṃ* 2. *Siddhya siddhya* 3. *Sādhyaya* 4. *Hūṃ*. Such is the lotus-hand seal (*mudrā*) samaya.
If one constantly relies upon each [mantra] according to the samaya,
maintaining it through visualization corresponding to the syllables and reciting it,
all obscurations and the grave sins of the five heinous acts will be purified.
One shall personally eliminate [defilements] and not fall into the evil realms;
whatever one undertakes will then be accomplished.
One beholds the samaya of the vast and non-empty Lotus Maṇḍala of Liberation.
In a future age, at the place where they shall realize and attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*,
they will become true children of Amitābha Buddha,
born through transformation from the Dharma.
They have paid homage to and made offerings to as many Sugata-Tathāgatas as there are grains of sand in hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Gaṅgā rivers,
thereby accumulating immeasurable stores of merit and provisions.
These Tathāgatas...
Immeasurable praises of various meritorious deeds;
the bestowing of the prediction of enlightenment for all;
and the seal of the ground of all weapons.
The maṇi-jewel seal and the jewel-flower seal;
the precious lotus seal and the precious pearl-flower garland seal;
the rosary seal and the white conch seal.
The five-colored conch seal, the precious golden wheel seal,

the single-pronged vajra seal, and the three-pronged trident seal.
The seal of the bowl-placed *śa* (patra-nyasta-śa), the seal of the horizontal vajra,
the seal of the vajra-axe (*vajrakuṭhāra*), the seal of *ekatriśūla*,
the seal of the vajra-jewel-staff (*vajramaṇi-kunta*), and the seal of the jewel-lance (*ratna-śakti*).
The seal of the Karma-vajra, the seal of the wish-fulfilling jewel,
the seal of the great curved sword, the seal of the precious staff,
the seal of Rāgula, and the seal of the trident of Maheśvara.
The seal of the sword and noose, the seal of the iron hook and dragon;
the seal of the *turu-ma* and the red jewel-tree;
the seal of the battle-axe and wheel, and the seal of the battle-axe and staff.
The hand-seal of the flame-emanating jewel-light radiance,
the seal of the five-colored light, the seal of the mūsala-pestle,
the seal of the nūra-tree rope, and the seal of the battle-axe.
The ear-ornament seal, the auspicious vase seal,
the five-colored auspicious stone seal, the mountain-tree-and-stone seal,
the Mount Sumeru seal, and the coiled dragon seal.
The parasol mudrā, the great banner mudrā,

The *bhikṣu-maṇḍali* seal, the *bhikṣu* seal,

The *ūrṇakośa* seal, the conch-wheel seal,

the *saṃjīva* bird seal, and the wild duck and goose bird seals.
The mudrā of the ruddy sheldrake bird,
the mudrā of the sārasa crane, the mudrā of the white heron, the mudrā of the white egret, the mudrā of the peacock, the mudrā of King Yama’s staff,
the mudrā of the four-faced deity, and the mudrā of the four surrounding mirrors.

the half-moon wheel seal, the sun disk seal,

The seal of the precious belt, the seal of the crest of the *ḍānava*,

“World-Honored One, regarding this King Ajamaga’s vast liberation lotus maṇḍala seal samaya,
if one were to paint it,
all colors must be applied according to the Dharma and be bright and pure.”
Do not mix them with animal glue;
they should be painted or printed in colors that are all exquisite, with the blue and white clearly distinguished.
Its form is to be generated by tracing and painting each detail according to the rules of the mandala,
either upon white cotton cloth or silk.
On walls, on boards, or on paper,
one should draw the samaya according to the heart-mind, following the respective dimensions of each individual mandala.
All shall obtain offerings.
If one constantly draws this vast liberation lotus maṇḍala according to the Dharma and makes offerings while reciting and contemplating it,
[the same result shall be attained].
The ten evil deeds, the five heinous crimes, the four grave offenses, and other such sins will be naturally eliminated and extinguished.
One shall receive the empowerment of the crown-touching by Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva,
who will then instruct one in this dharani mantra and the dharma of the maṇḍala.
Those who witness this seal-dharma shall likewise have their evil karma and karmic obstacles extinguished,
and they shall further attain [the vision of] all Buddhas of the ten directions.
I, Śākyamuni Buddha, together with all the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas,
shall protect and assist you as if you were our own beloved children.
Therefore, the wise should always apply themselves with diligence,
truly upholding and practicing according to the Dharma,
so as to correctly attain the samaya of the vast liberation lotus maṇḍala seal of the King of Non-Emptiness.
The Amoghapāśakalparāja Sūtra, Scroll Four; The Amoghapāśakalparāja Sūtra, Scroll Five.
