Chapter Six: The Chapter on the Accomplishment of the Noose (Pāśasiddhi). Part One of Six.
Bhagavān, if one wishes to extensively manifest great supernormal powers (*ṛddhi*) and travel to the palaces of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, [one should practice as follows].
This extends to all the palatial abodes where the reward bodies (saṃbhogakāya) of all Buddhas reside, up to the realm of Akaniṣṭha;

as well as the palaces of the sun, the palaces of the moon, the palaces of the nāgas, the palaces of the yakṣas, the palaces of the rākṣasas, the palaces of the gandharvas, the palaces of the asuras, the palaces of the kinnaras, and the palaces of the mahoragas.
Regarding the accomplishment of all mundane and supramundane dharmas:
having first completed the service [to the preceptor],
one’s physical vessel is purified through the diligent observance of the precepts.
Having generated the mind of great compassion,
one should pay universal homage to the Triple Gem and duly cultivate the samaya of the eight kinds of no-void king’s snares (*aṣṭavidha-amoghapāśa-samaya*).
As for the image of this *pāśa*-samaya:
Cast the body of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara with the Amoghapāśa from gold or silver;
it should be eight finger-widths in length, measuring two hand-spans, and have three faces and two arms.
The front face is compassionate;
the left face is greatly wrathful with wide-open eyes and an agape mouth;
the right face is slightly wrathful with furrowed brows and a closed mouth.
On his head he wears a jeweled crown upon which resides an emanation Buddha;
his left hand holds a lasso, while his right hand has its palm raised.
He is adorned with necklaces, bracelets, and armlets made of the seven precious gems, and wears celestial robes.
One should adorn it and seat it upon a lotus throne.

Furthermore, one should fashion a trident out of silver or high-carbon steel (*vimala-loha*), sixteen finger-widths in length and one cubit (*hasta*) in height. The noose (*pāśa*) and other components should be made from lotus stalk fibers or the fibers of the *duzhong* tree (*Eucommia ulmoides*).
Using the bark-fiber of the śukamūṣika tree and silkworm silk,
one should properly process and refine them according to the Dharma.
On the eighth day of the bright fortnight, one should construct a maṇḍala.
At the center of the mandala, using pure white sandalwood paste,
aloeswood paste, and saffron paste,
one should draw a one-cubit lotus flower with thirty-two petals in full bloom.
Place five strands of silk upon the mandala on the flower pedestal.
Offer pure white food, incense, flowers, and scented water according to the ritual rules.
Every day, one must cease all idle chatter and frivolous laughter.
Recite the Mātṛ-dhāraṇī mantra and the Secret Heart-mantra one hundred and eight times to consecrate five threads.
On the fifteenth day, observe a fast.
Recite and maintain the mantra without interruption.
When binding the strands of the cord, join them into a single length;
do not keep them as separate strands.
Folding eight strands together to form a long cord sixteen cubits in length,
they shall be joined to create a noose;
one end of this cord is to be tied to the Bodhisattva.
A trident with an *āmala* fruit is tied to one end.
On the eighth day of the bright fortnight of the month of Ṛṣabha,
having bathed cleanly and put on pure garments, [one should proceed].
Having partaken of the three white foods, one constructs a maṇḍala.
In its center, one elaborately adorns a Dharma throne with precious silks;
this throne is square and circular, measuring one cubit in height and width.
Place the image upon the seat with the noose and trident;
the noose should be wide and coiled, and the image placed within it.
Recite the Mother Dhāraṇī mantra and the Secret Heart mantra.
One should empower the image, the cord, and the trident twenty-one times and then place them there.
One should empower the unguents and apply them to the image, the cord, and the trident.
Furthermore, various powdered incenses should be scattered over them all.
Furthermore, empower white mustard seeds and scatter them upon it.
Make offerings according to one's inclination with various incenses, flowers, scented water, food, and fruits.
Place vases of fragrant water at the four corners.
Place a bowl of fragrant water before the seat at each of the four gates.
Every day, at the six periods, sit facing east according to the ritual rules.
Upon the seat, contemplate the mind in tranquility.
Incense the King of Fragrances,
form the mudrā, and recite the Mother Dhāraṇī mantra and the Secret Heart mantra to consecrate the image,
the cord, and the trident.
One who practices this dharma should sever all discursive speech.
One should not consume any food or drink brought from outside;
such food is defiled by contact.
During each period of the first watch and the last watch of the night,
one should consecrate white mustard seeds once and strike the trident-noose once.
For thirty-six weeks, he practiced with diligence and maintained the Dharma without interruption throughout the days and nights—
at the first watch, the middle watch, the fifth watch, and at dawn.
The image on the cord simultaneously emits light;
if it emits flames, one shall accomplish the worldly *siddhi* rites;
if it emits various mixed-colored radiances, [one shall accomplish the supramundane *siddhi*].
It shall become the samādhi of supramundane siddhi.
At that time, a voice resounded from the sky, declaring:
"Excellent, excellent, O son of good family!"
You have now perfected the samaya of the noose of the supramundane and mundane bodhicitta.
By the power of this noose, you shall draw in and gather the supreme king of bodhicitta.
Abiding therein, one attains the perfection of the merits of the ten pāramitās,
like a wish-fulfilling jewel.
At this time, one should perform confession, make supreme vows, and offer argha water.
Holding a trident and lasso in his right hand,
he chanted the Mother Dhāraṇī mantra and the Secret Heart mantra with a resounding voice for ten thousand repetitions,
thereby realizing the vidyā-mantra and the samaya of the King of Amogha.
One will obtain the respectful accompaniment and protection of hundreds of thousands of koṭis of mantra-vidyādhara sages;
one will soar through the ten directions, with merit and lifespan increased such that one’s life span lasts ten koṭis of years;
and whatever one contemplates regarding the Dharma will be accomplished accordingly as it is recollected.
If there are sentient beings who have committed the five heinous crimes and the ten evil deeds,
yet upon encountering this sutra,
they suddenly give rise to faith and wisdom and take deep delight in this Dharma.
If one practices with single-minded diligence and without indolence,
one will certainly achieve accomplishment;
how much more so for those who possess pure faith, maintain pure precepts, and cultivate themselves through diligence!
Is it not that this dharma is most greatly accomplished?
If a practitioner conceives doubt regarding the dharma, then no manifestation will be achieved.
If one wishes to subdue all devas, nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, and vināyakas, [this is the means].
Recite the Mātṛkā Dhāraṇī mantra seven times;
recite the mantra of the Wrathful King seven times;
and summon all devas, nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, and vināyakas.
If one rotates the cord with the right hand,
they will all arrive immediately to be employed as servants.
If one wishes for people of the world to respect and keep one in mind, [one should perform this rite].
Recite the mantra and perform the ritual of the rotating cord, and your wish shall be fulfilled.
Furthermore, there is another method: recite the mantra of the Wrathful King seven times.
With the right hand, one should hold a wheel and a noose,
visualizing that all evil devas, nāgas, yakṣas, and rākṣasas are being seized and bound;
thus they will all be bound and not released.
One shall never be bound in fetters for months or years.
If one is released from them,
one should give rise to great compassion and recite the Secret Heart Mantra three times.
They shall all be released immediately.
If one is to subdue wicked and evil persons,
one should recite the mantra while rotating the noose.
When one is thus compliant and submissive,
if one wishes to keep the samaya secret,
one should hold the cord, recite the mantra, and bind the pāśa-mudrā.
Once the body has been empowered by the mudrā, it departs at will.
If one wishes for dragons and devas to send down rain,
or to stop the rain, [one should perform this].
Constructing the mandala according to the Dharma, one makes offerings to the image and the cord;
gazing at the deity while reciting the mantra and performing the ritual with the cord,
rain shall fall whenever it is required.
One should cease when it is time to cease.
If one wishes to avert all calamities, epidemics, and diseases,
one should go to a high tower or the summit of a high mountain.
Recite the mantra seven times and cast the noose;
all calamities, epidemics, and evil winds, hail, and rain will then be dispelled and scattered.
Thus is this samaya of the bodhicitta accomplished.
Without allowing thoughts to become disordered,
he maintained the pure precepts and focused his mindfulness upon all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, as well as Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva,
constantly keeping them before his eyes with reverence and making offerings to them.
By reciting and contemplating according to the Dharma without ever forgetting, one will immediately attain accomplishment.
O World-Honored One, regarding the Samaya of the Wheel and the Lasso:
one should cast a wheel out of gold, silver, or red copper.
Measuring eight finger-widths in both length and breadth, with two hands' span,
it was six spokes in circumference; the hub, spokes,
and rim were all complete, distinct, and adorned in accordance with the Dharma.
Take equal portions of lotus stalk fibers, *duzhong* (Eucommia) wood fibers, and silkworm silk for the *pāśa* (lasso) and other implements.
Purify and refine them according to the ritual rules.
On the eighth day of the bright fortnight, construct a maṇḍala according to the ritual rules.
Upon a square of sandalwood paste, white sandalwood paste, saffron paste, and aloeswood paste,
one should draw a one-cubit lotus flower with one hundred and eight petals in full bloom.
Mark the boundaries of the enclosure and the paths.
Upon the flower altar, arrange three strands of thread in a circular pattern.
Offer various foods of the "three whites," incense, and flowers according to the ritual rules.
Every day, recite the Mātṛ-dhāraṇī mantra and the Secret Heart Mantra.
Empower three threads by reciting them one hundred and eight times.
On the fifteenth day, observe a fast and continue the recitation.
The strands should be spun continuously and without interruption.
Combine the strands of the rope into a single length and do not treat them as separate strands.
Fold three strands together, making the total length thirty-six cubits.
The method for constructing the wheel of the noose is likewise:
tie one end of the cord to the hub of the wheel on the eighth day of the bright fortnight of the month of Ṛddhi.
Having bathed for purification and donned clean garments,
one should partake of the three white foods and construct an altar according to the Dharma.
On the eastern side of the altar, place an image of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara with the Amoghapāśa.
At the center of the mandala, one should arrange a highly adorned, multi-colored high seat;
this seat is one cubit in height, width, and circumference.
Upon the seat, a tray is placed, upon which a wheel and a noose are set.
Empower the ointment for anointing and apply it to the wheel and the cord.
Empower the powdered incense and scatter it over the wheel and the cord.
Empower the white mustard seeds and likewise scatter them upon them.
Make offerings according to the ritual using various incenses, flowers, perfumed water, and the three white foods;
place incense-water jars at the four corners and bowls of perfumed water on the four sides of the seat.
Every day, facing east, burn the King of Incenses (Gandharāja).
Make offerings according to the ritual for robes and sit in the full lotus posture (paryaṅka).
Constantly and without interruption, recite the Mother Dhāraṇī mantra and the Secret Heart Mantra.
First, hold the wheel and the noose.
Whether it be during the first watch of the night or the last watch of the night,
empower white mustard seeds and first strike the wheel and the noose with them.
For thirty-six days and nights, he practiced with diligence, upholding the Dharma without interruption throughout the day and night—
from the first watch to the last, through the five watches and the break of dawn.
The wheel and noose simultaneously emitted light,
ascending into the air and spinning aloft;
above the head of the mantra-practitioner, a blazing mass of fire and flames burst forth.
The words of praise for the image of Avalokiteśvara say:
"Excellent, excellent, son of good family!
You have now accomplished the samaya of the *Amoghasiddhi-cintāmaṇi-cakra-pāśa*."
At this time, one should perform the offering of argha and make a petition.
Form the wheel mudrā by holding a wheel with the left hand,
and form the noose mudrā by holding a noose with the right hand.
Recite the mantra of the Wrathful King one hundred and eight times.
Recite the Mother Dhāraṇī and the Secret Heart Mantra.
Consecrate the wheel and the noose one hundred and eight times.
Circumambulate three times clockwise above one's own crown;
then, forming the consecration mudrā, empower the crown and perform self-consecration by circling three times clockwise.
When one realizes the samaya of the great supernatural power of the Amoghapāśa-cakra,
all the great vidyā-dhara mantra-siddhas will appear before one and respectfully protect them, saying: [Please command us].
"Great Seer, what is it that you now intend to do?
I am able to act for all of it; I shall be your refuge and your companion.
Even if you enter the cave of the asuras," [I will follow].
Dwelling at the entrance of the asura cave,
he fasted for one day while reciting and upholding the mantra,
continuously empowering the wheel and the lasso.
At the entrance of the asura cave,
perform one consecration and brandish the weapon one hundred and eight times;
then each gate will open of its own accord, and you may enter directly without obstruction.
If one enters the caves of yakṣas, rākṣasas, kiṃnaras, or nāgas,
the ritual procedure is likewise to be applied accordingly. When entering the cave:
He constantly holds a wheel with his left hand at his chest and grasps a rope with his right hand level with his right shoulder.
Upon entering the cave door, the earth shakes in six ways.
The wheel emits rays of light that illuminate the interior of the cave;
one beholds various jeweled trees, flowers, fruits, and palaces surrounding the enclosure.
Upon reaching the path to the palace:
Suddenly, there appeared a manifested deity of Pure and Stainless Medicinal Essence,
whose form was like that of a celestial being,
with a body fully adorned with garments of various jewels.
He then grasped the branch and fruit of the *Kuyanya* tree; it was a stainless medicinal essence of great poisonous power.
Within a distance of one *yojana*, anyone who beheld it would have their vital energy forcibly drained away.
When seeing [the enemy], one should be fearless and free from anger;
holding a wheel in the left hand and a lasso in the right,
one stands before them with a sound of great wrathful fury.
Recite the mantra of Mahācanda with twenty-one or thirty-seven recitations in a wrathful tone to subjugate the medicinal spirits (*yakṣas*).
Furthermore, recite the mantra of Caṇḍamahāroṣaṇa twenty-one or thirty-seven times in a voice of great fury.
The medicinal essence descended from afar.
At that time, its stainless medicinal essence caused his face to sink into the ground,
and sweat flowed from his entire body like a surging spring.
When the mantra-holder has seen this, he must not touch the sweat on the body;
otherwise, the medicinal essence will again become greatly enraged and glare at him with its eyes.
Thus it is for the mantra-holder.
Holding a cord, strike the stainless medicinal essence three, four, or seven times vigorously;
it will then be terrified and submit, and nectar will emerge from its body.
The mantra-holder should take this and smear it upon both eyes and the palms of both hands.
Upon smearing it over one's entire body, one immediately ascends into the air;

abiding there upon the first wind-wheel, one realizes the supernormal power of the divine eye (*divyacakṣus-abhijñā*) and fully beholds all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, as well as all celestial beings (*deva*), in the ten directions.
Furthermore, one shall also behold all the Buddhas of the past who abide within their śarīras;
the body of the mantra-practitioner shall likewise transform into the color of gold.
His hair is like a spiral shell, and his lifespan increases by a thousand kalpas.
He is constantly accompanied by eighteen thousand koṭi-nayuta-hundred-thousand celestial sages (*deva-ṛṣis*),
seventy-two Gaṅgā-sandhi-koṭi-hundred-thousand kinnara mantra-vidyādhara ṛṣis, and kinnara mantra-vidyādhara ṛṣis.
As for the offerings of respect and protection—
the various celestial ambrosial delicacies he desired—

and you will behold the palaces and towers of the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Amitābha Buddha and all the Bodhisattvas,
with their marks and signs, radiance, and various supernormal powers,
simultaneously praised him, saying: "Excellent, excellent, son of good family!"
"The body you have received is your final body.
After casting off this life, you shall be born and dwell in my land,
possessing the wisdom that knows the destinies of seven thousand past lives."
At that time, the mantra practitioner, holding a lotus noose in his left hand,
shall recite the Mother Dhāraṇī Mantra and the Secret Heart Mantra ten thousand times, and the Mantra of the Wrathful King one thousand and eight times.
Having realized great supernormal powers and attained a lifespan of ten thousand years, he was venerated and protected by all the mantra-vidyādhara mahārājās who hold the pāśa-noose.
Eighteen thousand mantra-vidyādharas who uphold the pāśa-mantra will follow him with reverence until the attainment of bodhi; O Bhagavat, this is the Vajrapāśa-samaya.
Using white sandalwood measuring twelve finger-widths in length and three handfuls in volume, carve a five-pronged *vajra* according to this diagram;
the central prong and both ends [of the side prongs] should have the faces of *bhūta* spirits.
The remaining eight prongs have surfaces of golden-colored light and flames.
The mallet penetrates the body and mind at both ends of the prongs.
[Therein dwell] the Nanda Nāga King and the Upananda Nāga King.
To the left and right, they intertwine and entangle in forward and reverse directions,
each forming many ghost-heads;
these are the heads of two dragons.
Each [of these] should extend three or four finger-widths beyond the heads of the *bhūta* demons.
Take equal portions of tree-bark fibers, white cotton thread, and silk from silkworms;
having cleaned and refined them, fashion the maṇḍala.
Perform the ritual empowerment of the thread.
Hold the pāśa (lasso) together;
it should consist of a single long strand and must not be divided into separate strands.
Interlace three prongs to form a noose;
tie one end of the noose around the waist of the mallet.
Having bathed cleanly and put on pure garments, adorn oneself as described above.
On the high seat within the maṇḍala of the vajra-noose, place the vajra and the noose.
To the east, install the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara with the Amoghapāśa,
and present various offerings.
As for the mantra practitioner, they shall spread white *kusa* grass at the western gate upon the Dharma seat;
with their left hand, they hold a staff and press it down upon the *vajra* and *pāśa*.
During the day, one should recite the Mother Dhāraṇī mantra and the Secret Heart-mantra,
first holding the vajra and the lasso.
During the first watch of the night and the last watch of the night, one should recite the mantra of the Wrathful King (Krodharāja).
Consecrate white mustard seeds first by striking them with a pestle and rope;
maintain the practice with diligence and without interruption for a period of thirty-six ten-day cycles.
When light is emitted from the vajra or the pāśa,
one should hold the vajra and pāśa and recite the Mātṛ-dhāraṇī mantra one hundred and eight times,
and recite the mantra of the Krodharāja one hundred and eight times.
The Tathāgata family, the Vajra family, the Maṇi family,
and the Padma family all manifested simultaneously,
soaring through the air with mastery of supernatural powers.
His physical form and majestic power are like vajra;
all the deities of the Vajra family will protect him from afar,
extending his lifespan for twelve thousand years.
If one wishes to transform and guide all devas, nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, gandharvas, asuras, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, and garuḍas;
Reciting the name of each deity in turn,
chant the mantra of the Wrathful King while brandishing the wheel,
the noose, and the vajra.
They will all immediately submit with reverence and respectfully serve as guardians.
If one wishes to convert and guide all wicked people, one should act in this same manner.
Furthermore, there is a rite to be performed at midnight on the fourteenth or fifteenth day of the dark fortnight.
Reciting the mantra of the Wrathful King with a great roar of rage,
and brandishing the wheel, lasso, and vajra,
one should form the intention to bind all yakṣas, rākṣasas, and piśācas who steal vital essence and harbor malice.
They shall all be bound.
If one wishes to release them,
one should recite the Secret Heart Mantra.
If one is afflicted by illness caused by ghosts or spirits,
by standing before that person and brandishing a mallet toward them,
the illness will be cured immediately.
If one recites the mantra of the Wrathful King with a great roar of anger in a śmaśāna (cemetery), brandishing a wheel,
a noose, and a vajra with the right hand;
Then one will attain the *āttadhāna* [state] and see the gates of the palaces of various ghosts and spirits open;
if one is at the gate of an asura cave, one should empower the ritual staff (*vajra*) and point it toward it.
The gates open of their own accord.
Within the cave, all spirits, ghosts, and venomous dragons do not harm one another.
The path to the cave is level and straight; once inside, there is no fear.
He saw within the cave wonderful playthings;
whatever he desired was obtained,
and he moved in and out without obstruction, constantly enjoying peace and happiness.
One should know that this is the power of the Great Vajra Hook and Noose,
which is able to initiate all worldly activities. *Amoghapāśakalparāja-sūtra*, Scroll Five.
The Amoghapāśakalparāja Sūtra, Scroll Six.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Bodhiruci of India during the Great Tang Dynasty.
Chapter Six: The Accomplishment of the Pāśa, Part Two.
The Blessed One’s maṇi-jewel cord samaya is made of vajra-jewels,
or lapis lazuli, or sapphire, or sphatika crystal.
If one obtains any one of these four jewels,
it will be like a *jambu* fruit, free from all blemishes and impurities;
or even larger, it is the most excellent and supreme.
One should polish white silver into a lotus flower according to the prescribed proportions;
the size of the flower should resemble a natural lotus,
and it should be placed at the center of a diamond-jewel lotus pedestal.
The lotus pedestal is adorned with pearls.
A red cord is used as a lasso according to the previously described ritual;
one constructs the maṇḍala and consecrates that cord.
Combine the strands of the cord into a single length;
do not make separate strands.
Fold three strands together so that the total length is twenty-one cubits.
Construct a lasso;
at each of its two ends, tie one end to a lotus stalk and the other end to a vajra hook.
The hook is made of gold, measuring four spans in length with a handle;
its shaft is adorned with jewels and its body is pure and bright.
One should construct a maṇḍala and arrange a seat of precious, colorful silk.
On the tray upon the seat, place a maṇi-jewel cord,
with a lotus-jewel hook positioned at its center.
To the east, place images of Śākyamuni Buddha, Amitābha Buddha, and Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.
One should make offerings according to the Dharma with various fragrant flowers, incense, fruits, melons, and the three white foods;
burn the King of Incenses that cuts off all discursive speech;
and [accept] food offered by others that was not prepared by oneself.
None of these should be eaten nor offered as sustenance.
One should eat the three white foods and sit in the *paryaṅka* posture according to the Dharma.
With the left hand holding a staff, one should press it down upon the precious cord.
Holding a rosary in his right hand,
he should recite the Mother Dhāraṇī mantra and the Secret Heart mantra during the daytime,
while first holding a jeweled cord.
During the first and last watches of the night, recite the mantra of the Furenwang (Krodharāja) once;
empower white mustard seeds once and strike the precious cord with them.
Practice this ritual continuously throughout the days and nights.
When thirty-six months had passed,
during the first watch of the night, the last watch of the night, and at dawn on the fifteenth day,
the image of Avalokiteśvara atop the precious cord and the body of the practitioner simultaneously emitted light.
At that time, the mantra-practitioner performs the offering of argha;
holding the noose with the left hand and grasping the lotus with the right,
they recite the mantra of the Wrathful King twenty-one times.
From the midst of the void, a great sound emerged in the form of songs and hymns of praise.
The Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara manifested his body,
as did Śākyamuni Buddha, Amitābha Buddha, and the Tathāgata Lokaprabhāsvararāja.
At that time, he manifested his body and extended his hand to stroke [the disciple’s] head.
With one voice, he praised him, saying: "Excellent, excellent, son of good family!
You have now accomplished the worldly and transworldly samaya of the Non-empty Pure Maṇi Jewel Rope."
Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva addressed him, saying:
"You have now attained my *amogha-viśuddha-mahā-cintāmaṇi-pāśa-siddhi-samayam*."
"You shall become a treasury of all worldly jewels;
you should manifest various divine transformations just as I have manifested my own."
They manifest oceans of clouds of various mani-jewel radiances and oceans of clouds of various priceless precious incenses;
they manifest oceans of all the exquisite celestial flowers and flower garlands.
Clouds of various kinds of ointments and powdered incenses;
clouds of various kinds of ambrosial delicacies; clouds of various kinds of precious banners, pennants, and canopies;
and clouds of various kinds of celestial, exquisite garments and precious ornaments.
Ocean-clouds of various palaces, towers, pavilions, and terraces made of diverse jewels;
ocean-clouds of various subtle and exquisite celestial music; and ocean-clouds of various jewel trees with flowers and fruits.
I make offerings to Śākyamuni Buddha, Amitābha Buddha, the Tathāgata Lokaprabhāsvara-rāja, and the assembly of all Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas.
Furthermore, may they grant deliverance to all sentient beings.
All shall attain liberation;
having cast off this life, they will immediately go to the West to be born by transformation within a lotus flower.
At that time, one should recite the mantra of the Wrathful King three times.
The right hand holds a precious cord;
the hands are folded and interlaced, placed within the two elbows,
with both ends extending downward for four or five inches.
He holds a lotus-flower-topped lasso in his left hand;
the hook-end of the lasso is placed inside his left elbow,
with the rest hanging down outward.
Holding a jewel in his right hand, he makes offerings with burning incense;
generating great compassion for all sentient beings,
he contemplates that from within this jewel emerge infinite oceans of clouds of offerings.
Recite the Mātṛkā-dhāraṇī mantra three times.
Recite the Guhyahṛdaya mantra twenty-one times.
Prostrate and take refuge in all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, entreating their divine power and supernatural faculties.
Recite the mantra of the Great Amoghapāśa-ratna-dhāraṇī as follows:

Nineteen: HŪṂ PHAṬ; Thirty: SVĀHĀ. Having recited this one hundred and thirty-one times, one hundred and eight times in total, place the upper part of the jewel-noose upon the image and the lower part upon the body of the practitioner.
At one time, they emitted light that measured the limits of space;
at another time, they universally manifested clouds-seas of various mani-jewel lights and clouds-seas of various priceless precious incenses.
Ocean-clouds of various exquisite flowers and flower garlands;
ocean-clouds of various ointments and powdered incenses;
ocean-clouds of various ambrosial foods and drinks; and ocean-clouds of various precious banners, flags, and canopies.
Ocean-clouds of various kinds of exquisite celestial garments;
ocean-clouds of various kinds of precious ornaments;
ocean-clouds of various kinds of precious palaces, pavilions, towers, and terraces.
With clouds of oceans of various kinds of exquisite celestial music and clouds of oceans of various jewel trees with flowers and fruits,
they made universal offerings to Śākyamuni Buddha and Amitābha Buddha.
When the World-Honored One, King of Radiant Light Tathāgata,
and the entire assembly of Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas were present,
the mantra-practitioner at that time attained great supernormal powers (mahābhijñā).
They beheld Śākyamuni Buddha, Amitābha Buddha, and the Tathāgata Lokendrarāja, together with the entire assembly of Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas,
abiding in the midst of space, simultaneously offering praise.
For the purpose of making offerings with clouds of various oceans of non-empty mani-jewels,
the mantra-holder shall become a member of the retinue of the Universal Monarch of all Mantra-Vidyādhara Wheels.
He will be revered, protected, praised,
and circumambulated; his lifespan will be eighty thousand kalpas,
and he will be named Vast and Unfailing Jewel-Crest (Mahā-amogha-maṇi-śekhara).
If I were to dwell among humans with a lifespan of ten thousand years,
the people of that age would revere and pay homage to me,
as if I were without equal.
The devas protect, revere, and praise them;
all sentient beings always love and stand in awe of them;
they realize and understand the profound eloquence and wisdom of the world.
Penetrating all things without obstruction,
you shall expound upon the peerless Dharma before the entire assembly of devas and humans.
At that time, the mantra-practitioner shall further manifest the maturation of all buddha-fields throughout the ten directions,
as well as all buddhas, all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas,
pratyekabuddhas, śrāvakas, and all the eight classes of devas, nāgas, and so forth.
Regarding the samaya of the merits of the physical form and supernormal powers:
one should reverently make offerings,
gaze upon the Bodhisattva, join the palms, and prostrate with the head.
I entreat all Tathāgatas and all Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas of all lands throughout the ten directions to bestow their various supernatural powers for protection and grace,
so that we may sit according to the Dharma.
Within those jewels, one beholds the manifestations of all Buddhas of the ten directions, all Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, Pratyekabuddhas, Śrāvakas,
and all classes of devas, nāgas, and the eight divisions of supernatural beings.
Various supernormal powers manifested simultaneously: various colors, fragrances, ambrosial delicacies,
various ointments and powdered incenses, and various flower garlands and necklaces.
Various types of monastic robes and garments; various precious parasols, banners, and streamers;
various precious ornaments and decorations; various celestial and wondrous sounds;
various wish-fulfilling jewel trees, flower trees, fruit trees, and various trees of fragrant oil lamps.
Various clouds of palaces, towers, pavilions, and terraces made of the seven kinds of precious jewels appeared all at once,
filling all the lands throughout the ten directions,
as offerings to the assemblies of all Buddhas and the multitudes of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas.
Recite the Maṇiratna Dhāraṇī mantra seven times and wind the wheel-rope seven turns;
immediately, in each of the lands of the ten directions, within the assemblies of all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Mahāsattvas, [the light will appear].
One beholds all these Buddhas, Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas,
Pratyekabuddhas, Śrāvakas, and all the devas, nāgas, and the eight classes of beings,
as well as all their various forms and diverse supernatural powers.
One should perform various offerings, such as oceans of clouds of offerings. In making these offerings,
one should employ all kinds of incense, flowers, precious banners, streamers, canopies, jeweled ornaments, food, drink, rare treasures, clothing, and lamps.
Serving and making offerings to all Buddhas and Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas in all lands throughout the ten directions is no different; in this way,
one is able to daily cultivate and accumulate merit throughout all lands in the ten directions.
All Buddhas and Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas, with all their supernatural powers,
meritorious virtues, marks and signs of excellence, the power of mindfulness,
the power of wisdom, the power of generosity, and the power of ethical discipline.
Through the power of diligence, the power of majestic virtue, the mass of merit, and roots of goodness,
all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas of the ten directions observe,
praise, and protect [them].
Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva will joyfully protect and assist them.
You should know that such a person obtains the vast accumulation of merit, virtue, and roots of goodness of Avalokiteśvara.
In this life and in future lives, they shall not be harmed by any evil devas, nāgas, the eight classes of beings, ghosts, or spirits.
It creates various calamities, terrors, and disasters;
yet, for anyone who sees or hears this dharani-mantra samaya,
all their karmic obstructions shall be eliminated and extinguished.
If there should be one who, for seven days and seven nights,
refrains from all speech and discourse,
and recites, reads, and upholds this dhāraṇī mantra.
All the various offenses committed over hundreds of thousands of koṭis of kalpas—
the four grave offenses, the five heinous crimes, and the ten evil deeds— will be extinguished at once;
one shall certainly not undergo any of the suffering of the offenses in the Avīci Hell.
The place where one is born shall be like a lotus flower,
unstained by dust or defilement; with little effort and practice,
one attains the ground of peace and happiness.
If one who constantly upholds this mantra according to the Dharma attains the non-retrogressive Vajra Supreme Samādhi of a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva,
World-Honored One, then if there are those who recite this dhāraṇī-mantra one hundred and eight times every day, [they shall likewise attain it].
One should immediately practice the maṇḍala rites of the ten non-empty pāramitās;
through this perfect correspondence,
all mantra-deities and vidyā-goddesses will constantly and joyfully provide protection.
If there are sentient beings who, throughout hundreds of millions of kalpas, have fully committed the four grave offenses, the five heinous crimes, the ten evil deeds, and other such transgressions,
and upon the dissolution of the body at the end of life fall into the Avīci Hell—
if one takes the remains of such a deceased person, whether it be their limbs, bones, or clothing—
For the practitioner of mantras, upon the shadow of their body being cast [upon it], they shall attain liberation;
casting off this body of suffering, they will be born directly in the Pure Land.
World-Honored One, this is the Samaya of the Mantra-Dhāraṇī of the Unfailing Jewel (Amoghapāśa).
This is true and not false;
it is called the Samaya Gate of True Liberation that Extracts One from Evil Destinies.
How much more so for monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen who possess pure faith!
With a sincere mind, one should diligently apply oneself day and night,
making offerings with purity and reverence according to the Dharma,
while receiving, upholding, reciting, and contemplating its study.
Those who write it themselves or teach others to write it—
will they not be liberated and attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*?
This is the *Amogha-maṇi-ratna-dhāraṇī-mantra*.
Among all mantra-samayas, this is the foremost;
it accomplishes all vast accumulations of merit, blessings, and roots of goodness.
Therefore, the wise should act in accordance with the Dharma.
If one upholds, recites, reverently makes offerings to, transcribes,
or explains this sutra, World-Honored One,
anyone who sees such a person is said to truly see Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.
If a practitioner of mantras who possesses the true Dharmakāya wears a jeweled cord coiled around their neck,
holding the lotus end of the cord in the right hand and the hook end in the left hand while reciting the mantra, they shall attain the secret samaya.
Those who enter and dwell within the abodes of all devas, nāgas, asuras, ghosts, and spirits, as well as in mountains, marshes, and caves,
shall encounter no obstacles;
their lifespan shall equal the number of years in the celestial realms.
All latent afflictions and the darkness of obstructions will be completely extinguished of their own accord.
If one wishes to observe the signs of all phenomena,
one should do so on the eighth, fourteenth, fifteenth, or the final day of the bright fortnight of the moon.
Having bathed for purification and donned clean garments,
one should construct a maṇḍala and adorn the Dharma seat;
upon the seat, place a jeweled cord on a tray.
Place that silver lotus at the center of the cord.
Scatter flowers upon it as an offering.
Prepare sixteen portions each of agallochum and guggulu incense.
Take two parts each of *sahakāra* incense and *vajrasāra* incense, and two parts of white *candana* incense;
blend them together and burn them. With the left hand hold the hook (*aṅkuśa*), and with the right hand perform the *mudrā* on the prayer beads (*japamālā*).
Recite the Mātṛkā Dhāraṇī mantra three times;
recite the Guhyahṛdaya mantra one hundred and eight times;
recite the Krodharāja mantra three times.
Recite the Maṇiratna Dhāraṇī mantra twenty-one times.
Sitting cross-legged in quiet contemplation, visualize and contemplate Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva;
he will come and speak to you, after which you may dwell in peace according to your wish.
At that time, one will behold all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, devas, nāgas, and the eight classes of beings;
or see all those who act as enemies and bring harm;
or perceive the signs of long life and short life.
Some see signs of illness or signs of death;
some see signs of the king’s virtue or vice;
some see signs of obtaining gold, silver, precious gems, various garments, and ornaments.
Or one may see signs of various skillful arts;
or see signs of various illusory and transformative phenomena;
or see signs of hidden treasures beneath the earth.
Or one may see signs of abundant harvests or of famine;
or signs of success or failure in various undertakings;
or the appearance of boys and girls.
Or one may see various signs of the methods for subduing people through the accomplishment of mantras;
or see signs such as wealth, nobility, poverty, or low status;
or see times of rain and times of drought.
Or one may see signs of pestilence and epidemics among all people and animals;
or see various signs of fear and dread;
or see signs of foreign enemies, rebels, and insurgents invading the country.
Or one may see various signs indicating that all sought-after aims and aspirations will be fulfilled.
The World-Honored One has declared these signs to be true;
the wise should not harbor doubts or suspicions regarding them.
If there is a drought in the heavens,
one should hold a precious cord by a deep pool and recite the mantra;
the waters of the pool will then bring down a great rain.
If there is persistent rain,
one should hold a precious cord while standing in an open, elevated place;
by gazing at the sky and reciting the mantra, the rain will immediately cease.
If one gazes upon the Sun Deity while holding a precious cord and reciting the mantra with a request,
one will obtain the Sun Deity’s gaze and protection.
If one gazes upon the Moon Deity while holding a precious cord and reciting the mantra with a request, [the same shall occur].
Then one will obtain the protection and surveillance of the Moon Deity (Candradeva).
If one holds a precious cord at the banks of rivers or the shores of the ocean and recites the mantra,
one shall summon the various treasures within the waters.
Then one will be able to manifest and employ them without obstruction.
If one holds a precious cord in a deep forest and recites the mantra while summoning all medicinal essences, [they shall appear].
At that time, they will manifest their forms and say to the mantra-practitioner:
"We, the medicinal essences, are at your disposal; you may take and consume them as you wish.
Furthermore, if one takes a precious cord and ties it around the head of an image of Mahākāla:
Reciting the mantra, one invokes Mahākāla;
he leads all his clans to appear simultaneously and vows to become a servant,
remaining at one's disposal for whatever tasks are assigned.
If one holds this precious cord, when seeing noble persons, they will feel joy, love, and respect;
even when seeing commoners, they will all likewise turn toward them with reverence.
Should calamities or epidemics arise in any land, [this cord shall quell them].
On the fifteenth day of the waxing moon, having bathed for purification and donned clean garments,
one should arouse a heart of great compassion toward all sentient beings and ascend to a high tower, or to the top of a stūpa, or beneath a banner.
Constructing the maṇḍala according to the Dharma and holding the precious cord,
one should recite the Mother Dhāraṇī Mantra and the Secret Heart Mantra one hundred and eight times,
and recite the Mantra of the Wrathful King forty-nine times.
Recite the Maṇiratna-dhāraṇī mantra one hundred and eight times.
While visualizing the nine directions as a revolving wheel of precious cords, make this aspiration:
"May all calamities, obstacles, floods, droughts, and irregularities of the seasons within the land be pacified."
It shall immediately extinguish and eliminate [all calamities],
enabling all varieties of grain, flowers, fruits, clothing, ornaments, and other such items to become entirely abundant.
The people shall live in peace and happiness, free from all fears;
furthermore, may all beings of evil nature come to cherish and love one another, rather than harming or harassing each other.
The World-Honored One’s Sword-Noose Samaya consists of a sword made of tempered iron;
the length of the blade is sixteen finger-widths, the handle measures four hand-widths in length, and it is fixed with a hilt made of white silver.
On both faces of the sword are golden-colored flames.
For the *pāśa* (lasso) and other implements, use fibers of *duzhong* wood, silk cocoons, and tree bark;
these should be refined and purified to construct the maṇḍala.
Empower the strands of the cord by joining them together;
let them form a single length without being divided into separate strands.
Fold these three strands over one another to a length of sixteen cubits.
Construct a lasso; tie one end of this lasso to the hilt of a sword.
Construct a maṇḍala and adorn it with a precious, colorful seat.
Place an image of the World-Honored One Avalokiteśvara, King Amogha, upon it.
Now, arrange the sword and rope according to the ritual;
present various offerings and burn the king of incenses.
During the day, sit according to the ritual with a wrathful facial expression.
With the left hand, hold a staff and press a sword against the cord;
recite the Mother Dhāraṇī mantra and the Secret Heart mantra while first grasping the sword and cord.
At night, recite the mantra of the Furenwang (Krodharāja).
Having empowered white mustard seeds, first strike the sword-noose.
For thirty-six weeks, perform the uninterrupted ritual; upon the sword and the noose, great flames of light are emitted.
At that time, the mantra-practitioner, holding a sword in his right hand and grasping a lasso in his left,
recites the mantra of the Wrathful King one hundred and eight times with a great roar of fury.
He thereby realizes and attains the vidyā-mantra of the Amogharāja, the supernatural power of the sword, and the samaya of the sword-vidyādhara.
The lifespan was eighteen thousand years.
At that time, there were the Vidyādhara Great Universal Monarchs of the Sword-holders, who all wield swords, and the Vidyādhara Great Universal Monarchs of the Secret Swords.
At that time, manifesting before him, he praised and protected him as his companion, sporting with supernatural powers (*ṛddhi-vikrīḍita*).
If one recites the mantra of the Wrathful King seven times with a great roar of anger,
one should brandish a sword and a lasso in a circular motion above the crown of the head.
Then all the most wicked vināyakas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, ghosts,
and spirits will simultaneously have boiling blood flow from their mouths,
or their heads will split open.
If, amidst a military array, one recites the mantra of the Wrathful King (*Krodharāja*) one hundred and eight times with a voice of great rage,
while brandishing a sword and a lasso in a circular motion above one's head,
then the enemy troops will scatter and flee in all directions, and none will be able to stand against him in combat.
If one recites the mantra of the Wrathful King seven times with a voice of great fury in a śmaśāna,
a sword-noose will whirl above the crown of the head,
thereby causing all malevolent spirits and ghosts to [submit].
Terrified and struck with great fear, they fainted upon the ground.
At that moment, the gates of the palaces of the spirits and deities opened simultaneously,
as did the gateways to the caves of the asuras and the entrances to the lairs of the nāgas.
Recite the mantra of the Wrathful King one hundred and eight times with a great, furious voice.
One should brandish the sword and lasso in circular motions above the crown of the head;
then the cave door will open of its own accord, and all the spirits and deities within the cave will be completely subdued.
They will serve as attendants, none daring to refuse;
if one seeks for them to perform various tasks,
they will all act accordingly, and nothing will fail to be accomplished.
O Bhagavat, regarding the Nāgapāśa-samaya:
take equal portions of the seven precious gems, yellow cinnabar, realgar, lotus filaments, nāga-flowers, and licorice flowers;
purify them and grind them into a fine powder.
Prepare the resin of the *duzhong* tree according to the prescribed method.
Recite the Secret Heart Mantra ten thousand times to empower it.
Then, fashion a statue or painting of the Dragon King in the likeness of a celestial deity.
From his head emerge three nāga heads;
the necks of the nāgas are slightly curved,
and their bodies and limbs are entirely adorned with gold.
The lasso should be made from five kinds of silk, dyed in five colors.
Having established the maṇḍala-samaya,
one should hold the threads together with the mantra while forming the strands of the lasso.
Make it a single long cord and do not divide it into separate strands.
Fold three strands together, sixteen cubits in length,
to form the noose.
Tie one end of the cord to the dragon’s neck.
Arrange the maṇḍala and adorn it with a precious, ornate seat;
place the dragon upon the seat facing east.
A lasso encircles the four sides of the dragon’s body.
One should place there an image of the King Amoghapāśa Avalokiteśvara and offer various kinds of worship while burning the king of incenses.
Every day, sit facing west with the seal of the wheel.
Recite the Mother Dhāraṇī, the Secret Heart Mantra, and first hold the dragon-rope.
At night, recite the mantra of the Wrathful King to empower white mustard seeds, and first strike the dragon-rope.
For thirty-six days, he performed the uninterrupted ritual.
From atop the dragon and atop the rope, he emitted a great mass of fiery light,
rising of his own accord three, four, or five inches above his seat.
At that time, holding a nāga with the left hand and a lasso with the right hand,
one should recite the mantra of the Wrathful King one hundred and eight times with a great roar of wrath.
Thus, one realizes and attains the *Amoghanāgapāśa-samaya*.
Wandering through the world without obstruction,
one shall enter the dragon palace;
before a dragon pool, a mountain stream, or a dragon cave.
Recite the mantra of the Wrathful King one hundred and eight times with a great, wrathful voice.
While turning the right wheel and brandishing the lasso,
the gate of the nāga palace will immediately open of its own accord.
Furthermore, recite the Mother Dhāraṇī and the Secret Heart Mantra one hundred and eight times to empower the gate of the dragon palace; then,
turning to the right, brandish the lasso toward the dragons.
Immediately, the Dragon King, leading his attendants,
appeared all at once; with palms joined in reverence,
he said, "Great Seer, we pray that you will enter the palace."
If, upon entering, one recites the mantra,
it is like a wheel or a lasso used to subdue various venomous dragons,
causing all their locks and fastenings to open without obstruction.
Upon arriving at the dragon palace, one receives various dragon maidens who offer and present precious flowers.
At that time, the practitioner of mantras should accept these flowers and place them upon the crown of his own head.
Together with the nāga maidens, he ascends into the sky with sovereign ease.
At that time, each of the nāga maidens pours forth her milk,
which the practitioner receives in his cupped hands and drinks.
His countenance transformed accordingly, becoming upright and exquisitely beautiful;
his hair was like a conch-shell topknot, and his lifespan extended for twelve thousand years.
Among all the nāgas, he was the most preeminent in majestic power and efficacy.
Every day, one should recite the Mother Dhāraṇī mantra and the Secret Heart mantra one hundred and eight times.
One should empower the Nāgarāja-śṛṅkhalā (Dragon’s Chain) and hang it around the right arm, never parting from the body.
With the left hand, form the *kṣaṇa* mudrā by using the thumb to press against the root joint of the ring finger.
With the index finger held straight up,
the middle, ring, and little fingers are firmly clenched around the thumb to form a fist; with this mudrā, one should daily threaten the dragon-noose.
Every day, he receives all manner of supreme-flavored food and drink as a wondrous offering from the Dragon King within the dragon palace;
furthermore, none of the venomous dragons therein ever harm one another.
Furthermore, if one recites the mantra of the Wrathful King one hundred and eight times while brandishing the right wheel and the lasso toward the dragon,
one will obtain all the garments, precious jewels, and ornamental implements of the dragon kings.
If it is the first or second month of spring, or the seventh or eighth month of autumn,
there will be clouds appearing during these months.
Looking toward the place where the clouds emerge from afar, one should hold a rope in the right hand and grasp the dragon with the left hand.
Recite the Mātṛkā-dhāraṇī mantra and the Secret Heart-mantra one hundred and eight times.
Visualize the right wheel of the clouds as a lasso and direct it toward the dragon;
then, for the duration of one year, you will cause all the dragon kings to send down sweet rain.
All crops and fruits will ripen and flourish in great abundance.
Furthermore, recite the mantra of the Wrathful King one hundred and eight times,
circling to the right with a rope while pointing it toward the dragon’s palace.
One should cause all the waters of the flavor of nectar to descend.
Furthermore, recite the mantra of the Wrathful King and brandish the wheel and lasso toward the dragon.
Immediately, one will be protected and assisted by all the retinues and servants of the dragon kings.
If there is a severe drought,
recite the Mother Dhāraṇī Mantra and the Secret Heart Mantra one hundred and eight times on the summit of a high mountain.
If one intends to cause a great rain to fall using the right wheel-rope,
or if there is excessive rain,
one should grasp the dragon-rope and place it atop a high banner.
If one places [the image] atop a stupa or on a mountain peak, the rain will immediately clear.
If fierce winds, thunder, and hail arise repeatedly,
one should go to a high vantage point and utter a great, wrathful roar.
Recite the Mātṛkā-dhāraṇī mantra and the Secret Heart Mantra one hundred and eight times.
If one then circles a dragon with a rope clockwise,
there will be no harmful winds or hail for one year.
If one wishes to guide and transform all people,
place the nāgapāśa upon the maṇḍala and recite the Mother Dhāraṇī mantra and the Secret Heart mantra.
Consecrate pomegranate seeds and white mustard seeds.
Recite the mantra once for each strike seven times upon the dragon-rope.
One should then hold the dragon-rope toward that [target].
If one mimics the wheel-noose dragon,
it will cause all beings to revere, believe in, and submit;
if one faces an opposing army while in the midst of battle, [the same result follows].
Recite the mantra of the Wrathful King one hundred and eight times with a great, furious voice.
As you brandish the noose of the right wheel toward the enemy forces, all shall see it as a most terrifying venomous dragon.
With eyes bulging and mouths agape like a great mass of fire,
they were all suddenly overcome with panic and fled in all directions;
whatever various dharmas they had sought [vanished].
The aforementioned procedures are all accomplished.
This is the Samaya of the World-Honored One Maheśvara’s trident and noose;
the trident is made of tempered steel.
The trident should measure four cubits in length, with a handle of the same measurement.
For the noose and other implements, take the tail-hair of a living bull and the hair of a living young boy.
Purify them with the five-fold purification (*pañcagavya*) and erect the maṇḍala.
Consecrate the strands of the cord with mantras;
they should be made into a single long strand rather than separate strands.
Fold them together into three strands, each sixteen cubits in length.
Construct a noose (*pāśa*).
Tie one end of this noose to the shaft of a trident (*śakti*).
On the eighth day of the dark fortnight, construct a maṇḍala.
Adorn a seat with precious fabrics and place a trident with a lasso;
the lasso should be wide and coiled around the four sides of the trident.
Install an image of Avalokiteśvara, King of the Unobstructed.
Perform various offerings daily, reciting the Mother Dhāraṇī and the Secret Heart Mantra.
First, hold a trident and a noose;
at night, recite the mantra of the Furenu King (Krodharāja).
Empower white mustard seeds.
First, brandish the trident-noose.
Perform the ritual of the thirty-six weeks without interruption.
A great mass of fire-light is emitted from the trident and the noose.
At that time, the practitioner of mantras holds the trident with his left hand and grasps the noose with his right hand,
reciting the mantra of the Wrathful King one hundred and eight times.
Then one realizes the samaya of the supernatural powers of Maheśvara;
one's lifespan extends for eighteen thousand years,
and one wanders throughout the world.
He attains fearlessness among all ghosts and spirits.
Maheśvara and all the ghosts and spirits serve as his attendants.
If he is in a śītavana cemetery, he holds a right-turning wheel and a trident.
Reciting the mantra of the Wrathful King seven times with a great roar of fury,
the spirits and deities within the forest all manifested their forms;
at once, the gates of the spirits' palaces opened and appeared.
Within it are precious jewels that may be taken at will without obstruction.
If one ties one end of a rope around the neck of the person to be summoned,
the mantra-holder wields a spear while reciting the mantra over the person being summoned.
Command the yakṣa to speak of all matters of worldly fortune and misfortune as they are asked;
if he is compliant, untie the cord.
If the cord is tied around the neck of the yakṣa image, [the result will be as follows].
The mantra-holder should grasp a trident and brandish it,
uttering the wrathful sound of a great roar while reciting the Mantra of the Wrathful King one hundred and eight times with each drawn-out cry.
Then the true yakṣa will appear before him in person and ask the mantra-practitioner, "What shall I do?
To which he should reply, "I now require you."
"Until the end of your life, you shall serve me;
you must always follow me in all matters.
The yakṣa replied, "I shall now comply with your command."
If one ties a cord around the neck of an image of a yakṣiṇī,
the mantra-practitioner should grasp a trident and brandish it,
reciting the Mantra of the Wrathful King once with a voice of great fury.
If one chants the summoning sound one hundred and eight times,
a true yakṣiṇī will appear before them and say to the mantra-practitioner: "What do you wish to do now?"
He spoke again, saying, "I seek three wishes;
grant them to me now.
The yakṣiṇī replied, "Take whatever you desire."
If you become my mother, you shall always provide me with all manner of wealth and treasures;
if you become my elder sister, you shall always supply me with all clothing, food, and drink;
and we shall constantly follow one another, playing together everywhere.
She will become my sister, placing herself at my disposal to fulfill all manner of wishes.
If one ties a cord around the neck of an image of Vaiśravaṇa and the mantra-holder brandishes a spear, pointing it toward him, [she will appear].
Uttering a great roar of wrath, recite the mantra of the Wrathful King once;
then, perform the rite of summoning Vaiśravaṇa one thousand and eight times.
True Vaiśravaṇa will then appear before you in person.
The mantra-holder addressed the Great Deity, saying,
"I beg for one thousand great taels of gold and one thousand gold coins every day.
The Deity replied, "As you wish."
If you obtain money, do not allow it to accumulate;
as soon as you receive it, give it away and perform various meritorious deeds.
Furthermore, if you tie a cord around the neck of an image of Mahākāla, [the desired results will follow].
The mantra-holder should grasp a trident and brandish it.
Uttering the Great Wrathful Sound, he should recite the Mantra of the Wrathful King (*Krodharāja*) once to empower his own hand, generating a state of great wrath.
He should strike the face of Mahākāla three, five, or seven times.
The image will let out a great cry;
at that time, the practitioner of mantras must not give way to fear.
He should form the *kṣepaṇī-mudrā* and point it toward the image of Mahākāla.
Tears then flowed from the eyes of the image;
he took those tears with his finger and applied them as a dot upon his forehead.
Thereby, he attained the secret samaya and beheld hidden treasures.
Furthermore, if one strikes the image three, four, or seven times with the mantra-hand,
blood will immediately flow from its eyes;
by cupping it in one's hands and drinking it, one will immediately realize the supernormal power of the body.
Soaring freely through the air, he is foremost in the majestic power of all yakṣas.
If one wishes for the deity Mahākāla to manifest his physical form and appear,
one should burn agallochum incense and utter a great, wrathful cry.
Recite the mantra of the Wrathful King once,
utter the name of Mahākāla once,
and chant the sound "Hūṃ" one thousand and eight times.
She will immediately appear before one's person, and all the various aspirations sought shall be fully realized.
Even the great spirit Hārītī will personally submit.
If there are other various aspirations one seeks, they too shall be fulfilled.
By performing it in this manner as well, one shall achieve all accomplishments.
World-Honored One, such is the Amoghapāśa Avalokiteśvara Image Pāśasamaya;
it is indeed the true locus for accomplishing all supreme samayas.
In accordance with various types of manifestations, by the power of the great samaya of illusory transformation,
one displays all manner of miraculous signs;
that is to say, manifesting a thousand hands and a thousand eyes.
Holding the wheel, the seal of immeasurable supernormal powers, and various ritual implements,
he manifests diverse physical bodies throughout the three realms to guide and entice all sentient beings according to their needs.
Or he manifests all manner of secret and wondrous form-bodies to benefit sentient beings and bring to maturity the various roots of virtue conducive to enlightenment.
The mantra practitioner should diligently study and train in all mundane and supramundane dharmas,
proceeding toward the stage of all Tathāgatas, the stage of tranquil contemplation, and the stage of the Bodhisattvas.
Then one shall constantly behold the true and wondrous form-body of all Tathāgatas,
as well as the pure lands and the vast, great supernormal powers of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva. For this reason:
The wise should revere and honor this Pāśa-samaya as they would the body of the Buddha or the body of Avalokiteśvara. Why is this?

Because this dharma can manifest the true, wondrous form-body of King Amogha, Avalokiteśvara’s most supreme liberation, the non-empty supernormal powers, and the great sovereign samaya; it is the samaya of all the non-empty Tathāgatas, the Peerless Arhats, and the Samyaksaṃbuddhas.
The practitioner of mantras should constantly guard their mind day and night,
remaining ever-vigilant and unwearied,
abiding in the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, as well as in a heart of great compassion.
Practice according to the Dharma and offer respectful worship,

fully conforming to the teachings. One by one, fashion images— whether through modeling or painting— of all the Buddhas, of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara of the Amoghapāśa lineage, and of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas of the Lotus family, as well as the forms of devas, nāgas, yakṣas, and spirits.
With reverence and respect, one should make offerings of various flowers and incense,
while maintaining a mind free from distraction and upholding the Samaya of the Heart-King Mother Dhāraṇī Mantra of Amoghapāśa.
If one never neglects or forgets the seal and samaya of the vast liberation lotus maṇḍala,
one will then attain the samaya of the Āmoghapāśa King Mother Dhāraṇī mantra.
Through the samaya of the noose-mantra of the Wrathful King,
one achieves various supernatural powers and samādhis,
and attains the accomplishments of all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, and all Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas.
All the samayas of supernatural powers;
furthermore, one obtains [the favor of] all devas, nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas.
The deities Bhīṣma, Sūkṣmarūpa, Yama-rāja, Vaiśravaṇa, Īśvara, Maheśvara, Mahābrahmā, and Nārāyaṇa.
The samayas of Maheśvara, Kumāra, Agni, Vāyu, Sūrya, Candra,
the celestial bodies, the deities of day,
the deities of night, the bhūtas, and the other spirits are all fully accomplished.
The World-Honored One’s manifestation of such teachings is spoken for the sake of securing the benefit and happiness of all sentient beings;
it is spoken for the sake of subduing all sentient beings with false views so that they may enter the Right Path.
For this reason, I now manifest and teach this Dharma instruction in accordance with the needs of sentient beings for their respective taming.
Any wise person should not give rise to doubt regarding this teaching.
As for the method of practice:
first, one must clearly understand all the mandalas, mudrās, and dharmas, as well as the days, months, times, and seasons.
Then, in a secluded and quiet place that is pleasing to the mind, [one should proceed].
In accordance with the Semblance Dharma (*pratirūpaka-dharma*), one should construct a maṇḍala by seeking out the requisite materials.
Within it, place images of the Buddha, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara with the Amoghapāśa,
and the forms of the devas, nāgas, and the eight classes of supernatural beings, including spirits and ghosts.
Whether it be an image of a Buddha, a Bodhisattva, or Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva according to one's own inclination,
or the forms of various devas, spirits, or ghosts,
one may have them depicted or sculpted according to whatever ritual method is being performed.
If there are images of devas, nāgas, spirits,
or ghosts that bear witness to the Dharma, they shall all have [the mantra] tied around their necks.
If there are images of Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, or Vajradharas...
All dharmas that are to be realized are placed upon the hands and beneath the feet;
by practicing according to the three samādhis— superior, middling,
and inferior— one brings all dharmas to complete fulfillment.
If one seeks all dharmas of liberation,
one should place a maṇi-jewel cord beneath the feet of the Buddha and the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara and recite the Maṇiratna-dhāraṇī mantra.
One will then realize the gateway to liberation of all phenomena;
after this life, one will attain great bodhi,
achieve equal and perfect enlightenment, and turn the great wheel of Dharma.
The Amoghapāśakalparāja Sūtra, Scroll Six; The Amoghapāśakalparāja Sūtra, Scroll Seven.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Bodhiruci of India during the Great Tang Dynasty.
Chapter Seven: The Ritual of Homa for Augmentation.
This is the World-Honored One’s *Amogharāja-homa-samaya*, which is capable of accomplishing all meritorious virtues and roots of goodness.
It can extinguish all karmic obstacles of the past and present;
it can shatter all vetālas and the like;
and it can eliminate all malevolent vināyakas.
It can suppress all evils and *nṛśaṃsa* (cruelty);
it can extinguish all inauspicious signs;
and it can ward off the sufferings of the sixteen great hells.
It can eliminate the fear of the eight great terrors;
it can shatter all enmity, strife, and challenges;
and it can subdue all the weapons of enemy armies.
It can eliminate all epidemics and famines;
it can realize the great wisdom of all Buddhas;
and it can enter the bodhi of all Buddhas.
If there are sentient beings who practice and study in accordance with the Dharma,
they shall always cause all the devas of the Four Great Heavenly Kings, as well as the eight classes of spirits including devas and nāgas,
to provide them with protection and assistance.
All Tathāgatas and Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva observe and bestow their blessings.
The World-Honored One has taught the Śāntika Samaya,
which brings peace and happiness to sentient beings and extinguishes all calamities and epidemics.
It is taught that the pauṣṭika samaya increases the merit, lifespan, and wealth of sentient beings;
it is taught that the ābhicāruka samaya subdues and eliminates all evil-natured yakṣas and rākṣasas who devour the vital essence of humans.
All [obstacles] are naturally subdued,
causing sentient beings who are lost in the dense forest of false views to enter into right view.
For this reason, the homa rite is taught.
To accomplish the samaya of supramundane and mundane liberation,
one should perform the rites according to the Dharma:
summoning all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, fire deities, celestial deities, nāgas, dragon spirits, mantra-vidyādharas, and offering them burnt food (homa).
Change into clean robes.
At a location neither too far from nor too near the site of the ritual arena (maṇḍala),
behold the venerable countenance and construct a homa altar.
The ritual ground is to be prepared as a square or circle measuring four cubits, with its site adorned and its gateways and passages opened wide.
The foundation is raised by the thickness of a side-handspan; within the inner enclosure, a hearth is to be dug, measuring one and a half cubits in width and one cubit in depth.
It is surrounded by double borders;
the inner border measures two finger-widths in height and width,
while the outer border measures four finger-widths in height and width.
Fashion an eight-petaled lotus at the base of the hearth;
upon the flower pedestal, mold a clay wheel and polish it according to the ritual rules.
The outer courtyard is one cubit [in width].
In the east, place the seals of Mahābrahmā, Śakra, and Sūrya.
In the southeast, place the seals of Agni and the various ṛṣis.
In the south, place the seal of King Yama and the seal of the Indian messenger deity Ekajaṭī Rākṣasī.
In the southwest, place the seal of the deity Nīlīti and the seals of the various rākṣasas.
In the west, place the seals of Varuṇa, the Dragon King, Pṛthivī, and Candramas.
In the northwest, place the seals of Vāyu and Garuḍa.
In the north, place the seal of Vaiśravaṇa and the seals of all the yakṣas.
In the northeast, place the seal of Maheśvara and the seal of Īśāna;
having bound these seals to expel obstructors, protect the body,
and demarcate the boundary, one then invokes them.
Place *argha* vases at the four corners.
At the four gates, place incense burners and burn various kinds of incense.
Spread flowers, perfumes, food, and drink as offerings.
Consecrate the purified kusa-grass ashes and apply them to the foreheads and bodies of the companions for protection;
then spread out a seat of kusa grass.
At the hour of You (5–7 p.m. or Xu (7–9 p.m.), sit facing east.
Take wood from the *duzhong* tree, the *muyu* tree, or the cypress tree, cut into pieces the size of a thumb and twelve finger-widths in length.
Light a fire within the hearth.
Fan it into flame, but do not blow upon it.
One should sprinkle purified water over the fire and snap the fingers three times.
One should visualize that the flame-like gold transforms into the syllable *raṃ*, which becomes the Fire God (*Agni*).
He has one face, three eyes, a white body, four arms, and yellow hair bound in a topknot.
His first two left hands hold a *kamaṇḍalu* and a jeweled staff (*daṇḍa*).
The right hands hold one in the gesture of granting fearlessness (*abhaya-mudrā*) and the other grasps a rosary.
Seated in the half-lotus posture (*ardhaparyaṅka*), emitting great flames of fire, he is invoked with incense.
[Offerings are made] with rice grains, white mustard seeds, and high-quality clarified butter (*sarpis*).
The mantra for invoking the Fire Deity (Agnideva) for the purpose of Vidyā-mantra homa is as follows: Oṃ jvala jvala prajvala tiṣṭha samaye hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. Recite this seventeen times.
Summon the Fire Deity.
Perform seven rounds of homa with ghee, white mustard seeds,
and agallochum incense while reciting the mantra.
With various powdered incenses and sweet-tasting fruits,
perform seven recitations of the mantra for homa.
Then, sprinkle purified water upon the fire while reciting the mantra and snap the fingers three times.
Using wood from the *candana* tree, the *śamī* tree, the *sāla* tree, the lotus stalk, or white sandalwood,
cut pieces sixteen finger-widths long and kindle a fire within the hearth, consecrating it with mantras.
Any one of these woods may be used to perform the rite with success:
white sandalwood, olibanum, spikenard, rice-panicles, or clarified butter.
One should recite the Secret Heart Mantra and the Mantra of the Wrathful King.
Perform the consecrated homa one hundred and eight times.
Steam non-glutinous rice;
prepare one thousand and eight balls of ghee.
Perform the consecrated homa.
When this homa is completed for twenty-one days or forty-nine days,
at that time the Fire Deity will manifest his form within the altar.
Gazing toward the ten directions, he praised, saying:
"Excellent, excellent! O upholder of mantras, you have now attained the accomplishment of this homa rite."
Whatever wish you require shall be fulfilled.
At that time, one should offer arghya water;
furthermore, one should offer one thousand and eight balls of rice mixed with ghee.
If one performs the consecrated homa while requesting a specific boon,
the Fire God (Agnideva) will take a silver vessel filled with medicinal elixir in his hands and present it to the practitioner of the mantra.
If one partakes of this bait, one will attain benevolence and joy;
the body will emit flames of light, and one's lifespan will extend for ten thousand years.
One shall realize the knowledge of past lives and attain the Samaya of the Heart-King Mother Dhāraṇī Mantra, the Amoghapāśa.
If the Fire Deity (Agnideva) does not accept the medicinal offering,
one should again perform one thousand and eight *homā* oblations of dough-balls;
then the ritual platform (*maṇḍala*) will tremble.
The Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara manifested his form to comfort him, praising him, saying: "Excellent, excellent!
You have already accomplished this homa rite."
"Whatever boon you require, I shall now fulfill for you.
At that time, the mantra-practitioner offers argha-water as an offering;
Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva then personally takes the medicine and gives it to the mantra-practitioner.
Prostrating with reverence, he received the medicine and consumed it.
His appearance transformed into one of exquisite beauty, and his body emitted blazing flames.
He realized and attained the vidyā-siddha’s samaya of the Great Mantra of Amoghasiddhi and its supernormal powers.
Ninety-two *gaṅgā*-sands of mantra-vidyā-rishis appeared simultaneously to pay their respects and become his companions;
they dwelt in ninety-two *koṭi*-hundred-thousand palaces made of the seven precious gems, situated where Avalokiteśvara resides.
They dwell in peaceful and joyful contemplation.
These palaces are adorned with an infinite variety of jewel trees interspersed with flowers and fruits.
In the gardens and groves of that land, there are many kinds of golden, silver, and precious jewel trees, all bearing various types of flowers and fruits.
All the ponds are filled with water of eight meritorious qualities,
its fragrance as sweet and pervasive as that of sandalwood.
Within those waters abound many varieties of blue utpala flowers, red padma flowers, yellow kumuda flowers, and white puṇḍarīka flowers.
The various springs and ponds have their bottoms strewn with golden sand and their banks composed of diverse jewels; these palaces,
terraces, pavilions, and towers, as well as the flowers, fruits, springs, and ponds— [all are thus adorned].
They reflect one another, making the entire area vast, majestic, and pure.
All the deva-men, deva-women, kinnara-women, and gandharva-women constantly and universally sport therein.
Such is the body received by the mantra-holder.
Until reaching unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, they shall no longer undergo rebirth;
they will constantly travel to all lands in the ten directions to reverently make offerings to all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Mahāsattvas.
All Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas who uphold this Samaya of the Seal of the Lotus Maṇḍala of the Vast Liberation of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva and the Amoghapāśa.
They paid homage with deep reverence and offered praise;
all the devas, numbering in the hundreds of thousands of koṭis,
up to the Akaniṣṭha heaven, did likewise.
All the dragon kings, asura kings, kinnara kings, gandharva kings, garuḍa kings,
and mahoraga kings shall provide all necessary requisites.
Sweet delicacies and food and drink will be spontaneously abundant.
Those who obtain these fruits do so entirely because of this *samaya* of the great *ājñā-mukha* king’s *homa* offerings.
If a practitioner of mantras has many grave offenses and meager merit, [they shall not attain them].
Although by taking this medicine one may attain wealth and abundance as well as a long life,
one will not be able to realize or witness the various forms, comings and goings, supernatural powers, and transformations of the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Mahāsattvas.
It shall cause all karmic obstructions of the past and present to be completely extinguished;
one will be loved and praised by others,
and all words spoken will be trusted and accepted by them.
At the time of death, with body and mind tranquil and free from all enmity or fear,
all the Tathāgatas and Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva will simultaneously manifest their forms to welcome the practitioner of mantras.
He will go to the West to be born through transformation from a lotus flower.
Attaining the knowledge of past lives,
he will fully recognize the events of his births throughout hundreds of millions of kalpas.
Until they reach enlightenment, they shall never again undergo any body born from a womb, an egg, moisture,
or transformation. From one buddha-field to another,
they shall listen to and uphold all dharmas and make offerings to all buddhas.
If one applies this medicine to the forehead and wanders through the world, one will be loved and respected by people;
whatever one subsequently desires shall be attained.
If one recollects the Fire Deity (Agnideva), he will manifest his form;
one should then make requests according to one's wishes,
and all shall be fulfilled.
Furthermore, as for the samaya:
cut and prepare sticks of clove wood and pomegranate wood, kindle a fire,
and recite the Mātṛ-dhāraṇī mantra and the Krodharāja mantra.
Consecrate non-glutinous rice, mung beans, steamed cakes, lotus powder, white mustard seeds, clarified butter, honey, and rock sugar,
and fashion them into *modaka* (joy-balls).
Perform consecrated *homa* offerings for seven days.
Within the furnace, there further appeared the upper half of the body of the Fire Deity (Agni), holding a precious platter filled with medicinal powder.

Addressing the practitioner of the mantra, he said: "This wondrous medicinal powder is the final medicine; please deign to accept it. At that time, the practitioner immediately paid him reverent homage.
Having received the medicine and taken it as an elixir, his body immediately became comfortable and joyful.
He realized the Mahā-mantra-vidyā-siddha-abhijñā-samaya of the King of Non-Voidness (Amogharāja).
There were eighteen thousand mantra-holding siddhas.
All the fire deities will simultaneously appear,
respectfully attending as companions and providing protection and blessings.
For all mantra-practitioners who consume this medicine:
One will then attain realization of this *asunyata-rāja-citta-dhāraṇī-mantra-maṇḍala-mudrā-samaya*.

Whether on a mountain peak or atop a tower facing the heavens,

Furthermore, perform one thousand and eight rounds of homa.
All devas, nāgas, the eight classes of beings, ghosts, and spirits will respectfully praise and submit;

Furthermore, by performing one thousand and eight homa offerings,

The Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara manifests his form and offers praise,

the samaya-body of the Amogha-viśuddha-vipaśyanā.
If one uses *khadira* wood, white sandalwood, or cypress wood,
