from within the hearth, the youth Agni shall manifest.
Holding a precious plate filled with *māṇibhadra-piṇḍa* medicine in his hand,
he then recites the mantra over white mustard seeds and strikes the boy one, two, or seven times.
The youth said, "What do you seek now?
He replied, "I seek all the great vows of enlightenment; may they be fulfilled for me."
At that time, the youth said to the mantra-practitioner:
"Accept this medicinal pill;
for this medicine is indeed the unsurpassed, wondrous ambrosia among all medicines."
One will immediately accomplish the most supreme great vow.
At that time, the mantra-practitioner receives and holds it,
saying to the youth:
"You should then always be my companion.
The youth replied, "I shall follow your command and be your companion;
wherever you perform the rite, we shall meet there."
One should immediately cut and prepare wood from the *duzhong* tree to kindle a fire.
Reciting the mantra of the Vidyārāja Viśvāmitra,
one consecrates white sandalwood, *guggulu*, white mustard seeds, and clarified butter.
Perform one hundred and eight *homa* offerings to the youth;
he will then constantly be your companion, never parting from you,
and all ritual acts will be brought to fulfillment.
Furthermore, to ward off all ghosts and spirits who create obstacles and difficulties,
one should offer this medicine to Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva; then,
one shall take this medicine.
He immediately realized the *amogharāja* supernatural power samādhi;
his physical form was dignified and majestic, his hair was curled like a spiral,
and his lifespan extended for sixty thousand kalpas.
Eighty-four million mantra-vidyādhara sages will simultaneously appear and attend upon him as companions.
If one gives this medicine to all śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, and common people for them to eat, [they shall be benefited].
All shall attain longevity,
and all past and present sins, illnesses, and afflictions shall be eliminated.
If this medicine is applied to various objects, [the same shall occur].
All these immediately transform into Jambūnada gold.
If one throws this medicine into a pool,
all the dragon kings will appear and submit.
If one appoints this as an official to dispel all calamities of wind, rain, and drought,
or if one strikes the gate of the Asura cave with this medicine,
that gate shall immediately open.
The entire retinue of Suluo will simultaneously manifest and station themselves as messengers.
If one scatters this medicine within a mountain forest,
then the essences of all medicinal herbs will appear, which may be taken and ingested at will.
If one scatters this medicine within a cemetery (śītavana),
the palaces of the ghosts and spirits will immediately open and manifest;
the ghosts and spirits will reveal their forms and place themselves at one's disposal as servants.
If one has newly acquired, unbroken rice husks,
one should bathe with fragrant water, put on clean white garments,
and place these medicinal substances into two alms bowls.
Consecrate white mustard seeds and mix them with these medicines;
scatter them over the person.
Then, having consecrated them, inquire about matters concerning the three times—past, present, and future—both mundane and supramundane.
Regarding the methods of divination, physiognomy, medicine, incantations, arts, crafts, and supernormal powers,
all are explained based on inquiry;
if it were otherwise, [they would not be so].
Holding water, one sprinkles it on the face to wipe away the medicine.
If this medicine is buried in the ground at the entrance of a dwelling,
then the calamities and diseases of the people will be eliminated.
If one places this medicine in the hands of an image of Śrī-devī and recites the mantra of the Wrathful King one hundred and eight times,
Śrī-devī will immediately manifest her form and bestow upon one various kinds of wealth and treasures.
If one wraps this medicine in clean white cloth and carries it with one wherever one goes,
people's eyes will not take notice of it.
If one buries this medicine at a riverbank or beneath a large solitary tree, [the same shall occur].
Recite the mantra of the Wrathful King seven times;
all ghosts will manifest their forms and submit, placing themselves at one's disposal for whatever tasks are required.
If one places this medicine upon the head of an image of Mahākāla and recites the mantra of the Wrathful King (Krodharāja) seven times over white mustard seeds and water, consecrating them with it.

If one places this medicine in the hand or bowl of an image of Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva,

Furthermore, one sprinkles the altar and the hearth with mantra-water, and kindles a fire within the hearth.

At the site of the mandala ritual, he shall constantly manifest his form to provide instruction and admonition, so that one may attain the Dharma and fulfill all aspirations.

On the eighth or fifteenth day of the waxing moon,
during the first watch, the last watch, or at dawn during the fifth watch,
a great flame will emerge from the cauldron atop the medicinal substances.
One will attain great accomplishment;
by upholding and making offerings to it, one will possess great majestic power,
like a wish-fulfilling jewel.
If one wishes to eat or drink,
place the cauldron in a clean location, arrange vessels around it,
and burn the incense-king while reciting the mantra.
If one performs the ritual invocation for a brief moment according to the sūtra,
there will appear a hundred flavors of sweet delicacies and food;
if one burns fire-food, it shall appear before the cauldron and hearth.
The fire ritual brings swift and efficacious results.
If there is a valiant general wishing to array his forces against the enemy,
he should purify his body and clothing, take up his weapons, place a cauldron upon his head, and advance alone into the enemy ranks.
All those soldiers saw great flames of fire issue from their bodies; they were simultaneously subdued, fleeing in panic and fear.
[The practitioner] is courageous and fearless.
If one places a cauldron at the entrance of the asura cave and performs the rite...
Recite and maintain the mantra;
then the hosts of asuras will all appear at once, joyfully submitting to one's commands.
If one places a cauldron in a dragon pool or stream and performs the rite, [the desired result will follow].
By reciting and upholding this mantra, the waters will be completely dried up, and the nāgas will appear and be subdued.
Furthermore, the five grains of the land will flourish, fruits and crops will be abundant, and there will be no calamities or diseases.
This is the gateway to the accumulation of immeasurable masses of merit.
O Bhagavān, this is the Samaya of the Amoghaprabhāvalokiteśvara-bhaiṣajya, the *saurmila-anjana*.
Consecrate the clay with mantras and wrap it securely;
place it inside the hearth and kindle a fire using trimmed pieces of *duzhong* wood.
Using night-blooming jasmine, white mustard seeds, white sandalwood, clarified butter, curd, and honey,
one should recite and maintain the Mother Dhāraṇī mantra and the Greatly Radiant King Aṅkuśa mantra.
Perform one thousand and eight rounds of homa.
Consecrate agallochum, white sandalwood, aloeswood, white mustard seeds, ghee, curd, and honey,
and perform one thousand and eight rounds of homa.
The Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara spoke these words:
"Excellent, excellent, son of good family!
You have now accomplished the medicinal rite of radiant flames."
Having fulfilled his request,
he waited until the fire had cooled, then went out to retrieve the medicine, which was *saumilāñjana*.
Mixing camphor, storax, and musk, he ground them together to form an ointment for the eyes;
using realgar and orpiment, he prepared an unguent for the body.
Thoroughly refine [the medicine] and place it separately within the mandala.
Recite the Mother Dhāraṇī mantra and the Great Mantra of Aṅkuśa, the King of Vidyārājas,
to empower the medicine so that signs of warmth, smoke, and light appear.
This is called the "Accomplishment of the Radiant Flame Medicine" rite.
At that time, one uses the medicine to dot the forehead, the eyes,
both shoulders, and the palms of both hands.
One shall immediately realize the samaya of the medicinal vidyā-mantra of Unfailing Radiant Flames,
increase one's lifespan by a thousand years,
and remain unimpeded by any vināyakas or māras of the desire realm.
All people will revere and make offerings to them.
If they enter into battle, they shall achieve victory.
They will be respected by others.
One will not fear the strife, disputes, and verbal quarrels of the world, nor the calamities of the mountains;
one will not suffer from ailments such as headaches, eye pain, ear pain, or diseases caused by ghosts and spirits.
If one applies [this ointment] to the eyes of an image of Mahākāla, [these benefits shall be attained].
If one recites and maintains the mantra of the Wrathful King,
his image will weep;
this causes the great deity Mahākāla and his retinue to be subdued and made to grant protection.
If one dots the eyes of the image of Śrī-devī and gazes upon the image while blinking, reciting the Mātṛ-dhāraṇī mantra,
it will cause the true Śrī-devī to come and protect and assist them, so that their wealth and treasures may increase and be fulfilled.
If one applies [this ointment] to the eyes while sleeping,
one will obtain all superior auspicious dreams and receive the grace, protection, and guardianship of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.
If one applies it to the eyes of an image of the Unfailing Lasso Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva...
One will swiftly obtain the empowerment of the supreme vow of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.
If one mixes medicine with ox bezoar and applies it to the upper eyelid, [the eyes will be restored].
If one sees it by a king or his attendants,
they will attain great joy;
if it is applied to the eyes of an image of Maheśvara, [the same result follows].
If one recites the mantra of the Wrathful King seven times,
all ghosts and spirits will be subdued and rendered protective. Furthermore,
if one dots the forehead of an image of Mahākāla [with this mantra], [the same result follows].
One who recites and maintains the mantra of the Wrathful King shall cause all yakṣas to submit and be subdued. Furthermore,
when a śramaṇa goes out to beg for alms, [the yakṣas will likewise follow].
One who applies this medicine to the eyes and goes out to beg for alms will quickly obtain pure food;
if it is applied to the eyelids, the same result follows.
If one enters all mountains, forests, ponds, and marshes,
one shall not fear any difficulties caused by malevolent spirits, tigers, wolves, and the like.
If one applies [the ointment] to the eyelids and enters a celestial shrine, [one shall likewise be unafraid].
One who gazes with eyes wide open at Hārītī while reciting the mantra of the Wrathful King shall cause Hārītī and her retinue to be subdued and made to grant protection.

Furthermore, there is another method: take the roots, branches, leaves, flowers, and fruits of the *khadira*, *kārañja*, *duzhong* (*cudrā*), and *pālāśa* trees, cut them into pieces, and kindle a fire.
Then [use] non-glutinous rice, wild rice, black sesame, and white mustard seeds.
Using white grains, rice, barley, wheat, large beans, small beans, sesame seeds, clarified butter, honey, and curd,
one should recite and maintain the Mother Dhāraṇī and the Mantra of the Wrathful King while performing *homa* one thousand and eight times.
Furthermore, mixing *guggulu* incense with black mustard seeds,
one should recite the mantra of the Great Vidyārāja Aṅkuśa and the mantra of Caṇḍarūpa,
performing one thousand and eight *homa* offerings.
They shall then obtain wealth and riches as abundant as they desire;
until the end of their lives, they shall lack for nothing,
and the deity Maṇibhadra shall protect them.
The World-Honored One, Amoghasiddhi, possesses the samaya of supernatural power through ox-gallstone;
he is foremost in converting and subduing the world,
entering into marshes and wetlands as well as mountain forests.
They enter the caves of asuras and the palatial chambers of dragon pools;
they enter the palatial chambers of the ocean dragon kings and descend into the earth.
All supernatural transformations beneath the earth are thereby accomplished.
All those who fear various illnesses and sufferings,
past and present karmic obstructions, enemies and calamities,
military conflicts, disputes, sorcery, talismans, and curses—
All fevers caused by devas and spirits, malignant stars and portents,
imprisonment and confinement, shackles and fetters, and execution—
all shall be extinguished and eliminated.
Through the accomplishment of this rite, one will achieve wealth and abundance;
all śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, and all people will hold one in precious esteem and affection.
[This includes] Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, the Śuddhāvāsa deities, and Īśvara.
Maheśvara, Mahābrahmā, Śakra-devendra, Nārāyaṇa, and all the devas,
nāgas, and the eight classes of divine beings shall all provide protection.
To purify the body, clothing, and other items, one should use ox-gallstone (*gorocanā*), red sandalwood, and saffron;
having purified and finely ground them,
one should reduce the medicinal powder by one-third using the ashes of burnt firewood.
Consecrate a separate vessel with mantras,
fill it with [the substance], and place it within the mandala before an image of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva;
cover it with a clean cloth or a lotus leaf.
The fire consumes the ashes.
Using *candana* wood, *duzhong* wood, rice-panicle flowers, white non-glutinous rice, white mustard seeds, sesame, clarified butter, honey, and curdled milk,
perform *homa* according to the ritual rules to obtain fine white ash.
Recite the mantra of the Mother Dhāraṇī, the Great Mantra of the Vidyārāja Aṅkuśa, and the mantra of the Krodharāja;
empower the previously prepared medicine so that it manifests the three signs.
First is the sign of warmth, second is the sign of boiling smoke, and third is the sign of light.
One who realizes these three signs is called a great adept (*mahāsiddha*).
Using the medicinal substance, one should apply it to the crown of the head, the forehead, the eyes, the space between the eyebrows, above the eyebrows, the palms of both hands, and the heart.
He realized the Samaya of the Non-empty Cow-Horned Immortal’s Supernatural Powers,
his various marks becoming perfectly complete and his lifespan extending far beyond the ordinary.
He clearly beheld the palaces of all the devas, nāgas, the eight classes of beings, and ghosts and spirits.
There shall be no obstructions whatsoever.
All ghosts and spirits will be terrified and submit, and all undertakings will be accomplished.
If the medicine is applied to the eyes, one will see all hidden treasures and the palaces of the ghosts and spirits beneath the earth without any hindrance.
At night, one sees everything without any obscuration or darkness.
Whether entering or crossing rivers, streams, or the great ocean, it is as if dwelling in a house on dry land;
one does not fear any aquatic creatures that might cause harm.
Furthermore, one obtains various kinds of precious jewels from within the water.
If one bathes cleanly and anoints the body with medicinal ointments,
then upon entering the fray to fight in battle, one will not be harmed and shall achieve victory.
If one carries this medicine to the royal palace,
the king, queen, and consorts will all rejoice upon seeing it.
If one applies this medicine to the eyes and goes to a village, [the same shall occur].
Those who see him will rejoice, love, and respect him, providing offerings of food and drink.
If one applies medicine to the index finger of the right hand and empowers it by reciting the mantra of the Wrathful King, [the desired result will be achieved].
If one fixes the gaze upon the ten directions with eyes wide in wrathful intent,
one shall obtain a square or circular area of one *yojana* where there will be no untimely calamities of wind, hail, or rain to damage the crops.
If there is persistent rain, apply medicinal ointment to the left hand,
recite the mantra of the Wrathful King to empower the left hand,
and brandish it throughout the ten directions; the rain will then clear and cease.
If there is a severe drought among the heavens,
one should apply medicinal ointment to the palm and fingers of the right hand;
having empowered the hand with mantras, one strikes the surface of the dragon pool with it.
After seven days have passed, a great rain will surely fall. If it does not rain,
one should again thoroughly smear the medicine over both hands.
With one mantra, clap the hands once and strike the water thirty-seven times;
the dragons and other beings within the pool will instantly become feverish and distressed.
If it does not rain, [the following shall be done].
Furthermore, smear the medicine thoroughly over the hands once more.
Recite the mantra once and strike the water with the hand one hundred and eight times; then a great rain will fall.
If it does not rain, the Nāga King within the pool and his retinue will all suffer from the affliction of heat and distress and flee from the outer pool. Furthermore,
for those suffering from various demonic illnesses or spirit illnesses, if one administers medicine and applies it to their eyes, they shall be cured.
If one suffers from any kind of fever caused by ghosts or spirits,
applying this medicine to the forehead will bring immediate recovery.
If the illness is difficult to treat, mix the medicine with warm water.
If a sick person bathes their body, they will be healed.
If one has been stung by a snake or a scorpion,
[one should] mix the medicine with water.
If one applies it as a medicinal plaster, the ailment will be cured.
For those suffering from abdominal tumors, chronic nodules, hemorrhoids, dysentery, or other diseases within the abdomen,
if the medicine is mixed with warm water and administered for drinking, they shall be healed and restored to health.
If one smears [the ointment] on the soles of the feet, fire will not burn them;
if one smears it on both shoulders, the upper arms, and the thighs,
one will obtain strength equal to that of a great wild elephant.
If one competes in strength with another, one will prevail over them.
Furthermore, if one applies medicinal ointment to both shins and palms,
one may cross rivers and seas without the water reaching the ankles.
If one applies this medicine to the crown of the head and enters marshes, lakes, mountain forests,
or places frequented by snakes, tigers, spirits, and the like, one will have no fear of such dangers;
all medicinal essences will manifest simultaneously.
Take whichever one is superior.
If you are in a mountain forest where medicinal herbs grow,
recite the mantra of the Greatly Terrifying Vidyārāja Aṅkuśa seven times with a loud voice.
The palaces of all the medicinal goddesses opened and appeared;
the medicinal goddesses manifested themselves to attend to his life-sustaining needs and brought forth the most supreme medicines.
Upon seeing the various medicinal deities (*oṣadhī-devatā*), one should not feel fear, but should instead employ them for service.
If one applies the medicine to the heart center and recites the mantra while performing the ritual, one will swiftly attain accomplishment (*siddhi*).
If one applies this medicine to the abdomen, flanks, spine, ears, fingers, or wrists,
then wherever one goes, food, drink, clothing, bedding, beads, earrings, bracelets, and riding mounts will all be provided according to one's wishes.
If one prepares medicinal honey pills the size of beans or similar,
reciting the Secret Heart Mantra to empower the medicine each day—
one pill on the first day, two on the second, three on the third, and so on up to seven pills on the seventh— this shall be the measure; continue this for a full hundred days.
His eloquence in speech and wisdom in exposition were unimpeded.
His voice was harmonious and refined, like the sound of the kinnaras or the kalaviṅka bird;
its tone was deep and resonant, causing all who heard it to rejoice.
If a woman who has not yet conceived takes this medicine mixed with ghee,
she will obtain a fetus;
if a person is imprisoned, shackled, or confined behind bars, [they shall be released].
If one applies medicinal ointment to the gates of hell as well as to the shackles and fetters,
and empowers them by reciting and upholding the mantra,
one will attain liberation.
If one bathes with medicinal herbs mixed with fragrant water until it is pure and performs the ritual while reciting and upholding the mantra, then all offenses—
such as the ten evil deeds, the five heinous crimes, and the four grave transgressions— will be completely eradicated.
Furthermore, one shall swiftly achieve accomplishment in the Samādhi of the Mudrās of the Secret Maṇḍala of King Amogha.
All hostile obstacles and inauspicious signs shall likewise be extinguished.
If one mixes medicinal herbs with raw sesame oil and applies it to the forehead or the eyes,
then upon seeing various persons of high status, they will all regard them with reverence and admiration.
If one anoints the body with it, one will not be harmed by swords, arrows, spears, or lances.
If the medicine is bound to both arms,
wherever one goes, one will receive the highest respect from the multitude.
If one stands on a high vantage point and gazes from afar at a town, city,
or village while reciting the mantra of the Great Vidyārāja Aṅkuśa,
one should empower the right hand by grasping white mustard seeds.
If one scatters it toward them, they shall naturally submit with reverence.
If one binds it to the right hand and strikes upon the doors of all treasuries containing gold, silver, and wealth, [they shall open].
The doors of the kitchen, storehouses, and medicine shops were all filled with malevolent spirits and ghosts who fled in terror;
yet they did not cause any depletion or loss of any wealth or treasures.
Nor does it steal or inhale any of their vital essence or flavors.
If one strikes the main gate seven times with the hand used for medicine,
all calamities and obstructions within the household will be eliminated.
If this medicine is buried in the ground at the gate of an enemy’s house,
that enemy’s family will naturally become harmonious and respectful.
If this medicine is smeared upon swords, arrows, spears, or halberds, they shall spontaneously break and shatter.
If one fears evil bandits or various calamities,
by burying the medicine at the threshold of the house,
those evil bandits will be unable to do any harm.
Calamities will be eliminated.
If one applies medicine inside a conch shell and blows it seven times from atop a high tower or pavilion, [the same result shall follow].
It can cause all strife, contentious speech, sorcery, incantations, and worldly calamities and portents to be completely extinguished.
This applies even to places where milk is sold or where cattle and sheep are penned.
As for blowing the seven notes:
the milk of both cattle and sheep will possess the supreme flavor.
If one blows the seven notes before a great assembly, [the same result follows].
Whatever the people hear shall eliminate all calamities and obstacles.
If medicinal substances are smeared upon the surface of a drum and it is struck with great force from atop a high tower, its sound will resound.
Then it shall cause all untimely hail and rain to be completely prohibited,
and all pestilential diseases shall be eradicated.
If one burns firewood and consumes the ashes from within a brazier, [the same result follows].
Recite the incense-water mantra seven times;
by sprinkling it throughout the ten directions, the boundary is established.
If one mixes ash with hot water for a communal bath, [the same effect is achieved].
All calamities, transgressions, and obstacles shall be eliminated.
If one suffers from malaria,
applying ashes upon the forehead will immediately bring about a cure.
If one applies ashes to the cangue, shackles, pillory,
or fetters and empowers them by reciting the mantra,
one shall attain liberation.
If one is bitten by a snake, one should apply ash over the wound;
the poisonous pain will then be removed. O World-Honored One, this is the *śāntika* samaya:
[use] the wood of *duzhong*, *mumuqie*, *shami*, cypress, mulberry, *gou*, and *yehe*.
Cut [the wood] into pieces twelve finger-widths long;
purify them with the fivefold ritual bathing and empower them.
Recite the mantra over them according to the prescribed number and kindle the fire while maintaining the empowerment.
Recite the mantra of the Wrathful King (*krodharāja*).
Purify with water and fire, and bind the boundary (*sīmābandha*) by forming the wheel-seal (*cakramudrā*).
Kneeling to the south of the hearth, recite the Mother Dhāraṇī and the Secret Heart Mantra.
If one consecrates rice grains, white mustard seeds, lotus stalks and leaves, clarified butter, and honey,
performing one thousand and eight *homa* offerings,
one will obtain [a realm] extending for one hundred *yojana*s in both length and breadth.
It wards off yakṣas, rākṣasas, bhūtas, piśācas, and spirits that devour vital energy;
furthermore, it eliminates all calamities, epidemics, famines, and fierce beasts.
May there be no rebellion by enemy troops or treachery by ministers;
may all strife and malevolent spirits be pacified;
and may the land be bountiful, with rains falling in their proper seasons to nourish all crops, flowers, and fruits.
All trees, great and small— roots, stems, branches, leaves, and various types of medicinal herbs—
shall all flourish and abound in nourishment;
the people shall be happy and possess abundant wealth and treasures.
Free from all calamities and afflictions,
they will further praise and extol one another with mutual affection;
you should know that within the kingdom, no disasters shall be wrought by malevolent devas, nāgas, spirits, or ghosts.
These include the gods of the Four Heavenly Kings, Īśvara, Maheśvara,
Mahābrahmā, Śakra-devānām-indra, Nārāyaṇa, and Maheśvara.
Each leading immeasurable retinues and servants,
they shall constantly provide protection within a hundred yojanas, both inside and outside the kingdom,
increasing the physical strength and vitality of all sentient beings.
All Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the ten directions, including Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, shall protect and keep them in mind;
the sentient beings of that land shall all attain peace and security, like cherished children.

The Sun Deity, the Moon Deity, and the twenty-eight lunar mansions and planetary deities shall constantly remain within the kingdom, preventing calamities and portents, and bestowing their protective empowerment.
Chapter Eight: The Secret Empowerment. The World-Honored One is the Seal of the Samaya of the Vast Liberation Lotus Maṇḍala of the King of Amogha.
One will be able to extensively accomplish hundreds of thousands of siddhis and samayas;
one will move all things and shall behold hundreds of thousands of koṭis of buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Gaṅgā.
Accumulating merit and cultivating Buddha-works,
Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva bestows infinite protection through his illusory transformations and supernormal powers upon those who,
with faith and understanding, receive, uphold, read, and recite this Āmoghapaśa-rāja-samaya.
One should give rise to great compassion for sentient beings and,
out of pity for all, cultivate and purify this dharma on the eighth or fifteenth day of the waxing moon.
In a secluded and pure place, bathe thoroughly,
wear clean garments, and consume the three white foods.
Construct a ritual altar according to the Dharma, ensuring that no aspect of the majestic deportment is deficient.
They completely sever all discursive speech,
or else they practice the Dharma by divining and examining all auspicious signs both internal and external.
Then one shall attain accomplishment.
This great sūtra contains the mantras and methods for both mundane and supramundane accomplishments.
If it is a layperson, they should daily observe the eightfold precepts of the fast.
Construct a square altar measuring four cubits, purifying it thoroughly.
Mix cow dung with scented water and yellow clay to coat,
rub, and polish the surface, opening wide the four gates.
Delimit the boundaries of the mandala using powdered white conch shell;
within it, draw a blooming lotus flower with one hundred and eight petals,
using white sandalwood incense paste for the petals.
A platform shall be made of saffron paste.
On its four sides and four corners, one should depict lotus flowers in full bloom made from fragrant paste.
Yellow silk banners and flowers should be arranged and displayed all around.
To the east, place an image of Avalokiteśvara with the Amoghapāśa;
at the four corners, place incense-filled water vases containing white mustard seeds.
All branches, twigs, leaves, and flowers are inserted into the mouth [of the vessel].
At the four gates, arghya perfumed water is placed,
with flowers floating upon the surface of the water.
Incense the King of Fragrance;
throughout the six periods of day and night, perform the invocation and the boundary-binding,
and visualize all Buddhas of the ten directions as being present.
Various kinds of light were emitted, illuminating and refreshing body and mind;
pure, clear, and bright, one saw without obstruction.
At that moment, they prostrated themselves and paid homage to Avalokiteśvara.
Perform the offering of argha, repentance, and taking refuge;
arouse the bodhicitta, make the invocation, and dedicate the merit.
Prostrate, form the mudrās, and visualize yourself [as the deity].
Its intrinsic nature is equal and its measure is coextensive with the *dharmadhātu*.
It is beyond the measure of differentiation and the measure of non-differentiation.

One should contemplate all the Buddhas and Tathāgatas surrounded by all the Bodhisattvas, abiding in the state of tranquil contemplation, adorned with the syllable *raṃ*—complete with its bindu—blazing like a garland of radiant sunbeams.
Contemplate the true meaning of the syllable *nam*:
that the intrinsic nature of all phenomena is unstained, free from all dust and defilement, and is the naturally pure ground of mind;
it is the site for purifying the path, removing all impurities and filth.
Just as the characteristic of space forms the vajra-ground,
one visualizes below it the wind-circle (vāyu-maṇḍala), upon which is the syllable HAḤ,
emitting black light and flames.
One contemplates that upon the wind-wheel there is a water-wheel, its color like snow or milk;
within it is the syllable *ba*, as clear and pure as crystal or the light of the moon.
Visualize upon the lunar disc the great Maitreya-vajracakra maṇḍala,
emitting golden light and flames.
Above, visualize that the syllable *Sra* transforms into an eight-petaled lotus flower that opens of its own accord.
Its stalk is made of vajra with a pedestal of various precious jewels;
it emits immeasurable light and is surrounded on all sides by immeasurable hundreds of thousands of jewel lotuses.
Upon the platform was set a precious lion throne,
surrounded on all sides by various jeweled poles and pillars,
atop which were placed diverse ornate canopies, banners, and streamers.
Hanging pearl necklaces and garlands, and various exquisite jewel garments;
spreading everywhere all kinds of incense, flowers, and jewels;
giving rise to clouds of wondrous fragrance and raining down various miscellaneous blossoms.
The ground was strewn with profuse offerings,
as various extraordinary musical instruments were played,
and various wish-fulfilling jars and *argha* water were extensively distributed.
The branches and leaves of the mani-jewel trees were spread with radiant light,
arranged in rows all around, shining as lamps.
Each was adorned with the pure and perfect radiance of the Buddha’s pāramitās, offering praise.
The profound words and meanings of all bodhisattvas,
with Brahma-sounds clear and resonant, pervade the infinite realms;
by my own power and through the Buddha’s sustaining power.
By the power of the dharma-realm, one contemplates abiding in making offerings;
all phenomena are unarisen by nature and are quiescent from the very beginning.
This is the lion throne.
Above, one visualizes the syllable VAṂ,
which is Śākyamuni Tathāgata,
his body the color of pure gold, seated in the full lotus posture.
Adorned with crowns, robes, and pendants,
they emit wondrous light that pervades boundless realms;
an inexhaustible assembly of noble ones appears within the midst of these blazing flames.
Its light pervades the entire realm of sentient beings,
emitting wheels of radiant flames according to their individual dispositions to bring them understanding;
the body and speech of this Buddha-Tathāgata are immeasurable.
It abides eternally through the three periods of time, serene and imperishable.
From within this body, it manifests immeasurable bodies;
it unites these immeasurable bodies into the single body of a Buddha.
To the right, one beholds Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva;
to the left, one beholds Vajrapāṇi Guhyapati Bodhisattva, surrounded before and behind by the assembly of great bodhisattvas of various lineages,
all seated in the lotus posture.
As for the practitioner of the *Sīta Avalokiteśvara* mantra, they sit with their mind focused on the visualization without distraction.
If the mind becomes distracted, all the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, mantras, vidyās, and deities, as well as the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, [will respond].
Since there is nothing to be empowered and nothing to be observed or protected,
the wise one should accordingly sit upon the Dharma-seat,
observing the seal of the recitation and mindfulness of the Noble One.
With the left hand, join the index finger and thumb together and extend them straight;
form a fist with the middle, ring, and little fingers tucked toward the palm.
Place this mudrā at the chest.
With the index, middle, and thumb fingers of the right hand, one should hold the beads.
With the sound of the *samādhi* of the empowerment of the vajra-maṇi body of all Tathāgatas,
one should recite and maintain the Mother Dhāraṇī mantra, the Secret Heart mantra, and the Wrathful King mantra.
Contemplate the dhāraṇī-mantra of the Arrayed Contemplations;
each syllable and sound takes the form of a noble being,
encircled by blazing light.
Its pure radiance shatters the abode of ignorance.
At that time, without interval,
the earth beneath the mandala shall tremble at midnight.
Forming mudrās and calming the mind, one should gaze directly at the feet of the image and recite the mantra of the Wrathful King,
causing the ground of the mandala to tremble and shake violently.
The Bodhisattva emitted a great radiance from between his eyebrows,
which illuminated and shone throughout the maṇḍala;
at that time, the body of the mantra-practitioner trembled and his hair stood on end.
One should simply give rise extensively to the great bodhicitta and gaze upward at the face of the image; there,
one will see its right side turn as the eyes look toward the reciter of the mantra.
A great Brahma-voice issued forth, praising the mantra-reciter:
"You have realized this sign of the purification of the three karmas;
furthermore, you shall serve hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Tathāgatas, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges."
Planting roots of goodness,
all bodhisattvas together observe the physical and mental well-being [of others],
and contemplate their future places of birth after they have relinquished this body.
His physical form was upright and graceful, his hair curled like a spiral conch;
his voice was exquisite and his eyes were wide, noble, and majestic.
His mind was liberated and luminously pure, and his vision of the Dharma was pristine.
Forever eliminating ignorance— the root of all suffering such as birth, old age, sickness, and death—
he realized the samādhi of the pure-nature contemplation of all sentient beings.
At the time of the fifth watch, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara appeared before him and touched his head with his hand.
Furthermore, all the great mundane and supramundane aspirations that are sought shall be fully satisfied.
At that time, the practitioner of mantras—
I pray for the divine power of the feet;
I pray for the vow of the secret rishi;
I pray for the divine power of the celestial eye.
The vow for beholding the Buddha-fields;
the vow for realizing the great accomplishment of dhāraṇī;
and the Amoghapāśa vow.
The vow to realize the various meanings of all sūtras;
the vow for the great accomplishment of all mantras and samādhis;
and the vow of dhāraṇīs and vidyās.
The aspiration for all eloquence;
the aspiration to take up hidden treasures; the aspiration to produce gold and silver;
and the aspiration for the arts and crafts.
The vow to go to the celestial palaces;
the vow to enter the caves of the asuras;
the vow to enter the palaces of the nāgas.
The vow for the increase of crops and the abundance of fruits;
the vow for the subjugation of yakṣas and rākṣasas;
and the vow for the restoration of former friends.
The vow to enter mountain valleys to gather the essences of various medicinal herbs;
the vow for the accomplishment of the method of becoming a sword-ascetic who soars through the air;
and the vow of the Great Mantra-Adept.
The vow to subdue all evil people of wrong views;
the vow concerning objects of mockery;
and the vow to enter the waters of the ocean.
May all worldly dharmas fulfill their vows;
may the four grave offenses and the five heinous crimes, along with all transgressions, be extinguished.
May such vows as these be granted according to whatever is requested.
All shall be fully satisfied.
If one constantly recites and maintains [this practice] throughout the six periods of the day without interruption,
one will further attain the samādhi of observing all sentient beings as free from hindrances and pure.
The Samādhi of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva’s Manifestation of Supernatural Powers and Transcendent Observation;
the Samādhi of the Secret Adornment Radiance and Supernatural Powers of the Observation and Empowerment of All Tathāgatas.
By the power of this samādhi,
one perceives the long lifespans of the Great Brahmā Heaven,
as well as all the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Mahāsattvas within the pure lands.
Before Amitābha Buddha,
they praise and inquire about the profound Dharma,
sitting together upon the platforms and pavilions of a pure lotus-flower palace of radiant jewels.
If, on the eighth and fifteenth days of the bright fortnight,
one abstains from food for the entire day and night, refrains from all speech,
and recites and maintains the Mother Dhāraṇī mantra and the Secret Heart mantra;
Then all beginningless karmic obstructions will be completely extinguished.
After the end of this life, one shall attain rebirth in the Land of Peace and Bliss,
where one will constantly behold all the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Mahāsattvas.
For those who perform the ritual by consecrating the water in the *argha* vases within the empowered maṇḍala, bathing the body, and sealing the body with mudrās,
they shall attain a vajra-body free from affliction and decay.
All Tathāgatas constantly and joyfully observe it;
all devas, nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, and vināyakas subdue it with reverence.
It accomplishes the dharmas of mundane siddhi.
Entrusted as a Messenger and Protector.
*Amoghapāśakalparāja-nāma-mahāyānasūtra*, Scroll Seven.
*Amoghapāśakalparāja-nāma-mahāyānasūtra*, Scroll Eight.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Bodhiruci of Central India during the Great Tang Dynasty. Chapter Nine: The Three Samaya Images.
World-Honored One, if there are bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās who possess pure faith...
Those who wish to be liberated from all realms of existence— the realms of nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, asuras, hell-beings, pretas, and animals—
should practice the samaya of the mantra of the Heart-King Mother Dhāraṇī, Amoghapāśa.
The vast liberation lotus maṇḍala seal samaya;
the samādhi of the wisdom-adornment of the three samayas for the accomplishment of the image of Avalokiteśvara with the Amoghapāśa.
A pure gold image, fashioned according to the ritual rules,
with three faces and six arms;
the front face is serene and smiling.
The left face has a frowning brow and bulging eyes, with its mouth agape and canine teeth protruding;
the right face has a frowning brow and bulging eyes, with its mouth closed.
On his head he wears a jeweled crown, within which is a transformation Buddha.
One hand holds a lotus, one hand holds a noose, one hand grasps a trident;
one hand holds a flask, one hand bestows fearlessness, and one hand raises its palm.
He sat in the full lotus posture upon a lotus throne.
That throne was atop a mountain,
adorned with various celestial garments, precious necklaces, and jeweled bracelets.
Having filled the hollow interior of the image with powdered white sandalwood and camphor mixed with the Buddha’s relics,
place them within the belly of the image;
then, on the left side of the image, the practitioner of mantras shall perform the rite.
Kneeling upright, he sat with his hands holding an incense burner, gazing up at the image.
One who upholds this Dharma should give rise to great compassion for sentient beings and resolve to attain bodhicitta.
One who creates such an image of Avalokiteśvara of the Amoghapāśa will attain immeasurable roots of goodness for awakening;
how much more so for one who extensively and fully cultivates this dharma.
Yet they shall not attain the supreme great accomplishment.
World-Honored One, such persons shall behold eighty-eight hundred-thousand-koṭi-nayuta-gaṅgā-sand numbers of Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas.
Reverently making offerings and planting various roots of goodness,
one eliminates the ten evil deeds, the five heinous crimes, and the four grave offenses;
one purifies the body and clothing and partakes of the three white foods.
Consecrate pure water with mantras and sprinkle it over the body.
Perform the ritual according to the Dharma and construct a maṇḍala according to one’s inclination.
Smear the interior of the maṇḍala with a paste of pure saffron.
Using vermilion, one should draw two cubits of a blossoming lotus with one hundred and eight petals.
Furthermore, surrounding the lotus, one should paint a garland of lotuses,
interlacing them to mark the boundaries and paths.
Upon the lotus pedestal is a high seat of yellow silk;
upon this seat, place the image facing west.
On a yellow *argha* vessel, fill it with white sandalwood and saffron water.
Place it before the seat.
One should coil the rosary and place it atop the vase.
Place vases of incense at the four corners.
Place argha water at each of the four gates,
with flowers floating upon the water.
At each of the four gates and at the center of the mandala, place an incense burner and burn the king of incenses.
One should arrange offerings of exquisite fragrant flowers and the three white foods;
on all four sides, one should set out rows of ghee lamps and oil lamps.
The mantra-holder should place his mind within the [deity’s] mind.
Contemplate one's own mind as the samādhi of the vast, born, and supremely sublime five-pronged vajra produced by all the Buddhas and Tathāgatas.
Emitting golden light that illuminates and melts away all various fetters and protections,
recite the mantra of the Wrathful King.

empower a piece of *śrīparṇī* wood smeared with clarified butter and perform one thousand and eight *homa* offerings; the cave door will open of its own accord, and one may enter without obstruction.
If one is in the deep mountains,
one should perform a homa ritual one thousand and eight times using *kumuda* flowers, *tagara* powder, white mustard seeds, and clarified butter, empowered through mantra-recitation (*adhitiṣṭhati*).
The essences of those various medicinal herbs will manifest in bodily form and present themselves for collection.
Furthermore, empower a wood-apple (*kapittha*) branch, trim it, and kindle it as a fire;
likewise, empower black pepper and clarified butter (*ghṛta*).
If one performs the homa ritual one thousand and eight times,
the Great Brahmā, Śakra Devendra, Nārāyaṇa, and Maheśvara will manifest their bodies to protect and mindfully attend to the practitioner.
Upon seeing them, whatever vows one requests shall all be fully fulfilled.
Furthermore, by consecrating *sumana* flowers, *karnikāra* flowers, *utpala* flowers, and clarified butter (*ghṛta*),
and performing one thousand and eight *homa* offerings,
the deity of the sun and the deity of the moon will both appear before one at that same time.
Emitting great light, he illuminates, protects, and bestows empowerment, thereby attaining great supernormal powers (*abhijñā*).
Furthermore, one should empower a soapberry wood stick, trim it, and kindle it as a fire.
One should also empower cumin seeds, *tianshengdong* (asparagus), powdered *sufangmu* (caesalpinia sappan), powdered white sandalwood, white mustard seeds, barley, and cow’s ghee.
Perform the homa for seven days;
one will cause all obstacles and sufferings of the kṣatriya royal lineage and their attendants to be completely removed.
Furthermore, empower white mustard seeds, non-glutinous rice, and ginger roots.
Performing the homa one thousand times,
one will obtain the protection of all yakṣas and rākṣasas, who will become submissive and obedient.
Regarding such methods as these, whatever one wishes to perform—
One should form both the Amoghapāśa mudrā and the Krodharāja mudrā,
and recite the Mother Dhāraṇī mantra and the Secret Heart mantra.
If the Krodharāja mantras are used alternately in pairs, one will attain accomplishment.
Chapter Eleven: The Pure and Stainless Lotus King. The World-Honored One is the Samaya of the Form of Amogharāja.
It should be drawn upon white cotton cloth, fine linen, or silk,
measuring four cubits square or eight cubits square.
While the painter is drawing, he must bathe once for every stroke made.
Anoint the body with incense and don clean garments;
partake of the three white foods, remain silent and abstain from speech, and observe the eight precepts of purification.
Ensure that the cups, brushes, and pigments are all clean and of excellent quality.
Do not use leather glue to mix the pigments.
In the center, depict Mount Potalaka made of the seven treasures;
its mid-slope should resemble the mid-slope of Mount Sumeru.
The mountain peak has nine peaks resembling lotus flowers, the central one of which is shaped like a lotus pedestal.
Upon the mountain, one should depict various jewel trees, flowers, fruits, and all kinds of medicinal herbs.
In the waters of the great ocean at the foot of the mountain, there are various kinds of fish, beasts, and water birds.
In the center of this [ocean] is a palace made of the seven treasures, adorned with all manner of ornaments;
the floor of that palace is composed of many precious gems.
Within the hall is a precious lotus lion throne,
upon which sits the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara with the Amoghapāśa,
having one face, three eyes, and eighteen arms; his body is the color of pure gold, he sits in the full lotus posture, and his countenance is serene and joyful.
On his head he wears a jeweled crown upon which resides an emanation Buddha.
His two hands are joined in *añjali* at his chest;
his other two hands are joined in *añjali* and hang downward at his navel.
With both thumbs doubled back within the palms,
join the wrists beneath the centers of the two hands;
the five fingers of the left hand are each slightly spread and bent, resembling an opening lotus flower.
Press the tips of the right thumb and middle finger together;
let the index, ring, and little fingers be slightly extended and bent.
Form the pāśa-mudrā (noose seal) with both hands below the navel.
With one hand he holds a trident;
with another hand he grasps a jeweled banner;
and with another hand he holds an opened lotus flower.
In one hand he holds an unfailing lotus scripture;
in another hand he grasps a noose;
and in another hand he holds a vajra hook.
One hand bestows fearlessness;
one hand holds a kunda;
one hand holds a precious vase.
In one hand he holds a precious flower-disk;
he wears a garment of deerskin,
as well as necklaces of the seven jewels, celestial robes, and precious bead bracelets and armlets.
Adorned with ornaments and a body radiating flames,
he holds the Amoghapāśa; to his right is the Bodhisattva Tārā.
The left hand, with its palm facing upward below the navel, holds a blue utpala flower;
the right hand has its palm raised.
With the head slightly tilted to one side, he sits in the half-lotus posture.
Behind him is the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara of the *Vikūṭi* [type],
with a single eye between his eyebrows and four arms;
one hand holds an open lotus flower, and another hand grasps a water-pitcher (*kamaṇḍalu*).
With one hand at the navel with the palm facing upward and the other hand holding a rosary,
he sits in the half-lotus posture.
Behind him is the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara of Great White Body.
The left hand holds open a lotus flower;
the right hand is held with the palm facing upward below the navel;
he sits in the half-lotus posture.
The messenger who follows behind has a blue body,
is wrathful, with canine fangs protruding upward;
he wears a skull upon his head and possesses eight arms, half of which are raised.
The left hands hold a three-pronged vajra, a blue lotus,
and a trident, while one hand has its palm raised;
the right hands hold a sword and a battle-axe.
Holding a curved knife in one hand and a noose in the other,
he gazes up at the Bodhisattva;
this is Amoghapāśa Avalokiteśvara on the left.
The Bodhisattva Vimalamati sits in the half-lotus posture (ardhaparyaṅka), holding a lotus flower in his left hand and raising his palm with his right hand.
Following this is the mantra practitioner.
Kneeling on his heels, he gazes upward while holding an incense burner in his hand.
Behind him is Acala-krodharāja (the Wrathful King),
whose face is contorted with rage and who has four arms.
With one hand he holds a noose, with another a sword;
with one hand he rests a trident, and with another he holds a lotus.
He sits in the half-lotus posture, his hair coiled like a spiral shell.
Behind her is the white-robed Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvarī Mātṛkā.
Her left hand rests upon her hip with the palm facing upward,
holding a lotus flower that she does not open.
With her right hand raised in a palm-facing-outward gesture, she sits in the half-lotus posture.
Behind her is a single-tufted rākṣasī messenger with a blue body,
wrathful, adorned with snake necklaces, and fangs protruding.
He wears a crown of skulls with half of them protruding, and possesses six arms:
the left hands hold a three-pronged vajra, a lotus, and a noose;
the right hands hold a battle-axe.
One holds a vajra staff and one holds a trident;
they gaze up at the Bodhisattva.
To the left, beneath the seat of Amoghapāśa Avalokiteśvara, [are these two].
He stands with his feet placed wide apart;
he holds a three-pronged vajra in his left hand,
while his right hand is raised with the palm facing outward at the side of his chest.
He sat in the full lotus posture.
Subsequently, there were the mantra-vidyādhara Āṭavika and the mantra-vidyādhara Bhṛṅgin.
The vidyādhara mantra-sages of Nīlaśa each held flowers in their hands and sat in a long-kneeling posture upon lotus leaves.
Beholding and making offerings,
to the right of the seat of Avalokiteśvara with the Amoghapāśa,

With his left hand he holds a single-pronged vajra,
and with his right hand he grasps a white fly-whisk;
he sits in the full lotus posture.
The Vidyādhara-mantra-siddha Kūṣmāṇḍa;
the Vidyādhara-mantra-siddha Śukra;
and the Vidyādhara-mantra-siddha Brahmā.
Each holding a flower in their hand,
they knelt upright upon lotus leaves and gazed up in worshipful offering.
Those bodhisattvas had joyful and serene countenances and sat upon lotus seats;
they were adorned with crowns, necklaces, and bracelets made of the seven precious gems,

On the left side of the mountain peak outside the palace,
one should place Śakra-devendra, Virūḍhaka, Vāsava, Vemacitrin, the earth deities, and the deities of crops.
He sits in the half-lotus posture.
On the right peak of the mountain outside his palace,
he places Mahābrahmā, Śrīdevī, Sarasvatī, Varuṇa, and Yama-rāja.
He sits in the half-lotus posture.
At the midpoint of the mountain, on both the left and right sides,
the Four Heavenly Kings are stationed, each holding their respective weapons and sitting in the half-lotus posture.
Adorned with various exquisite garments and armor,
he stationed hosts of ascetic sages on the upper left and right sides outside the palace.
With a body emaciated and thin, he displays a gesture of praise.
To the upper right outside the palace,
place the Sun Deity (Sūrya).
Afterwards, the Śuddhāvāsa devaputra and the devaputra Īśvara made offerings of flowers.
To the upper left outside the palace,
the Moon Devaputra was placed.
Thereafter, the devaputra Mahesvara and the various other devaputras offered flowers as worship;
they also presented celestial rishis' flower garlands and garments.
Adorned with various kinds of precious pearl necklaces,
the palace rises straight upward,
wherein are placed Amitābha Buddha, Śākyamuni Buddha, and the Tathāgata Lokarāja.
Manifesting the appearance of preaching the Dharma, he sat cross-legged upon a precious lion throne, mounted on clouds of various colors.
Upon that great ocean shore, there arose mountains of the seven treasures,
and upon these mountains were various jewel trees with flowers and fruits.
Upon those various trees were vines, branches, flowers, and leaves of manifold colors.
Among the mountains there were also ponds,
pools, rivers, and streams, within which grew lotuses, kumudas, puṇḍarikas, and utpalas.
Upon the mountain there are also lions, white elephants, all kinds of birds and beasts, as well as kumbhāṇḍas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, and so forth.
Encircling its base are five empty caves.
On the left and right sides of the mountains at the edge of the sea,
there are five small peaks made of the seven precious substances;
upon each of these five peaks, a nāga king is stationed.
He resembles a celestial deity;
from his head emerge snake heads— one, three, five, seven, and nine snake heads respectively.
Each holding a precious flower, they sat in the half-lotus posture, gazing up with reverence and making offerings.
The small mountains on the four sides were adorned in various ways;
this image is the assembly within the precious palace of Mount Potalaka.
The body of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara Amoghapāśa:
if there are sentient beings whose faith is pure who gaze upon him for even a moment, it is as if they were seeing me.
One shall attain the extinction of all defilements, obscurations, and grave offenses;
how much more so for sentient beings who have cultivated purity and upheld the precepts in past lives,
who constantly delight in making offerings and reciting the mantra while holding my name?
In this present life, there is no fruit that will not be obtained;
this is the true Dharma of Suchness, which should be revered and made offerings to.
Those who cultivate this Dharma—
Then one should serve sixty-four hundred thousand koṭi-nayuta Ganges-sand-like Tathāgatas,
planting roots of merit that reach maturity and correspondence.
I shall constantly manifest before you in dreams and waking states,
bestowing the samaya of the King of All Dharmas’ Non-empty Vows;
in every thought-moment, may calamities be extinguished for hundreds of thousands of millions of kalpas.
Regarding the five deeds of immediate retribution and all other grave offenses,
if there are sentient beings who joyfully prostrate and recite my name,
I too shall remember them, look upon them with grace, and protect them.
If there are sentient beings who are emaciated, exhausted, and gravely afflicted,
they should constantly gaze upward and keep my name in mind;
thus, even they shall eliminate the clouds of karma from birth and death.
If any birds, beasts, or sentient beings of the animal realm see this image,
they shall cast off this body and be reborn in the heavens.
Whether in temples, royal palaces, cities, towns, villages, or the private residences of commoners— wherever [this image is placed]— it shall bring about such results.
If there are various calamities, fears, afflictions, or states of unrest,
one should then welcome and invite this image into one's home with banners, flowers, various musical sounds, and medicinal herbs.
Purify and adorn the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa).
Smear the ground with fragrant mud, suspend various banners and flowers, and install the image. Offer various flowers, incense, fruits, ghee, milk, food, and drink.
By making offerings and presenting gifts, reciting and upholding mantras,
performing the rites of purification (*saṃskāra*), and conducting *homa* rituals,
one shall extinguish all calamitous stars and portents of misfortune.
The yakṣas, rākṣasas, bhūtas, piśācas, and kumbhāṇḍas shall all be dispersed and extinguished;
the inhabitants of the house shall be at peace, and the crops shall be abundant.
The sentient beings herein shall all attain roots of goodness corresponding to the six pāramitās.
After casting off their bodies, they will be reborn within lotus flowers in the Western Pure Land,
where they will behold Amitābha Buddha and all the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.

Whether in a garden or by the edge of a lotus pond,

fill it with pure earth to level the ground,
and construct a foundation one cubit deep, smoothing and leveling the surface.
One should prepare and adorn the ground of the maṇḍala with cow dung, scented water, and yellow earth,
and mark out the boundary lines with five-colored thread.
He opened wide the courtyard of the realm and the paths of the various jewel realms:

With the left hand held against the chest, grasp the corner of the *kāṣāya*;

Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva holds a precious seal upon a lotus pedestal in his left hand,

Next is the Bodhisattva Ratnākara,

Next is the Bodhisattva Ratnapāṇi.
With his left hand, he holds a precious three-pronged vajra atop a lotus pedestal;
with his right hand, he rests his palm upon his thigh.
He sits in the half-lotus posture (*ardhaparyaṅka*).
Next is the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha.
His left hand holds a lotus pedestal upon which stands a single-pronged vajra;
his right hand has its palm facing upward.
He sits in the half-lotus posture.
Next is the Bodhisattva Vajra,
who holds in his left hand a five-pronged precious vajra atop a lotus pedestal.
With his right hand raised in the gesture of the open palm,
he sits in the half-lotus posture.
Next is the Bodhisattva Dṛḍhamati.
With his left hand, he holds a precious ten-spoked, three-pronged vajra atop a lotus pedestal;
his right hand is extended upward across his thigh as he sits in the half-lotus posture (*ardhaparyaṅka*).
Next is the Bodhisattva Ākāśavimala.
His left hand holds a lotus pedestal upon which a sword is upright;
his right hand raises its palm.
He sits in the half-lotus posture.
Next is the Bodhisattva Ākāśamati,
whose left hand holds a lotus pedestal upon which a wheel is erected upright.
With his right hand raised in the gesture of holding a maṇi jewel,
he sits in the half-lotus posture.
Next is the Bodhisattva Viśuddhamati.
The left hand holds a lotus pedestal upon which a conch is upright;
the right hand has its palm raised.
He sits in the half-lotus posture.
Next is the Bodhisattva Cāritramati.
His left hand holds an opened lotus flower,
and his right hand forms an empty fist pressed against his chest.
Sitting in the half-lotus posture,
facing west, the first from the south is the Bodhisattva Vajra Mahābhayānayanī.
The left hand holds a vajra; the right hand is raised with the palm facing outward;
he sits in the half-lotus posture.
Next is the Bodhisattva Hayagrīva Avalokiteśvara.
His left hand holds a battle-axe,
and his right hand grasps the stem and leaves of a lotus flower.
He sits in the half-lotus posture.
Next is the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara with a Thousand Hands and Thousand Eyes,
sitting in the full lotus posture.
Next is the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara of the Wish-Fulfilling Wheel (Cintāmaṇicakra).
His body has six arms:
one hand holds a wheel, one hand holds a rosary, and one hand holds a wish-fulfilling jewel.
With one hand supporting his right cheek, one hand holding a lotus, and one hand pressed upon the ground,
he sits in the full lotus posture (*paryaṅka*). Next is Vināyaka-vajra.
The left hand holds a vajra-axe,
and the right hand grasps a noose;
he sits in the half-lotus posture.
Next is the rākṣasa messenger Ekajaṭī,
whose body is a true blue color, with a face of wrathful expression and six arms.
The three left hands hold,
first, a three-pronged vajra, second, a lotus, and third, a noose. The three right hands hold,
first, a battle-axe, second, a vajra staff, and third, a trident.
He sits in the half-lotus posture (*ardhaparyaṅka*).
Beneath the falling axe, the *vināyaka* stands bowed in fear.
Next is the blue-necked Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.
The left hand holds a lotus flower;
the right hand raises its palm;
he sits in the full lotus position.
Next is the Eleven-faced Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva,
seated in the full lotus posture.
Next is the Vidyārāja Śveta-mahākāla.
His face is wrathful,
standing majestic and powerful like a vajra;
next is the messenger Padma-sunāri.
The left hand holds a battle-axe,
and the right hand grasps a lasso;
he sits in the half-lotus posture.
Next is the Bodhisattva Mahāśikhivajra.
His left hand holds a three-pronged vajra,
and his right hand is raised with the palm facing outward.
Sitting in the half-lotus posture,
facing north, the first from the west is the Messenger Acala.
The left hand holds a noose,
and the right hand holds a sword;
he sits in the half-lotus posture.

his two hands each hold a lotus flower,

his left hand holds a lotus flower,
and his right hand has its palm raised.

whose left hand rests sideways against his abdomen.

he sits in the half-lotus posture.
Next is the Bodhisattva Sitātapatrā Aparājitā Uṣṇīṣa.
The left hand holds the seal of a parasol atop a lotus pedestal;
the right hand raises its palm grasping a lotus flower.
He sits in the half-lotus posture.
Next is the Bodhisattva Jinaśirṣa;
his left hand holds a lotus pedestal upon which he displays the upright sword mudrā,
and his right hand holds a blue utpala flower.
He sits in the half-lotus posture.
Next is the Bodhisattva Prabhakūṭoṣṇīṣa;
his left hand holds a lotus pedestal upon which is the seal of the Buddha-uṣṇīṣa.
The right hand is placed against the chest;
he sits in the half-lotus posture.
Next is the Bodhisattva Uṣṇīṣavijaya.
With his left hand holding a lotus pedestal upon which he displays the upright wheel mudrā,
and with his right hand raised with the palm facing outward,
he sits in the half-lotus posture.
Next is the Bodhisattva Cūḍāmaṇi-vināśana (Cui-sui Foding).
His left hand holds a precious seal atop a lotus pedestal,
and his right hand has its palm raised.
He sits in the half-lotus posture.
Next is the Bodhisattva Anantabuddhoṣṇīṣa,
whose left hand holds a lotus flower.
Their right hands are raised with palms facing upward;
they sit in the half-lotus posture.
The countenances of these Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Mahāsattvas are serene and joyful.
Adorned with celestial garments, jeweled crowns, necklaces,
pearl earrings, bracelets, and various other ornaments,

At the four gates,
the deities of the Four Heavenly Kings hold swords and spears and sit in the half-lotus posture at the four corners;

Next, at the four gates and four corners of the inner court are the precious Sumeru mountains;
upon each mountain are the celestial palaces of the various devas.
All the devas, nāga kings, yakṣas, rākṣasas, bhūtas, pretas, and so forth [are depicted] on all the small mountains surrounding the four sides;
on each mountain, various jeweled trees with flowers and fruits are painted.
Upon the various trees there were parrots, śārikas, white cranes, peacocks, and *jīvamjīvaka* birds;
the necks of these birds were adorned with jeweled necklaces.
In the Lotus Garland realm of the inner court,

The mountain peaks follow one after another.
To the east of the maṇḍala,
place a painted image of Amogharāja.
There were various banners and flowers, golden and silver lotuses,
lotuses made of five-colored silken fabrics, and flower trees of various colored silks;
they were adorned both inside and out with five-colored lapis lazuli bubble-flowers.
One should use a golden vessel or a silver vessel,
filled to the brim with water scented with white sandalwood, aloeswood, and camphor,

Above, place a five-colored maṇi-jewel lasso.

Place it before Śākyamuni Buddha.

There are eight golden trays with the three white foods and drink,
and eight silver trays with various kinds of food, drink, fruits, and melons.
Sixty-four portions of the three white foods, various kinds of food, and melons and fruits were arranged both inside and out;
thirty-three types of incense were spread and offered;
and eight incense burners made of gold and copper were placed both inside and out, burning the king of incenses.
In the four cardinal and four intermediate directions of the outer courtyard,
place large copper basins filled with scented water and floating flowers;
in the inner courtyard, light eight wax candles.

however, with the sole exception of alcohol, meat, the five pungent vegetables, and all leftover food, leftover flowers, foul-smelling incense, or foul-smelling flowers.

Forming the initiation mudrā and pressing it upon the crown of the head,
one is empowered by the mantra and instructed in samādhi;
this person shall then be embraced and blessed by all the Tathāgatas of the ten directions.
One shall realize the samaya of the seal of the Maṇḍala of the Lotus King of Vast Liberation of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, the Unfailing Lasso;

One shall be liberated from the ten non-virtues, the five heinous crimes, and all karmic obstructions;
the three karmas will be purified, and one will attain merit, longevity, peace, and happiness,
as well as all mantra-vidyā-mantras, maṇḍalas, mudrās, and samayas of the Heaven of the Thirty-three.
The mantras, maṇḍalas, mudrās, and samayas of all the nāga kings;
the mantras, maṇḍalas, mudrās, and samayas of all the asura kings.
All the mantras, maṇḍalas, mudrās, and samayas of the yakṣa kings and rākṣasa kings shall be fully accomplished;
one will not be harmed by any celestial māras or followers of external paths.
If one seeks out ways to afflict, destroy, imprison, or subjugate others,
and if sentient beings thus mutually invade and disturb one another,
they will incur calamity and retribution.
Even if this person performs repentance, it will not remove their transgressions;
only this samaya can rescue them, while no other can. One should therefore employ the wheel mudrā.
Recite the Mother Dhāraṇī mantra and the Secret Heart Mantra one thousand and eight times.

and the painted image moves of its own accord, emitting seven kinds of light.

All the devas, including the Four Heavenly Kings together with their retinues,

One shall realize the great gateway of wisdom of the immeasurable and non-empty samaya,
and further attain the accomplishment corresponding to the great aggregate of merit consisting of the virtues of non-empty, courageous diligence, ethical discipline, and meditative concentration.
It is associated with the accomplishment of the non-empty six pāramitās;
it is associated with the fulfillment of non-empty roots of virtue;
and it is associated with the accomplishment of all dhāraṇīs, mantras, maṇḍalas, mudrās, and samayas.
One will be endowed with the accomplishment of the complete merits of the Amoghasiddhi Buddha-field;
furthermore, one will attain the accomplishment of being sustained by the roots of virtue of sixty-four hundred-thousand-ten-million-billion *gaṅgā*-sands of *amogha* Tathāgatas.
Furthermore, one attains the samaya of the unfailing veneration and prostration of all sentient beings throughout the three realms,
which accords with the accomplishment of the reliquary stūpas (śarīra-caitya) of the Bhagavān.
