At that time, when the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara spoke this mantra, [the earth shook in six ways].
He emitted a great radiance that illuminated Mount Potalaka;
its palaces and halls shook six times, and in the midst of the void,
[the sound of music resounded].
A rain of various celestial flowers fell: *utpala*,
*kumuda*, *padma*, *puṇḍarīka*, *māndārava*,
and diverse kinds of precious flowers.
With clouds of oceans of precious incense, jeweled crowns, celestial garments,
pearl necklaces, bracelets, armlets, and various precious ornaments,
they made offerings to the Tathāgata.
Furthermore, they made offerings to the great assembly gathered there, scattering flowers until they reached their knees.
In the void above, immeasurable celestial music resounded spontaneously without being struck.
Within the assembly were all the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, asuras, gandharvas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and so forth.
At that time, they were filled with joy; joining their palms and gazing up at him, they praised him with one voice, saying: "Excellent, excellent, O Great Compassionate One!
You have been able to wonderfully proclaim this most supreme vidyā-king mantra of the Amoghapāśahṛdaya."
Like a wish-fulfilling jewel,
it can bestow a great rain of jewels upon all sentient beings of the three realms, so that they all attain liberation.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, if there are sentient beings who, with a heart of great compassion, delight in receiving and upholding this mantra..."
One should always bathe, anoint the body with fragrances, and wear clean garments.
Eating the three white foods, one should sit in a quiet room,
placing the mind within the mind and observing it oneself.
Abiding in the pure bodhicitta,
one should recognize that all forms follow that meditative practice and not perceive them otherwise.
This applies to the śāntika samaya.
One should face north,
sit in the auspicious posture with legs crossed like Mount Sumeru,
firm and unmoving, with a mind that is tranquil and serene.
With eyes of compassion, his eyelids do not blink;
he gazes upon the face of Avalokiteśvara, which is serene and still,
its form round and white, as he sits upright in tranquil meditation.
Seated in the full lotus posture upon a white lotus throne,
her left hand is held at the heart with the palm grasping a maṇi jewel,
while her right hand is extended upward, displaying the mudrā of granting fearlessness.
Emitting white light that illuminates and melts away all obstructions,
the sound of the recitation is clear and distinct, its tonal qualities pure and harmonious,
neither hurried nor sluggish, but perfectly even in every detail.
With the phonemes and syllables appearing like a garland of white light,
if one recites this twenty-one times, seven times, seven hundred times, or one hundred and eight times,
all calamities and misfortunes shall be eliminated.
All obstacles of sin, all spirits and ghosts, and all evil diseases;
the most supreme accomplishment of the worldly and transworldly samaya-ground, whether it be the pauṣṭika-samaya or other rites.
One should face east,
sit with legs crossed in the lotus posture, and with a joyful countenance, maintain a mind of gladness.
With diamond-like eyes, filled with joy and deep affection,
he gazed upon Avalokiteśvara in accordance with his nature;
the Bodhisattva’s face was serene and his countenance was full of pleasant radiance.
At the first light of day, his body is serene and joyful;
he sits in the full-lotus posture upon a golden lotus-light throne, holding a vajra at his chest with his left hand.
The right hand is extended upward, forming the mudrā of fearlessness.
It emits golden light that shines forth, penetrating all things without obstruction.
Recite clearly, with the tone and rhythm of the voice perfectly even and harmonious.
Neither too large nor too small, it was clearly perceived as swift and effective;
its compassionate sound was heard beyond [the city],
and its tonal rhythms and character forms were like a garland of golden light.
If one recites it three hundred and seventy-seven times,
one shall attain the fulfillment of the worldly and supramundane samaya-accomplishments.
This applies whether it concerns the guiding samaya or otherwise.

One should sit facing west on a vertical seat, squatting with legs joined; with a countenance of fierce wrath, one should gaze with eyes wide open by means of a joyful mind, repeatedly blinking the eyelids.
One should contemplate the face of Avalokiteśvara as radiant and beautiful; though the form appears formidable, the mind is filled with joy, maintaining an upright body and a vigorous, alert bearing.
Sitting cross-legged upon a moonlight lotus throne,
one recites with distinct articulation, the sounds and rhythms closely linked and rapid;
the voice is sharp, clear, and resonant, its sound solidly audible to those outside.
With the phonemes and syllables like a garland of moonlight,
recite twenty-one times, seven hundred times, seven thousand times, and one hundred and eight times; thus,
one shall attain the perfection of the samaya-stage that subdues both the supramundane and the mundane.
If it is the Abhijit-rucaka samaya,
one should stand facing south with the feet together.
The right foot is placed at the head [of the body] and the left foot at the tail;
it is drawn diagonally toward the left,
or one sits in the uḍupada posture.
He sits with his right foot placed upon his left,
his buttocks not touching the ground,
his countenance wrathful, and his mind filled with malice.
With both eyes slanting and glaring in wrath, he gazes upon the military strategy;
observing the face of the King of Fierce Anger, he bellows with rage.
His canine teeth protrude upward, appearing fearsome, blue, and massive.
He sits in the squatting posture upon a blue lotus seat;
his left hand holds a *daṇḍa*,
and his right hand grasps a *khaṭvāṅga*.
He emits great flames that are most terrifying;
he clearly recites with fierce roars and shouts, and his crushing,
scolding, and threatening sounds are heard from afar.
With the phonemes and syllables like a wreath of fire,
reciting twenty-one, seven, seven, one hundred, or eight times,
one shall be able to subjugate all ghosts and spirits.
All shall flee in terror and no longer cause mutual calamity or disturbance;
their majesty will be sovereign.
On the fifteenth day of the waxing moon, by the side of the Avalokiteśvara image...
Place an image of Śrī-devī and daily present offerings of pure food and various flowers.
Consecrate white mustard seeds with the mantra.
If one recites the name of Śrīdevī and strikes her image for twenty-one days, she will manifest her presence;
she will bestow precious jewels and grant supreme vows.
The Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara appeared in person upon awakening from his dream,
and for the purpose of eliminating calamities and removing the five sins of immediate retribution,
he empowered white mustard seeds with mantras and consumed them as an oblation, reducing them to ash.
Bind the boundary and protect the body according to one's intention.
Recite mantras over khadira-wood stakes while following the various spirits and deities.
Tie five-colored threads around them and perform the boundary-binding with needle knots.
If one suffers from malaria,
take thread of five colors and have a young girl join them together;
empower it with the mantra and tie twenty-one knots.
If it is tied around the neck, one will be cured.
For those with the disease of "hot wind" (uṣṇavāta),
one should prepare a medicinal paste by boiling together cow’s ghee, black sesame oil, the filaments and leaves of dried lotuses, and the husks of lotus seeds.
If one consecrates [the medicine] with mantras one hundred and eight times,
and then consumes it, applies it as an ointment, and administers it by nasal drops according to the count, one will be cured.
If one wishes to cure those afflicted by bewitchment (gū-bhaya),
one should empower clarified butter mixed with medicinal ointment through mantra-recitation and smear it upon the body.
Next, empower dry noodles,
spread them out to cover [the area],
and rub them off to mold them into the shape of the practitioner of sorcery.
If one consecrates an iron blade and cuts [the object] into seven pieces, the affliction will be eliminated.
If one is terrified by ghosts or spirits, [the same applies].
If one empowers a cord of five colors with one hundred and eight knots through mantra-recitation and wears it upon the body, one will be cured.
If one suffers from abdominal pain, [the same applies].
If one consumes red salt water empowered by mantra, one will immediately recover.
If bitten by a venomous insect,
apply yellow clay empowered by mantra.
If one applies [this] to the site of the bite, the affliction will be cured.
If one suffers from a swollen throat,
by reciting the mantra over powdered *pippalī* mixed with honey and ingesting it, one will be cured.
If one suffers from eye pain,
consecrate licorice water or camphor-scented water with mantras and wash the eyes repeatedly; thus, the ailment will be cured.
If one suffers from earache,
empower sesame oil and fennel seeds by boiling them together;
if several drops are poured into the ear, it will be cured.
If one constantly consecrates water at dawn to rinse the mouth and wash the face,
one will always obtain auspicious signs. If there are any calamities or strange omens within the house,
one should smear a thousand and eight stalks of lotus flowers with ghee, consecrate them, and offer them by burning.
Furthermore, by consecrating water three times each day and sprinkling it throughout the house, these [calamities] shall be eliminated.
As for all evil winds, hail, and rain disasters—
On the summit of a high mountain,
empower a pomegranate branch twenty-one times with mantras;
hold the rosary in the left hand and grasp the staff in the right hand.
Furthermore, with another empowerment of a single snap of the fingers,
he causes the evil winds, hail,
and rain to descend upon the wildernesses and between the great mountains.
If one recites it one hundred and eight times,
then [the affliction] will be dispelled. If the Vināyakas cause harassment and distress,
one should take the husks of sesame seeds mixed with water and hulled oil.
If one performs consecrated offerings to the vināyakas,
they will become joyful and no longer create obstacles or afflictions;
this is for those who would eliminate calamities.
For one week, one should fill a clean jar with scented water and place it before the Bodhisattva,
consecrating it one hundred and eight times.
If one bathes the body with the consecration of the "warmth of the Dharma," then [the afflictions] shall be eliminated.
If various ghosts and spirits should create obstacles or cause distress, [this shall likewise remove them].
Mix sesame oil with non-glutinous rice;
perform one consecration and one burning for one hundred and eight times,
and [the affliction] will be eliminated.
If one suffers from a disease caused by *māraṇa* spirits,
drinking water consecrated with the mantra will bring about recovery.
If there are sentient beings who have short lifespans and many ailments, [the same applies].
If one can personally burn the King of Incenses before an image of Avalokiteśvara every day and recite the mantra of the Most Victorious Vidyārāja one hundred and eight times,
for a full hundred days.
Then one will be able to transform the karma of premature death and attain an increase in lifespan.
Even if one's body is bound by cangues, fetters, stocks, shackles, or prison bonds, [one shall be liberated].
Provided that one recites and maintains the mantra of the Most Victorious Vidyārāja with utmost sincerity day and night for an unlimited number of times, one will attain liberation. Furthermore,
if one empowers the right hand and rubs the face, [the same result is achieved].
Those whom one goes to see will rejoice.
If one empowers a peacock feather with mantras and brushes it over the body of a sick person, they will be cured.
If one consecrates the ashes of *vajra* wood and scatters them in the ten directions after further consecration,
it constitutes the establishment of a boundary (*sīmābandha*).
If one constantly contemplates the image, forms mudrās,
and recites the mantra of the Supreme Vidyārāja without ever ceasing;
This person shall realize hundreds of thousands of samādhis.
If there are bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās who desire to bring the six pāramitās to perfection and remain in accord with them, [they should do so].
Construct a maṇḍala by mixing cow dung with yellow earth and smearing it according to the ritual rules.
Using white sandalwood, spikenard, saffron, camphor, and musk mixed with clay,
prepare and adorn a garland of lotus flowers;
place the Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra upon a seat magnificently decorated in its center.
Place an image of Avalokiteśvara with the Amoghapāśa and an image of Prajñā Bodhisattva.
Arrange various banners and flowers,
and offer various incenses, flowers, scented water, white foods, fruits, and lamps.
Incense the King of Fragrances,
purify one's body and garments, perform the protection of the person and the delimitation of the boundary,
and recite the mantra of the Supreme Vidyārāja.
Recite the name of the Bodhisattva Prajñā ten thousand times;
chant and maintain the mantra of the Furenwang (Krodharāja), while reciting the name of the Bodhisattva Prajñā.
Upon completing ten thousand recitations,
the Bodhisattva Prajñā will manifest in person to offer praise,
bestowing the complete fulfillment of the six pāramitās.
King Amogha, endowed with supreme roots of goodness and perfection,
shall act as a great guide for sentient beings;
should he subdue the celestial Māras.
Seated facing east upon the summit of a high mountain,
holding a vajra in his right hand and counting beads with his left,
he recited the mantra of the Most Victorious Vidyārāja one hundred and eight times.
Furthermore, by forming the wheel-seal and reciting the mantra of the Wrathful King one hundred and eight times,
all devas, māras, ghosts, and spirits will be brought into submission.
This should be done regularly on the eighth and fifteenth days of the waxing moon.
Consuming the three white foods and remaining silent, abstaining from speech,
one should sit in the *paryaṅka* posture facing east with hands in the *cakra-mudrā*,
reciting the mantra of the Supreme Vidyārāja one hundred and eight times.
Then one will obtain the *ābhoga-rāja* mantra, whereby all dharmas and all heart-wishes shall be completely fulfilled.
If one performs self-consecration,
use a white porcelain jar.
Fill [a vessel] with water scented with white sandalwood, spikenard, and camphor,
and place it at the center of the maṇḍala.
Bind the initiation mudrā and empower it with the mantra.
Consecrate one’s own crown;
likewise, seal the water jar one hundred and eight times and bathe the body with it for consecration.
This is equivalent to all the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Mahāsattvas.
One should confer empowerment while [the deity] is manifest before one.
Alternatively, if one enters the *tathāgata-lakṣaṇa-samādhi* before a relic or an image,
one should recite and maintain the mantra of the Supreme Vidyārāja once.
First, request the Tathāgata’s ten powers and supernormal faculties to bestow grace, protection,
and guardianship one hundred and eight times;
you shall then attain correspondence with the merits of the Tathāgata.
If one presses the foot of the image of Amoghapāśa with the right hand,
makes a great vow,
and recites the mantra of the Most Victorious Vidyārāja one hundred and eight times;
One shall then attain the qualities corresponding to those of Amogharāja.
Furthermore, burn agalloch incense and press the right hand upon the feet of the image of the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, Lord of Secrets.
Recite and maintain the mantra of the Most Victorious Vidyārāja once;
recite the name of the Bodhisattva Guhyakādhipati Vajrapāṇi one hundred and eight times.
One shall attain correspondence with the merits of the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, Lord of Secrets.
Thus one should cultivate the mantras of the most supreme vidyārāja and the mantras of the krodharāja.
Regarding the mudrās for binding the boundary, conferring empowerment, and protecting the body,
one should constantly give rise to the four immeasurable minds;
thus one will swiftly attain the rapid correspondence with all dharmas.
Auspicious signs of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara’s protective grace will appear:
their merit and virtue will increase, their complexion will become full and pure,
and they will attain the presence of the Buddhas of the ten directions.
The body of the Bodhisattva, armored with the Great Consecration Mudrā,
spontaneously accomplishes all the mantras and dharmas of the most excellent Vidyārājas.
One shall realize the Sarvārthasiddhi-rāja Dhāraṇī-mantra and all samayas.

Chapter Fourteen: The Chapter on the Wrathful Kings.

This is the mantra of the Supreme Unfailing Wrathful King.
As the Buddhas have taught, one should always bathe cleanly,
anoint the body with incense, and wear pure garments.
Possessing great wisdom,
one shall attain accomplishment by properly relying on this fundamental method.
He then spoke the mantra of the Wrathful King:
Namo sarva-tathāgata-āryāvalokiteśvara-bhadrāya.

Furthermore, one should not sit opposite another person, converse with them, or share food from the same vessel.

As for what is called "internal protection":
First, one should always earnestly restrain the mind in accordance with the Dharma,
neither praising oneself nor disparaging others regarding wholesome or unwholesome karma,

Second, their minds are constantly pure through an untainted mind (*anāsrava-citta*),
such that they do not dwell upon worldly, defiled, or evil dharmas, nor contemplate fame or profit. Third,
they maintain the perfections (*pāramitās*) of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
Irrigating one's own mind, one should give rise to great compassion toward all sentient beings;
day by day, one should receive, uphold, read, and recite [the teachings] according to the Dharma,

Whether in a family of kṣatriyas or in a family of śūdras, they all delight in making offerings by anointing the feet, shins, knees, and palms;
they travel without lack, and fire, water, tigers, wolves, and the like do not cause them harm.
They mix it with the milk of a nursing infant and use it to anoint the eyes.
If one applies the various *terma* (hidden treasures) of the *darśana-bhūmi* to the abdomen, the disease of abdominal pain will be eliminated.

If taken with cow’s milk, the body becomes purified; one will not be harassed by spirits or ghosts, and all curses, malevolent sorcery, and poisonous charms will be extinguished, as well as the signs of evil dreams.
One should always consume it mixed with cow’s milk, or mixed with ghee and curd, or again mixed with honey;

this will swiftly cause one to attain clarity of mind. One will recite texts differently day by day, and all the mantras, mandalas, mudrās, and samayas of this family will be fully accomplished, with wisdom and understanding like the ocean.
One will be respected by others, and one’s lifespan shall not be cut short by calamity or untimely death.
All karmic obstacles, past deeds, and the suffering of various illnesses shall be entirely eliminated.
If one applies sesame oil mixed [with this] to the head, ailments of the head-wind (vāta) shall be swiftly cured. These are the three mantras.
Consecrate the mature Acorus calamus (changpu) so that it manifests signs of warmth and smoke; one should then mix it with cow’s ghee and consume it on an empty stomach.

After a full hundred days have passed, one’s voice will become clear, harmonious, and elegant, and the teeth and tongue will be freed from chronic ailments. All people who hear the sound of one’s speech [will be moved].
Calamities and karmic obstructions are eliminated; if one constantly wears it as an amulet, one will possess great memory and eloquence.
All mantras of this lineage, as well as mandalas, mudrās, and samayas, shall be fully accomplished.
One’s wisdom and understanding will become like the ocean. If it is worn upon the upper arm, one will not be harmed by any ghosts or spirits.

When evil spirits and demons afflict and harm one another, if one grinds white mustard seeds and burns them as incense, all illnesses caused by spirits that are otherwise difficult to cure will be immediately eliminated.
Thus, these three mantras are likewise empowered. [The substances are: *bīrāṅgaka*, *yavakṣāra*, *hiṅgu*, and *tagara*.
Take blue *turmeric*, *kustha*, *śamī*, *bṛhatī*, lotus root, *gandhatṛṇa*, and mustard seeds from offered flowers;
mix these in equal proportions and form them into pills the size of jujube fruits.
Place these within a ceramic vessel and set it upon the altar.
Manifested through the empowerment of mantras, it is dried in the shade while exhibiting signs of warmth and smoke.
It cures diseases such as malaria, sores, scabies, and the effects of poisons; when used by mixing the medicine with water, applying it, or ingesting it, these ailments are eliminated.
For a headache, mix the medicine with oil; by applying it to the head, the pain will quickly subside. If one suffers from toothache:
If one takes the medicine, the illness will be removed. For abdominal pain, mix the medicine with water;
by drinking it, all pains in the bones and joints will be cured. To treat aching spots, apply the medicine mixed with clarified butter (*ghṛta*);
the pain will then be relieved and healed. For chronic wasting diseases (*yakṣman*), mix the medicine with warm water and bathe the body every day.
It swiftly extinguishes all sinful defilements and the afflictions of every disease.

If one suffers from a spirit-induced illness, one should mix medicine with clarified butter (*ghṛta*), administer it as nasal drops (*nasya*), and fumigate the body with it; then one shall surely be cured.
If one has lost their voice due to the calamity of a spirit, one should sprinkle the medicine mixed with water upon the fontanelle (*mūrdhnaḥ sīman*); then one shall be healed.
If one suffers from heart pain, mix medicine with salt water and drink it; thus one will be cured.

Recite these three mantras and likewise empower them. When the warm smoke and light-signs of realgar and silver ore appear, apply a dot of realgar to the crown of the head, the forehead, the shoulders, the heart, and above the throat.
When one perceives the silver mine within the eye, one realizes the secret;
the mantra-vidyādhara sages enter the caves of yakṣas, rākṣasas, asuras, and spirits without obstruction.
If one enters a śmaśāna, all spirits and ghosts submit upon seeing them; likewise, if one anoints one’s body, hands, and feet [with this substance].
By forming mudrās and reciting mantras, one shall attain accomplishment;
for Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva bestows grace upon this supreme vow, and the Śuddhāvāsa deities,
Īśvara, Maheśvara, Mahābrahmā, Śakra, and King Nārāyaṇa shall provide protection.
These three mantras and others empower the following: ox-gallstone, realgar, *saurabheya*, *añjana* medicine, saffron, and the juice of *kākapuṣpa*.
When these medicinal substances are blended and empowered, they manifest warmth, smoke, and light.
All incense, flowers, and exquisite perfumed waters [are likewise empowered].
Offer various kinds of food and drink as an offering; With pure, clean, and well-selected clothing for the body, If one is a layperson,
every morning One should observe the eight precepts (*aṣṭāṅga-śīla*), apply medicinal ointment to the eyes,
mark the forehead and the wheel on the ears, form mudrās, and recite the Mātṛ-dhāraṇī mantra.
By means of the Amoghasiddhi-rāja-mantra, one shall behold Avalokiteśvara in the palace of seven jewels on Mount Potalaka;
one shall also behold Amitābha Buddha and the various bodhisattvas in the jeweled palaces of the western direction, as well as all the buddha-fields of the ten directions.
All Buddhas and the assembly of Bodhisattvas, Brahmā, Śakra, the Heavenly Kings, and all the devas—
Even for a caṇḍāla who commits deeds and has created offenses of the immediate retribution in the past or present,
one who applies this medicine shall not see me, nor the lands of the ten directions.
All Buddhas and the assembly of Bodhisattvas— If one merely succeeds in seeing all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the ten directions in a dream, And Avalokiteśvara bestows his grace and protection,
he shall immediately be liberated from the sins of the Avīci hell, And shall be born as, and attain the state of, King Amoghasiddhi.
Through the supernatural powers of mantra, one achieves accomplishment; one’s lifespan becomes equal to that of the gods, and blessings are immeasurable.

All manner of poisons, venomous insects, and the like, as well as all fears of ghosts, spirits, and enemies, shall naturally come to an end and be utterly extinguished. All whom one encounters will be filled with joy.
The Amoghapāśakalparāja Sūtra, Scroll Eleven; The Amoghapāśakalparāja Sūtra, Scroll Twelve.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Bodhiruci of India during the Great Tang Dynasty.
Chapter Sixteen: The King of Vast and Extensive Maṇi Incense.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara...
Again, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, this Samaya of the King of Non-empty Mani Incense possesses great supernatural power;
it is able to summon all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas Mahasattvas, and all the devas, mantras, and vidyadharas of the ten directions."
Through empowerment, it brings about the vast *siddhi* of all dharmas for the mantra-holder;
furthermore, it is able to subdue and overcome all jealous deities, *nāgas*, *yakṣas*, *rākṣasas*, *gandharvas*, *asuras*, *kiṃnaras*, *grahas*, *mahoragas*, and all other malevolent spirits.
It can also eliminate worldly poisons from medicinal herbs, insect venom, snake venom, sorcery, curses, and diseases caused by spirits and deities.
It causes the people to rejoice and increases and matures their accumulations of merit and roots of goodness.
It also dispels and eliminates the transgressions of the ten evil deeds, the five heinous crimes, and the four grave offenses of the past and present.
Since ancient times until now, Śakra, the Lord of the Heaven of the Thirty-three,
has constantly applied this incense to his body and used it for fumigation and consumption.
By the supernatural power of this incense,
when he engages in battle against the hosts of asuras, he always achieves victory.
Nārāyaṇa, too, uses this incense for the same purpose.
By the supernatural power of anointing the body and wearing incense,
one subdues all asura kings and constantly attains victory.
Maheśvara also used this incense to smear his body and wear it as perfumed incense; by the supernatural power of this incense,
he burned the gods of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven and again attained victory.
Furthermore, in the past, before a Buddha had appeared in the world,
there was a king named Bhaṇḍalāśrī who likewise anointed his body with this incense and used it for fumigation and consumption.
By means of the supernatural power of artificial incense,
he joined with King Kaurava in battle against the enemy and likewise achieved victory. Furthermore,
when the World-Honored One first attained perfect enlightenment beneath the Bodhi tree, [he likewise employed this power].
Seated upon the Vajrāsana,
he likewise anoints his body and fumigates himself with this incense while subduing the hosts of Māras;
by means of the supernatural power of the incense and the power of his compassion.
He utterly crushed the armies of Māra, scattering and destroying them all at once.
Long ago, there was a merchant leader known as the householder Siddhārtha,
who traveled upon the great ocean.
Having obtained the precious jewel, he was about to lose it again;
he likewise smeared this incense upon his body and inhaled its fragrance.
Relying on the supernatural power of the incense, he made a solemn vow and aspiration, swearing to exhaust the waters of the great ocean.
Standing upon the seashore, he scooped up the waters of the great ocean;
in less than a single day, he sought to exhaust the sea,
causing all the dragon kings to be filled with panic and fear as they returned the jewel to the merchant leader.
The merchant leader obtained the jewel and immediately returned home;
he placed this precious jewel atop a banner and further fumigated the jewel with this incense.
At that time, for seven days and seven nights, that jewel rained down various precious treasures.
For this reason,
it is said that this king of incense possesses great supernormal power.
The mantra-holders who are able to achieve great accomplishment—
now those Dragon Kings Nanda and Upananda were,
in the past, together with the Dragon King Sāgara.
For seven days and seven nights they fought in the midst of the ocean;
the three [deities] spat forth poison, so that the waters of the great ocean were entirely transformed into poisonous water.
Maheśvara also used this incense.
By the supernatural power of the incense he applied to his body and wore as perfume,
he inhaled and swallowed the venom of the three dragon kings from the sea;
in an instant, they were transformed into a blue color.
It subdues and transforms the poison of dragons into nectar. For this reason,
it is said that the power of this incense can extinguish poison.
In the past, there was a king named King Mandhātṛ.
He likewise anointed his body with this incense and used it for fumigation and consumption.
Relying on the supernatural power of the incense, he recited mantras and made aspirations, thereby attaining the status of a Golden Wheel-Turning King.
He was constantly attended by hundreds of thousands of sages who practiced asceticism, who carried him in palanquins;
as king of the four continents, he traveled through the void of space and went to the Heaven of the Thirty-three to sit upon the same couch as Śakra, the Lord of Devas.
If one suddenly gives rise to an evil mind and utters a great falsehood,
one will immediately fall back and lose the status of a Wheel-Turning King.
For this reason, those who uphold mantras [must remain pure].
One should always, in accordance with the Dharma, utter words that are true and real, and resolve upon bodhicitta.
By constantly practicing great compassion and burning this incense,
one will attain the empowerment and accomplishment of the spiritual powers of all Tathāgatas.
When the World-Honored One speaks thus,
he does so for the sake of liberating all sentient beings from the sufferings of the sixteen hells;
he speaks for the sake of liberating them from the sufferings of all hunger, thirst, and emaciation of the hungry ghosts.
It is taught for the purpose of dispelling all worldly calamities and fetters;
it is taught so that those who maintain the mantra now and in the future may achieve accomplishment;
and it is taught so that those who burn this incense while seeking the fulfillment of their own or others' aspirations shall all give rise to a heart of compassion.
If seeking for oneself, one should utter one's own name;
if for another, one should utter that person's name.
By making offerings and reciting the mantra in this manner, one shall likewise attain their wishes.
During lunar or solar eclipses, when malevolent stars appear,
or when kings, ministers, śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, and all the people encounter calamities and hardships,
one should perform ritual purification by bathing.
One should apply this incense to the body, inhale its fragrance,
and burn it as an offering;
by means of the supernatural power of this incense.
By reciting the samaya-mantra of the Amoghapāśahṛdaya-rāja-dhāraṇī,
all calamities, misfortunes, and painful ailments shall be dispelled and extinguished.
Through the divine protection and empowerment of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva,
the mantra-holder shall bathe with purity and anoint their body and perfume their robes with this incense.
With a heart of great compassion,
universally offer this burning incense as an offering to all sentient beings throughout the ten directions— those in the hells, hungry ghosts, and the animal realm.
Relying on the supernatural power of the incense, recite the mantra of the Amoghapāśa Dhāraṇī.
It enables all sentient beings throughout the ten directions— those in the realms of hell, hungry ghosts, and animals—
who encounter this fragrant wind, to attain liberation. Furthermore,
for those sentient beings whose natures are dominated by anger, ignorance, or hindrances, [it brings about their deliverance].
Always bathe in purity and constantly smear this incense upon one's body and perfume one's robes.
Give rise to great compassion for all sentient beings and perform sincere repentance.
By reciting and upholding the mantra of the Amogharāja-dhāraṇī,
one will swiftly attain the liberation from all fetters of anger and delusion, as well as the grave sins of the hells.
If one constantly bathes, anoints the body, and perfumes one's garments, [the benefits shall be realized].
If one performs the ritual according to the Dharma and recites the Mātṛ-dhāraṇī mantra one hundred thousand times and the Siddhirāja mantra one hundred thousand times,
one shall realize the stage of the irreversible consecration and abide therein.
One attains the Vajra-Continuous Samādhi empowered by all Tathāgatas;
wherever this incense is burned as an offering,
that place becomes like a stūpa containing the relics of all the Tathāgatas of the ten directions.
It was also like the abodes of the palaces of fragrant cloud-light belonging to all the Tathāgatas of the ten directions;
it was also like the lands of the wheel-turning Dharma of sixty-four hundred thousand *koṭi-nayuta* Ganges-sand-like Tathāgatas, where fragrant clouds abide.
It is also for all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas,
the vidyā-mantra sages of the vajra devas,
the deities of the Four Great Kings, the aṃśakas, and the yakṣa generals.
The yakṣa general Sata, the yakṣa general Māpata, and the yakṣa general Maṇibhadra.
The yakṣa general Pūrṇabhadra, the yakṣa general Buddhavala, and the yakṣa general Nāṭakuvera.
As well as the various yakṣa generals, each together with their retinues,
who respectfully protect and bestow their vows upon this place;
these are also the god Īśvara and the god Maheśvara.
May Mahābrahmā, Śakra-devendra,
Nārāyaṇa, and the gods of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven reverently protect and bestow their blessings upon this place.
Furthermore, there are the gods of the sun, the moon, and the stars;
the host of lunar mansions and the presiding star deities; Vemacitrin, Śrīdevī, and others.
The goddess Sarasvatī, the Earth-holding goddess,
Varuṇa, the deity Śakunī, the deities of groves and forests,
the deities of mountains, ponds, rivers, and oceans.
It is also reverently protected by King Yama, the gods Kuberavas and Kumāras, and the hosts of ascetic sages,
who guard, honor, and make offerings to it day and night.
It is like the stūpas containing the śarīra relics of all Tathāgatas throughout the ten directions;
it is also the dwelling place for the dharma assemblies and fragrant cloud palaces of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva Mahāsattva and his entire retinue.
If there are sentient beings who obtain this fragrance, they shall be able to cultivate the path to *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
He addressed the devas, saying: "You should listen attentively."
For the benefit of all sentient beings who uphold mantras, I shall speak these verses on the King of Maṇi Incense:
One hundred and eight parts each of black aloeswood, agallochum, guggulu, gandharasa, and boiled incense; thirty-two parts of frankincense.
New saffron, small-nail incense— two types, each ten parts;
tagara incense, resin incense, nāmilu incense, *sukha-saṃyoga* incense,
*pṛthuka* incense, *kuṣṭha* incense, and *śrīveṣṭaka* incense— seven types, each four parts.
White sandalwood incense, camphor, and musk—these three types, each three parts;
cow bezoar, realgar, and *xiangfuzi*; *duzhong*, wood sap, *nenu* (pronounced *nu* with a light tone), lotus rhizome tips, *wutouhua*, and *harītakī*; *suvāraṇa* and *kiśara*.
*Śimiseṇu kḷande | mṛhama putrasenoha kṣīraya | sumāra īna kuli gandhana kulija ya | These seventeen [syllables] constitute one part.*
Taking only the most refined, exquisite, and superior items, on the fifteenth day of the waxing moon,
one should bathe cleanly in a secluded place,
anoint the body with incense, put on pure garments, and eat the three white foods.
Having silenced all debate, construct a maṇḍala.
Anoint and decorate it with saffron paste and white sandalwood paste,
and place an image of Amogharāja therein.
Arrange offerings of various incenses, flowers, scented water, lamps, and the three white foods upon the incense altar;
empower them one hundred and eight times with the mantra.
Combine and pound them together.
Take equal parts of granulated sugar, rock honey, and white honey.
Empower [the mixture] one hundred and eight times with mantras.
Purify it according to the Dharma, divide it into two portions,
place them in ceramic vessels, and set them upon the altar.
Facing east, perform the ritual procedure.
Empower the maṇi-fragrance king one thousand and eight times with the Mother Dhāraṇī mantra.
Empower the maṇi-fragrance king one thousand and eight times with the Furenwang (Krodharāja) mantra.
Consecrate the King of Maṇi Incense with the King of Siddhi Mantras one thousand and eight times.
Seal it securely so that no fragrance escapes.
Bury it in the ground of this altar for fifty days until the period is complete.
Take up incense and burn it as an offering for all.

Recite the Amoghapāśahasta-mantra: Oṃ vīra sarvatathāgata-vajrodake ’mogha-hṛdaya jara jara jaja mahākāruṇika svadhā hūṃ abhiṣiñca amogha-prasādaka ṭi svāhā. With this mantra, empower the king of incense one hundred thousand times.
The King of Maṇi Incense, empowered by the spiritual power of all Tathāgatas,
is named "Incense Contemplated by All Tathāgatas," and is also called "Incense of Avalokiteśvara for Upholding All Bodhi Vows."
Burn one portion and fumigate with another.
Recite the incense mantra: *Oṃ vimala-sarvatathāgata-vairocana-mahāmudrāja jaya jaya svāhā*. Empower the king of incenses with this mantra and offer it as a burnt oblation (*dhūpa*).
One should bathe and purify oneself, empower the king of incenses,
anoint the body, fumigate the garments, and wear clean clothing; then,
according to the ritual, one who upholds this mantra shall do so.
Then one shall obtain the supernatural powers and blessings of all Tathāgatas of the ten directions;
Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva will manifest in person upon awakening from the dream and bestow the Samaya of the Non-empty Ocean of Wisdom.
To eliminate the eight difficulties, the four grave offenses, the five heinous crimes, and all other transgressions;
it is venerated by all śramaṇas and brāhmaṇas. If one perfumes śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, or any other person with it, [they shall be purified].
One will also be able to eliminate all fetters and afflictions.
On the eighth or fifteenth day of the bright fortnight,
having bathed with purity, one should smear this incense upon the body.
Wearing clean garments and consuming the three white foods,
one should construct a maṇḍala on a mountain peak or atop a high tower facing the heavens,
and offer various incenses, flowers, scented water, and white foods.
Burn this King of Incenses and offer it facing west to all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Mahāsattvas in all lands throughout the ten directions;
thus, before all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Mahāsattvas in all lands throughout the ten directions, [one shall make offerings].
At that time, they all manifested clouds of this unfailing mani-jewel, ox-head sandalwood incense, palaces, pavilions, various platforms and seats, banners, pennants, flowers, and canopies,
and made offerings therewith.
At that time, all the Buddhas of all the lands in the ten directions simultaneously praised him, saying:
"Excellent, excellent, O mantra-practitioner!
We, the Buddhas, made such offerings when we were on the path of practice in the past."
In the Western Pure Land, Amitābha Buddha,
Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, Mahāsthāmaprāpta Bodhisattva,
and all the bodhisattvas joyfully praise [this].
Furthermore, he accomplished the rites of the King Amoghapāśa,
as well as those of all the Great Brahmā, Śakra-devendra, Nārāyaṇa, Maheśvara, Sūrya, Candra, the stellar deities, and even up to the Akaniṣṭha heaven.
They all made offerings to it.
At that time, those devas who smelled the fragrance were simultaneously filled with joy and wondered, "From what direction does this praised fragrance come?"
One who performs this rite shall obtain a great mass of merit and bring their roots of virtue to maturity.
If one seeks to bring rain or to stop rain,
one should draw a maṇḍala on a high and remote vantage point.
While burning incense and holding aloft the "King of Fragrances," one should recite this supreme vidyārāja mantra with a loud and rapid voice,
calling upon the names of the nāga king Nanda and the nāga king Upananda.
When rain is required, it shall rain; when its cessation is required, it shall cease.
Furthermore, it shall suppress all evil winds, torrential rains, thunder, and lightning.
One should recite and maintain the mantra of the Furenwang (Candaroṣaṇa) and burn the incense-king.
All the vināyakas and malevolent spirits will flee in terror for a hundred yojanas if one burns this King of Incenses and recites the mantra of the Most Victorious Vidyārāja.
If one invokes the name Mahākāla— the name of all celestial deities—
one will achieve subjugation and receive protection and blessings.
One should constantly offer incense-king offerings while reciting and contemplating [the mantra].
One shall swiftly attain the fulfillment of all great vows.
Chapter Seventeen: The Section on Vajra-Maṇi Medicines. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara...
Again, he addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One,
this vajra-maṇi medicine can also benefit all practitioners of mantras in the future."
For all sentient beings,
may they be liberated from various calamities, illnesses, afflictions, and inauspicious signs;
may all their undertakings be fully accomplished.
If one applies it to the eyes,
all celestial deities and spirits will secretly provide protection;
and all people who see them will be filled with joy.
If applied to the face,
facial blemishes are eliminated and the complexion becomes fresh and white;
if applied to the eyes, the vision becomes clear and bright.
When people see one another, they greet each other with joy and inquiry. Furthermore,
for those who smear [this] upon their bodies, wear it as an amulet, or recite and contemplate it,
the Vināyakas and all evil spirits and ghosts [shall be subdued].
They fled in terror, not obstructing one another;
they attained great power like that of Nārāyaṇa,
such that even the gods of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven and the hosts of nāgas were all struck with fear and trembled.
By the power of the mantra and the medicinal herbs, even Mount Sumeru may be moved.
Should there be any illnesses or all manner of calamities,
by anointing the body and its limbs with this medicine, they shall be completely extinguished.
If one bathes with purity, anoints the body, perfumes the robes, recites the name, and performs repentance,
then all karmic obstacles of the ten evil deeds and the five heinous crimes shall be cleansed away.
Those who see this person will regard them with joy and respect.
The Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, through his supernatural powers, majestic virtue, grace, and protection,
acts for the fulfillment of all aspects of the sphere of enlightenment.
Sixty-four hundred thousand *koṭi-nayuta* of Tathāgatas, as numerous as the sands of sixty-four *Gaṅgā* rivers, [do likewise].
Through the protection encompassed by the contemplation associated with roots of goodness,
all enmities, difficulties, calamities, and misfortunes shall be entirely extinguished;
and Vajrapāṇi, the Lord of Secrets, shall grant his protective care.
If one constantly wears [the beads], anoints the body with them, perfumes the robes with them,
and wears them while maintaining purity and reciting the mantra,
one will receive from all the Tathāgatas the prophecy of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
Up until the time of attaining equal enlightenment while seated upon the Bodhi throne,
one will not be disturbed or afflicted by any of the celestial Māras or malevolent ghosts and spirits. Furthermore,
if this [substance] is applied to bells and drums and they are struck to produce melodic sounds, [the same protection is granted].
All sentient beings who hear this shall be liberated from all the karmic pains of the sixteen hells,

and they shall also attain liberation from the great terrors of the eight difficult conditions, such as water, fire, precipices, cliffs, blades, staves, hostile bandits, tigers, wolves, malevolent poisons, thunder, and lightning.
If any ghosts, spirits, birds, or beasts hear this,
their karmic retributions and sufferings shall likewise be extinguished;
having cast off this body, they will be reborn in the realms of humans or devas.
If one applies it to a conch shell and blows it loudly from atop a tower or a mountain,
any sentient beings who hear it—
All shall attain the eradication of every obstacle of sin;
after casting off this body, they will be reborn in the celestial realms.
If the medicine is placed at the top of a banner, [the same result shall follow].
It shall dispel calamities and pestilence caused by the spirits of the land, as well as evil winds and torrential rains;
it shall ensure an abundant harvest of grain,
and for all sentient beings who behold it, it shall ward off and remedy misfortunes and obstacles.
Regarding the number of substances such as the vajra-maṇi and medicinal herbs, several verses state:
*Tagara* incense and superior cow bezoar (*gorocana*), *Utpala* flower and superior yellow orpiment,
Lotus filaments and stamens and superior realgar, White sandalwood and the root of *darbha* grass.
Bilvaka incense, saffron; bilva, agaru, nāgapuṣpa, vālaka, and red sandalwood incense;
harītakī, tagara, lodhra, elā, and cārattī-pattraka incense.
Sumanā flowers, jātī, khaṭakāśa, fragrant fennel, sañjāraśa, aloeswood, the resinous sap of Eucommia,
cloves, and cinnamon bark— on the eighth day of the bright fortnight,
having purified one's body, one should wear these.
Having partaken of the three white foods, construct a maṇḍala.
Place an image of Amogharāja facing east and offer various incenses,
flowers, scented water, food, and drink.

In the final age, O World-Honored One, those sentient beings—

[they are as you have described].

It is also like my own body’s various methods of mastery in transformation and craftsmanship,
the methods of sovereign secrecy,
and the methods of supernormal powers.
The method for entering the cave of the asuras;
the methods for [entering] the palaces of the devas, the nāgas, and the kiṃnaras;
the method for treading upon water; and the method for entering fire.
The method for entering all mountains and forests; the method for producing gold and silver;
the method for requesting rain; the method for stopping rain;

Methods for extracting hidden treasures (*pātāla*), methods for crossing rivers and seas,

The methods for long-life elixirs, the methods for transforming various objects,

At that time, Avalokiteśvara extended his hand and touched his head,

The physical vessel becomes pure like a snake shedding its skin;

They realize the knowledge of past lives spanning hundreds of thousands of koṭis of births;

He realized the non-empty samādhi of immeasurable hundreds of thousands of spiritual transformations,

That is to say: summoning and rebuking all spirits and ghosts;

It eliminates all diseases such as sores, scabs, ringworm, malaria, abdominal ailments, and disorders of the six sense organs;

Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva will manifest his form and speak words of praise:

You have now entered into the vast liberation of the Lotus Mandala and Seal Method of the Heart-King Dhāraṇī Mantra of Amoghapāśa;

When the mantra-practitioner who holds a lotus flower receives it,

Chapter Twenty-one: The Worldly Section on the Universal Mind-Seal Mantra. O World-Honored One, if one constructs a homa altar by a lotus pond...

If one fills a lapis lazuli vase with saffron-scented water and red fragrant flowers,

He travels three thousand yojanas in a day and perceives sounds and forms within three thousand yojanas.

By marking the forehead with the three signs, one attains supernatural powers and is sustained by spiritual companions;

Furthermore, one should spread lotus petals in a square pattern upon the altar.
Wash and purify the ox-gallstone with red and yellow cow's ghee;
place it upon a lotus leaf and offer incense and flowers as worship.

If one dot is applied to the forehead, all yakṣas, rākṣasas, and malevolent spirits will be completely subdued;

Treading upon a single wind-wheel, he ascends into space with sovereign ease;

The Verse on the Universal Mind-Seal Mantra (Cittamudrā-mantra) and the Agada Medicine:

One should employ realgar (*manaḥśilā*), antimony (*śilājatu*), *kunkuma* saffron, and *uragasāra* musk; orpiment (*haritāla*) from *aśoka* flowers, *duzhong* tree sap, and cow bezoar (*gorocana*); *campaka* flowers, purple-gold (*jāmbūnada-suvarṇa*), *bodhi* tree sap, and red cow’s milk; *sugandhika* jasmine, *bhaṅgā*, *nāgakeśara*, and *nāgaramothā* medicine; *saindhava* salt, *kuṣṭha*, and *viṣṇukanda* medicine.
Having refined it through equal enumeration,
on the fifteenth day of the waxing moon,
one should thoroughly purify and smear the ground, and adorn the maṇḍala.
Place an image of Eleven-faced Avalokiteśvara upon the medicinal altar and make offerings according to one's ability with various incenses, flowers, scented water, food, and lamps.
With a vast heart of compassion, one should mindfully recollect the Triple Gem and Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva,
seeking only unsurpassed *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*,
while making offerings of incense.
Empower the medicine with the mantra of the Universal Mind-Seal (Purbien Xin-yin) and prepare it through compounding.
Empower red honey and granulated sugar.
Combine [the ingredients] in a vessel of refined red copper,
place it upon the altar, form mudrās, and perform the ritual procedures.
Empower the offerings with the mantra of the Wrathful King (Krodharāja).
When the medicinal substances are empowered by the mantra of the King of Siddhis and the heart-seal (hṛdayamudrā) mantra,
signs of heat, smoke, and light appear;
at that time, the practitioner’s body emits flames of light.
The earth quaked at the altar;
one should personally rejoice, for the medicinal accomplishment has been verified.
Mix the medicine with *mṛtasaṃjīvanī-taila* (the "Oil of the Son of Brahmā," as translated into Chinese) and smear it upon the body, hands, feet, and other parts.
His body is like a vajra;
no swords, staves, water, fire, poisons, or medicines can harm it.
He gathers a retinue of a hundred people and soars through the air with sovereign ease.
If one *liang* of this medicine is used for alchemy,
it can transform one hundred *liang* of red copper into gold;
if it is taken as an elixir, [the same result follows].
Prepare a medicinal ointment by frying cow’s milk ghee.
For three days prior, one should consume buffalo ghee and milk;
then, one should take this medicine.
Having consumed cow’s milk for a full six months,
his complexion became fresh and lustrous like a lotus flower;
his voice was pure and elegant, and his hair curled like a spiral shell.
Their lifespan shall be one hundred thousand years.
No weapons, water, fire, poisons, yakṣas,
rākṣasas, ghosts, spirits, or evil persons shall be able to harm them.
When the year of service is complete,
one shall obtain the company of various devas and humans as companions;
one's merit and longevity will be like those of the heavens.
If one mixes this medicine with sesame oil and applies it to the head, the hair will become fragrant.
If one applies it to the eyes or the forehead,
one will see the gates of the palaces of all yakṣas, rākṣasas, and ghosts open.
Entering therein without obstruction, one will be revered and loved by the people of the world.
If one consumes it with cow’s milk and rock honey for three full years,
one will realize the samaya of the King of Vidyādhara Sages of all mantras.
His lifespan shall last for one great kalpa.
Within that kalpa, he will see each and every Buddha attain equal and perfect enlightenment beneath a bodhi tree and receive the prediction of future buddhahood from those Buddhas.
When going to the Brahma Heaven palace,
one should recite "Oṃ" while raising the voice to call out the syllable;

Regarding the universal heart-lotus agada-elixir, the verse says:
Furthermore, with lotus filaments, *sulodana*, bezoar (*gorocanā*), and nāgakesara;
with silver ore, agallochum (*agaru*), *utpala*, and *mṛdvīkā*; and with rock honey and blue lotuses.
The filaments of the *campaka* flower, the filaments of the *kettaki* flower,

*apāmārga*, mixed with clarified butter and fragrant oil.
On the fifteenth day of the waxing moon, construct a maṇḍala.

using one part entirely for making offerings to Avalokiteśvara.
Furthermore, every day he prepared various fragrant waters to make offerings to the deity Maṇibhadra;
one portion was entirely used to make offerings to the Triple Gem,
while another portion was used for himself and given to the poor.
Dedicate all the merit thus obtained entirely to the deity Maṇibhadra;
do not accumulate it for yourself.
Practice daily in this manner until the end of life.
If one has accumulated [wealth], one will no longer obtain it.
If on a journey through a wilderness one encounters a place without water,
and with his right hand holding a staff, he observes that the ground is largely covered in green grass and damp spots.
Recite the *Pūrvāvatīrṇa-cittamudrā-mantra* aloud while striking the ground one thousand and eight times with the staff and circling the staff one thousand and eight times.
With a loud voice, prostrate and entreat Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva:
"I pray only that your great compassion may save me from hunger and thirst.
Recite this one thousand times.
At the spot where he struck the ground, a spring and pond welled up;
its water was clear and delicious.
He recited the King of Siddhi mantra and struck the water with his staff.
A red-yellow deva emerged from within the water and,
with palms joined, asked, "What do you seek now?
The mantra-practitioner replied.
"Please grant me whatever food and drink I require.
Then, the practitioner of mantras shall offer various virtuous words of blessing to the celestial deities:
"May the gods be ever at peace; may they long receive the constant protection and guardianship of all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Brahmā, Śakra, and the other devas."
Having spoken these words, "May you be endowed with the various great merits and vows of awakening as vast as the heavens," he vanished into the water.
In an instant, he returned holding various celestial delicacies and fine foods in his hands.
The one who upholds the mantra shall then receive it;
with this celestial food, he shall provide for hundreds of thousands of people.
Having eaten their fill together,
they further take various kinds of exquisite ornaments and offer them to the mantra-practitioner.
In this way, the mind of the mantra-practitioner is like a pool or spring;
if it is not cleared away, it will remain forever in the world.
This water will always be drunk by all people without ever being exhausted.
If one forms the mudrā to protect the body and holds a staff in the right hand,
one should silently recite the *Pūrvavartana-cittamudrā-mantra* while proceeding into the midst of the great assembly.
One hundred and eight times, a wheel-staff revolves in the air;
whatever various objects one contemplates in the mind will all be obtained according to one's wish.
If one recites the *Purbbyan* Heart-Seal Mantra within a *śītavana* (cemetery), [the same occurs].
Circling the staff seven times constitutes one *yojana* for the establishment of the boundary protection; construct a mandala of six cubits and purify the ground by smearing it.
Adorn the surface of the mandala with cow dung and yellow earth mud.
Empower a stake made of *śirīṣa* wood with mantras and drive it into each of the four corners of the maṇḍala.
Encircle the four sides with boundary lines of five-colored cords.
He takes a new, unblemished *mṛttikā* vessel from a noble *manuṣya* family;
he bathes it with the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*) for purification,
and then bathes it again with scented water for further purification.
Place [the practitioner] dressed in pure white garments upon the altar and cover them with a white cloth.
Set out the three kinds of white food at the four sides of the altar.
Arrange the offerings and scatter various flowers throughout the altar.
Place bowls of fragrant water at each of the four corners and four sides.
At that time, the mantra practitioner sits facing west in the ritual posture,
burning the king of incenses as an offering to all;
he always holds a wish-fulfilling staff in his right hand.
Recite the *Prabhūta-citta-mudrā-mantra* one thousand and eight times to consecrate the *mīḍhala*; likewise,
recite the *Siddhi-rāja-mantra* to consecrate it as well.
Without ceasing his chanting,
he repeatedly stroked Mithila’s body with his left hand,
while pressing down upon Mithila’s body again and again with his staff in his right hand.
Command him to rise from his seat and look toward the four directions.
When he is looking at the directions, do not let him feel any particular fear or trepidation.
Firmly press the staff down upon the head of Mitraka.
When Maitreya speaks, do not feel fear or apprehension upon hearing his words; instead,
contemplate within your mind all matters of the past, present, and future.
Recite the King of Siddhi Mantra without ceasing even for a moment.
Mīḍhala will then relate everything that is on your mind.
Furthermore, press the staff against Mīḍhala’s heart.
Recite the King of Siddhi mantra,
which will cause Maitrāyaṇī to vomit up rudhira; take this rudhira.
Having had their eyes and foreheads marked,
they see the palaces of the various ghosts and spirits with their gates open, entering them all without hindrance;
those ghosts and spirits who see them all rejoice.
Then, using a staff to press down upon the heart of the *mi-tsa-la*,
recite the *Siddhirāja* mantra to cause the *mi-tsa-la* to vomit up the *hrīṇaya*.
He then took hold of it,
immediately attaining the power to soar through the air with sovereign ease and without obstruction,
and obtained the samaya of all the great powerful spirits and deities.
Just as Maheśvara attains great sovereignty and lives for ten thousand years,
yet upon uttering the syllable "Hūṃ" but once, [his life is ended].
First, he struck Māṭhara’s chest seven times with the staff,
and then he struck his throat seven times with the staff;
Māṭhara then spat out his tongue.
If one takes a blade and cuts it off, it immediately transforms into a sword;
by wearing it upon one's person,
one attains all the samayas of the sword-siddhas.
His lifespan was ten thousand years,
and he was accompanied by eighteen thousand sword immortals.
Furthermore, with his staff, he struck the head of Mitraka seven times.
He dismissed the mantra-deities from within Mitraka’s body,
and they returned to their palace and departed.
Mitraka was transformed into Jāmbūnada gold.
"One *tola* of this gold and one hundred *tolas* of red copper,
when blended, melted, and cast, become the finest pure gold.
The World-Honored One has taught this worldly method of accomplishment."
Out of compassion for all sentient beings of the future,
so that they may attain realization and entry into Bodhi,
this *Amoghapāśakalparāja-sūtra* (The Scripture of the Miraculous Mantra of the Unfailing Lasso) is spoken. Fascicle Thirteen.
The Amoghapāśakalparāja Sūtra, Scroll Ten, translated by the Tripitaka Master Bodhiruci of Central India during the Great Tang Dynasty.
Chapter Twenty-Two: The Dharani-Mantra of the Inconceivable Contemplation. Chapter Twenty-Two: The Dharani-Mantra of the Inconceivable Contemplation.
At that time, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, saying:
"You should once again proclaim the supreme, vast, and great liberation of the Lotus Secret Heart-King Maṇḍala Seal Samaya."
May those who uphold it attain the awakening of wisdom and understanding;
may they be entirely unimpeded, sovereign, and preeminent;
and may they ascend to realize the supreme, most excellent, and unsurpassed bodhi of all resolute understandings.
The *siddhi* was fully accomplished.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara rose from his seat,
leaping for joy with great exultation.
Baring his right shoulder, he joined his palms in reverence and prostrated at the Buddha’s feet; then, before the Buddha,
he offered various types of unguents, powdered incense, burning incense, jeweled banners, pennants, and canopies.
With various precious flowers, jeweled necklaces, celestial garments,
and all manner of divine musical instruments,
they extensively prepared offerings for the Tathāgata, the World-Honored One, and the assembly of all Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas.
Abiding here in the samaya of the seal of the vast liberation lotus maṇḍala of King Amogha,
all the deities of the maṇḍala, the mantra-vidyādharas,
and the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, and rākṣasas.
Asuras, gandharvas, kinnaras, mahoragas, and all the mantra-vidyādhara sages who practice asceticism and dwell on Mount Potalaka.
Before all other mantra-deities, vidyā-deities, and spirits,
one should offer various exquisite incenses, flowers, garments, precious parasols,
banners, pennants, jewels, and necklaces.
With exquisite ornaments,
he made offerings all around;
the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara joyfully joined his palms in reverence.
Having circumambulated the Tathāgata several hundred thousand times to the right, he withdrew to stand before the Buddha and sat down.
He then addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One."

This is the inconceivable contemplation *dhāraṇī-mantra-samaya* within the *samaya* of the mudrās and maṇḍalas of the supernatural powers of the Secret Heart-King, the Lotus of Supreme and Vast Liberation, through which all Tathāgatas appear in the world and are not empty.
This is the samaya of the seal of the vast, true, and miraculous liberation-giving (*dāna*) of all Tathāgatas.
This is the samaya of the seal of the vast liberation-maṇḍala of Vairocana Tathāgata.
This is the samaya of the supreme heart-seal of the Amoghasiddhi-visualization.
Merely by reciting it,
one shall attain the siddhi of the supreme, true heart-samaya that transcends the world.
This samaya is, moreover,
the specific place where all Tathāgatas bestow empowerment through their supernormal powers and grant predictions.
I have now obtained the empowerment and seal of the Tathāgatas’ supernormal powers.
This was spoken in the presence of the Buddha so that all mantra-holders might attain the most excellent siddhi,
and out of compassion for all sentient beings.
It is taught for the purpose of eliminating all karmic obstacles of the three periods of time and for the sake of liberating one from the cycle of birth and death caused by ignorance;
it is taught for the purpose of crushing, destroying, and obstructing entry into all realms of existence, such as those of hell-beings, hungry ghosts, and animals.
It is taught for the sake of all sentient beings who hold wrong views, are arrogant, and are destitute of the Dharma,
in order to resolve and treat their slanders of the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Bodhisattvas, Śrāvakas, and Pratyekabuddhas, as well as their heinous crimes.
Blessed One, if there are sentient beings who fear various sinful karmas and are able to constantly,
throughout day and night, fully maintain the ritual procedures and recite, read,
and uphold the mantra of the *Acintyadhyāna-dhāraṇī*, [they shall be liberated].
Those who repent of their various sins and uphold the pure precepts;
those who copy or paint [this scripture], or who see, hear, rejoice in, or joyfully make offerings to it;
or those who possess the vision of this sūtra.
World-Honored One, for such persons as these, all afflictions—

including the heavy karmic obstructions of ignorance, greed, hatred, delusion, jealousy, pride, and arrogance, as well as diseases caused by malevolent spirits and various distinct retributions of karma— shall be completely dispelled and resolved.

They shall not be harmed by any calamities: the perils of kings, the perils of thieves, imprisonment with weapons, the perils of water, the perils of fire, thunderbolts, lightning strikes, or various beasts such as tigers, leopards, foxes, wolves, vipers, snakes, scorpions, elephants, and dragons.
No such disasters shall afflict them.
All evil winds, thunder, hail, and lightning that destroy crops shall likewise be extinguished.
World-Honored One, for those who have formed aspirations regarding this samaya and those who repent of grave offenses,
[may these benefits be granted].
One should not give rise to even the slightest doubt regarding these mantra scriptures.
He addressed the World-Honored One, saying: "For what reason?
Among both unwholesome and wholesome dharmas, doubt is the most evil of evils."
Out of doubt, they do not diligently seek the supreme dharmas of the Two Truths;
like foolish merchants, though encountering true treasures upon sea or land,
they harbor doubts and lack understanding, failing to gather those priceless jewels.
Encountering this unfailing Dharma, one who harbors doubt is likewise so;
if such doubt arises, the shackles of Māra and the jailers shall bind one,
just as the lion king seizes and tears apart small beasts.
One cannot attain liberation; doubt is likewise [an obstacle] regarding awakening and saṃsāra.
These two are truly the definitive dharma.
If one harbors doubt regarding these two, one is deaf and blind, lacking the eye of wisdom.
If there are those possessed of wisdom, they should give rise to pure faith;
thus practicing recitation and upholding [the teachings] is the gate of liberation through great compassion.
It is like a merchant of wisdom whose wealth travels upon a level road.
The path that exclusively pursues victory and the fruit of acquiring abundant wealth—
O Bhagavān, for this reason,
the mantra-practitioner should give rise to pure faith.

This is the Dharani-mantra of the Samaya-mudra of the Sovereign Mind-King of Secrets, the Lotus of Supreme and Vast Liberation, the Manifestation of All-Accomplishing Tathagata; it is to be transcribed according to the Dharma, received, upheld, read, and recited.
The mantra of the Wrathful King;
the mantra of the King of Siddhis;
the mantra of the Universal Heart-Seal.
One who constantly and purely contemplates the yoga-visualization of the Dharma through the mantra of the *Acintya-dhyāna-dhāraṇī*—
it should be known that such a person...
Then one attains the realization and vision of the Great Inconceivable, Vast, True, and Miraculous Transformation Maṇḍala-Seal Samaya of all Tathāgatas,
as well as the Vairocana Tathāgata’s Supernatural Power-empowered Vast Liberation Maṇḍala-Seal Samaya.
The Samaya of the Heart Seal of the Supreme Lasso of Amoghasiddhi is fully endowed with and corresponds to the great aggregate of merit of all supramundane liberations;
it is called the Stage of Non-retrogression.
All Tathāgatas shall remember and empower them,
bestowing upon them the prophecy of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
World-Honored One, if there are sentient beings who seek unexcelled, perfect enlightenment...
Maintaining pure precepts, they are always able to act in accordance with the Dharma;
with diligent effort and without retreat, throughout the six periods of day and night,
they give rise to great compassion and bring all sentient beings to mind.
I behold those who, with reverence and making offerings, join their palms in prostration,
and uphold, recite, and contemplate this inconceivable Avalokita-dhāraṇī mantra in such a manner.
This is called the body of the Dharma-aggregate of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara of True Reality;
it is also called the body sustained and protected by the empowerment of the Dharma of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
It is also called the body empowered by the Dharma of all Tathāgatas and granted the prophecy of enlightenment;
it is also called the body through which Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara fulfills mundane and supramundane vows for those of the future and present.
I shall constantly don the firm armor of great compassion and diligence,
and for the sake of this person, I will firmly bind it upon my body, cherishing and protecting them with steadfast mindfulness.
On what day shall I cause them to sit at the site of enlightenment and turn the great wheel of Dharma, becoming equal to us?
With a heart of great compassion, they deliver all sentient beings within the three realms,
and their aspirations and dharmas are all brought to fulfillment.
At that time, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni praised the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, saying:
Excellent, excellent, O Great Compassionate One!
Your proclamation of the aspiration for the Dharma is most rare and marvelous.
Should anyone see, hear, believe in, or make offerings to it, [they shall attain great benefit].
One will thereby attain liberation from the karmic suffering of immeasurable kalpas of accumulated sins;
how much more so for those who observe the fast and precepts,
and who receive, uphold, read, recite, and contemplate them according to the Dharma.
How could one not realize *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*?
You should expound the mantra and samaya of the *Acintya-vipaśyanā-dhāraṇī*.
Now is precisely the right time.
At that moment, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara,
with joyful vigor and a serene smile, looked upon them.
Beholding the Tathāgata, he then spoke the mantra of the *Acintyadhyāna-dhāraṇī*, saying:
*Namo bhagavate aparimitāyur-jñāna-suviniścita-tejo-rājāya tathāgatāyārhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya.* (That is to say:
Namo se sang khri du khe te po no ga da pa.)

with little effort, one attains great accomplishment,

One enters all the letter-gates of the dhāraṇī-mantras by taking non-apprehension as the skillful means.
One enters the letter-gate of the syllable A because one understands that all phenomena are fundamentally unarisen.
Entering the gateway of the letter *ka* (pronounced as in *kāñjala*), one understands that all phenomena are free from karmic activity.
Entering the gateway of the letter *kha*, one understands that all phenomena are equal to space and are ungraspable.
The letter-gateway *ga* (pronounced as in *gāyana*, or alternatively with the final *a* pronounced as *ka* and *la*) explains that all phenomena and all conditioned activities are unattainable.
The letter-gateway *gha* (with the initial *gha* pronounced as in *gha*) explains that all phenomena are unattainable as a unified whole.
One enters the letter-door *la* because one understands that all phenomena are free from dust and defilement.
One enters the letter-door *pa* because one understands that the teaching of the ultimate truth (*paramārtha*) regarding all phenomena is unattainable.
The letter-gateway *ja* is the entrance for understanding that all phenomena are without death or birth.
The letter-gateway *na* is the entrance for understanding that all phenomena are free from the marks of names and words and are thus ungraspable.
Entering the letter-gateway *ca* (pronounced *chī*, with a retroflex *ṛ*), one understands that the images of all phenomena are unapprehendable.
Entering the letter-gateway *ba*, one understands that all phenomena transcend the world.
Because the causal conditions for the limb of craving never manifest;
because one enters the gateway of the syllable *hūṃ* to understand that the arising of all phenomena is unattainable;
and because one enters the gateway of the syllable *ta* to understand that adversaries of all phenomena are unattainable.
One enters the gateway of the letter *ḍha* because all phenomena are understood as being tamed, quiescent, suchness, equal, and non-conceptual.
One enters the gateway of the letter *va* (pronounced with a retroflex) because all phenomena and all sentient beings are understood to be free from bondage.
One enters the gateway of the letter *ca*, for one understands that the grasping and maintaining of all phenomena is unattainable because it is pure.

One enters the gateway of the letter *ṣṭha*, for one understands that the nature of all phenomena—consisting of subduing, maintaining, and driving forth—is unattainable because it is characterized by pride.
One enters the letter-gateway *cha* (pronounced *chā*) because one realizes that the nourishment of all phenomena is unattainable.
One enters the letter-gateway *sa* (pronounced *sā*) because one realizes that all phenomena are without obstruction.
One enters the letter-gateway *ṇa* because all phenomena are understood as having no adversary that can be apprehended;
one enters the letter-gateway *va* because all phenomena are understood as having the path of speech and sound severed.
One enters the letter-gateway *ta* (pronounced with a retroflex *ṭa*) because the abiding place of the suchness (*tathatā*) of all phenomena is unapprehendable.
One enters the letter-gateway *ya* (pronounced with a retroflex *ṭya*) because the non-arising of all phenomena according to reality across all vehicles (*yāna*) is unapprehendable.
One enters the gateway of the syllable *ta* (pronounced with the *ṇya* reversal) because the dwelling place of all phenomena is unattainable;
one enters the gateway of the syllable *dha* because the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*) of all phenomena is unattainable.
One enters the gateway of the letter *pau* (pronounced with the *bi* and *yao* finals) because the equality of all phenomena cannot be apprehended;
one enters the gateway of the letter *ma* because the nature of "mine" (*mamakāra*) in all phenomena cannot be apprehended.
One enters the letter-gateway *pha* (pronounced *p'ei*, with the retroflex *r*) to understand that all phenomena are not solid or substantial, being like a mass of foam.
One enters the letter-gateway *ma* to understand that the bondage of all phenomena cannot be apprehended.
One enters the letter-gateway Ja because the arising of all phenomena is unapprehendable.
One enters the letter-gateway Śva (the combination of the two aforementioned letters) because the nature of stability in all phenomena is unapprehendable.
One enters the letter-gateway *ra* because one understands that all phenomena are free from all defilements of dust.
One enters the letter-gateway *la* because one understands that in all phenomena, no characteristics can be apprehended.
One enters the gateway of the syllable *ka* because the nature of all dharmas is found to be unattainable;
one enters the gateway of the syllable *śa* because the nature of the tranquility of all dharmas is found to be unattainable.
One enters the gateway of the letter Kha to understand that all phenomena are like the nature of space, for they are unattainable.
One enters the gateway of the letter Ṛ to understand that all phenomena are of an exhausted nature, for they are unattainable.

One enters the gateway of the letter *ḍha* because one realizes that the nature of all phenomena—which are the basis for maintaining what is possible (*sthāna*) and what is impossible (*asthāna*)—is unshakeable and ultimately unattainable.
One enters the gateway of the letter *hrīṃ* because one realizes that the nature of all phenomena as objects of cognition is unattainable.
One enters the letter-lakāra gate because the nature of attachment to all phenomena is unapprehendable;
one enters the letter-ha-kāra gate because the causal nature of all phenomena is unapprehendable.
One enters the gateway of the letter *ba* because the destructible nature of all phenomena is found to be unattainable.
One enters the gateway of the letter *ku* because the nature of all phenomena being obscured by desire and pleasure is found to be unattainable.
One enters the letter-gateway *saṃ* (pronounced *sāṅ*) because the nature of all phenomena as being capable of being recollected is found to be unattainable.
One enters the letter-gateway *dva-bha* (the same as above) because the nature of all phenomena as being capable of being summoned is found to be unattainable.
One enters the syllable-gateway *sra* because the courageous and heroic nature of all phenomena is unattainable;
one enters the syllable-gateway *oṃ* because the thick and equal nature of all phenomena is unattainable.
One enters the letter-door *da* because the nature of accumulation of all phenomena is unattainable.

One enters the letter-door *e-hi-ye-he* (pronounced with the retroflex *he*) because all phenomena are free from clamor and contention, and the acts of going, coming, walking, standing, sitting, and lying down are unattainable.
One enters the gateway of the letter *pha* because the pervasive retribution of all phenomena is found to be unattainable;
one enters the gateway of the letter *saṃ* (pronounced as in *sanghe*) because the nature of the accumulation of aggregates (*skandha*) in all phenomena is found to be unattainable.
One enters the gateway of the letter *iṣa* because the nature and characteristics of senescence in all phenomena are found to be unattainable.
One enters the gateway of the letter *ja* because the footprints of the accumulation of all phenomena are found to be unattainable.
Entering the *pha* syllable-gateway, one understands that all phenomena are ultimately unattainable.
Entering the *ga*, *ṅa*, *na*, *ma*, *hūṃ*, *phaṭ*, *svāhā* syllable-gateways, one understands all samayas.
All are sovereign and able to swiftly accomplish all matters, the samaya, artha, and siddhi.
O Lotus-Handed One, such a syllable-gateway is the fundamental limit for entering into the Dharma.
Apart from these syllables that represent all phenomena, nothing else can be found. Why is this?
O Lotus-Handed One, such is the meaning of these syllables.
It cannot be proclaimed, it cannot be displayed;
it cannot be grasped, it cannot be written down or maintained;
it cannot be observed or received.
Because they are free from all characteristics.

The meanings and principles of all dharmas enter this gateway and only then become manifest.

This is called entering the gates of all syllables.

Regarding all sounds and speech that can express and signify,

One who is able to hear such seal-signs and seal-words that enter all letter-gates,
