By virtue of these causes and conditions, one attains twenty kinds of sublime qualities.
What are these twenty? They are as follows:
one attains powerful mindfulness.
One attains superior shame and remorse;
one attains firm and steadfast power;
and one attains the essential purport of the Dharma.
They attain superior awakening;
they attain preeminent wisdom;
they attain unimpeded eloquence.
They attain the gate of dhāraṇī;
they attain freedom from doubt and confusion;
and they attain the state where neither anger nor attachment arises toward speech that is either contrary or compliant.
One attains dwelling in equanimity free from high and low;
one attains skillfulness regarding the vocal expressions of sentient beings;
and one attains skillfulness regarding the aggregates, skillfulness regarding the bases, skillfulness regarding dependent origination, and skillfulness regarding causes and conditions.
He is skillful in attaining the knowledge of the superior and inferior faculties of beings; skillful in the knowledge of others' minds;
skillful in observing and interpreting astrology and calendrics;
and skillful in the knowledge of the divine ear.
Skill in the knowledge of recollecting past lives;
skill in the knowledge of supernormal powers; skill in the knowledge of death and rebirth;
and skill in attaining the knowledge of the exhaustion of outflows.
He attains skill in the knowledge of what is possible and what is impossible,
and he attains skill in the modes of deportment such as coming and going.
Padmapāṇi, these are the twenty kinds of sublime qualities.

Padmapāṇi is the upholder.
He dwells in the four foundations of mindfulness. What are these four?

The four foundations of mindfulness: first, the foundation of mindfulness of the body; second, the foundation of mindfulness of feelings; third, the foundation of mindfulness of the mind; and fourth, the foundation of mindfulness of phenomena.
One should practice the dhāraṇī-mantras.
Taking non-apprehension as the skillful means,
although one dwells in the contemplation of the body with respect to the internal body,
and although one dwells in the contemplation of the body with respect to the external body.
Although he dwells contemplating the body in the internal body,
although he dwells contemplating feelings in the internal feelings,
and although he dwells contemplating feelings in the external feelings.
Although one dwells observing feelings in feelings internally and externally;
although one dwells observing the mind in the mind internally and externally.
Although he dwells observing the mind in the internal mind,
although he dwells observing phenomena in the internal phenomena,
and although he dwells observing phenomena in the external phenomena.
Although he dwells in the contemplation of phenomena regarding internal and external phenomena,
he ultimately does not give rise to discursive thoughts associated with the body, feelings, mind, or phenomena;
he is ardently energetic, possessed of mindfulness and clear comprehension.
In order to subdue worldly greed and sorrow,
this is the locus of the four foundations of mindfulness for those who uphold [this practice].
O Padmapāṇi, one who practices in this way—
It should be known that this person is equal to me when I first set out on the ground of the causal stage as a bodhisattva,

To the right, Bodhisattva Tārā sits in the half-lotus posture, holding an utpala flower;
behind her, Bodhisattva Bhṛkuṭī sits in the half-lotus posture;
and to the left, Bodhisattva Śvetā sits in the half-lotus posture, holding a kumuda flower.
Behind [him] is the Bodhisattva Padmaśūnyāri, holding a lotus flower and seated in the half-lotus posture (ardhaparyaṅka).
The Bodhisattva wears a crown, necklaces, earrings, bracelets, and various celestial garments.
Adorned with various ornaments, he sits upon a lotus throne.
Beneath the seat to the right is the Bodhisattva Amoghapāśa,
kneeling with palms joined and holding a lasso.
Thereafter, there were the Bodhisattva of the Perfection of Generosity, the Bodhisattva of the Perfection of Ethical Discipline,
the Bodhisattva of the Perfection of Forbearance, and the Bodhisattva of the Perfection of Diligence.
The Bodhisattva Dhyānapāramitā;
beneath her seat to the left is the four-armed Bodhisattva Amoghapāśakrodharāja.
With palms joined in *añjali*,
holding a lotus flower in one hand and a noose (*pāśa*) in the other,
he sits in a long-kneeling posture (*utkuṭukāsana*).
Subsequently, there are the Bodhisattvas of the Prajñāpāramitā, the Bodhisattvas of the Upāyakauśalyapāramitā,
the Bodhisattvas of the Praṇidhānapāramitā, the Bodhisattvas of the Balapāramitā,
and the Bodhisattvas of the Jñānapāramitā.
The ten pāramitā bodhisattvas wear flower crowns,
necklaces, earrings, bracelets, and armlets, and are clad in white celestial garments;
adorned with various ornaments, each treads upon a lotus flower.
Following the Bodhisattva of the Dhyāna-pāramitā is the one-tufted rākṣasī, her body a true blue color,
with a face of wrathful anger and canine fangs protruding upward.
He wears a skull upon his head and possesses six arms.
Of his left hands, one holds a three-pronged vajra, another holds a lotus, and another holds a noose.
Of his right hands, one holds a battle-axe, another holds a wish-fulfilling staff (cintāmaṇi-danda), and another holds a trident.
Adorned with a snake as a necklace and wearing a tiger skin around the waist,
he sits in the half-lotus posture with a body encircled by flames behind the Bodhisattva Prajñāpāramitā.
The messenger Tattva is deep blue in color;
his face is wrathful with canine fangs protruding upward,
and he wears a skull upon his head and possesses eight arms.
The left hands hold a three-pronged vajra and a blue lotus;
one hand holds a trident and one hand has its palm raised.
The right hands hold a sword and a battle-axe.
In one hand he holds a curved knife and in the other a lasso;
his necklaces are made of snakes, and his waist is bound with tiger skin.
He sits in the half-lotus posture, his body enveloped in circular flames.
Beneath the seat of the Bodhisattva Amoghapāśa are the assembly of five ascetic ṛṣis and the assembly of devaputras,
holding various flowers and fruits, seated in the half-lotus posture.
Beneath the seat of the Unfailing Wrathful King (Amoghapāśakrodharāja) sit the assembly of five ascetic sages and the assembly of devaputras,
holding various flowers and fruits, seated in the half-lotus posture.
Above the head of Avalokiteśvara,
seven Buddhas are seated in cross-legged posture, extending horizontally; their right hands perform the gesture of stroking the head.
The lion throne emits various radiances.
Before the fourth Buddha stands the Vajradhara Guhyapati.
With one hand held at his chest, he grasps a vajra;
with the other hand, he holds a white fly-whisk,
gazing up in reverence at the Tathāgata.
Above the Seven Buddhas are Vairocana Buddha on the left,
Amitābha Buddha, and Lokeśvararāja Tathāgata on the right.
He sits in the full lotus posture upon a lion throne of jewels.
To the left and right of Avalokiteśvara,
thirty-two Buddhas are seated in the full lotus posture.
The lion throne emits various radiances.
Surrounding the exterior of the Buddha,
one should paint trident vajras and flower garlands.
Outside the flower garland,
draw thirty-two celestial deities arranged in a circle;
they hold various weapons and jewels, flowers, and fruits, and sit in the half-lotus posture.
Outside the thirty-two celestial deities,
one should draw, arranged in a circle, the Great Brahmā,
Nārāyaṇa, Maheśvara, and Īśvara.
Maheśvara, Śakra Devendra, the gods of the Heaven of Delight Without Pride (Abhāsvara), the gods of the Vast Fruit (Bṛhatphala),
and the gods of the Lesser Light (Parīttābha) and Tuṣita Heaven.
The Akaniṣṭha Heaven, the Nirmāṇarati Heaven,
the Śuddhāvāsa Heavens, the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven,
and the Paranirmitavaśavartin Heaven.
The Sun Deity, the Moon Deity, the Four Heavenly Kings, King Yama, Varuṇa, Kuvera,
Agni, Vāyu, and the deity Mahākāla.
The gods Nandikeśvara and Śvāra;
the nāga kings Nanda and Upananda; and the deities Bhṛṅgin and Bhaṭṭāraka.
The deity Maṇibhadra and the various celestial devas were adorned with flower garlands, garments, and diverse ornaments;
holding weapons and various jewels, flowers, and fruits, they sat in the half-lotus posture.
Outside the various devas,
draw a garland of lotuses and a garland of three-pronged vajras around the perimeter.
Outside this garland, [draw further].
Around the perimeter, one hundred and eight lotus flowers made of the seven precious gems are depicted in full bloom.
Upon each pedestal, either one hand or two hands are placed;
in each hand, various mudrās are held, encircling a blaze of fiery light.
In the midst of that mountain, one should paint the nāga kings Nanda and Upananda;
within their palace, all the nāga maidens hold precious flowers,
gazing upon and offering them to the Bodhisattva.
To the right of the mountain base are the goddesses Apratimā, Vasundharā, Bhūmī, Vimalā, Sasya, and Oṣadhī.
To the left of the base of the mountain are the goddesses Śrīdevī, Sarasvatī, and Saṅkarī.
The Śaṅkhinī goddesses, the Rākṣasī goddesses,
and all these other goddesses were adorned with various ornaments, such as flower garlands and garments.
Holding various precious flowers, they gaze upon and offer them to the Bodhisattva.
Above the exterior of the assembly hall of the precious palace,
eight stūpas containing śarīra relics are depicted arranged horizontally.
To the right of that stūpa, paint a Bodhi tree;
beneath the tree is Śākyamuni Buddha,
seated in the full lotus posture upon a lion throne of jewels.
Facing Avalokiteśvara, he displays the mudrā of preaching the Dharma;
to his right is the Venerable Ānanda,
and to his left is the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi Guhyapati.
His body is azure in color;
one hand holds a white whisk and the other palm grasps a vajra.
He stands to the left and right of the Buddha, amidst the assembly of great bodhisattvas.
The assembly of ascetic rishis and the assembly of devaputras held precious flowers, stood with bodies bowed,
and faced Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva to make offerings.
To the left of that stūpa, Śākyamuni Buddha is depicted,
sitting cross-legged upon a lion throne made of jewels in the posture of preaching the Dharma;
to his right is the Venerable Ānanda.
To the left was the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi Guhyapati,
his body blue in color, holding a white fly-whisk in one hand and a vajra in the other.
Surrounding the Buddha on both sides were the great bodhisattvas, śrāvakas, and pratyekabuddhas.
Facing toward Avalokiteśvara,
there were the assembly of ascetic sages and the assembly of devaputras beneath the pavilion.
Holding precious flowers, they stood with bodies bowed,
facing Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva in worship.
Above the stupa, there were horizontal rows as well as vertical rows extending to the left and right.
The fifty-four Buddhas sit cross-legged upon lion thrones made of jewels.
To the right of Avalokiteśvara,
the mantra-practitioner kneels and gazes up at the Bodhisattva.
With one hand holding a rosary and the other hand grasping a flower-incense burner—
World-Honored One, this is the samaya of the mantra of the Heart-King Dhāraṇī of Amoghapāśa.
The inconceivable visualization of the dhāraṇī-mantra, the world-transcending liberation maṇḍala image,
is named the place where all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas pay homage.
It is also called the Great Secret Image Samaya of the Bodhimaṇḍa Contemplated by the Eyes of All Tathāgatas.
If there be bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, kings, princes, queens, court ladies, ministers, officials, brahmins, or any other people;
Upon beholding this image, those who feel joy, faith, and devotion and offer various kinds of worship will be purified of all their immeasurable heavy offenses for slandering the Buddha,
slandering the Dharma, and slandering the bodhisattvas, śrāvakas, and pratyekabuddhas.
Those who were destined to fall into and dwell within the Avīci Hell shall all have their [karmic retribution] extinguished;
they shall obtain a pure body and achieve mastery through its integration.
That is to say, they serve and make offerings to ninety-nine hundred-thousand-koṭi-nayuta-gaṅgā-sand numbers of Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas throughout the ten directions,
as they sit at the site of enlightenment and turn the great wheel of Dharma.

The mass of merit and virtue of all the Buddhas and the great assembly of Bodhisattvas within the precious palaces of Mount Potalaka shall be attended to and honored; such is the mass of merit and virtue.
If there are sentient beings whose faith is pure,
who join their palms, gaze upon [the image], praise it, and prostrate,
they shall immediately attain the corresponding reception of an immeasurable mass of great merit.
Through the mindful protection and empowerment of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva,
one shall attain the supernormal powers of all Tathāgatas,
and by maintaining control over body and mind, the six sense faculties will become pure.
Greed, anger, jealousy, and all heavy karmic offenses shall be completely extinguished.
One will always be loved and respected by the people of the world;
one’s life will not be cut short by premature death or illness, and one will be freed from all past obstacles.
After the end of one's life, one shall go to the Land of Peace and Bliss to be born miraculously upon a lotus throne.
This is the image of the supramundane liberation maṇḍala,
for it enables one to advance toward the unsurpassed and peerless Dharma.

Chapter Twenty-Seven: The Chapter on the Mantra of the Samaya of Liberation to Which All Bodhisattvas Pay Homage, Part One. The World-Honored One said: "The mantra of the samaya of liberation to which all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas pay homage is as follows:"
Out of great compassion for all sentient beings,
if one merely recites and maintains this,
the gates to all Buddha-lands in the ten directions will open of their own accord.
All Buddhas and Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas,
all dhāraṇī deities and maṇḍala deities,
and all celestial gods shall provide protection and guardianship.
One shall obtain various methods of mantra, maṇḍala, and mudrā.
This is the mantra of the Samaya of Liberation, which is pure, supramundane, and venerated by all infinite and boundless bodhisattvas.

O Seven-Syllable World-Honored One,
this mantra is the object of veneration for all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas;
it is also the profound treasury within the secret hearts of all Tathāgatas.
Furthermore, this is the supreme secret heart-mantra of Avalokiteśvara;
it can eliminate all latent propensities and karmic obstructions,
and it can purify all paths of supramundane dharmas.
One is able to enter the gate of the lineage of all Tathāgatas, which is not empty.

With this ocean-cloud samaya offering of the mantra of the perfection of generosity, which arises unfailingly from all Tathāgatas,
one consecrates the body and mind to cultivate and prepare for the offering.
One shall attain the complete correspondence with the perfection of all giving of all Tathāgatas of the ten directions,
continuing until the attainment of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
One's merit shall not be lost or diminished.

The Mantra of the Pāramitā of Pure Ethics: *Namo sarvabuddhānāṃ* (1) *Namo āryā-avalokiteśvarāya* (2–3) *Bodhisattvāya* (4) *Mahāsattvāya* (5) *Mahākāruṇikāya* (6) *Oṃ amoghaśūra* (7) *Sara sara* (8) *Vara vara* (9) *Sattva-vapratoma* (10) *Mibusiḍa-bhuja* (11) *Dhara dhara* (12) *Samantraparigṛhīta* (13) *Hūṃ phaṭ svāhā* (14) Blessed One, if there are sentient beings who cultivate and purify the ethical precepts...
With this ocean-like cloud of samaya offerings consisting of the mantra of the perfection of pure ethical discipline born from the non-empty bodhi of all Tathāgatas,
I empower my body and mind.
One shall attain perfect correspondence with the perfection of all pure ethical discipline (śīla-pāramitā) of all Tathāgatas of the ten directions;
the fragrance of one's virtue will be exquisitely pervasive, filling the ten directions.
If a bhikṣu or bhikṣuṇī has violated the pure precepts,
they shall abstain from food for one day on the fifteenth day of the waxing moon and recite this samaya.
One shall attain the aggregate of pure ethical discipline (*śīlaskandha*) and remain endowed with it until reaching unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment, never falling away from it.
The mantra of the perfection of patience (*kṣāntipāramitā*): *Namaḥ sarvabuddhabodhisattvebhyaḥ*. (1)
Namaḥ āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya oṃ amoghadhiṣṭhite sarvabodhisattva-pūjite. (1) (2) (3) (4) (5) (6) (7) (8)
Kṣamaṇi (9) kṣaṇa kṣaṇa (10) mahā-maitrī-karuṇa (11) sattva-ghora (12) mahā-kāruṇika (13) sarvasattvavaśīkaraṇi (14) hūṃ phaṭ.

*Svāhā*. Fifteenth phrase: "Blessed One, if there are sentient beings who cultivate peaceful patience, they shall thereby offer this ocean-like cloud of samaya of the mantra of the perfection of patience—the unerring, unsurpassed Dharma-awakening of all Tathāgatas."
By blessing the body and mind,
one shall attain perfect correspondence with all the perfections of patience (kṣānti-pāramitā) of all Tathāgatas of the ten directions,
never regressing until the attainment of unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment.

The Mantra of the Perfection of Vigor: Namo sarvabuddhānāṃ. (1) Namo ārya- (2) Vajracchediśvarāya. (3) Bodhisattvāya. (4) Mahāsattvāya. (5) Mahākāruṇikāya. (6) Oṃ mahāmīrye (7) Āmukha-milocite. (8) Cara cara. (9) Jvalini jvalaya. (10) Mahāvala. (11) Vala vala. (12) Mahāsādhanagavalabodhani. (13) Hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. (14) World-Honored One, if there are sentient beings who cultivate and practice vigor, [they shall attain success].
With this ocean-like cloud of samaya offerings of the mantra of the Perfection of Diligence of All Tathāgatas, which is non-empty and does not abandon saṃsāra,
I empower my body and mind.
One shall attain the complete correspondence with the perfection of all the vigor of all Tathāgatas of the ten directions,
never regressing until reaching unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

The Mantra of the Dhyāna-pāramitā: Namo sarvadharmatānām (1) Namo āryāṇām (2) Vairocaniśvarāya (3) Bodhisattvāya (4) Mahāsattvāya (5) Mahākāruṇikāya (6) Oṃ sarvadharmatānām (7) Mahāmogha-kāruṇa (8) Jaṅghana-samādhi (9) Mimukṣāpāra-gate pāra-saṃgate (10) Cūru cūru (11) Hūṃ phaṭ svāhā (12) World-Honored One, if there are sentient beings who cultivate and practice meditative concentration (*dhyāna*), [they shall attain this mantra].
With this ocean-cloud samaya offering of the mantra of the non-empty, unsurpassed meditative concentration (dhyāna-pāramitā) of all Tathāgatas,
one consecrates the body and mind.
As for the form of Avalokiteśvara:

one who wears the image of Avalokiteśvara upon their crown shall attain the perfect correspondence with all the meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*) and perfections (*pāramitā*) of all the Tathāgatas of the ten directions.
One shall be born in the buddha-field of Amitāyus and attain the direct realization and mastery of all samayas,
never again falling back until the attainment of unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment.
The Prajñāpāramitā Mantra: 1. Namaḥ sarvadharmatebhyaḥ 2. Namo ’rye 3. Vajracchediśvarāya 4.
Bodhisattvāya 5. Mahāsattvāya 6. Mahākāruṇikāya 7. Oṃ ārya...
Ā Vairocana (12) Bhagavan (13) Parākrama (14) Vajraketu (15) Jāṅgulīśvara (16) Mahāparākrama (17) Varadāna (18)
Bhaṇi (18) mahāpāraśreṇya (19) pratimudrāṇi pūṇe (20) hūṃ phaṭ svāhā (21). Blessed One,
if there are sentient beings who cultivate the Prajñāpāramitā...
With this samaya offering of the ocean-like cloud of mantras of the non-empty, unsurpassed Prajñāpāramitā of all Tathāgatas,
I empower my body and mind.
One shall attain perfect correspondence with all the skillful means of the *prajñāpāramitā* of all Tathāgatas throughout the ten directions,
never regressing until the attainment of unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment.
The Amoghapāśakalparāja Sūtra, Scroll Fifteen; The Amoghapāśakalparāja Sūtra, Scroll Sixteen.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Bodhiruci of India during the Great Tang Dynasty.
All Bodhisattvas pay homage. Chapter Twenty-Seven, Part Two:

The Mantra of the Ground-Purification (Kṣitigarbha). The mantra for purifying the ground is: Oṃ ā-mogha-mi-mukta-saṃvara | mahā-pūta-māle | dhara-dhara | dharidhari | mahā-tapodakamala | āmitābha-mukuṭa-dhara | hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. This is the mantra.
With the miraculous light of the King of Wrathful Deities,
empower white mustard seeds and scented water,
and scatter them everywhere across the site where the mandala is to be constructed.
It is perfectly circular, measuring one yojana,
and as pure as vaidūrya crystal. If there are sentient beings who tread upon this mandala ground, [they will be purified].
Upon the relinquishing of this life, one will be reborn in a pure land,
attaining a perfect endowment of great merit and virtue,
continuing until the attainment of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
They shall never again fall back into decline.
Furthermore, if any birds or beasts tread upon this ground, they shall,
at the end of their lives, be reborn in the celestial realms.
The Dharani for Subduing Water: Oṃ ā-mogha-naru-ma-late mirikṣa-śakhe pratāra-puṣpa-phala mita-prahāna-vidyā-gaṇa puṣpa-karīṣaṇi rāṇa.
Suṇḍara sapta saṃhara saṃhara rāsaṃ hana rāvaṇa mi mi dhama citrara praluṭhaya pātaya māraya samasama samantānaya.
3. *pari-maṇḍala* 14. *pariśodhaya* 15. *māramaṇḍa* 16.
*mīmaṇḍa-kṣamaṇḍa* 17. *parijñāta* 18. *pṛthivīm āpṛccha* 19. *jvalam alaṃ mījaṅgha* 20. *śodhaya śoṣaya*
*Gatodhya* (21) *pramama mahā-sattva* (22) *hūṃ phaṭ namo ṣṭri-bhuve* (23) *hūṃ phaṭ svāhā* (24). This mantra,
by means of the miraculous light of the Wrathful King (*krodharāja*), [is empowered].
Consecrate white sandalwood-scented water and white mustard seeds,
and scatter them over river water, spring water,
well water, fruit trees, flowering trees, crops, and medicinal herbs.
If there are sentient beings who touch it, play with it, drink from it,
eat it, or even bathe in it,
they shall all be liberated from all karmic obstacles and transgressions.
One shall be reborn in the heavens or in a pure land,
and attain the realization of the samādhi of immeasurable wisdom and liberation.
Furthermore, if one receives empowerment and enters therein to bathe, [the same result shall be achieved].
There are three grades of immersion for the body:
first, immersing up to the neck; second, immersing up to the navel; and third, immersing up to the knees.
These constitute the methods of bathing through superior, middling, and inferior recitation.
The mantra for bathing, which purifies all defilements of sin and accomplishes the realization of the wisdom of all paths:
Oṃ āmukhi āmṛte amṛtodbhave amṛtavati sarva-pāpa-viśodhani svāhā.
Mārapakariṣye mahābodhisattvaparāyaṇe varapradhāraṇīpratiṣṭhe mahāmaṇiratnagarbhapratiṣṭhe maṇi maṇi śuddhe mā.
Hemogha-jintāmani-ja (10) hṛṇadya-ja (11) karyakamala (12) mahāmanipari-ja (13) hulu hulu (14) paravārapāṇi (15) mahābhujapara-tara (16)
16. *ni* 17. *duru duru* 18. *mahāsattva ṣṭīḥ* 19. *pariśodhaya* 20. *mama pāpam kṣapaya me dharmatām* 21.
*svāhā* This mantra is the light of the miraculous transformation of the Wrathful King (*krodharāja*).
Clearly visualize [the deity], and empower white sandalwood, saffron, and camphor with water.
Furthermore, recite the mantra of the Furenwang (Krodharāja).
Empower the scented bathing water for consecration, drinking,
and rinsing; perform a pure ablution, don the adorned robes,
and further sprinkle for purification while binding the mudrās for protection.
Visualize the assembly of noble ones as they offer three handfuls of water,
purifying their own bodies and minds to liberate sentient beings;
pay homage to the noble ones who have distanced themselves from the three poisons.
If one contemplates the purity of body and mind and enters the chamber of refinement,
one will then be able to dispel all defilements and obstacles;
all vināyakas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, and malevolent spirits will not cause disturbance.
Furthermore, one will attain peace and security in actions, work, sleep, and dreams.
All Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, devas, and celestial spirits will gaze upon and protect them.
After the end of their life, they shall be reborn upon a lotus pedestal in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
One shall possess the knowledge of past lives and not regress until reaching enlightenment.

The Boundary-marking Mantra is: Oṃ ā-mogha-paṭu-mati-male padma-rasāla-samanta-ukṣi svāhā. This mantra, through the majestic power and miraculous transformations of the Furenwang (Krodharāja), [accomplishes this].
Consecrate a five-colored thread to mark the boundaries of the maṇḍala.
The mantra for the colored powders is: Oṃ ārya-maitreya maitri-jitāra-santāra saṃvara-pravarapūjine svāhā. This mantra, through the miraculous radiance of the Wrathful King, [accomplishes the task].
Consecrate colored powders, scented water,
and fragrant resin to paint all the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, all celestial deities, all mudrās, and all mountain flowers, aquatic creatures, and beasts.
The mantra of the Jewel Ground is: Oṃ āḥ mukuṭa parimaṇḍala prasādaya hūṃ. This mantra, by means of the miraculous radiance of the wrathful king’s divine transformations, [accomplishes its purpose].
Empower white mustard seeds to demarcate the boundaries of the mandala site and form the jeweled stairway.

The boundary-binding mantra is: *Oṃ ā-mukāya mi-mi-dhāru-pa-mi jī-taraṇa-śā-ni samaha-simeṃ bandhaya dhuru dhuru hūṃ phaṭ svāhā*. This mantra possesses the majestic power and miraculous transformations of the Wrathful King.
Consecrate white mustard seeds and scented water.
Scatter them to demarcate the boundaries of the mandala and bind the Vajra City.

Recite the protection mantra: Oṃ ā-mukāya rakṣaṇi bhañja ha saṭṭi tura tura svāhā. By means of the majestic power and miraculous transformations of this Wrathful King’s mantra, [the protection is established].
Consecrate white mustard seeds and scented water.
Sprinkle them upon yourself as a protection for the body.
The Mantra of the Topknot is: Oṃ āmukha-jūṭā-maṇi hulu hulu nagnāpasa-paṃ hūṃ svāhā. This mantra possesses the majestic power and miraculous transformations of the Wrathful King.
One should empower the hair by arranging it into a topknot (*uṣṇīṣa*).

The mantra for protecting the disciple is: *Oṃ āmukha ṭi kṣe samantena mahāpārśve phuru phuru svāhā*. This mantra, through the miraculous light of the Wrathful King (*Krodharāja*), [accomplishes this].
Consecrate white mustard seed ashes.
Have the disciple, their companions, and attendants apply them as a protective amulet.
The mantra for purifying the hands is: Oṃ āmukha-jvala-mīle sulu sulu svāhā. This mantra possesses the radiant light of the miraculous transformations of the Wrathful King.
Consecrate pure water to wash the hands and rinse the body.

For the mantra to purify the mouth and face, recite: *Oṃ āryamogha-āmitateja-munivara-jvara-jvara svāhā*. This mantra possesses the radiant light of the miraculous transformations of the Wrathful King (*Krodharāja*).
Consecrate pure water with mantras to wash the hands and face,
rinse the mouth and teeth,
and apply it to the eyes, ears, and shoulders.
Perform the ritual recitation.
The mantra for treating robes is: Oṃ āmogha-vaśīkari julu julu svāhā. This mantra, by means of the radiant spiritual transformations of the Wrathful King (Krodharāja), [accomplishes its purpose].
Consecrate the robes and fasten the belt according to the ritual rules.
The Armor Mantra is: Oṃ āmukha-sarvāṅga-baddhe varaṇi jiri jiri svāhā. This mantra, by means of the miraculous radiance of the Wrathful King’s divine transformations, [protects].
Consecrate saffron water and white mustard seeds, sprinkle them upon the body to prepare the armor, and don the cord with this mantra:
*Oṃ āmukha-māra-hamana-bhūje parjanya-dāna-pātra-svara svāhā*. This mantra possesses the miraculous radiance of the wrathful king.
Consecrate a five-colored thread as a knot;
wear it upon your body or hold it in your hand.
The empowerment mantra is: Oṃ ārya-mogha-pāśa-hṛdaya mamā-sarva-duḥkha-gatāni śamaya maṇi maṇi svāhā. This mantra possesses the radiant light of the miraculous transformations of the Wrathful King.
Consecrate the *argha* perfumed water. To perform the empowerment, recite the seat mantra:
Oṃ ā-mogha-paṭu-maṃtra-vaśanare dhara-dharani maṇḍale hūṃ. By means of this mantra, the radiant light of the wrathful king’s miraculous power [is manifested].
Having consecrated one’s seat, one should sit in the corresponding posture.
For sleeping, the mantra is: Oṃ ā-mogha-samaya-prati-pālaya svāhā. This mantra, by means of the radiant supernatural power of the Wrathful King, [accomplishes this].
Consecrate the bedding and lie down to sleep according to the Dharma.
Recite the Flower-holding Mantra: Oṃ ā-mukha-sara-pi-cuṣye praprapa hūṃ hūṃ. This mantra consecrates the incense and flowers.
One should extensively present offerings with clouds of various fragrant flower-oceans of the Amogharāja [Tathāgata].
The mantra for powdered incense is: *Oṃ āmukha-mimida-yantra-dhara-prasare puru-praṇipate svāhā*. This is the empowerment of the powdered incense through this mantra.
One should universally present offerings with various clouds of sea-like powdered incense of the Amogharāja.
The mantra for the unguent is: Oṃ āmogha-mi-mita-lepana-pratara-vīre vire svāhā. This is the empowerment of the unguent through this mantra.
With various clouds of oceans of un-empty king ointments, one should anoint the altar and present them as a universal offering.
For the incense mantra: Oṃ ā-mogha-gagana-saṃparāṇamiga-dhuru dhuru hūṃ. This is the mantra for consecrating the incense by means of empowerment.
One should universally present offerings with various clouds of the ocean of incense of Amogharāja.
For the mantra of food and drink, it is: Oṃ āmukāya śukla rasārasa arāta ramiṭara hūṃ. This is the mantra for consecrating the food and drink.
One should extensively present offerings with ocean-like clouds of various sweet foods and drinks from the Amogharāja [Tathāgata].
The mantra for the fruit is: Oṃ miyadhā ajamukha para para hūṃ. This mantra consecrates the fruit.
One should extensively present offerings with clouds of various fragrant fruits of the Amogharāja.
With the water-vessel mantra— *Oṃ āmukāya abhyudgate jñāpaya hūṃ phaṭ*— one consecrates the *argha* perfumed water.
One should universally present offerings with clouds of oceans of fragrant water from the *amogharāja* jewel *argha* vessels.
Adorned with mantras, the mantra is: Oṃ āḥ mūka mi-mi-ta maṇibhūsana dhara dhara svāhā. With this mantra, one consecrates the banners and flowers.
One should perform the offering with adornments consisting of clouds-seas of light-flames from various jeweled banners and parasols of the Amogharāja.
The mantra for the food vessels is: Oṃ ā-mukāya mi-mi-ta vāryaṇi jaya jaya svāhā. This mantra consecrates the vessels containing the food.
One should make extensive offerings with ocean-like clouds of various precious vessels and food and drink of the Amogharāja.
The mantra for entering the maṇḍala is: Oṃ ā-mukāya pā-ra-vāra-bhā-manapūme tra-tara svāhā. This is the mantra to be recited each time one enters the maṇḍala.
To empower the entrance to the maṇḍala,
one enters the maṇḍala to perform the ritual through the sovereign miraculous transformations of the various forms and characteristics of the Amogharāja.
The mantra for prostration is: Oṃ āḥ mūka namas-kāraṇa sarva-tathāgata-tantra-jri hūṃ. This mantra is praised by the ocean-like clouds of all bodily actions of the King of Amoghasiddhi.
Praise, eulogize, and prostrate to all Buddhas.
Present these offerings before them.
Recite the mantra for walking the path: *Oṃ ā-mogha-pāśa nṛ-nṛ vara-nṛ svāhā*. This mantra is the Ocean-Cloud of All Secret Practices of the King of Amogha.
Praise the practice of the path and present extensive offerings.
The mantra for awakening is: Oṃ ārya-mogha-samudra-ye tūṣṇīmbhava bhava bhava svāhā. This mantra is the Ocean-like Cloud of the Sovereign King of Unfailing Miraculous Transformations.
Praise and exhort all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and devas;
then recite the mantra: Oṃ ā-mogha-pratimaṇi-prakāśaya dhuru dhuru svāhā. This mantra is the Unfailing King Maṇi Ocean-Cloud.
The Praise and Exhortation for the Simultaneous Assembly of All Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Devas at the Maṇḍala.
The Mantra for Summoning is: Oṃ ā-mogha-ni-mantraṇa mi-muk-kṣe maṇḍala miri miri svāhā. This mantra is the Ocean-Cloud of the Miraculous Transformations of the Unfailing King (Amogharāja).
Praise and invoke all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and all celestial deities to take their seats within the maṇḍala.
Then, for the consecration of the lamps, recite this mantra: Oṃ āmukāya mahāraśmi-prabhāsahare prabhā-prabhā samantadīpe svāhā. This mantra empowers the lamp-light.
One should universally present offerings with the ocean-clouds of various radiances of the Amogharāja.
The empowered mantra is: Oṃ ā-mukha-prasāda-dhāraṇī mahāsāmanye jvale hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. This mantra is the ocean-cloud of the miraculous transformations of the Amogharāja.
Praise and entreat all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas to bestow their supernatural powers upon this samaya,
so that its signs may be manifested and accomplished.

The mantra for dispatching is: Oṃ ā-mukha-prasara hāse ti-pāra-sara sara gaccha svabhāvanam mi-sarvārthasi sara sara hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. This mantra is the Ocean-Cloud of the Miraculous Transformations of the King of Amoghasiddhi.
Praise all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and devas.
Perform the *argha* offering and dismissal.

The mantra for making offerings to the messenger is: Oṃ ajamukha samantaja padmaravara sara sara mahāpūtiśvara dṛdhi dṛdhi hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā. This is the mantra of the King of Amogha’s Ocean-Cloud of Miraculous Transformations.
Consecrate the *mudga* bean cakes, parched grain flour, radishes, the "three white foods," incense, flowers, and scented water,
and offer them as a sacrifice to the Vināyakas,
so that they may be filled with joy and refrain from creating obstacles.
Chapter Twenty-Eight: The Mudrās of the Supramundane Liberation Maṇḍala. O Bhagavān, this is the samaya of the mudrās of the supramundane liberation maṇḍala.
One is able to assemble all the lineages’ liberation maṇḍalas, mudrās, and samayas.
One shall realize the empowerment of the supramundane, unsurpassed samādhi maṇḍala and mudrā.
Joining the wrists so that they touch one another.
Place the two thumbs and the two little fingers so that they are bent into the palms;
flatten and bend their tips so that they touch one another and lie side by side.
The middle fingers of both hands are each bent like a hook,
with their tips one inch apart;
the two index fingers and the two ring fingers are held upright and slightly bent.
The tips of the two index fingers are two inches apart;
the tips of the two ring fingers are one and a half inches apart.
This is the seal for the mantra: *Oṃ bhaṭṭa-mabūṇe bhaṭṭa-makāre bhaṭṭa-mimale svāhā*. For the empowerment and liberation seal: join the palms with the hollows of the hands facing outward.
The two index fingers, the two ring fingers, and the two little fingers are extended upward,
slightly bent, with their tips joined together.
The two thumbs are held upright and pressed side by side.
The middle fingers of both hands are bent at the upper joints,
with their tips separated by half an inch;
the intervals between all ten fingers are three *fen* apart.
This seal-samādhi is the place where all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas pay homage.
If one constantly binds this seal and regards it with reverence,
one will perpetually behold the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
One shall cause them to definitely realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
The Seal-Mantra:
Oṃ bhaṭṭa-mi-svabhaṭṭa-mi-mi-mukṣe maṇḍala-bhaṭṭa-mabhūṇi hūṃ svāhā. The Tathāgata Liberation Seal: join the palms with the hollows of the hands joined together.
Press the backs of the joints of the two ring fingers with the two middle fingers.
Join the tips of the two index fingers, the two ring fingers, and the two little fingers so that they touch one another.
Hold the two thumbs upright, side by side, and touching.
This seal and samādhi can manifest the samādhi of true liberation.

For the seal and mantra that resolves all karmic obstructions: Oṃ ā-mogha va-jra-pāṇi-mudre mimi mimi svāhā. For the wish-fulfilling jewel seal (cintāmaṇi-mudrā), join the palms and place the two ring fingers and the two little fingers together.
Bend the fingers into the palms, crossing the right over the left;
the two thumbs are likewise in the palms, with the right placed over the left.
The two middle fingers are held upright, slightly bent at the tips, which touch one another.
Press the tips of the two index fingers against the middle joints on the sides of the two middle fingers,
with their tips touching.
This mudrā is for various offerings within samādhi.
One shall attain the karma of the unfailing perfection of the six pāramitās,
and the karma of the unfailing manifestation of the maṇḍalas of the supernatural powers and liberations of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
The mantra for purifying the five deeds of immediate retribution (*pañcānantarya*) so that they become non-empty is:
*Oṃ ā-mogha-maṇi maṇi mahāmaṇi paduma-maṇi svāhā*. For the Lotus Hook Seal (*padmāṅkuśamudrā*), join the wrists together and open the palms.
The two middle fingers are bent like hooks.
The two thumbs, the two index fingers, the two ring fingers, and the two little fingers are held upright and slightly bent.
The tips of the ten fingers are spaced one and a half inches apart.
This seal-samādhi can realize the unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment of all Tathāgatas.
It is the mantra of the supramundane liberation samādhi-seal:
Oṃ ā-mogha vaśire mahā-patīte jvala sujale mahājvale svāhā. [The mudrā: The vajra-lotus hook seal consists of joining the wrists together and opening the palms.
The two middle fingers are held upright and slightly bent, with their tips touching one another.
The two index fingers are bent,
pressing down upon the middle joints of the sides of the two middle fingers.
Like a hook:
extend the two thumbs, the two ring fingers, and the two little fingers, holding them upright and slightly bent.
[The same applies to] the two thumbs, the two ring fingers, and the two little fingers.
The distance between the heads [of the fingers] is one and a half inches.
One who performs this seal-samādhi as an offering will be able to realize the unexcelled,
perfect enlightenment, supernatural powers, and majestic virtue of all Tathāgatas.
The Samādhi-mudrā mantra: Oṃ āmukha sarvatathāgata-abhūṣita kuru kuru svāhā. For the homage mudrā, join the palms with the hollows of the hands facing upward.
Spread the two thumbs and the two little fingers apart,
with their tips separated by one and a half inches;
the two middle fingers are held upright and slightly bent.
The distance between the tips of the two thumbs is six finger-widths;
the tips of the two middle fingers [are likewise];
and the tips of the two ring fingers [are likewise].
The tips of the two index fingers are three parts apart;
the two index fingers and the two ring fingers are held upright with their tips touching one another.
The index, middle, and ring fingers should all be kept apart at their joints without touching one another.

By means of this seal and samādhi, one is able to realize and behold the pure body of Avalokiteśvara, attain all samādhis, and achieve non-retrogression toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
The Mantra of the Samādhi-mudrā:

Oṃ āvalokite mahāsattva sara sara samantabhasa guṇadhara amṛtabhāṣamukhatara jñātāmukha nava-janma-nirmita jara jara sañjara pūrvaniḥśvara pratimāpūrja svāhā. World-Honored One, these are the seven great mudrās.
He is able to manifest and transform the assembly for turning the wheel of Dharma within the palace of Avalokiteśvara.
Each of these mudrās numbers one koṭi,
surrounded before and after by the great mudrās of his attendants.
If there are sentient beings who bathe themselves, apply fragrant ointments, and wear clean garments,
and who three times each day stand before Avalokiteśvara,
or before a Buddha, or before a stūpa containing relics;
Receiving whatever offerings of incense, flowers, food, and drink one may obtain,
one should generate a heart of great compassion for all sentient beings and entreat all Buddhas of the ten directions.
They cause the great rain of Dharma to fall for the benefit of sentient beings;
reaching the stainless realm, they abide in the Dharmakāya,
contemplating their own bodies as having the characteristics of the Dharmadhātu.
The equality of intrinsic nature,
the pure dharma-nature,
is equal in extent to the dharma-realm and the pure void.
Visualize one's own body as being anointed with white sandalwood, aloeswood, and camphor; then,
with hands joined, form such mudrās as these.
If one daily binds the seven-koṭi mudrās of the samaya, sealing the body with these mudrās,
one will immediately attain the eradication of all slander and destruction of the True Dharma,
as well as all disparagement of the noble ones and sages.

The roots of goodness and the mass of merit from committing the five deeds of immediate retribution, as well as from serving and making offerings to ninety-two hundred thousand koṭi-nayuta Ganges-sand-like Tathāgatas with various vessels.
In perfect accord with the fulfillment of the six pāramitās,
one shall abide in the stage of non-retrogression and be further sustained and protected by all Buddhas and Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
All devas, nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas shall all protect them.
Īśvara-deva, Maheśvara-deva, the Four Heavenly Kings, Yama-rāja, Varuṇa-deva, Kubera-deva, and Kumāra-deva shall all protect them.
One shall attain the Dharma-body of the Tathāgata’s adamantine *śarīra*,
which cannot be harmed by worldly poisons, venomous insects, water, fire, swords, staves, or any other such calamities.
They shall constantly dream of the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva;
auspicious omens will abound,
and they will be revered and remembered by people of noble lineage.
All the sages of the Heaven of the Thirty-three revere and rely upon him.
Chapter Twenty-nine: Liberation Corresponding to the Supramundane. The Blessed One is the supreme samaya of the Lotus Maṇḍala, the supramundane yoga of liberation and miraculous power.
It can manifest śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, kings, princes, queens, concubines, ministers, officials, and all people— both boys and girls—
as well as the supramundane dharmas and the dharmas of arising and ceasing throughout the past, present, and future.
The phenomena of wholesome results and unwholesome results;
the marks of wealth and nobility, and the marks of poverty and low status;
the marks of long and short lifespans, and the marks of the wheel of birth and death.
Furthermore, he manifested the forms of Mahābrahmā, Śakra-devendra, Nārāyaṇa, Maheśvara,
and even all the other deities, nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, and so forth.
The various appearances of the hungry ghosts and the Avīci hell;
the signs of famine and the signs of abundance within the land;
the signs of pestilence and the signs of calamity and misfortune.
Regarding the signs of wind and rain during the four seasons, whether timely or untimely:
one who upholds this Dharma should speak truthful words according to the teaching and give rise to great compassion,
relying upon all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Mahāsattvas.
Benefiting all sentient beings without end,
his mind never abandons the vow for omniscience;
he shall surely bring about their salvation and purification, maintaining his body and robes and upholding the pure precepts.
One should not give rise to arrogance toward any person, whether they possess precepts or lack them;
by practicing with an even mind and cultivating oneself according to the teachings,
one will achieve accomplishment.
Purify [the site] according to the Dharma and fashion a silver lotus flower.
Use a mirror one cubit in length as the face of the lotus pedestal,
and adorn it with four rafters of precious jewel garlands.
One should fashion an image of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva from silver according to the Dharma, measuring one chi and two cun.
He has one face with three eyes and four arms;
one hand holds a trident, and the other hand holds a noose.
Holding a lotus flower in one hand and a wish-fulfilling jewel (*cintāmaṇi*) in the palm of the other,
he sits in the full lotus posture (*paryaṅka*),
wearing a jeweled crown upon his head that contains an emanation Buddha.
The interior of the image is hollow; within it are placed one hundred grains of śarīra relics, along with camphor and white sandalwood incense.
It is further adorned with flower crowns, necklaces, earrings, bracelets, and various celestial garments.
Place a mirror upon the heart;
smear the ground with pure clay to create a maṇḍala,
five cubits in circumference and square, with four wide-open gates.
In the inner courtyard, one should paint an eight-petaled lotus flower made of the seven precious gems in full bloom.
Upon its petals are the Bodhisattva Tārā, the Bodhisattva Śvetā,
the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi Guhyakādhipati, and the Bodhisattva Bhṛkuṭī.
The Bodhisattva Padmaśūṇḍalin and the Bodhisattva Vimalamati;
the Bodhisattva Aṣṭāpāpaharaṇa, Avalokiteśvara, and Siddhikarāja;
at the right of the eastern gate of the outer enclosure are Mahābrahmā and Śakra-devendra.
To the left are the gods Īśvara and Maheśvara;
at the right of the southern gate are the gods Kumāra and Kuvereśvara;
to the left are Yama and the terrestrial deities.
To the right of the north gate are Nārāyaṇa and Maheśvara;
to the left are the goddess Vimalā and the goddess Anuvratā.
To the right of the west gate are the goddesses Varuṇī and Vasundharā.
To the left is the one-tufted rākṣasī, the Vajra-Dūtī messenger;
at the eastern gate is the goddess Saṃkhanī;
at the southern gate is the goddess Puṣpanandī.
At the western gate is the goddess Puṇyavatī;
at the northern gate is the goddess Sarasvatī;
and in the four intermediate directions are the Four Great Kings.
The inner enclosure is the realm of the Lotus Garland;
the outer enclosure is the realm of the Trident-Vajra Garland.
In the center is placed the Silver Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.
Facing east,
various banners and flowers were arranged as adornments,
and the perimeter was demarcated by cords of five-colored thread.
Arrange argha water, the "three white" foods,
various kinds of food and fruit, incense burners,
and many exquisite flower garlands, all set out according to the ritual rules.
One should prepare white sandalwood incense, aloeswood incense, storax incense,
and camphor incense, mixed with rock honey, and burn them as an offering.
At that time, one should enter and exit after bathing and apply fragrant ointments.
Wearing clean garments and eating the three white foods,
one should protect and uphold [the practice] according to the Dharma during the six periods of day and night.
With resolute determination and without fear, one should contemplate the body as being like an image.
The appearance and countenance of the maṇḍala are majestic and stern;
with a joyful heart within, one subdues and establishes the six sense faculties,
which are tranquil and pure white.
Prostrating with the five limbs touching the ground, I pay sincere and reverent homage to all the Tathāgatas of the Buddhas throughout the ten directions and the three periods of time,
and to all the maṇḍalas, mudrās, and samayas of the Mahāyāna scriptural treasury.
Having established the boundary and performed the invocation, sit in the cross-legged posture.
Generate the bodhicitta and contemplate the five aggregates and elements:
the nature of both the grasper and the grasped is non-constructive.
One’s own body is empty and quiescent;
facing west, one opens the eyes wide, causing the eyelids to throb,
and gazes intently upon Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.
Recite the Mantra of the Wrathful King, the Mother Dhāraṇī Mantra,
the Universal Mind-Seal Mantra, and the Inconceivable Contemplation Dhāraṇī Mantra.
The Siddhirāja mantra. At that time,
one should separately empower the silver lotus with the light [of the mantra] of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva,
using the mantra and mudrā of the Krodharāja (Wrathful King) for oneself.
Through the empowerment of consecration,
light radiates from within the lotus mirror,
and nectar-water flows forth from the body of the image of Avalokiteśvara.
By emitting various rays of light and emitting light from one's own body,
one shall obtain the non-empty, stainless, and pure aggregate-body (skandha-kāya),
and achieve the samaya of the King of Non-Emptiness Mind.
At that time, while Kṣipra recited the mantra of the Wrathful King,
Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva appeared within a mirror and praised him, saying:
"Excellent, excellent!"
"You have now accomplished the ritual of the mirror-maṇḍala and mudrās of the supramundane and mundane realms.
What vow do you require that I shall fulfill for you?
Request all your aspirations through this offering of argha."
All shall attain fulfillment.
This includes śramaṇas, brahmins, kings, princes, queens, consorts, court ladies, ministers, officials,
and all the people who gaze upon this image in the mirror.
They all beheld various manifestations of supernatural powers and transformations;
they also saw the various signs of the karmic fruits of their own good and evil deeds throughout the past, present, and future;
and they saw the great assemblies within the palace of Avalokiteśvara on Mount Potalaka in all buddha-fields.
They also perceive all the auspicious and inauspicious signs of the seasons in the world,
with the sole exception of those who harbor jealousy, deceit, crookedness, doubt, or pride;
who violate the precepts, hold wrong views, or steal the samaya.
Cāṇḍāla bhikṣus and bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas and upāsikās, as well as various non-Buddhists and people of evil discipline—
all others behold it.
The Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara has spoken these words of praise and the means for extinguishing all defilements, obstacles, and grave offenses;
this definitive teaching is not false.
Those who practice this dharma should do so during the six periods of day and night.
Provided one does not become indolent, negligent, or lazy, one will swiftly achieve accomplishment.
*Amoghapāśakalparāja*, Fascicle Sixteen; *Amoghapāśakalparāja*, Fascicle Seventeen.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Bodhiruci of India during the Great Tang Dynasty.
Chapter Thirty: The Chapter on the Mantra of the Root Padma-śekhara Dhāraṇī.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, the Lord of Secrets, [spoke].
With palms joined in reverence, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, I have now reflected and observed Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva Mahāsattva."
This Great Liberation of the Lotus Mandala and Seal Samaya, consisting of the mantra of the Heart-King Dhāraṇī of Amoghapāśa,
is exceedingly profound, vast, and immeasurable.
It is difficult to understand, difficult to enter, and difficult to achieve mastery in.
Contemplating within these teachings,
there are immeasurable methods of maṇḍalas and immeasurable methods of mudrās.
The immeasurable forms of the Dharma, the immeasurable rules, and the dharmas of majestic deportment are like the great ocean, Mount Sumeru the king of mountains,
space, a mirage, and the number of atoms.
Furthermore, the Tathāgata’s immeasurable great wisdom—
wisdom with no equal and wisdom beyond conceptualization—
is entirely beyond the capacity for calculation by all devas, nāgas, the eight classes of supernatural beings, the six classes of desire-realm māras, humans, and non-humans.
This is solely the Tathāgata’s profound and great wisdom of vision and knowledge,
the treasury of wisdom, and the wisdom of great liberation;
it is also that of all the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and others.
The wisdom of the fundamental practice of the great wisdom-dharmadhātu—
this dharma cannot be apprehended in its prior limit, its middle limit, or its subsequent limit.
As my mind reflects upon this, it becomes utterly bewildered.
What is the preliminary, what is the middle, and what is the concluding?
What is the method for achieving universal understanding?
And what is the root mantra of the Lotus-Crested Dhāraṇī?
What is the secret heart-mantra?
What is the mantra of joyful mirth?
What is the mantra of the wrathful kings?
What is the heart-mantra (hṛdaya-mantra) of the Wrathful King?
What are the one-syllable, two-syllable, three-syllable, four-syllable,
and even the ten-syllable mantras?
What are the dharmas of peace, the dharmas of abundance, and the dharmas of subjugation?
What are the dharmas of medicinal drops and the dharmas of medicinal ointments?
What are the dharmas of images, the dharmas of mandalas, and the dharmas of mudrās?
What are the summoning and boundary-binding,
the combing of hair, bathing, and the mending of robes,
the nectar-consecration, and the donning of armor?
The rules for sitting and reclining;
what constitutes the methods for gathering flowers, burning incense, applying fragrant unguents,
using mustard seeds, eating cakes, consuming fruits, and wearing flower garlands.
What are the three white foods, the lighting of lamps,
entering the maṇḍala, prostrating, performing circumambulation, scattering flowers,
and the instructions for the rules of regulating one's deportment?
What are these: the taking of the jewel, the turning of the mantra, the requesting of dreams,
the protection of the body, the binding of the boundary, the burning of fire, the fire-offering,
the supernormal powers, the ritual implements, and the gathering of dharmas?
What is the method for inviting the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara,
approaching him, and dispatching him?
What is the method of the noose (pāśa)?
"What is this Vajra-dharma? O Bhagavān, I do not understand this dharma.
In what characteristics should it be emulated and practiced?"
When this is accomplished, how shall I,
in the future age of the final dharma, accord with the various mental activities of sentient beings and teach them which dharmas to cultivate?
By means of which dharani-mantra methods are beings guided and delivered?
And what siddhi is accomplished by one who practices this cultivation?
I am utterly bewildered by this Dharma;
lacking any wisdom or understanding, I pray that you will look upon me with compassion and,
speaking in accordance with the Dharma, unravel the net of my doubts.
At that time, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Śākyamuni addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, Lord of Secrets,
saying: "Excellent, excellent!"
"Lord of Secrets,
you have asked this question most excellently.
Why did you not ask sooner, that your eloquence should be so delayed?"
Since you are able to provide guidance so that all sentient beings and practitioners of mantras may attain the ground of supreme accomplishment,
this question you have asked is indeed the greatest of questions.

Lord of Secrets, this samaya of the mantra-dhāraṇī of the Heart-King of Amoghapāśa is as vast as the immeasurable great oceans of the ten directions; it is difficult to understand and difficult to enter.
One might as well count every drop of water in the great ocean;
yet the limits of this *Amoghapāśahṛdaya-rāja-dhāraṇī-mantra-samaya* cannot truly be known through calculation.
Furthermore, one would even know the total number of atoms if Mount Sumeru, the king of mountains,
were ground into fine dust;
such is the power of this mantra of the Samaya of the Heart-King Dhāraṇī of Amoghapāśa.
It cannot be calculated by any numerical limit;
it is even more vast than the number of atoms in the great ocean.
O Lord of Secrets, this applies to all the Tathāgatas of the ten directions throughout the past, present, and future.
The samaya of the various types of wisdom can also be counted;
however, the limits of this mantra-samaya of the *Amoghapāśahṛdayarāja-dhāraṇī* cannot be known through calculation.
Lord of Secrets, it is the dharma-knowledge of all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Mahāsattvas that knows the turning of the differentiated characteristics of the five aggregates and so forth;
it is their subsequent knowledge (anvaya-jñāna).
It is all conventional knowledge that knows the aggregates, elements,
bases, and all dependent origination— whether collectively or individually—
as being impermanent and so forth.
Knowing that all phenomena are merely provisional designations,
he possesses the knowledge of others' minds,
whereby he understands the minds and mental factors of all sentient beings as they practice and realize cessation.
All knowledge of suffering knows that suffering does not arise;
all knowledge of the origin knows that the origin is to be permanently severed;
all knowledge of cessation knows that cessation is to be realized.
All path-knowledge knows that the path should be cultivated;
all knowledge of exhaustion knows the exhaustion of greed, hatred, and delusion;
and all knowledge of non-arising [knows their future non-arising].
Knowing the various realms of existence and no longer being reborn therein—
this is all-knowledge as it truly is,
the understanding of all-knowledge and the knowledge of all aspects.
All faculties of "the unknown that is to be known" (anājñātam-ājñāsyāmīndriya) have not yet attained clear realization (abhisamaya) regarding the noble truths,
nor have they attained the fruits of the noble ones (āryaphala).
All those who possess the faculties,
having attained clear realization regarding the Noble Truths,
have attained the fruits of the noble ones.
All that constitutes the faculty of one who possesses full knowledge— namely, all śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, all buddhas, and bodhisattva-mahāsattvas—
and all their samādhis accompanied by vitarka and vicāra.
Detached from all sensual desires and unwholesome states,
with directed thought and evaluation, and with the joy and happiness born of seclusion,
he enters and dwells in the first dhyāna, having attained its full perfection.
All samādhis that are without vitarka and with only vicāra,
which exist during the first dhyāna, the second dhyāna, and the intermediate state;
and all samādhis that are without both vitarka and vicāra.
From the second dhyāna up to the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception,
there are all the recollections of the Buddha,
the Dharma, the Saṅgha, and the precepts.
The recollection of relinquishment, the recollection of the devas,
the recollection of peace and disenchantment, the recollection of inhalation and exhalation,
the recollection of the body, and the recollection of death.
When practicing the perfection of giving,
with the wisdom that all things are not empty and great compassion as the foremost,
one gives away all internal and external possessions of one's own.
Furthermore, they encourage others to give away all internal and external possessions.
When practicing the perfection of ethical discipline (*śīlapāramitā*),
they take as their foremost priority the wisdom of non-emptiness and great compassion.
Abiding personally in the ten paths of wholesome action,
they also encourage others to abide in the ten paths of wholesome action.
When practicing the perfection of patience, they...
With the wisdom of the non-emptiness of all phenomena and great compassion as his foremost [motivation],
he himself possesses superior patience and also encourages others to possess superior patience.
When practicing the perfection of diligence,
one takes as primary the wisdom that all things are not empty and great compassion,
personally cultivating the six perfections with tireless application.
He also exhorts others to cultivate the six pāramitās with tireless diligence.
When practicing the dhyāna-pāramitā,
he takes as his primary motivation the wisdom that all things are not empty and great compassion.
Cultivating skillful means for oneself,
one enters the various meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*), the immeasurables (*apramāṇa*), and the formless attainments (*ārūpya*),
yet ultimately does not undergo rebirth under their influence.
He also skillfully exhorts others to enter the various meditative concentrations (dhyāna), the immeasurables (apramāṇa), and the formless attainments (ārūpya),
becoming as skillful in these as he himself is.
When practicing the perfection of wisdom,
one takes as primary the great compassion of the wisdom that all things are not empty,
and observes the nature of all phenomena as they truly are, without any attachment.
He also exhorts others to contemplate the nature of all phenomena as being without attachment,
nor abiding in their own nature or specific characteristics,
because neither movement nor stillness can be apprehended.
When practicing the four right endeavors,
for the sake of preventing unarisen evil and unwholesome states from arising:
For the sake of permanently abandoning all evil and unwholesome states that have already arisen,
and for the sake of causing all wholesome states that have not yet arisen to arise.
The four bases of psychic power (*ṛddhipāda*) are cultivated so that wholesome states already arisen may be stabilized, not forgotten, increased, expanded,
repeatedly practiced, and brought to fulfillment.
When cultivating the samādhi of desire,
one achieves the basis of psychic power through the abandonment of formations.
When cultivating the samādhi of diligence...

The basis for the accomplishment of the bases of psychic power through the abandonment of formations is the basis for the accomplishment of the bases of psychic power through the abandonment of formations at the time of cultivating the samādhi of mental cultivation.
When practicing the samādhi of contemplation,
one accomplishes the bases of supernormal power through the abandonment of formations and detachment from reliance,
employing the method of non-apprehension.
When cultivating the faculty of faith, the faculty of diligence, the faculty of mindfulness,
the faculty of concentration, and the faculty of wisdom— namely, the nature of these faculties of faith, diligence, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom—
one is free from dependence and free from defilement, employing the method of non-apprehension.
When cultivating the power of faith, the power of diligence, the power of mindfulness,
the power of concentration, and the power of wisdom— namely, the nature of these powers of faith, diligence, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom—
one is free from dependence and free from defilement, employing non-apprehension as the means.
When one cultivates the mindfulness factor of enlightenment, the investigation-of-dharmas factor of enlightenment,
the energy factor of enlightenment, the joy factor of enlightenment,
the tranquility factor of enlightenment, the concentration factor of enlightenment, and the equanimity factor of enlightenment.
That is to say: the nature of the enlightenment factor of mindfulness, the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena,
the enlightenment factor of energy, the enlightenment factor of rapture,
the enlightenment factor of tranquility, the enlightenment factor of concentration, and the enlightenment factor of equanimity.
Being free from dependence and free from defilement, by means of non-apprehension as the skillful method,
one cultivates the factors of right view,
right intention, right speech, and right action.
At the time of the factors of right livelihood,
right effort, right mindfulness, and right concentration,
it refers to the factors of right view, right intention, right speech, and right action.
The nature of the factors of right livelihood, right effort,
right mindfulness, and right concentration is the abandonment of dependence and the abandonment of defilement.
When dwelling in the samādhi of the liberation of emptiness,
it means that one contemplates how the specific characteristics of all phenomena are empty,
and the mind abides therein. When dwelling in the samādhi of the liberation of signlessness...
It refers to when the mind dwells in peace while contemplating that the specific characteristics (*svalakṣaṇa*) of all phenomena are signless (*animitta*);
this is the time of dwelling in the wishless liberation-samādhi (*apraṇihita-vimokṣa-samādhi*).
It refers to when the mind dwells in peace while contemplating that the specific characteristics of all phenomena are wishless (*apraṇihita*).
Taking non-apprehension as the skillful means,
when cultivating the power of knowledge regarding what is possible and what is impossible,
one means to understand all classes of sentient beings as they truly are.
Regarding the characteristics of cause and effect, and the characteristics of what is possible and impossible,
one practices the power of knowing the maturation of karma through the skillful means of non-apprehension.
That is to say, one understands, as they truly are,
the various characteristics of the maturation of karma— the causes and effects of the various karmic actions and their resulting experiences—
among all classes of sentient beings, by means of the method of non-apprehension.
When cultivating the power of knowledge regarding the various elements (*nānādhātu-jñānabala*),
it means to understand, as they truly are, the characteristics of the immeasurable elements of all classes of sentient beings,
employing the method of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*).
When cultivating the power of knowledge regarding the various inclinations,
it means to understand, as they truly are, the immeasurable characteristics of the inclinations of all classes of sentient beings,
employing the method of non-apprehension.
When cultivating the power of knowing the superior and inferior faculties,
one knows, as it truly is, the characteristics of the superior and inferior faculties of all classes of sentient beings,
employing the method of non-apprehension.
When cultivating the power of knowledge regarding the practice of universal engagement,
it means knowing, as they truly are, the characteristics of the universal engagement of all classes of sentient beings,
by means of non-apprehension.
When exercising the power of knowledge regarding the defilement and purification of the meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*), liberations (*vimokṣa*), samādhis, and attainments (*samāpatti*),
it means knowing, as they truly are, the characteristics of the meditative concentrations,
liberations, samādhis, and attainments— along with their faculties, powers, factors of enlightenment (*bodhyaṅga*), and factors of the path (*mārgāṅga*)— in all classes of sentient beings.
Taking non-apprehension as the skillful means,
when cultivating the power of knowledge regarding the recollection of past lives,
one understands all classes of sentient beings exactly as they are.
When cultivating the power of knowledge regarding death and rebirth by means of non-apprehension,
one contemplates the characteristics of immeasurable billions of past lives.
That is to say, one knows, as they truly are, the immeasurable and innumerable phenomena of the deaths and births of all classes of sentient beings,
by means of non-apprehension as the expedient.

When cultivating the power of knowledge regarding the destruction of the outflows (*āsravakṣayajñānabala*), one knows as it truly is that all outflows are forever exhausted, and that there is liberation of mind through the absence of outflows and liberation by wisdom through the absence of outflows;
having personally realized this in the present life, one dwells in its full possession.
One correctly understands: "Birth for me has been exhausted, the holy life has been established,
what was to be done has been accomplished, and there will be no further existence," by means of the expedient of non-apprehension.
When establishing the fearlessness regarding being perfectly awakened,
one claims for oneself to be a perfectly awakened one,
employing the method of non-apprehension.
When cultivating the fearlessness regarding the exhaustion of outflows,
one declares: "I have eternally exhausted all outflows," employing the method of non-apprehension.
When practicing the fearlessness regarding the obstructing dharmas,

At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara...
When this dhāraṇī mantra was being spoken,
the trichiliocosm shook in six ways; and Mount Potalaka,
from its base to its summit and all around its circumference, trembled extensively throughout the earth.
At that time, a multitude of precious lotus flowers suddenly emerged from the navel of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara,
emitting great radiance and manifesting thousand-petaled lotus flowers made of various jewels.
Its trunk is made of blue lapis lazuli;
its pedestal is of Jambūnada gold;
its seeds are red pearls, and its filaments and anthers are white pearls.
Those flowers further emitted rays of light of various colors,
which thoroughly illuminated all lands throughout the ten directions.

They awakened and comforted all sentient beings in the palaces of the devas, the palaces of the nāgas, the palaces of the yakṣas, the palaces of the rākṣasas, the palaces of the asuras, the palaces of the gandharvas, the palaces of the kinnaras, the palaces of the mahoragas, and all other beings.
That light shone downward, illuminating the sixteen hells,
which were all transformed into ponds of lotuses;
therein, all sentient beings undergoing suffering attained liberation.
At one time, they will relinquish their lives and go to the Western Land of Peace and Bliss,
where they will be born upon a lotus pedestal,
their bodies adorned with celestial garments.
He realizes the knowledge of past lives.
All classes of sentient beings, whether aquatic or terrestrial,
who encounter this light cast off their karmically retributive bodies and are born together in the celestial realms.
Adorning their bodies with celestial garments,
the bodhisattvas present in the assembly— those on the first and second grounds—
all simultaneously realized and dwelt in the eighth ground.
All Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas on the third, fourth, fifth, and even up to the seventh bhūmi,
have all realized unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
All the mantra-vidyādhara sages of every lineage have realized the samādhi of the secret heart maṇḍala of the Unfailing King Lotus-Crown.
All the nāga kings...
All have realized the *Ratnaketu* samādhi;
all the devas have realized the *Vajrāgnicakra* samādhi;
and all the yakṣa kings and rākṣasa kings [have likewise realized it].
All have realized the *samādhi* of the Jewel Palace;
all the asura kings and gandharva kings have realized the *samādhi* of the Vajra Armor Banner.
All the kinnara kings, all the mahoraga kings, and all the mantra-deities have realized the vajratuṇḍa-mahājava-bala-samādhi.
All have realized the samādhi of the purity of the actions of body,
speech, and mind. All the bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās have been liberated from ignorance, volitional formations,
consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, existence, birth, old age, sickness, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, and affliction.
At that time, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni emitted from his body the light of the Banner of the Great Sun,
which entered directly into the heart of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, the Lord of Secrets, saying: "You should carefully contemplate this secret heart-mantra maṇḍala of sovereign spiritual powers, the Unfailing King Lotus-Top Samaya."
Thereupon, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, Lord of Secrets, addressed [the Buddha], saying:
"O Noble One, I have beheld this supreme secret heart-mantra samaya-maṇḍala of the Sovereign of the Unfailing Lotus Crown, characterized by the mastery of supernatural powers."
Vast, immeasurable, profoundly deep, extraordinary,
and difficult to behold— this is an unprecedented occurrence that accomplishes all supreme dharmas.
Together with all sentient beings, he removes their heavy burdens and causes those who uphold [this teaching] to attain a ground of great merit.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara...
Again, he addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajradhara Guhyapati, saying:
"Listen attentively, listen attentively! This is the Samaya of the Mantra-Realm of Sovereign Spiritual Powers, the Secret Heart of the Unfailing King Padmaśekhara."
It is able to bring vast benefit to all sentient beings,
eliminate all karmic obstacles, and drive away all vināyakas;
all māras, enemies, and malevolent spirits will naturally scatter in flight.
All poisons, venomous insects, tigers, wolves, and malevolent beasts,
as well as all manner of calamities, shall be entirely dispelled.
Merely by reciting this, one will swiftly attain true and unsurpassed accomplishment.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, Lord of Secrets,
smiling with joy and brandishing his vajra in his hand,
spoke these words to the Great Compassionate One:
"What is the samaya of the Secret Heart Mantra of the Sovereign Miraculous Powers of the True Lotus Crown Maṇḍala?
We pray that you will explain it to us.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara—
He then extended his right hand and stroked the area above his own navel;
from within the great radiance, a thousand-petaled lotus pedestal appeared.
Upon that pedestal, a jeweled canopy manifested, and within that canopy appeared the Lotus-Crested Secret Heart Mantra Maṇḍala of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, Sovereign of Spiritual Powers.
The Great Brahmā’s countenance is serene and joyful;
he has three eyes and four arms,
his body adorned with various precious necklaces and celestial garments.
On his head he wears a jeweled crown, within which resides an emanation Buddha.
One hand holds a lasso, one hand holds a precious lotus flower, one hand holds a jeweled staff, and one hand holds a vajra; he sits in the full lotus posture.
From his body he emitted various kinds of wondrous and marvelous colored lights that adorned his person;
these lights eclipsed the radiance of the sun, the moon, and the multitude of stars.
It is that which is beheld by the eyes of all Tathāgatas;
which all Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas reverently prostrate to;
and which all devas join their palms to honor and praise.
All the hosts of ascetic sages paid him homage and offered praise;
as did all the nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, asuras, gandharvas, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, and so forth.
With palms joined, they prostrated, circumambulated,
and sang praises. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, Lord of Secrets, together with his retinue,
beheld this great and wondrous manifestation of the Samaya of the Secret Heart of Padmaśekhara, the Sovereign of Spiritual Powers.
At that time, they all simultaneously realized the Samādhi of the Stainless Radiant Flame of the Unfailing Lotus Crown and the Samādhi of Unfailing Manifestation.
With palms joined in joy,
they simultaneously paid homage and praised the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara spoke this secret heart-mantra, saying:

Oṃ amogha-hṛdayāya | Padma-muṣṭi-saṃjñāya | Kūrma-ravita-sadara | Padma-miśra-varāya | Amīṣāya | Sarva-mogha-kula-samaya | Hṛdayāya | Sarva-siddhi-mojña | Parākhyā-śūrya | Padma-padma | Hūṃ hūṃ | Namo buddhāya | Svāhā. This mantra brings joy and serenity to body and mind.

The mass of merit obtained by those who practice the visualization of Amitābha Buddha with great compassion and the visualization of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva is equal to the aggregate of ethical discipline and liberation of all Tathāgatas of the three periods of time.
Furthermore, they are equal to Amitābha Buddha’s liberation of the aggregate of form,
and are like the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara,
who maintains a body that wields various kinds of weapons.
If one constantly binds the Lotus-Crown Mudrā,
sprinkles water upon one’s own crown, and recites the mantra,
one will obtain the same consecration as that bestowed by all Tathāgatas of the three times.
One shall realize a hundred thousand samādhis associated with a mass of merit.
The mantra of King Kula-hṛṣṭa is as follows:
Oṃ āmukha pātumuniśeṣa. (Recite "Oṃ" as before; "āmukha" is the first phrase; "pātu" is the second; "muniśeṣa" is the remainder.)
1. Vra 2. Padma 3. Miśravara 4. Āmantrāya 5. Sarvatathāgatānām 6. Amoghapadmoṣṇīṣa 7. Samayamakariseya 8. Phaṭ (twice)
Hara-miśāya (8) sarva-karma-siṃha-mi (9) para-āyava (10) abhūti-śvara (11) hūṃ hūṃ (12) mahā-pātma-usnīṣa-bhūje (13).
Svāhā (14). Thus, with a joyful mind and a face [radiant] with awe, one should contemplate with a heart of great compassion,
contemplating Avalokiteśvara.
In the Padmaśekhara Maṇḍala and the Avalokiteśvara Maṇḍala,
those who recite and maintain [this] are the Mantra-Vidyārājas of the Lotus Family.
The Mantra-Vidyārāja Maitreya, the Mantra-Vidyārāja Bhṛkuṭī,
and the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara shall all provide protection and guardianship.
One attains the siddhi of the Amoghasiddhi family, the siddhi of the Padma-śekhara family,
the siddhi of the vast Padma-maṇḍala, and the siddhi of the mantra-maṇḍala of the Amoghapāśahṛdaya-rāja-dhāraṇī.
The siddhi of non-empty abundance, wealth, nobility, and sovereignty;
the siddhi of the universal assembly of all bodhisattva lineages;
[these shall be attained] within hundreds of thousands of buddha-fields.
Born as a mantra-vidyādhara of great lineage,
he wanders among the gods, nāgas, all yakṣas, rākṣasas, asuras, gandharvas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans.
All shall attain mastery,
up to and including the realization of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
The mantra of the Wrathful King of the Family is as follows:

Oṃ mahācaṇḍa padmīśvara mimidharuṣa mikaṭṭapadma ḍaṃṣṭrākaraṇa bisanabakṣatara sarvaduṣṭān hṛdaye khādaya māṃ padma jñaptiṃ kuru jñapti huṃ svāhā. Thus, with this mantra, one should exert fury in body and mind.
When those who recite and uphold [this mantra] of the Wrathful King contemplate it,
Mount Sumeru, the Golden Mountains, and the Iron Mountains all tremble,
and the great ocean surges and boils.
Great fires broke out in all the dragon palaces;
all the malevolent vināyakas were bound and restrained;
and all the ghosts and spirits fled in every direction.
All the Great Wrathful Kings constantly provide protection,
as do Mahābrahmā, Śakra-devendra, Nārāyaṇa, and Maheśvara.
King Yama, Varuṇa, Sāgara the Nāga King,
Nanda the Nāga King, and Upananda the Nāga King.
The Dragon King Upānanda, the Kumāra devas,
and the deities of the Four Great Kings constantly follow and protect it.
If one faces the direction of the calamity and recites this with a great roar of wrath,
those calamities will be extinguished.
The practitioner who performs the ritual of cultivation while reciting this secretly within the maṇḍala will swiftly attain accomplishment.
The heart-mantra of the Family Wrathful King is as follows:

Oṃ amogha-pātumuniśe mahāpātumāpośe krodhakariṣaye paravidveṣaye mahābhaṣpatye yamaparurṇakrośare mṛlahāmaveśadare mahācaṇḍamige amoghakulasameye pātu mi hūṃ hūṃ. With this mantra, one should exert both body and mind.
Regarding the King of Wrathful Deities:
