That great lotus was surrounded on all four sides by red and yellow campaka flowers, white pāriyātaka flowers, blue utpala flowers, and red lotuses.
Fashion a flower garland,
threading open lotus flowers at its four corners;
upon the center of each lotus pedestal, place the pāśa (noose) mudrā.
The seal of the wish-fulfilling jewel flask,
surrounded by flames, is at each of the four corners of the next enclosure.
The Four Heavenly Kings are positioned according to their respective directions;
their faces are wrathful,
and they sit in the half-lotus posture upon thrones of Mount Sumeru.
Each held a halberd and spear,
adorned with armor and necklaces made of the seven treasures, as well as flower garlands.
On all four sides were placed Sumeru thrones.
Upon each seat, lotus flowers bloom; upon each pedestal,
there are the pāśa (lasso) mudrās and the cintāmaṇi-ghaṭa (wish-fulfilling vase) mudrās.
The vajra seal, the maṇi-jewel seal,
the five-colored conch seal, the vajra-hook seal,
the vajra-chain seal, and the seven-jeweled wheel seal.
The seal of the pervasive blazing light, the seal of the vajra staff, the seal of the vajra fist,
the seal of the turning of the wheel of Dharma, the seal of the flower vase and vajra,
the seal of the great holder of the flower garland, and the seal of the most supreme in the three realms.
The mudrā of the Vidyārājñī Hayagrīva Avalokiteśvara; the mudrā of the Mother Avalokiteśvarī;
the mudrā of Yaśodharā; the mudrā of Tārā Bodhisattvī;
the mudrā of Cundā Bodhisattvī; and the mudrā of Bhṛkuṭī Bodhisattvī.
Extending even to all the mudrās,
each individual mudrā is encircled by radiating flames.
Next, Sumeru jewel thrones are placed throughout the surrounding courtyard.
Upon each seat, a lotus flower blooms;
upon the calyxes are various hand-seals (mudrās).
In the four gates of the next enclosure, Mount Sumeru is placed.
Below the mountains lies the great ocean.
Upon those four mountains dwells the formidable Vajrapāṇi, Lord of Secrets,
his face wrathful and his canine fangs protruding upward.
Their hair and beards were tawny and bristling; each held a weapon and sat in the half-lotus posture.
All wore flower crowns, celestial robes, and necklaces, adorned with various ornaments, their bodies surrounded by a halo of blazing flames.
On each of the four sides and four corners is a precious *sumeru* throne;
upon each throne, a lotus flower is in full bloom,
and atop each flower pedestal are placed various mudrās.
Upon a square pedestal is the seal of the vajra;
from all these seals, radiant flames swirl upward.
The ground of both the inner and outer courtyards consists entirely of blue jewels.
Upon the boundaries of the three enclosures, there are red lotuses, blue utpala flowers,
campaka flowers, sumana flowers, vārṣika flowers, pāṭala flowers, and atimuktaka flowers.
Fashion flower garlands to demarcate the boundaries.
At the boundary of the fourth enclosure, erect single-pronged vajras with their tips aligned one after another.
When the decoration was completed all around,
it was further adorned with various banners, flowers, canopies, bells,
and ribbons arranged in alternating patterns.
The four boundaries are enclosed with cords of five-colored silk,
establishing the ritual boundary according to the Dharma.
There are twelve vessels in total, consisting of both gold and silver.
Fill it with various scented waters and place the seven precious jewels within;
insert various branches, flowers, and leaves into its mouth,
and tie a white flower garland around the neck of the jar.
There were sixteen argha vessels filled with various scented waters, upon which flowers floated;
there were thirty-two silver plates filled with *sugandha*, white sandalwood, aloeswood, and *guggulu* incense.
Place offerings for all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas:
twelve incense burners containing *bīlīka* incense,
resin incense (*śrīveṣṭaka*), saffron, and *khaṭṭarasa* incense.
Camphor and musk should be compounded according to the ritual rules and mixed with rock honey;
this is then placed within a silver vessel.
In the outer courtyard, one makes offerings to all the deities of the mandalas and celestial beings.
These include various miscellaneous flowers obtained at appropriate times,
one hundred and sixty portions of food and drink of a hundred flavors, and one hundred and eight fruits, melons, branches, and flowering trees.
One hundred and eight butter lamps and one hundred and eight sesame oil lamps should be arranged and offered in succession.
Place eight portions of large vinegar, radish, parched barley flour, *mudga* beans,
and fruit together in a vessel outside the north side of the eastern gate of the altar.
Summon all the vināyakas and offer them an oblation consisting of fresh vegetables,
cakes, rice, cow's curd, parched barley flour, soup, and greens,
prepared in two equal portions.
One portion is for the invocation and offering to all yakṣas outside the northern gate of the maṇḍala;
one portion is for the invocation and offering to all rākṣasas outside the southwest of the maṇḍala.
Milk, curd, and non-glutinous rice are to be placed together in one portion.
Outside the eastern side of the southern gate of the maṇḍala,
summon all the bhūta spirits for offerings:
one portion consisting of parched barley flour, non-glutinous rice, *modaka* cakes, sesame powder, and boiled vegetables, all combined together.
Outside the western gate of the southern entrance of the maṇḍala,
summon all the preta and pilipada spirits for offerings. Take cow’s milk and non-glutinous rice porridge,
mixing them together and dividing the mixture into two portions.
One portion [is for] the outer area south of the eastern gate of the maṇḍala,
where one summons and makes offerings to the celestial deities of the sun.
One portion [is for] the outer area south of the western gate of the maṇḍala.
Summon the Moon Deity and the Star Deities for worship.
Boil seven kinds of grain seeds with water until cooked, and set aside one portion outside the northern gate of the mandala.
Summon all the celestial maidens to make offerings.
Take one portion of a mixture of milk, curd, fruit, and various flowers,
and place it outside the north side of the western gate of the maṇḍala.
Invoke all the deities of the earth to receive offerings.
Take one portion of parched barley flour, rice gruel, water, and non-glutinous rice, mixed together;
place it outside the northwest corner of the mandala.
Summon all the wind deities for offerings.
Prepare a portion consisting of a mixture of cow’s ghee, fried cakes, granulated sugar, rock honey, and rice cakes;
place this outside the western gate of the mandala.
Summon all the dragon kings to receive offerings.
Prepare one portion consisting of cow’s ghee, milk, curd, cakes, white sandalwood, and fragrant water mixed with non-glutinous rice;
place this outside the southern gate of the maṇḍala.
Summon all the retinues of the Māra kings to offer them sustenance.
Take one portion of saffron, water, and non-glutinous rice, mixed together,
and place it outside the northern side of the western gate of the maṇḍala.
Invoke all the river deities (*nadī-devatā*) and make offerings to them.
Prepare one portion consisting of a mixture of *kuśa* grass water, cow’s milk, black mustard seeds, and rice cakes.
Outside the southwest corner of the mandala, invoke all the *mṛtyu-mārakṣasa* spirits and make offerings to them.
If a mantra practitioner performs such offerings to all the devas and spirits,
they will attain accomplishment in accordance with the perfection of generosity (dānapāramitā).
Furthermore, it causes all devas, nāgas, spirits,
and ghosts to be entirely joyful and not to cause mutual disturbance for the holder of the mantra.
One should prepare a portion consisting of a mixture of cow ghee, milk, curd, milk-gruel, granulated sugar, and rock honey,
and place it outside the western gate of the mandala to offer to the constellation to which one personally belongs.
One shall obtain longevity, peace, and happiness, free from all calamities and obstacles.
If one can perform offerings according to the Dharma every day,
one’s body will never be harmed by poisons, venomous insects, tigers, wolves, or the like.
Their merit and lifespan will increase, and their bodies shall be free from untimely death or calamity;
they shall not be harmed by any enemies, difficulties, talismans, yakṣas, rākṣasas, evil nāgas, spirits, or vināyakas.
They shall create various obstacles and afflictions;
yet one will swiftly attain the accomplishment corresponding to the dhāraṇī, mantra, maṇḍala, mudrā, and samaya,
and be honored and protected by all devas and humans.
Having thus performed the internal and external invocations and made offerings to all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Vajras, devas, nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, vināyakas, spirits, and deities;
Furthermore, one should protect oneself and others, perform invocations and boundary-binding (*sīmābandha*),
carry out ritual procedures and practices,
prostrate, recite, scatter flowers, form mudrās, make aspirations, and offer praise.
Regarding the ritual for inviting [the deities] through the western gate:
those who enter this maṇḍala must receive the empowerment, instructions, and samaya vows.
One shall obtain the protection of all one hundred thousand koṭi-nayuta-gaṅgā-saṃkhyeya Tathāgatas;
furthermore, one shall have planted roots of merit before all one hundred thousand koṭi-nayuta-gaṅgā-saṃkhyeya Buddhas numbering eighty-four thousand.
They shall obtain a great mass of merit like Mount Sumeru.

Furthermore, they will plant, ripen, and bring to fulfillment roots of goodness in the presence of all Buddhas, numbering nine hundred and ninety-nine *koṭi-nayuta-śata-sahasra* times as many as the sands of the Ganges River, thereby achieving perfect correspondence.
One shall attain the secret mandala,
mudrā, samaya, and siddhi of all Tathāgatas, as well as the comprehensive assembly of the dhāraṇīs,
mantras, mandalas, mudrās, and samayas of the great lineage of all Bodhisattvas, together with their corresponding accomplishments.
When one enters the stage of non-retrogression of all Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas,
the celestial hosts of the thirty-three palaces of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven and the assembly of Śakra, Lord of the Devas, will all come to provide protection.
O Vajradhara, Lord of Secrets, together with the assembly of immeasurable koṭis of mantra-sages,
you should bestow immeasurable valor, diligence, majestic power, and mindfulness;
saturate the field of the body, and grant it protection.
All the five crimes of immediate retribution accumulated over immeasurable billions of kalpas,
for which one would otherwise have to undergo the Avīci Hell,
shall be entirely extinguished.
One shall attain the signs of accomplishment for the samaya of all dhāraṇī mantras of King Amogha;
all greed, anger, jealousy, and obstructing veils shall likewise be eliminated.
They will be loved and respected by others;
all Tathāgatas shall joyfully observe them,
and Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva will bestow his protective care and mindfulness upon them.
If, after this life ends, one goes to the Pure Land and is born by transformation within a lotus flower—
such is the person who enters the maṇḍala and receives the samaya.
Those who seek the supreme accomplishment of this Dharma should respectfully revere and honor their preceptors and ācāryas.
Just as I reverently serve the Tathāgata Śākyamuni and Amitābha Buddha,
so too do I pay homage to Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara and Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta.
Once the mantra practitioner has bestowed the samaya upon his disciples,
he forms the mudrā at the western gate,
performs the empowerment and protection of the body, and sits in the full lotus posture.
Burn the empowered King of Incenses as an offering,
and recite the root Padma-śekhara Dhāraṇī mantra and the secret heart mantra one thousand and eight times.
If one recites it two thousand or three thousand times,
one will certainly attain the state of being upon the thirty-two-petaled lotus pedestal of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva;
the body will emerge from the water, and one will behold the ten directions.
The mantra-reciter said, "Excellent, excellent!
You have now attained the accomplishment of the *Amoghapāśa-rāja-mūla-padma-śekhara-dhāraṇī-mantra*."
"What wish do you require?
I shall now grant it to you in its entirety,
so that in all future births you may be born with a physical body."
Born by transformation from a lotus and endowed with the knowledge of past lives,
one shall attain the samaya of the mudrās of the Maṇḍala of the King of Mantras, Amoghapāśahṛdaya;
and the samayas of the dhāraṇī-mantra of Amogha-viśuddha-padma-śekhara shall all manifest before one.
When the mantra-holder beholds Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva,
they should present an offering of arghya water to Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva,
burn incense, scatter flowers, and petition for their desired aspirations.
Having prostrated, praised, and resolved to attain bodhicitta,
he respectfully took his leave of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva and returned to his original palace,
whereupon the Bodhisattva immediately vanished from sight.
One who attains this mark realizes the Samādhi of the Adorned Radiant Flames of the Non-empty Pure Lotus Crown,
soaring freely through the air,
surrounded by a retinue of sixty-four *koṭi-nayuta* hundreds of thousands of mantra-vidyā-siddhas.
He becomes a great Vidyādhara of the Lotus Family, possessing a lifespan of nine hundred and ninety *koṭi-nayuta* hundreds of thousands of *kalpas*.
Chapter Thirty-Six: The Image of the Fundamental Lotus-Uṣṇīṣa. O Lord of Secrets, this is the image of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara as the Fundamental Lotus-Uṣṇīṣa.
Using fine, exquisite white cotton cloth or high-quality silk,
measuring four cubits in length and breadth,
one should begin the painting on the fifteenth day of the bright fortnight.
Use pure, high-quality colors and do not employ animal glue.
When the artist paints, they must constantly bathe and wear clean clothing.
With focused attention, they should paint the fundamental lotus at the crown of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.
Mahābrahmā has three faces and four arms;
his countenance is serene and joyful.
Between the eyebrows of the central face is a single eye.
On his head he wears a crown of seven precious jewels, within which resides an emanation Buddha.
His first right hand holds a trident;
his second right hand holds a lotus and a lasso.
The first hand on the left holds a seven-jeweled blossoming lotus flower;
from within the center of the flower emerges the face and head of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva,
wearing a jeweled crown upon his head from which flames of fire emanate.
The second hand on the left extends its five fingers downward, raining down the seven treasures;
from the back of the hand, flames issue forth in a swirling circle.
It is adorned with various precious necklaces, earrings, and bracelets.
Adorned with various celestial garments and ornaments,
he sat cross-legged upon a precious lotus throne,
his body radiant with a halo of blazing light.
Beneath that lotus, one should paint the waters of the great ocean with shores and banks of the seven precious gems;
from within the water, two nine-headed nāga kings emerge with their bodies revealed.
To the left and right, lotus stalks are entwined.
From the water on the right, the Nanda Nāga King emerges with his upper body,
joining his palms in reverent gazing.
To the left of that lotus, within the water, the Nāga King Upananda appears with his upper body revealed, joining his palms in reverent gazing.
Within the water are white cranes, peacocks, jīvaṃjīvaka birds, and ruddy sheldrakes.
There are various birds, fish, and beasts, along with flowers of many colors.
To the right of Avalokiteśvara,
the Bodhisattva Tārā sits in the half-lotus posture.
Slightly bowing with palms joined in reverence while holding flowers,
to the left of Avalokiteśvara sits the white-robed Bodhisattva Pāṇḍaravāsinī in the half-lotus posture.
Slightly bowing with palms joined in reverence while holding flowers,
she stands behind the Bodhisattva Tārā.
The Bodhisattva Bhṛkuṭī sits in the half-lotus posture.
Behind the Bodhisattva Pañcarakṣiṇī is the Bodhisattva Śvetabhadra,
who sits in the half-lotus posture and wears a white lower garment around his waist.
These bodhisattvas were adorned with various precious crowns, necklaces, earrings, and bracelets,
as well as celestial garments of diverse adornments;
they sat upon lotus seats, their bodies radiant with the blaze of a halo.
Following the Bodhisattva Śvetaketu is the rākṣasī goddess Ekajaṭā;
her face is wrathful, and her body has six arms.
Holding weapons in his hands, he sits in the half-lotus posture.
Behind the Bodhisattva Bhṛkuṭī is the messenger Duti, whose face is wrathful and who possesses eight arms.
Holding weapons in their hands and seated in the half-lotus posture,
each adorned their bodies with various exquisite garments and necklaces.
In the space above the crown of Avalokiteśvara’s head,
to the right, are placed Mahābrahmā and Maheśvara, along with their respective hosts of devas;
each holds precious flowers as offerings while gazing up in reverence.
To the left are placed Śakra Devendra and Nārāyaṇa, together with their respective hosts of devas,
each holding precious flowers as offerings while gazing up in reverence.
Below the seat of Bodhisattva Tārā, [is...]
The Kings Yama, Varuṇa, Virūpākṣa, and Vaiśravaṇa are seated in the half-lotus posture, each holding their respective weapons,
beneath the white-robed Bodhisattva Pañcāla-vatsinī.
Therein were the gods Kuvēra and Kumāra, and the celestial kings Dhṛtarāṣṭra and Virūḍhaka,
seated in the half-lotus posture, each holding their respective weapons.
Beneath the seat of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva,
the mantra-practitioner kneels on the right side and sits;
holding a rosary in one hand and an incense burner in the other, they gaze up at the Bodhisattva.
Lord of Secrets, this fundamental image of Avalokiteśvara from the Lotus Summit can encompass all the images of the vast liberation lotus maṇḍala of the Āmoghapaśa Kings.
If one constantly and uninterruptedly observes, pays homage to, and makes offerings with joyful palms joined,
then one shall be liberated from all misdeeds and the five sins of immediate retribution,
and attain the stage of the Great Accomplishment of Non-Vainness.
One shall be loved, revered, and respected by all people in the world;
one shall attain great peace and happiness, with abundant wealth and treasures;
and one’s eloquence, wisdom, physical appearance, and strength shall increase and be fully awakened.
Having accumulated roots of virtue and possessing great majestic power.
Chapter Thirty-Seven: The Secret Mudrās of Supernatural Transformations. O Lord of Secrets, this is the samaya of the Fundamental Lotus-Crest Wheel-Turning Dharma-Mudrā.
It brings about great benefit and extinguishes all grave sins;
this is the place of supreme accomplishment.
If there is anyone who can daily arouse a heart of great compassion before the image, [they shall attain success].
If one forms this seal and recites the mantra of the Root Lotus-Crown Dhāraṇī,
that person shall eliminate the grave offenses of the Avīci Hell of Uninterrupted Suffering.
May they be swiftly exhausted and extinguished.
All Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the ten directions throughout the past, present, and future shall mindfully observe them.
Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva will manifest before them to grant their wishes.
All the hosts of Tuṣita Heaven, the hosts of Akaniṣṭha Heaven,
the hosts of Mahābrahmā Heaven, and the hosts of Śakra, Lord of the Thirty-three Heavens,
all beheld, protected, and empowered him with diligence.
Its majestic power and physical strength cause all the hosts of Māras, Vināyakas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, and all spirits and ghosts to tremble with fear in battle and flee in all directions.
For the Lotus-Crest Seal (padmottara-mudrā), join the two hands in *añjali*.
The two little fingers and the two ring fingers are crossed,
with the right hand pressing over the left, tucked into the palms;
the two middle fingers are held upright and extended, their tips separated by one cun.
Bend both index fingers and hook them over the middle joints on the sides of the middle fingers.
Place both thumbs against the sides of the "tiger mouth" (the base of the ring fingers).
Bending like a hook so that they do not touch one another,
one should place the seal against the heart and recite the mantra of the Wrathful King of the Family;
such a person can shake all Buddha-fields throughout the three times.
In each Buddha-field, they rain down vast clouds of all kinds of celestial jewel-flowers, garments, necklaces, and exquisite ornaments of the sea,
making offerings to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
It is endowed with the merit of hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Gaṅgā-sand grains of seals;
it is the seal of all Tathāgatas of the ten directions, the seal of Vairocana Tathāgata.
The mass of merit obtained by empowering this mudrā is equal to seven piles of the seven precious jewels as vast as Mount Sumeru;
it is equivalent to making offerings to all Tathāgatas, the Perfectly Enlightened Ones.
Because all Tathāgatas constantly maintain contemplation,
the Seal of Pure Contemplation follows the previous seal with this modification:
extend the tip of the right index finger together with the middle finger.
Do not allow them to become attached.
This mudrā can be applied in all situations;
it brings about a correspondence with a vast and firm accumulation of merit and provisions.
It encompasses the seal of the pure contemplation of the hearts of all Buddhas and Tathāgatas;
it extinguishes all fears, calamities, obstacles, and misfortunes,
and ensures that no ghosts or spirits harbor malice or cause harm.
All Tathāgatas shall appear before them;
they will have planted roots of virtue in the presence of all Buddhas numbering ninety-nine hundred-thousand-ten-million-billion *gaṅgā-sa* sands.
The samaya of the mudrās of the entire Tathāgata family;
the samaya of the mudrās of the entire Avalokiteśvara family;
the samaya of the mudrās of the entire Vajra family.
This is the samaya of the seal of the entire Maṇi family;
this is the samaya of the seal of the entire Gandhahastin Bodhisattva family.
Among all seals, this seal-samaya is the Great Seal King.
This is the Samaya-seal of the Great Illusory Transformation and Supernatural Manifestations of Avalokiteśvara.
If there are those who practice all dharmas,
they shall all bind this seal and swiftly attain the dharma of unimpeded accomplishment.
To perform the Awakening Seal (Vibodhana-mudrā), modify the first seal by changing the left and right index fingers so that each is extended slightly bent,
with their tips one inch apart and not touching the middle fingers.
When awakening and summoning,
move the index finger back and forth;
this mudrā awakens all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
Invoke all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas;
protect oneself and others, bind the boundary and bind the hair;
enter the maṇḍala, make offerings, prostrate, and practice the path.
Consecrate the crown-seat, the bathing water, and the protective garments;
wash the hands and rinse the mouth, receive the samaya vows,
and offer scented ointments, incense, food, drink, flowers, and fruit.
Vessels for water and vessels for food should all employ this mudrā;
by practicing all dharmas, they shall all be accomplished.
This includes the mantras of the Family Kings and the mantras of the Wrathful Kings.
Mantras of one, two, three, or even ten syllables all employ this seal.
These are the Three Great Seals, which are most great, most venerable, and possess great supernormal powers.
It is called the Seal of the Power of the Enlightenment of All Buddhas.
By means of this, all Tathāgatas of the three periods of time constantly bestow their empowerment through the six supernormal powers and the ten powers.
The Buddhas of the three periods of time and Vairocana Tathāgata always praise this seal.
This seal is the samaya-seal of the secret maṇḍala of the great lineage of all Tathāgatas.

Chapter Thirty-Eight: The Chapter on the Mantra of Divine Transformations. The Mantra for Summoning: Oṃ ā-mogha-hṛdaya padma-senāpate ākarṣaya sādhaya vara-vara mahā-padme svāhā. Recite this mantra seven times in praise.
Alertly summon all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and celestial deities.
Recite the boundary-binding mantra three times—*Oṃ bhūmūrṇisa āmukha-maṇḍale hūṃ*—to consecrate white mustard seeds and scented water.
Scatter [the materials] inside and outside the altar and along the courtyards of the ten directions;
this shall constitute the boundary (sīmābandha). Recite the Keśapāśa mantra five times: Oṃ bhatuma śikhari hūṃ. Thus, recite the mantra five times.
Perform the empowerment for binding the hair into a topknot.
Recite the bathing mantra three times: Oṃ bhaṭṭārikāmuṇḍini āmukha-jarja hūṃ. Thus, [recite] the mantra three times.
Empower white mustard seeds and fragrant bathing water to bathe the body.
The mantra for purification is: Oṃ mīmāra śuddhe hūṃ. Thus is the mantra.
Five times, empower pure water with mantras to rinse the mouth, wash the hands, and wash the face.
Recite the *Cīvaradhāraṇī* mantra—Oṃ sañca kṣaṇaya pāṭhame hūṃ—three times.
Consecrate one’s clothing by reciting this mantra five times while putting it on, taking it off, or setting it aside. The Amṛta-mantra is: Oṃ milimilya śuddhe hūṃ.
With this mantra, consecrate milk, curd, ghee, and honey five times, and then offer them as an oblation and consume them.
The Consecration Mantra: Oṃ padma-senā-garbhe āviśa tvaṃ maṃśruti hūṃ. Recite this mantra three times.
Sprinkle the head and body with consecrated perfumed water.
Recite the Armor Mantra three times: Oṃ bhaumā-kavaca 1, ṭiṭṭibhi-rudra 2, bandha hūṃ 3, prabala svāhā 4-5. Thus, [recite] the mantra three times.
It is said that by holding the right hand and stroking it all over the body, one immediately becomes armored and protected.
Recite this Vajrāsana mantra three times: Oṃ vajra-tejovaty-āmi hūṃ.
Having empowered the seat, one sits upon it.
Recite the *bhūmiparigraha-mantra* three times: Oṃ jvala pṛthivī dhara dhara hūṃ. Thus, recite this mantra three times.
Consecrate the site of the maṇḍala, draw the maṇḍala, and arrange the seats.
Recite the mantra for purifying the seat three times: Oṃ padmamāśraya rūpa dharadhara hūṃ. Thus, [recite] the mantra three times.
Having empowered the bed with mantras, one sits or lies upon it.
For the mantra to purify flowers, recite: Oṃ jvaḥ padme hūṃ. Recite this mantra five times.
Empower the flowers and present them as an offering.
Recite the incense mantra five times: Oṃ padmamīka svāhā hūṃ. Thus, recite the mantra five times.
Empower the incense by burning it as an offering;
likewise, burn it to fumigate the hands and the robes.
Recite the mantra for the unguent three times: OṂ BAHTMAKAṆTI ŚVAPALI HŪṂ. Thus, [recite] the mantra three times.
Consecrate the unguent for offering upon the altar, and likewise smear it upon one's own arms and body.
Recite the mantra of white mustard seeds three times: *Oṃ bhaṭṭārambarakīlanidhāraṇi svāhā*.
Empower the rice grains, flowers, and white mustard seeds, and scatter them upon the altar.
Recite the perfume mantra: Oṃ padmārye sugandhe hūṃ. Thus is the mantra.
Consecrate the *argha* perfumed water three times and present it as an offering.
For the food and drink mantra, recite: Oṃ śuklavatre rasāyanauṣadhe hūṃ. Thus is the mantra.
Consecrate all the cakes and foods by reciting this three times and offer them as an offering.
The mantra for the three white foods is: *Oṃ sulu sulu pāṇḍitī svāhā*. Thus is the mantra.
Consecrate the three types of white rice food by reciting [the mantra] three times and offer it as an oblation.
The mantra for the rice is: *Oṃ bhadramāśrīṇi svadhāya hūṃ*. Thus is the mantra.
Recite this three times.
Empower the various grains of rice and present them as an offering.
The mantra for the fruits is: Oṃ phala-miśrite pāra-sara hūṃ. Thus is the mantra.
Consecrate all the fruits three times and offer them as an offering.
The mantra for the flower garland is: Oṃ bharavara puṣpajāya svāhā. Thus is the mantra.
Recite this mantra three times to consecrate all flower garlands and offer them as an offering:
*Oṃ jvala jvalaya rāśvara kharaṇi hūṃ*. This is the mantra for food and drink.
Consecrate all food and drink by reciting [the mantra] three times and offer them as an offering.
Recite the lamp mantra—Oṃ padma-nīpāya jvala hūṃ—three times.
Consecrate the lamp and present it as an offering.
The practitioner of the Dharma visualizes that all obscurations of darkness are dispelled.
Recite the mantra for entering the maṇḍala three times: Oṃ samabhatoma pūvane parāśara hūṃ. Thus, recite the mantra three times.
Having consecrated the entrance to the mandala, enter the mandala and make offerings.
Perform prostrations and recite the mantra: Oṃ bhaṭṭārikā-īśvarī-ārya-mogalāni hūṃ. Thus is the mantra.
Recite the praise three times.
Prostrate with the five limbs touching the ground.
Recite the mantra for walking the path: Oṃ cakre maṇḍale maṃte pṛthivī hūṃ. Thus is the mantra.
Recite this three times while proceeding on the path.
For the mantra for scattering flowers: Oṃ samantāvalokitana padme svabhāva hūṃ. Recite this mantra three times.
Having empowered the flowers, they are bestowed upon the disciples to be scattered.
The instruction for the mantra is: Oṃ padma-samaya-uṣṇīṣa mahāmudrā samaya hūṃ. This is the mantra for the rite of receiving [the empowerment].
Consecrate three times and bestow the samaya.
Recite the mantra for adjusting the robes, *Oṃ samantānugraha-pratimī hūṃ phaṭ*, three times in praise.

Sitting in the full lotus posture (*paryaṅka*), one should adjust one's robes and maintain a dignified demeanor. Recite the mantra *oṃ āryāvalokiteśvara hūṃ* three times. Thus, the mantra is recited three times.
Consecrate the rosary, take it up, and hold it while counting the beads.
Recite the mantra three times: OṂ ŚĀNTA SVAHĀ RAḤ JVALITE PRADĪPTE DHĀRA DHĀRA HŪṂ. Thus, [recite] the mantra three times.
While consecrating the rosary, one should recite the mantra for requesting dreams:
Oṃ samantānugrahāya pratimāṃ hūṃ. Reciting this mantra five times, one praises and invokes the empowerment for the request of dreams.
The mantra for protecting the body is: Oṃ samanta-avalokite hūṃ. Recite this mantra five times in praise.
Protecting oneself, one likewise protects others.
Recite the *dhāraṇī* of the boundary-marking: Oṃ samanta-mi-rū-kṣaṇi ṭhaḥ saṃ ṭhaḥ hūṃ. Recite this mantra three times around the altar, seven times for each circuit.
One should then bind the boundary of the Vajra Court.
Recite the Fire-Kindling Mantra: Oṃ samantād abhyantara-maṇḍale mahāpātāla-vare hūṃ. This is the mantra.
Recite the mantra while kindling the fire; this is the consecration of the fire.
With the Fire-Offering Mantra: *Oṃ dhu ru dhu ru pa ra śa ra du hu śri saṃtraye svāhā*, recite this mantra three times to consecrate the fire-offering and burn it as an oblation.
The mantra for supernatural powers is: Oṃ samantāvalokite guhye samayojaye padmāvati svāhā. Recite this mantra seven times in praise.
I invoke all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, mantras, vidyās, and deities.
May they manifest various miraculous transformations within the maṇḍala.

Regarding the mantras for the ritual implements: Oṃ śūpa-seṅktra (seṅ is pronounced as *sang* with a retroflex *ṭra*) dāmani pātma-bhūni hūṃ. By means of this mantra, cause all the ritual implements drawn within the maṇḍala to be gathered and brought under control.
Recite this seven times.
For the *dhāraṇī* of Gathering the Teachings: Oṃ samanta-karṣaṇi pāra-sara rucire hūṃ. With this mantra, cause all the dharma-gates within the maṇḍala to be gathered and drawn in.

This is the mantra for summoning; with it, empower the king of incense and burn it.
If one invokes Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva Mahāsattva,
even those who have committed the four grave offenses, the five heinous crimes,
or the ten evil deeds will likewise cause Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva Mahāsattva to manifest before them.
This is for the purpose of extinguishing and eliminating the four grave offenses, the five heinous crimes, the ten evil deeds, and other such transgressions,
and for the fulfillment of all vows;
how much more so for those with pure faith?
If good sons and good daughters receive,
uphold, read, and recite this according to the Dharma day and night,
will they not receive the certification of all dharmas in their present bodies?
If one consecrates a king of incense and burns it before an image of Maheśvara ten thousand times,
Maheśvara will manifest his body and appear to fulfill all one's wishes.
If one consecrates a king of incense and burns it before an image of the god Nārāyaṇa ten thousand times,
the god Nārāyaṇa will manifest his body, come forth, grant boons, and provide protection.
If one consecrates a king of incense and burns it before an image of the deity Mahākāla ten thousand times,
the deity Mahākāla will appear together with his retinue all at once.
He will respectfully protect [you] and grant your wishes, placing himself at your service.
If one consecrates the King of Incenses and burns it before an image of Vināyaka one hundred and eight times, [the result will be achieved].
All *vināyakas* shall be bound and unable to cause further affliction or disturbance.
If one consecrates the King of Incenses and burns it before an image of a celestial Māra one hundred and eight times, [the same result will follow].
One will not be disturbed or distracted by any devas, māras, spirits, or ghosts.
If one consecrates the King of Incenses (*gandharāja*) three times daily,
facing the sun, and burns it continuously for twenty-one days, [the desired result will be attained].
One will obtain the protection and the bestowal of blessings from the assembly of the Sun Deity appearing before one.
If one consecrates the King of Incenses and burns it continuously from the third day of the lunar month while facing the Moon Deity, [the same result shall be attained].
On the fifteenth or sixteenth day, at midnight,
the Moon Deity will appear before one and provide protection and empowerment.
If one consecrates the "King of Incenses," [the rite shall succeed].
If one performs ten thousand incense-burnings before an image of King Vaiśravaṇa,
King Vaiśravaṇa will manifest his form to provide protection;
by offering him wealth and treasures, one shall attain great abundance.
If one consecrates a thousand recitations with incense-king and burns it before the image of Śrī-devī ten thousand times,
the image of Śrī-devī will move and speak;
whatever questions are asked regarding the matters of bodhi, she will answer them all.
If one consecrates agallochum incense and burns it while reciting the mantra over one thousand and eight times over unbroken *mudrā* rice,
the deity will rise up, speak, and answer all questions regarding the sought-after dharma.
If one consecrates agallochum incense and burns it before the patient while reciting the mantra seven times,
that person will bind themselves.
If one consecrates agallochum incense and burns it while reciting the mantra over Jīvala one thousand and eight times,
Jīvala will move about, run, and speak of his own accord.
He will answer all that is asked and place himself at one's service.
If one consecrates agallochum incense by burning it before a vajra one thousand and eight times, [the same result follows].
Light radiates from the pestle.
If one consecrates *guggulu* incense and burns it while reciting the mantra one thousand and eight times over the wheel, [the rite is accomplished].
The wheel will rotate by itself.
If one consecrates *guggulu* incense and burns five-colored strips of cloth as an offering one thousand and eight times, [the wheel will turn].
Its form is like that of a coiled and winding serpent.
If one consecrates *guggulu* incense and burns it to fumigate a new jar, flask, or bowl one hundred and eight times, [the rite is accomplished].
Then one should rotate it oneself.
If one empowers agallochum incense and burns it as an offering before a consecrated sword one thousand and eight times, [the ritual is completed].
Emitting flames of light,
if one consecrates guggulu incense and burns it over a conch shell seven times, [the result follows].
Go to a high vantage point and blow [the conch] seven times;
all sentient beings who hear it will have their karmic obstacles of sin eliminated.
If one consecrates *guggulu* incense with this, [the same result follows].
If one fumigates a patient suffering from malaria twenty-one times with this incense,
they will be cured. Furthermore,
if there is no rain, [one may perform the same rite].
If one consecrates agallochum incense at the edge of a dragon pool and burns it in an unbroken stream of smoke one thousand and eight times,
a great rain will descend.
If the rain lingers excessively,
perform consecration over agallochum (guggulu) atop a high mountain peak;
burn it so that the smoke does not cease for one thousand and eight repetitions.
The rain will then cease and all calamities will be removed.
If evil winds, hail, or obstructive disasters frequently arise,
one should face the direction from which they originate and empower agallochum (guggulu) incense.
If one performs the fire offering one thousand and eight times,
wind and hail will cease for four months.
If one consecrates agallochum incense [with mantras], [the same result follows].
If one fumigates the body and clothes seven times with incense and wears it,
there will be no obstacles or difficulties wherever one goes. If one consecrates *guggulu* incense [in this manner], [the same result follows].
If one burns [this] one thousand and eight times within a storehouse,
it will cause wealth and treasures not to be wasted.
If one consecrates agallochum incense, [the same result follows].
If one fumigates all flowers, fruits, food, and drink twenty-one times,
those who eat them with others will all be able to eliminate all calamities and obstacles.
If one consecrates *guggulu* incense...
If one performs the empowerment of incense smoke, flower garlands, and human heads to be worn on the head,
those who question the person will all say that they have been bound by them themselves.
If one empowers the "King of Incenses" for twenty-one days, [the same result follows].
Offer burnt oblations to the image of Vajragarbha Bodhisattva,
reciting the mantra with each sound uninterrupted for one hundred thousand times.
Vajragarbha Bodhisattva will manifest his form and grant whatever boons are sought.
If one consecrates agallochum incense and burns it before an image of a yakṣiṇī one thousand and eight times,
one will cause the yakṣiṇī to manifest her form and provide respectful protection.
One shall serve as an attendant for whatever one seeks.
If one consecrates *guggulu* incense and burns it over a small bell or a large bell or drum twenty-one times, [the desired result will be achieved].
Even if one strikes [the drum], those who hear it shall have all their karmic obstacles and hindrances eliminated.
If one uses agallochum incense within a house,
reciting the mantra once for every hundred and eight burnings, [the same result will be achieved].
All calamitous and malevolent spirits and deities will flee in every direction.
If one wishes to verify this mantra for summoning,
by reciting it one hundred thousand times, all rites will be accomplished.

Recite the dismissal mantra seven times over white mustard seeds and water: *Oṃ ā-mukha-prasara padma-senā-dāra dāra abhyatāra-tu bhagavat saṃbuddhānāṃ tūru tūru mahā-padma-pūjane svāhā*. With these mantras empowered, scatter [the substances] throughout the ten directions; all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and celestial deities shall then return to their respective palaces.
Chapter Thirty-nine: The Chapter on the Bodhisattva Tārā’s Protective Sustenance. At that time, the Bodhisattva Tārā rose from her seat, joined her palms in reverence, and paid homage.
He prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, circumambulated him three times to the right,
and then standing to one side, addressed the Buddha,
saying: "World-Honored One, this is the Venerable Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara."

One who is able to skillfully expound this *Amoghapāśa-rāja-mūla-padma-kuṭa-dhāraṇī-mantra-maṇḍala-mudrā-samaya* shall bring about great benefit and happiness for those in the world who uphold the mantras.
"Blessed One, I also now possess the Samaya-mantra of the Root Lotus-Crown Dharani of Amoghapāśa.
If a practitioner [recites it] for twenty-one days,"

Empower white mustard seeds and water, pouring them over the crown of the head.
Furthermore, form the Great Empowerment Mudrā three times and empower the crown of the head.
Extensively teach the confession and the arousal of the bodhicitta.
Upon exiting through the four gates of the mandala, one should again perform prostrations.
One should extensively make offerings of food, drink, clothing, and precious wealth to the Triple Gem.

Those who can constantly practice in this manner according to the *Amogharāja-ṛddhivimukti-citta-saṃśodhana-dharma* (the Dharma of Purification by the Mind of the Unfailing King’s Supernatural Powers and Liberation), [shall attain the desired results].
One shall obtain a great mass of merit and be empowered by all the Tathāgatas;
all devas will constantly love and revere one,
and one will swiftly attain the most supreme accomplishment of all the *Amoghapāśa-dhāraṇī-mantras*.
All karmic offenses of the three doors, as well as obstacles, calamities, and illnesses,
will be incinerated and eliminated, resulting in the purification of the body.
Whatever Dharma one seeks in the mind shall all be accomplished.

43. The Universal Wheel-Turning King’s Āgada Medicine Section, Chapter Forty-Three. Furthermore, the World-Honored One possesses the Samaya of the Accomplishment of the Āgada Medicine for the Mantra Maṇḍala of the Amogharāja Abhijñā Vimokṣacitta Dhāraṇī.
To protect the kingdom and its cities from all calamities, he spoke these verses:
"By means of the *miñjaya-jaya* medicine, next by the *kṣudranakulī-pāyapāṇi-nakula*, and the *indrāpāṇitāga*."
*Khandapiṅgala oṣadhi | mahācakra pītacakra padmakeśara | miśrakoḷattha oṣadhi sumanā-sunandā | śvetacandanā nalanā* ||
Utpala flowers and saffron, Campaka flowers and nāgapuṣpa,
Tagara, sarja, and the resin of deodar; With śamīka incense, dūrvā grass, and other such substances,
Thoroughly refined and blended together, Along with uśīra and white sandalwood.
Combine these to form fragrant water and knead it into pills. Place them in a vessel of red copper, sealing it tightly.
In a secluded and pure place, prepare the ground with ritual purification. Construct a mandala four cubits on each side with its gate opening to the east;
in its center, draw a lotus flower with one hundred and eight petals. On the pedestal, draw two hands with their wrists joined together.
Spread the ten fingers apart like opening a lotus; on all four sides, one should paint opened lotus flower pedestals, upon which a vajra should be painted.
Together with the pāśa seal, there should be flames surrounding various lotuses, among which are many jewel trees;
the flowers and fruits of these trees are all composed of jewels.
Foliage, flowers, and fruits drape the tree; it marks the path to the jewel realm, pure, adorned, and established as the non-in vain king Avalokiteśvara.
With various banners, flowers, scented water, food, and lamps, one arranges offerings and makes worship;
a vessel of medicine is placed upon the great lotus pedestal.
Cover it with silk and perform the empowerment (*adhitiṣṭhet*). The mantra-practitioner, having bathed, anointed his body with fragrance, and donned clean garments, shall sit at the western gate.
Generating compassion for all sentient beings, he should recite the *Abhijñā-vimokṣa-citta* mantra and the *Hṛdaya-mantra*.
The empowerment of this medicine manifests three signs; this is called the accomplishment of the gāthā-medicine.
World-Honored One, if this medicine obtains the sign of light and a king wears it, he will eliminate all enemies and various calamities and epidemics.
If people wear this [amulet], they shall extinguish the four grave offenses, the five heinous crimes, the ten evil deeds,
and other such transgressions; their auspicious dreams will increase, they will encounter no obstacles wherever they go, and they will achieve victory in all discourse.
They shall attain liberation from all calamities, including those caused by kings, bandits, tigers, wolves, water, fire, thunder, lightning, and bolts.
They shall not be harmed by any dragons, snakes, insects, poisons, or toxic drugs that cause untimely death.
All spirits and demons will be terrified and flee in all directions;
the various devas and benevolent deities will cherish, revere, and protect them;
and all those who encounter one another will be filled with joy.
If those who sweep away [obstacles] wear this amulet, both men and women will be auspicious.
If it is placed atop a banner,
for a hundred li in every direction, there will be no calamities such as evil winds, thunder, hail, locusts, or any other such misfortunes.
It shall always be protected by all the devas, nāgas, and the eight classes of beings.
That medicine should then be dried in the shade within the maṇḍala.
Furthermore, World-Honored One, there is the Vidyārāja Amoghasiddhi-viśuddha-citta-dhāraṇī-mantra-maṇḍala-samaya Realgar-siddhi-samaya.
And he spoke in verse:
"Having purified a ground four cubits in length and breadth, adorn it by smearing it with white sandalwood paste;
open only the eastern gate, and in the center, paint a blooming lotus flower with one hundred and eight petals."
The petals are made of white sandalwood incense paste; the pericarp and filaments are made of turmeric incense paste;

and the seeds are made of aloeswood incense paste. Using white sandalwood, red sandalwood, turmeric, and other such substances as paste, one should paint two hands upon the pericarp with their wrists joined together.
The ten fingers are spread apart with the tips separated; on the four sides, open lotus flowers are depicted.
White sandalwood incense paste forms the petals, saffron incense paste forms the pericarp and filaments, and aloeswood incense paste forms the seeds.
They are arranged in a wide array, forming the appearance of the Vajradhātu path.

Place an image of the King of Unfailing Accomplishment (Amoghapāśa Avalokiteśvara), along with multicolored banners, flowers, various fragrant blossoms, scented water, food and drink, fruits, and lamps. Adorn and consecrate these as offerings;
then, using high-quality *rasāñjana* (orpiment) weighing three *liang*, place it within a refined silver casket.
Place it upon the hand-seal of the lotus pedestal; cover it with vermilion silk. When performing the empowerment of the rite, the mantra-practitioner shall purify their body and attire.

Throughout the six periods of day and night, burning incense and making offerings at the western gate, they shall sit cross-legged and form the wheel-hand seal, reciting and upholding the Heart Mantra of Supernatural Powers and Liberation.
Reciting the *dhāraṇī* and the heart-mantra (*hṛdaya-mantra*) continuously, one should empower white mustard seeds and strike them against the realgar without ceasing.
When hot smoke appears above it and its radiant form increases, at that time a great light will be emitted from the image. This is called the method for accomplishing realgar.

Blessed One, whoever has their eyes marked with this light-sign shall attain the samādhi known as the Vast Wisdom Adorned by the Radiance of the Non-empty Wish-Fulfilling Jewel, and shall realize supernormal powers.
The Great Mantra-Sage Samādhi of the All-Pervading Wheel of Amoghapāśa is constantly attended by ninety-nine hundred thousand koṭi-nayuta Ganges-sand-like great sages.
Surrounded by his retinue,
he wanders through all the palaces, mansions, and abodes of the mantra-vidyādhara sages,
acting as a great vidyādhara sage.
He constantly traverses all Buddha-fields throughout the ten directions,
while Amitābha Buddha perpetually dwells upon his crown,
never abandoning him as his lifespan increases for billions of kalpas.
Furthermore, he attained the samaya of the non-empty, pure Vairocana supernormal powers;
in a single kṣaṇa, he traveled throughout ninety-nine hundred-thousand-koṭi-nayuta buddha-fields in the ten directions.
In accordance with his buddha-field, he manifests vast and non-empty offerings to the bodies of all Tathāgatas, constantly emitting great flames of light;
all matters of his mindfulness and aspirations are fully accomplished.
If one applies the sign of smoke to the eyes,
one then realizes the samaya of all secret practitioners, vidyādharas, maharṣis, and ṛṣis, and intends to travel to visit all the devas and nāgas.
Within the mountain caves, pools, and palaces of the eight classes of beings,
one may enter at will without obstruction;
all gods and ghosts see themselves as subjects and submit.
They shall be appointed to serve as attendants and provide protection.
Furthermore, they will behold all the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Mahāsattvas,
who will bestow upon them the Samādhi of the Radiance Endowed with the Sovereign King of Non-Emptiness (Amogharāja-prabhāsa-sampanna-samādhi).
His feet were always four inches above the ground as he walked.
If one applies the "heat-sign" [ointment] to the eyes,
all people who behold him will have all their calamities and illnesses eliminated.
The two pay homage to one another.
This administrator of the medicinal ointment shall possess the knowledge of past lives (*pūrvanivāsajñāna*) regarding his future place of birth,
attain the contemplation of non-emptiness (*amoghadarśana*), and abide in a purified body.
He attained the realization of the samaya-gate of the all-pervasive equality of all non-empty Tathāgatas,
and received from all Tathāgatas the consecration and the prediction of the bodhisattva stages.
He dwells on the same stage as all the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.

Chapter Forty-Four: The Perfume of the Supernatural Powers of the Universal Turning Wheel-Turning King. Furthermore, within the *amogharāja-ṛddhi-vimokṣa-citta-dhāraṇī-mantra-maṇḍala-samaya*, there is the *samaya* for the accomplishment of the perfume of the supernatural powers of the Universal Turning Wheel-Turning King.
One should offer the supreme worship to all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Mahāsattvas,
and summon and gather all the Great Brahmā Kings, Śakras, Nārāyaṇas, Maheśvaras, and all other devas throughout the trichiliocosm.
It subdues all yakṣas, rākṣasas, vināyakas, and various malevolent spirits;
their bodies are all rent with pain as they flee in terror to the ten directions.
It crushes all enemies and eliminates all calamities.
If there are bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās who bathe for purification,
put on clean garments, and burn this incense to perfume their bodies,
they shall extinguish all heavy obscurations and calamities.
If one constantly burns and offers this incense while reciting the mantra of the *Abhijñā-vimokṣa-citta-dhāraṇī*,
then by the power of this *dhāraṇī* mantra and the supernatural fragrance, [the practitioner shall attain...]
The Mount Sumerus of the three thousand great thousandfold world systems;
all the celestial palaces of the devas, the palaces of the nāgas, spirits, and the eight classes of ghosts and deities;
the great oceans, rivers, and the sixteen hells.
The fragrances all arrived and transformed into various clouds of fragrant light,
which simultaneously illuminated everything and caused it to tremble.
Those in the various hells who encountered this light—
At that moment, it was transformed into a pond of lotuses;
all sentient beings therein were liberated from suffering and reborn either in the heavens or among human beings.
Sentient beings in the animal realm who encounter this light shall,
upon casting off these bodies, all attain liberation and be reborn among gods and humans.
Furthermore, those afflicted by any demonic illness, spirit possession, malaria, malignant sores, scabies, or any such painful diseases shall be freed from them.
Having all thoroughly bathed and perfumed themselves with the fragrance of burning incense,
they shall, through the power of this supernatural liberation-heart *dhāraṇī* mantra and its supernormal efficacy, immediately be cured of their ailments.
When their lives have ended, they will be reborn in the Pure Land;
because they are born by transformation from a lotus flower, they are liberated from all suffering.
Thus, he spoke these verses:
One hundred and eight parts of agallochum; thirty-two parts each of *gandharasa* and *an-sthi* incense; eight parts each of fresh saffron and *kshudra-nakhara*;
and [eight parts each of] *mushuruka*, *śrīveṣṭaka*, and *sugandhaka*.
Sallakī, agaru (aloe wood), nalada, candana (white sandalwood), jaṭāmāṃsī, and uśīra— these nine fragrances,
each three parts, along with fresh gandhapattraka and uśīra.
Take two parts each of *kunkuma*, *tagara*, *kakkola*, camphor, and musk;
take five parts of rock honey and two parts of white resin (*guggulu*).
Melt them together until blended, and first consecrate each ingredient individually with purification mantras.

Select and maintain them with purity, and prepare them for use. Constantly empower ceramic and silver vessels with the *mantra* from beginning to end, and place whatever is to be contained within them.
To compound this incense, one should bathe and purify the body on the eighth day of the bright fortnight in a secluded and clean place, put on clean garments, and thoroughly cleanse the ground.
Construct a four-cubit altar and smear it according to the ritual rules.
One should open the eastern gate and, at the center of the heart, paint a thirty-two-petaled lotus of the seven jewels.
On the pedestal, paint two hands with their wrists joined, the ten fingers splayed apart like opening lotuses. Above the two hands, encircle them with five-colored clouds.
On the four sides, one should paint blossoming lotuses; upon their pedestals, paint various hand-mudrās, and among the flowers, paint garlands of lotuses.
At the four gates, on the lotus pedestals, paint the noose mudrā;
in the four corners, paint the wind deity in the color of space, appearing as a half-body clad in celestial garments.
On all four sides are various colored flower garlands; banners and emblems adorn the vajra realm, pure and clean.
Incense boxes are placed upon the great lotus pedestal. Hand-mudrās are positioned at the heart, covered with crimson silk, where Amoghasiddhi and Avalokiteśvara reside.
Holding crimson cords, they encircle the boundaries of the maṇḍala.
Adorned with various banners and flowers, one should offer incense, flowers, scented water, the three white foods, ghee lamps, and oil lamps upon a seat.

Sitting at the eastern gate during the six periods of day and night, one should diligently protect [the rite] by burning incense and making offerings; at each interval, one should recite while forming the wheel-mudrā.
Empower the incense thirty-seven times with the *Amoghasiddhi-viśuddha-citta-mantra* and the *Hṛdaya-mantra*;
empower the incense seven times with the *Krodharāja-hṛdaya-guhyamantra*. Offer worship daily according to one’s inclination.
King Ajamukha, Avalokiteśvara, and the assembly of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas—
perform this rite for forty-nine days, or perhaps for one, two, three, or a hundred days,
until the three signs appear upon the incense; only then shall you attain the supernatural power of the "named incense."
In this manner, the World-Honored One constantly and perpetually, throughout the six periods of the day,
gives rise to great compassion for all sentient beings within the site of enlightenment. Within his own mind,
he contemplates the mind until the syllable *bhrūṃ* is perfectly accomplished.
Visualize that the syllable *SRA* completely transforms and appears as the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara King of Amoghasiddhi,
whose physical marks and radiant light are like the rising sun,
seated in the vajra posture upon a vajra pedestal.
Holding a censer in hand, burn this incense;
recite the Mantra of the Heart-Dhāraṇī of Supernatural Liberation and the One-Syllable Mantra to empower yourself,
making offerings to all the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Mahāsattvas of the ten directions.
From within this body, one visualizes the manifestation of immeasurable, boundless, unspeakably unspeakable numbers of bodies of the Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva King of Non-Emptiness,
filling all Buddha-fields throughout the ten directions before each and every Buddha, Bodhisattva, and Mahāsattva.
Recite the mantra of the *Ṣaḍakṣarī-vimokṣa-citta-dhāraṇī*,
holding an incense burner in hand while visualizing the appearance of immeasurable, boundless clouds of various colors,
fragrant light, banners, and precious canopies.
Flower crowns, necklaces, pearl earrings, bracelets, and armlets;
celestial and exquisite garments, wonderful flowers, and various fly-whisks;
palaces, pavilions, jeweled thrones, terraces, and gabled chambers.
Make offerings to all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Mahāsattvas;
form the offering mudrā and recite the mantra;
praise and pay homage to all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Mahāsattvas.
By the power of the great supernatural manifestations, offerings, and majesty of the mantra of the Heart Dhāraṇī of the King of Non-Emptiness,
it pervades the assemblies of the Tathāgatas throughout the ten directions— numbering ninety-nine hundred-thousand nayutas of koṭis of Gaṅgā-sand rivers.
They perform various kinds of offerings, immeasurable and boundless,
to all the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Mahāsattvas.
All those Buddhas simultaneously praise them.
All shall form the Seal of Non-empty Offering and recite the mantra of the Heart Dhāraṇī of the Sovereign of Non-empty Supernatural Powers and Liberation;
together with these supernatural powers, they shall provide consolation and empowerment.
One becomes endowed with a great mass of merit and roots of goodness;
for each and every Buddha, one attains roots of goodness accumulated through hundreds of thousands of millions of billions (*koṭi-nayuta*).
Furthermore, one contemplates that the dharmatā of the syllable *sra* is unborn.
Again, one contemplates immeasurable bodies as becoming a single body;
merging these into this single body, it becomes the syllable *Sra*.
One contemplates that the nature of the syllable is unborn, and further contemplates that the nature of one's own body is inherently empty.
If there be bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās who,
for one thousand days, remain pure and in accordance with the Dharma,
and prepare a maṇḍala according to their own wishes, adorned and purified.
At all times, one should make offerings to Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva with various grasses, flowers, and scented water,
burning this incense during the six periods of the day and night.
Confessing transgressions and making vows, one should practice contemplation according to the Dharma,
recite the Mantra of the Heart of Supernatural Liberation, and the One-Syllable Mantra; then,
with a solemn vow and earnest prayer, receive the Bodhisattva precepts.
Seeking anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi for a full thousand days, or two thousand days,
or three thousand days, or four thousand days.
They will certainly attain the simultaneous manifestation of the bodies of ninety-nine hundred-thousand-koṭi-nayuta-gaṅgā-sand numbers of Tathāgatas from the ten directions,
who will bestow upon them the prophecy of enlightenment.
He realized the samādhi of the vast wisdom of the light of the non-empty wish-fulfilling maṇi,
and the samādhi of the great mantra-adept of the all-pervading wheel of the Amoghapāśa.
The Amogha-purification-Vairocana-Abhijñā Samādhi and the Amogha-Tenth-Bhūmi-Abhijñā Samādhi;
one shall be born by transformation upon a lotus in a pure land.
One will remember and know one's past lives throughout ten million kalpas,
and shall never again fall back from unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment.
If one stays by the side of a dragon pool for seven days and seven nights, [one will attain these fruits].
Perform the rite of offering by consecrating this incense with the recitation of the *Abhijñā-vimokṣa-citta-dhāraṇī-mantra* and the *Ekākṣara-mantra* one thousand times. Then,
the Dragon Kings will be delighted and pay homage, causing a great rain to descend.
If one performs the rite of empowerment at the city gate,
burning and offering this incense while reciting this mantra one hundred and eight times,
it will cause all calamities and diseases within the city and its districts to be eliminated.
It causes all people to dwell in happiness and peace.
If one performs the rite of empowerment within a great assembly,
one should burn and offer this incense while reciting this mantra twenty-one times.
It causes all people to rejoice, pay homage, and extinguish all calamities and obstacles.
If a practitioner of mantras empowers this incense and burns it upon themselves,
they will always be respected and cherished by others.
If one consecrates incense and burns it over all sick people seven times,
they will be cured. If one consecrates incense and burns it over those who have been poisoned seven times, [they shall be freed from the poison].
Then one will obtain recovery from the illness.
If one circumambulates all fruit trees, fields,
or seedlings while reciting the ritual and empowering incense with one hundred and eight repetitions, [the same result shall follow].
Then it shall not be damaged by any evil winds, hail, or rain;
its fruits shall be abundant and fully endowed with flavor.
If, in any cities or villages, [this occurs]...
Within the monastery or one's residence, perform the rite of recitation;
by consecrating incense and burning it one hundred and eight times,
all calamities and anomalies shall be eliminated at once.
If one burns this incense to fumigate one's body and clothing,
there will be no obstacles or difficulties wherever one goes.
If one burns this incense on a high tower and fumigates a conch shell while reciting the mantra seven times, [the same result follows].
If one blows the great conch seven times, all sentient beings of the four modes of birth who hear the sound of the conch shall extinguish all karmic obstructions, calamities, and portents.
If one stands upon a mountain peak facing the direction from which fierce winds, thunder, and hail arise, [and blows it...]
Recite the mantra while performing the ritual of empowering incense by burning it one hundred and eight times;
thus, all [obstacles] will be immediately suppressed and dispersed.
If this incense is burned before a person who is approaching the end of life, [the same result shall be achieved].
If one recites the one-syllable mantra of the *Ṣaḍakṣarī-viśuddhi-citta-dhāraṇī* seven times,
upon casting off this body, one will immediately go to the Pure Land and be born by transformation within a lotus flower.
One will behold ninety-nine hundred-thousand-koṭi-nayuta-gaṅgā-sand numbers of Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas,
and thereby acquire great roots of virtue.
If one performs the ritual of recitation within a celestial temple, [the same result is attained].
Empower this incense while reciting the name of the celestial image,
and burn it before the image one thousand and eight times;
thus, all celestial deities will be pleased and provide protection.
If one performs rites regarding the forms of all the devas, nāgas, and the eight classes of beings,
one should always manifest wrath, glare with eyes wide open,
and gaze fiercely; while reciting the rite, one should empower this incense with a single consecration.
Recite the name of the deity as appropriate;
burn incense before the image of the deity one thousand and eight times,
causing the deity’s image to emit *turuḍīra*.
When the mantra-holder sees it, he shall take it; by dotting his forehead,
dotting his eyes, holding it in his mouth, or smearing it upon his body,
all the deeds he performs will be accomplished.
One will immediately obtain the protection and assistance of all yakṣas;
one will acquire great physical strength, and all ghosts and spirits will revere and protect one.
If one recites this mantra while performing the ritual empowerment of this incense, [the same result shall be attained].
Recite the name of Mahābrahmā and burn incense before an image of Mahābrahmā one thousand and eight times;
then milk will flow from the hands and body of the image of Mahābrahmā.
When the mantra-holder sees it, he should take it and smear it upon his body;
he will then obtain a body like that of Mahābrahmā.
If one recites the mantra while performing the ritual, a single empowerment of this incense [will achieve this].
One should recite the name of the deity Nārāyaṇa and incense the image of Nārāyaṇa one thousand and eight times. Then,
fragrant water will emerge from the body of the image of Nārāyaṇa.
When the mantra-holder sees it, he should immediately take it and smear it upon his body;
he will then attain a body like that of Nārāyaṇa,
and holding a great wheel in his hand, he will soar through the air with sovereign ease.
If one performs the ritual of recitation and mantra-empowerment upon this incense once,
and while invoking the name of Maheśvara,
burns it as an offering before an image of Maheśvara one thousand and eight times; then [the goal will be accomplished].
When the image of Maheśvara exudes perspiration from its body,
the mantra-holder, upon seeing it, shall take [the substance] and smear it upon his own body;
he will then attain a body like that of Maheśvara.
Holding a trident, he soars through the air with sovereign ease.
In this manner, for each of the celestial images when performing ritual practices,
one must first empower the head of the image with the One-Syllable Mantra ten thousand times.
Then, the ritual procedure was performed exactly as desired.
This is the Blessed One’s mantra of the Maṇḍala Samaya of the Heart Dhāraṇī of the King of Non-Emptiness and his supernormal powers and liberations.
The Nine-Headed Dragon King accomplishes the samaya.
He empowers white sandalwood powder mixed with wax and fashions the form of the dragon king.
His body was four spans in height;
his crown-knot, face, hands, feet, and finger-joints were adorned with ornaments and garments,
appearing as majestic and beautiful as a celestial deity.
Above his head, nine snake heads emerge;
his divine head and body are adorned with gold.
Construct a maṇḍala.
Place the dragon king in the center and arrange solemn offerings.
Every day, at each specific time, recite the mantra of the *Ṣaḍakṣara-viśuddha-citta-dhāraṇī* (the Heart Dhāraṇī of Supernatural Powers and Liberation).
Empower this incense by burning it before the dragon king twenty-one times.
Recite the heart-mantra of the Wrathful King to empower white mustard seeds;
strike the nāga king seven times.
Practice in this manner without interruption during the six periods of day and night.
When the image of the Nāga King rises and manifests its own movement,
the mantra-holder, seeing it move,
should recite the Heart Mantra of Caṇḍamahāroṣaṇa with a swift and wrathful mind.
Empower white mustard seeds and strike them upon the nāga king,
causing him to ascend into the air and travel with sovereign ease.
When the holder of the mantra beholds him ascending, [the rite is successful].
He then thought to transform this sacrificial ground into a great pond and to settle the nāga therein;
with a mind of great fury, he recited the heart-mantra of the Wrathful King.
Recite the empowerment mantra over white mustard seeds one thousand and eight times and strike this altar ground;
Nanda the Dragon King will then transform this altar ground into a great pond where two dragons shall dwell.
If there are people, birds, or beasts that drink this water or bathe in it,
they shall all eliminate all calamities, illnesses, defilements, obstacles, and grave offenses.
May there always be timely falls of great sweet rain,
so that fruits may ripen and be endowed with manifold flavors.
If [one is] at the entrance of a deep mountain or a great cave, [may this be accomplished].
Regarding the ritual procedure for holding incense and reciting mantras:
first, empower this incense; then, burn it one thousand and eight times. Thereupon, the portal of the cavern will open of its own accord, and one may enter within without obstruction.
The Amoghapāśakalparāja Sūtra, Scroll Twenty;
The Amoghapāśakalparāja Sūtra, Scroll Twenty-One.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Bodhiruci of India during the Great Tang Dynasty.

Chapter Forty-Five: The Section on the *Āgada* Medicine of Wish-Fulfilling Power. Chapter Forty-Five: The Section on the *Āgada* Medicine of Wish-Fulfilling Power. Furthermore, the World-Honored One possesses the Samaya of the Accomplishment of the Wish-Fulfilling Jewel *Āgada* Medicine, which is the Mantra Maṇḍala Samaya of the Heart-Dhāraṇī of the Sovereign King of Non-Voidness (*Amogharāja*) and the Liberation of Supernatural Powers.
All dharmas thus cultivated do not pass away in vain;
they are able to remedy the afflictions of various diseases caused by sorcery, poisons, and venomous insects, as well as calamities from kings, bandits, tigers, wolves, and the like.
Water, fire, blades, and staves shall all fail to cause them harm.
The people will pay them respect.
Even when facing enemies or disputes, they shall always emerge victorious.
Their lifespan shall be long and free from premature death.
They will be constantly protected by the Great Brahmā, Śakra Devendra, Nārāyaṇa, Maheśvara,
the Four Heavenly Kings, and all the celestial beings, nāgas, and the eight classes of divine attendants.

When the medicinal substances remain within a square area of one yojana,

Round as a jujube fruit, contained within a silver vessel; when compounding this medicine,
