Maheśvara is the foremost in the samaya of the maṇḍala for the accomplishment of homa; this is the homa-samaya.
All the Tathāgatas constantly bestow their blessings upon the samaya of the homa maṇḍala of these Vajrasattvas;
if one performs the burnt offering and presents the offerings three times throughout the day and night for seven days, [the result will be attained].
Then one shall attain the five supernatural powers (*pañcābhijñā*) and become a celestial immortal;
all the devas will assemble like clouds to grant wishes and provide protection,
as will all the Buddhas and Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas.
Rejoicing and offering praise, upon awakening from the dream,
all past and present heavy karmic obstructions and grave offenses,
as well as epidemics and hostile enemies, are entirely extinguished.
It subdues all yakṣas, rākṣasas, and vināyakas,
as well as all malevolent spirits and ghosts who inflict calamities and harass humans;
it causes them all to disperse, or else to submit with joy, joining their palms in reverent devotion.
The people of the land shall all be peaceful and happy;
the five grains will be abundant, and there will be no calamities or diseases.
All the fire deities will manifest in dreams and awakenings.
To fulfill all aspirations, they observe and protect [beings]:
all the celestial deities— the Sun God, the Moon God,
the Star Gods, King Yama, the Water God, and the Four Great Kings.
Each [deity], together with their retinue, shall protect [the practitioner] day and night.
Thus is accomplished the Heart-Dhāraṇī of Supernatural Powers and Liberation.
The mantra-practitioner shall bathe the body and don clean garments.
On the fifteenth day of the waxing moon, one should perform the rite without eating or speaking for the duration of the day and night.
One should take lotus flowers, cow’s ghee, and non-glutinous rice,
and perform the consecration and homa at the three periods of each day.
Upon reaching the seventh day, one attains accomplishment.
Even if one has committed the five heinous crimes of immediate retribution,
one shall attain accomplishment despite not yet having earnestly repented.
Thus, the mantrin should not allow a web of doubt to arise in the mind.
If one wishes to accomplish the samaya of the maṇḍalas, mudrās, and [mantras] of all Tathāgata families, [one must act accordingly].
Cut pieces of agalloch wood and *nyagrodha* wood and kindle them as fire.
Using lotus flowers, *śāli* rice blossoms, white mustard seeds, and cow’s ghee,
perform the consecrated homa ritual three times each day.
When the full seven days have passed, one will attain accomplishment.
If there are foreign enemies who invade and disturb the kingdom,
one should bathe the body, don clean garments, and kindle a fire using thorny branches of the purple *śiṃśapā* tree.
Using white mustard seeds, agallochum incense, cow’s ghee, honey, and curd,
perform the consecrated homa for a full seven days;
then those hostile military forces will retreat and disperse.
Furthermore, using the skin of a *sarpa* (serpent) as an offering,
with leftover flowers, white mustard seeds, salt, and black mustard oil, perform a consecrated *homa*.
Those military forces shall be harmed by wind and hail and will retreat and disperse.
If one seeks rain, for one day and one night,
one should refrain from eating and speaking, bathe the body, and wear clean garments; then,
one should make offerings of various incenses and flowers according to the ritual dharma.
Perform the consecration and homa ritual with white mustard seeds and fennel seeds for one day and one night without interruption,
and a great rain will fall. If it does not rain,
perform this rite in this manner for seven days without ceasing.
If a great rain falls throughout Jambudvīpa,
or if there is persistent drizzle,
one should take this "rain-seeking ash" and hold it high toward the clouds.
If one sprinkles [the water] while reciting the empowerment mantra one hundred and eight times, the rain will immediately cease.
If one wishes for the Fire Deity to manifest his form,
one should bathe the body, wear clean garments, and abstain from food and speech for one day and one night.
Burn *sumana* wood completely in the fire.
At three times each day, perform *homa* offerings of non-glutinous rice, honey, granulated sugar, black pepper, and *pippalī*, consecrating them with mantras.
When the seven days are complete, the Fire God will spontaneously manifest within the hearth.
"O White Mantra-holder who breathes forth flames from your mouth, what do you seek now?
I possess the nectar of immortality with its flaming radiance; I shall now bestow it upon you."
This nectar-light is contained within the darkness;
by loudly uttering the syllable HŪṂ,
a great flame issues forth from the mouth.
The mantra practitioner shall receive it;
thereafter, it will fulfill their wishes.
If they desire to behold the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara manifesting his form, [they shall do so].
Cut one hundred thousand pieces of white sandalwood and perform *homā* according to the ritual rules six times daily with cow’s ghee,
reciting mantras until they are completely consumed by the fire.
Then one shall obtain the manifestation of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara and the fulfillment of one's wishes.
If one desires to eliminate all illnesses, [one should use] rice,
large-grain barley, small-grain barley, white mustard seeds, black beans, sesame seeds, and white grains.
If one performs the consecrated homa for seven full days, one will immediately be cured.
If one desires to be treated with respect by persons of high status, one should perform the consecrated homa using white non-glutinous rice and cow’s ghee; then one’s wish shall be fulfilled.
If one wishes for all people to be joyful,
one should perform homa with white mustard seeds, rice grains, flowers, and cow’s ghee;
through this consecrated offering, those who see it will rejoice.
If one wishes to subdue all yakṣas and rākṣasas,
by performing *homa* with white mustard seeds, agallochum incense,
and cow’s ghee while empowered with mantras, they will all submit and come under control.

Furthermore, Blessed One, there is the Samaya of the accomplishment of the painted image of the Maṇḍala of the Mantra-Dhāraṇī of the Heart of the Abhiñjā-Vimokṣa of the King of Non-Emptiness (*Amogharāja*).
It manifests the accomplishment of various signs, ascends into all phenomena, and accumulates a boundless mass of merit and roots of goodness.
Having beheld the various transformed manifestations of the Tathāgatas and Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, as well as the siddhi-samaya,
one should [draw them] upon a white cotton cloth or silk,
measuring eight cubits in both length and width.
In the center is depicted the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara Amoghapāśa,
with three faces and ten arms, his body the color of pure gold;
on the central face, there is a single eye between the eyebrows.
His three faces are radiant with joy, and he wears a moon-crown upon his head,
within which resides an emanation Buddha. His right hands hold a noose,
a lotus flower, a trident, and a khaṭvāṅga staff.
The left hands hold a wish-fulfilling jewel (*cintāmaṇi*) and a precious staff;
one hand extends in the gesture of granting fearlessness (*abhaya-mudrā*), one hand holds a rosary,
and two hands are joined in *añjali* at the chest.
Wearing a garment of deer skin and a white necklace around his neck,
he was adorned with various celestial robes, precious earrings, bracelets,
and armlets; he sat cross-legged upon a lion throne of manifold jewel-lotuses.
The Bodhisattva Śvetaketu on the left slightly lowers his head;
with both hands joined in *añjali*, he sits in the half-lotus posture (*ardhaparyaṅka*).
The Bodhisattva Tārā on the right also slightly lowers her head.
With palms joined together and seated in the half-lotus posture,
behind Bodhisattva Tārā is the Great Furenu King (Mahāpracaṇḍarāja), who has three faces and four arms.
In the center of the main face, there is a single eye between the eyebrows.
The three faces are wrathful, and the heads are adorned with moon crowns upon which transformation Buddhas reside.
One hand holds a lasso, and the other hand grasps a sword.
Holding a trident in one hand and an axe in the other,
he sits in the half-lotus posture behind the Bodhisattva Śvetaketu.
The Great Mantra Vidyārāja has three faces and two arms.
His three faces are serene and smiling; his head is adorned with a moon-crown, upon which resides an emanation Buddha.
One hand holds a lotus flower, and the other holds a wish-fulfilling jewel (cintāmaṇi).
They sat in the half-lotus posture,
each adorned with various celestial silken garments,
precious necklaces, earrings, bracelets, and all manner of ornaments.
Adorned with blazing light and seated upon a lotus throne,
behind the Great Mantra-Vidyārāja sits the messenger Duti;
followed by the goddess Sarasvatī, the deity Śaṅkhinī, and the deity Āśvapatā.
Behind the seat of the Wrathful King are the rākṣasī goddess Ekajaṭā, the goddess Śivadūtī, the deity of crops, and the deity of the earth;
these deities, appearing like celestial maidens, sit in the half-lotus posture.
Each was adorned in their respective traditional attire and held various weapons.
Upon the head of the King of Amoghasiddhi Avalokiteśvara were Vairocana Tathāgata, Lokêśvararāja Tathāgata, and Śākyamuni Tathāgata.
He sat cross-legged upon a precious lion throne.
To the Buddha's right were the gods of the Śuddhāvāsa heaven, Mahābrahmā, Nārāyaṇa, Maheśvara, and Vaiśravaṇa.
Holding various celestial flowers,
to the left of the Buddha were Śakra-devendra, the son of Maheśvara, King Īśvara, King Maheśvara, and King Yama.
Holding various celestial flowers,
with the Sun Deity and Moon Deity on his left and right,
and the twenty-eight lunar mansions of the stellar deities on his four sides.
On all four sides, arranged in a circle, are great lunar discs.
Upon each disc are the seal of the vajra, the seal of the vajra-sword,
the seal of the wish-fulfilling jewel, and the seal of the trident.
The noose mudrā, the battle-axe mudrā,
the conch mudrā, and the wheel mudrā—
upon these mudrās, flames of fire swirl.
Furthermore, lotus flowers bloom all around the four sides;
upon their pedestals are various hand-seals (mudrās),
and from each seal, flames of fire blaze forth.
The boundary of the first inner court is a garland of precious lotus flowers;
the boundaries of the next two courts are vajra-wheels surrounded by flames;
and the boundaries of the outer three courts are streets of the seven treasures.
One should open four gates;
the innermost courtyard is circular, while the two outer courtyards are square.
If there is one who, according to the Dharma, draws this maṇḍala image and its mudrās and samayas:
Then one shall attain the eradication of all karmic obstructions and the defilements of sins from beginningless time;
one shall swiftly achieve the realization of dharanis and mantras,
and master the samayas of all mandalas and mudras of every lineage.
May all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas of the ten directions, past and present,
and all the Tathāgatas Vairocana,
grant their grace and protection to this maṇḍala samaya.
This samaya is the true secret maṇḍala mudrā-samaya of the Amoghapāśa;
should there be anyone who sees, hears, or rejoices in it with sympathetic joy.
One shall attain liberation from all beginningless fetters and defilements,
and realize the vision of ninety-nine hundred-thousand-ten-million-billion *gaṅgā-nadī-vāluka* Tathāgatas.
He also beheld the lineage assembly of all Vairocana Tathāgatas, which encompasses the samaya of all maṇḍalas and mudrās;
furthermore, he beheld the lineage of all Tathāgatas of the ten directions and the three periods of time, and all their maṇḍalas, mudrās, and samayas.
Furthermore, he beheld all the mudrās and samayas of the maṇḍalas of the entire Avalokiteśvara family;
he also beheld all the mudrās and samayas of the maṇḍalas of the entire Vajra family.
Furthermore, seeing all the maṇi lineages and all the maṇḍala-mudrā-samayas,
one should know that from this point onward,
such a person will constantly travel to the pure lands of the ten directions.
One is born through transformation from a lotus flower,
never again falling into the bodies of any of the realms of the three miserable paths.
Therefore, among all dharmas, this maṇḍala and its mudrā methods are the most supreme.
If there are those who rejoice in this samaya,
they shall obtain the greatest, immeasurable accumulation of merit, provisions, and roots of goodness.
Furthermore, O World-Honored One, there is the Amogharāja-ṛddhi-vimokṣa-citta-dhāraṇī-mantra and the samaya for the accomplishment of the white sandalwood image.
It measures sixteen finger-widths.
Empowered by mantra, it depicts the King of Unfailing [Vows], Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva,
with three faces and four arms, seated in the vajraparyaṅka posture.
The central face has a single eye between the eyebrows;
the three faces are compassionate and serene in expression.
Each head is adorned with a moon-crown made of various jewels, within which resides an emanation Buddha.
The left hands hold a noose and an opened lotus flower;
the right hands grasp a three-pronged vajra and extend one in the gesture of granting fearlessness.
A profusion of various jewels and celestial garments rains down.
Adorned with various ornaments such as pearl necklaces, earrings, and bracelets,
he sat upon a lion throne of precious lotuses,
his body wreathed in blazing radiance.
To the left sits the Bodhisattva Candanagandhā Tārā upon a lotus throne;
to the right sits the Bodhisattva Candanagandhā Śvetā upon a lotus throne.
They are adorned with celestial garments and precious necklaces, earrings, and bracelets.
One should properly adorn that altar with lotus-stamen mud and white sandalwood incense mud,
using white sandalwood incense mud, saffron incense mud, and aloeswood incense mud.
In its center is depicted a thirty-two-petaled lotus flower in full bloom;
lotus flowers are also in full bloom on its four cardinal and four intermediate directions.
The pedestal and petals are made of white sandalwood incense paste.
Use saffron paste for the filaments and anthers;
use aloeswood paste for its seeds and fruits.
Place the image upon a lotus pedestal.
One should first arrange *argha* offerings, scatter various fragrant flowers,
and burn aloeswood incense and white sandalwood incense.
The mantra-holder should always bathe cleanly and wear fresh, pure garments.
With great compassion, he further developed various supreme practices for enlightenment;
every month, beginning from the first day of the waxing moon, he partook of the three white foods until the fifteenth day.
For one day, do not eat or speak, and diligently maintain the practice.
Perform the boundary-binding (*sīmābandha*) and mudrās to protect yourself and others.
According to the ritual, visualize the image while sitting cross-legged facing east.
By means of the form of Avalokiteśvara as the King of Non-Emptiness,
and by means of the Vajra Body, Speech, and Mind Seals of the Wisdom-Seal that sustains all phenomena,
one enters the wheel of mantra syllables, which encompasses the form of Avalokiteśvara.
The Samaya of the Light of the Wheel of the Equality of Avalokiteśvara’s Wisdom:
Recite and maintain the Mantra of the Heart-Dhāraṇī of Supernatural Powers and Liberation without interruption.
When one prays for the image to emit a great radiance that covers and illuminates the altar,
the mantra-practitioner will behold Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva appearing before them.
Extending his hand to stroke the crown of [his head], he praised him in a loud voice, saying:
"Excellent, excellent, son of good family!
You are able to perform this vast and magnificent offering."
That which is now being composed is the universal compendium of the lineages of all Tathāgatas;
it reveals the dharma of the mantras and dhāraṇīs of the heart-liberation of the sovereign Amoghasiddhi, comprising the samayas of all profound and secret maṇḍalas and mudrās.
Because you have attained accomplishment,
what do you seek that I might fulfill for you?
This very body of yours in this life is a birth-body dwelling within a buddha-field.
Furthermore, you shall never again fall into the three evil destinies of birth from a womb, an egg, or moisture.
Your place of birth shall be the pure land of reward of Amitābha Buddha,
where you will be born by transformation within a lotus flower.
They constantly see all Buddhas and realize the various dharmakṣāntis.
Their lifespans last for immeasurable hundreds of thousands of kalpas,
until they reach anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, never again to regress.
I shall always protect you.
At that time, furthermore, empower a flower crown with the mantra of the Great Wrathful King and place it upon your head.
Even if one rapidly recites the mantra of the Great Wrathful King one thousand and eight times,
the secret protection and supernatural powers of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva will enter and abide within one's body,
whereby one realizes supernormal powers.
They travel to all Buddha-fields throughout the ten directions,
attaining the supreme accomplishment of the mantra, maṇḍala, mudrā, and samaya of the Great Stainless Unfailing King’s supernormal powers, liberation, and mind-dhāraṇī.
I shall eliminate the various grave offenses committed in previous lives— such as shedding the blood of a Buddha and causing a schism in the Saṃgha—
and thereby attain a body of pure integrity.
May all the aspirations of the world be fulfilled;
may all obstacles and burdens be abandoned;
and upon casting off this body, may one realize the samādhi of pure contemplation, the radiance of liberation.
Through the samādhi of the Pure, Stainless, Radiant Maṇḍala,
any sentient being who beholds this person shall likewise be cleansed of all defilements, obscurations, diseases, and afflictions.
If a person of the candāla caste performs this rite,
they shall purify all outflows over four thousand days;
by practicing mindfulness and purification without slackening, they will then attain accomplishment.
I manifest my body and dwell before such persons,
so that they may realize the supreme vows;
how much more so for those who are pure and possess the faculty of faith!
It shall certainly be accomplished.
This person of pure faith need only maintain constant, tranquil mindfulness without interruption;
for whenever I manifest my body, I shall grant the highest accomplishment to any practitioner who upholds this Dharma.
One should not give rise to even a slight thought of doubt.
Although that *caṇḍāla* was a sentient being with grave offenses,
the World-Honored One [responded] even after he had prayed once, twice, three, four, or five times.
If one possesses this rite and practices it with diligence,
yet does not achieve success, it is due to the obstruction of one's karmic offenses;
in such a case, I shall not manifest before them.
Regarding the body, it is for the purpose of accomplishing the Dharma.
Why? Because of the hindrance of transgressions, and because the power of faith and the power of mindfulness are not firm or pure.
By means of this, these individuals shall, throughout their entire lives,
diligently cultivate this dharma until their offenses are finally extinguished;
in future lives, they will certainly fully realize the seeds of unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
World-Honored One, there may be bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, sons of good family, or daughters of good family who,
although they uphold this Dharma, do not for the most part maintain the precepts;
their minds are constantly characterized by stinginess, greed, flattery, and double-tongued speech.
They cause schism in the Saṃgha and the Dharma with foul and evil speech;
they are mediocre and improper, ignorant of gratitude and righteousness;
they revile and speak ill of the Triple Gem, and fail to contemplate causes and conditions.
They crave wealth and sensual pleasures, failing to respect their teachers or what they have received;
they steal various dharmas such as mantras, vidyās, mudrās, letters, sūtras, and diverse teachings;
their minds are constantly wavering, characterized by malice and envy.
With a poisonous mind, indolence, and pride, they look down upon others;
they constantly act with arrogance, coveting wealth and sensual pleasures,
and do not truly revere the forms and symbols of the Triple Gem.
They do not truly respect or honor their preceptors and instructors who personally teach them the Dharma,
nor do they respect these sūtras of this section or other sūtras.
World-Honored One, such sentient beings possess perverse minds and are stubborn and recalcitrant.
I have indeed not attained what was to be attained; yet,
for the sake of manifesting great protection for this body,
O World-Honored One, the nature of these people is extremely [corrupt].
Deceitful and harmful,
with malevolent wisdom flourishing and ignorance hardened,
I too have constantly been treated with contempt and slandered.
It is said that they intend to extract the blood from my limbs and body.
Now, all the lineages and assemblies of the Tathāgatas of the ten directions and the three periods of time,
and all the most profound secret dhāraṇīs and mantras, are gathered here in unison.
They also slander and mock the samaya of the Great Maṇḍala mudrā with all manner of faults and evils;
such are these most wicked Caṇḍālas.
Day and night, thus failing to reflect upon themselves,
they sought only to destroy all Tathāgatas of the ten directions and three periods of time,
as well as all Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
By what means can the profound and secret dhāraṇī-mantra,
the great maṇḍala, and the samaya-seal be accomplished?
"World-Honored One, such bhikṣus and bhikṣuṇīs, as well as sons and daughters of noble family,
are truly great thieves of the Cāṇḍāla lineage;
though their speech, conduct, and demeanor appear to be virtuous,"
Internally, their undertakings are entirely rotten;
day and night they constantly contemplate and practice various kinds of the ten unwholesome actions,
and they do not perform even a hair’s breadth of the correct cultivation of the mind.
"World-Honored One, these people are great thieves of the caṇḍāla lineage.

Such slander, defamation, and malicious accusations truly constitute the destruction of the lineage and the assembly of all Tathāgatas throughout the ten directions across the past, present, and future."
One should know that those who [violate] all the profound and secret dhāraṇīs and mantras,
as well as the great maṇḍala mudrās and samayas,
are constantly abandoned by all Tathāgatas and all Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the ten directions and the three periods of time.
These are great thieves of the Caṇḍāla lineage;
they are capable of destroying the entire family of all Tathāgatas and obstructing the profound, secret dhāraṇīs, mantras, maṇḍalas, mudrās, and samayas.
It should be known that these individuals are further capable of destroying all Tathāgatas’ secret-heart dhāraṇī-mantras, great maṇḍalas, mudrās, and samayas;
they are also capable of destroying all Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas’ secret-heart dhāraṇī-mantras, great maṇḍalas, mudrās, and samayas.
Therefore, World-Honored One, you have clearly declared that these bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, sons of good family,
and daughters of good family are all called great thieves of the caṇḍāla lineage.
These sentient beings are constantly possessed by all the vināyakas, demons, ghosts, and spirits.
They have fallen away from all mantras and all sublime dharmas;
all their roots of virtue have been utterly consumed;
furthermore, they are completely abandoned by all dharanis, mantras, vidyas, deities, and mandala deities.
Having fallen away from all dhāraṇīs, mantras, vidyās, and the supramundane and mundane paths of samaya,
such individuals as these will certainly dwell in the Avīci hell.
This is the seed for experiencing uninterrupted and intense suffering.

O Blessed One, it is due to this karmic cause and not through my own fault that these sentient beings have themselves abandoned all the Tathāgatas of the ten directions and three times, as well as all the great Bodhisattvas, their various families, maṇḍalas, mudrās, and samayas.
One abandons for oneself all the samayas of the maṇḍalas, mudrās, and mantras of the vajra family throughout the ten directions and the three periods of time.
One abandons for oneself all the secret great maṇḍala mudrā samayas of the Vairocana Tathāgata family.
Huī knew that these people were constantly possessed by various māras, vināyakas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, and all manner of ghosts and spirits,
who had seized them with all kinds of karmic obstacles.
World-Honored One, such sentient beings are conditioned by these karmic causes; it is not my fault,
nor have I abandoned them.
"Blessed One, these types of candālas and the like have as their sole occupation the accumulation of the poisonous fires of greed, hatred, delusion, and ignorance;
they burn away all secret dhāraṇīs, mantras, great maṇḍalas, mudrās, samayas, and various roots of goodness."
Furthermore, one has already burned away all roots of goodness consisting of the practices of the maṇḍala, mudrās, and samayas of the Tathāgata family;
furthermore, one has already burned away all roots of goodness consisting of the practices of the dāna, mudrās, and samayas of the Vajra family.
Furthermore, they have already incinerated all roots of goodness—the secret great mudrā-samaya practices of the lineage of all Vairocana Tathāgatas.
World-Honored One, such individuals as these are *caṇḍālas*.
In the present and the future, they have never achieved [liberation].

Having cast off their bodies, they shall constantly undergo various kinds of uninterrupted and intense suffering within the great hells for as many eons as there are atoms in the lands of the ten directions.
These people, who are like *caṇḍālas*,
shall find no peace or happiness in either this life or future lives.

Therefore, O World-Honored One, those wise ones who seek this Great Liberation Lotus Maṇḍala Seal Samaya Sādhana Method of the Heart-King Dhāraṇī Mantra of the Truly Non-Empty Lasso should [strive for it].
One should show universal respect and humility toward all sentient beings,
firmly resolve upon the mind of great compassion to rescue and deliver them,
and abide in a mind that relies upon and upholds the truth.
Relying upon the upādhyāya and ācārya,
one should attend to and revere them as if they were the Tathāgata,
and even more so than one's own parents.
I shall transmit to you each of the dharanis, mantras, mandalas, mudras, samayas, letters, and phrases;
do not forget them or allow for any error.
All my limbs, bones, flesh, sinews, and marrow—[I entrust to you].
They all provided offerings and sought instruction in the Dharma;
how much more so with various kinds of wealth,
clothing, bedding, dwellings, servants, and food and drink?
Not abandoning this constitutes the offering of the Dharma.
If one can thus cultivate the Dharma,
then one is constantly making offerings to me.
This person [remains] for one week, two weeks, three weeks,
up to seven weeks; or again for a hundred days,
or a thousand days, or even three or four thousand days.
Furthermore, for those who constantly serve and mindfully recollect me,
I shall manifest my form to them, secretly guiding and pursuing them,
and provide them with protection and aid.
Bhagavān, it is just as when the great ocean, at every time of tide,
has its waves arrive simultaneously at the shore;
I likewise arrive whenever I bring them to mind.
They dwell in the darkness and manifest their presence to guard this person,
just as when a drop of oil is cast into water, it spreads and covers the surface following the flow of the drop.
I likewise recollect and conceal them accordingly.
Whether those sentient beings possess pure right knowledge or whether they are among humans or in the hells.
If you constantly keep me in mind,
I shall grasp the noose and the supreme hook to pull you out from all intense sufferings.
They shall reach the celestial palaces or the Buddha-fields,
realize unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment, and experience all manner of bliss; furthermore,
they shall be granted the power of immeasurable great diligence.
All their aspirations shall be completely fulfilled.
If there are sentient beings who behold this image,
they will immediately see my own body.
Why is this? Because I constantly abide within the body of this sandalwood image.
World-Honored One, wherever this image is located, that place is like a Buddha-stūpa and like the very body of the Buddha.
It is also like the place of the samaya of the mudrās of all Tathāgata families, which universally integrates all true secret great maṇḍalas;
it is also like the place of the samaya of the mudrās of the maṇḍalas of all the luminous devas.
It is also like the bodhimanda of all Tathāgatas,
where the great wheel of Dharma is turned, the four māras' armies are defeated, and great nirvāṇa is manifested;
it is a place of assembly with palaces adorned with the seven treasures.
World-Honored One, I now state this with certainty;

By practicing this seal-samādhi, one ensures that all dharmas are not practiced in vain;
the mass of merit thus obtained is equal to the virtues of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
For the Amoghapūjā-mudrā, join the wrists; with the two middle fingers, the two ring fingers, and the two little fingers, bend them together so that their tips touch one another.
The palms should be opened at a distance of two and a half inches.
The two index fingers are each held straight and upright,
with their tips three inches apart;
as for the two thumbs:
Extend both index fingers upright,
with their tips positioned at a distance of two finger-widths from the space between the third joints of the two middle fingers.
This mudrā is the samādhi-offering to all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Mahāsattvas of the ten directions and the three periods of time.
This is the gateway to the accumulation of merit from the unsurpassed and most excellent offerings.
For the Amogha-Hook Seal (*Amogha-aṅkuśa-mudrā*), join the wrists and bend the tips of the two ring fingers like hooks;
press them against the side of the middle joints of the middle fingers.
The tips of the thumbs do not touch.
Extend the two little fingers straight upward,
with their tips three inches apart.
Join the tips of the two middle fingers so they touch one another.
Extend the two index fingers and the two thumbs straight forward as before.
This mudrā, the Samādhi Hook, realizes the various samādhis and the bodhicitta-dharma of all Buddhas of the ten directions.
Because it accomplishes the fruit of the liberation of Amoghasiddhi,
the Seal of the Purification of the Non-empty Dharmadhātu follows the third seal,
with the sole modification being that the right index finger is bent.
Clasp the upper side of the middle joint of the middle fingers;
the rest is to be performed according to the previous instructions.
This samādhi-mudrā can shake the great earth.
Raining down various flowers from the midst of the sky as an offering to all Buddhas:
for the Seal of Great Non-empty Destruction, join the wrists and bend the tips of the two middle fingers inward like hooks;
the two ring fingers are held upright with their tips touching one another.
The two thumbs, the two index fingers, and the two little fingers are extended straight upward,
following the third seal as previously described.
By the power of this samādhi seal, one is able to destroy all hells.
The intense sufferings of sentient beings are all completely extinguished.
For the Amogha-maṇi-ratna-mudrā: join the wrists; slightly bend the heads of the two middle fingers so they touch one another;
and slightly bend the heads of the two ring fingers so they are separated by one and a half inches.
Extend the tips of the two middle fingers.
Place the sides of the two thumbs against the heads of the index fingers.
Slightly extend the two index fingers.
Slightly bend [the head] so that the distance between the heads is three inches;
extend the two little fingers outward and upward.
The heads are four inches apart.
From this seal-samādhi, immeasurable varieties of colored light emerge,
making offerings to the ocean-like assemblies of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the ten directions.
For the Amoghapāśa prostration mudrā, join the wrists; place the two middle fingers, the two ring fingers, and the two little fingers side by side with their tips touching;
extend the two index fingers straight, keeping them two and a half inches apart.
Place both thumbs straight upward inside the palms of the index fingers, with the tips of the thumbs separated by one *cun*.
With this mudrā, enter the maṇḍala for prostration,
invite the Buddhas for offerings, perform recitation, and practice the Way.
All should first offer worship to the ocean-like assembly of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
To form the Seal of the Great Boundary (*mahā-sīmā-bandhana-mudrā*), turn the left hand upward and cross the tip of the thumb over the index,
middle, ring, and little fingers, creating an opening at the base of the fingers.
Cover the right hand with the index, middle, ring, and little fingers inserted into the "tiger's mouth" of the five fingers of the left hand;
the thumb enters from beneath the left hand into the palm.
Lay the index, middle, ring, and little fingers across the upper shoulder blades.
Hook the two hands together to form fists.
This mudrā of samādhi possesses the power of a vajra for delimiting the boundary and protecting the body.
One shall not be harmed by any *vināyakas*.
For the Amoghapāśa Fist Seal (*amoghapāśamuṣṭimudrā*), the thumbs of both hands each press against the side of the proximal phalanges of the ring fingers.
Each [hand] forms a fist by grasping the thumb with the middle, ring, and little fingers;
each index finger is extended straight upward.
Each strikes their chest and ribs.
By the power of this seal and samādhi, one is able to make the great bodhicitta firm;
it is accompanied by compassion and protected by the blessings of all Tathāgatas.
These nine seals are the samaya of the Seal of Great Power of Amoghasiddhi;
they can eliminate all five sins of immediate retribution and enable one to enter all pure lands of the ten directions.
Because it manifests as the samaya-seal of the lineage of all Tathāgatas of the ten directions and the three periods of time,
and because this seal was taught by Vairocana Tathāgata.
Avalokiteśvara contemplates, protects, and praises [this].
If there is anyone who constantly forms this mudrā,
they will swiftly attain the perfect fulfillment of the six pāramitās.
The Great Wrathful King’s *mudrā* of the mace: stand with the body slightly tilted.
With the four fingers of both hands, cross the right over the left and insert them into the palms.
Quickly clench the hands into fists.
Press the two thumbs against the sides of the middle joints of the two index fingers.
Place the seal upon the crown of the head and extend the arms upward.
This seal-samādhi subdues all the Great Wrathful Kings, causing them to be utterly shattered and dispersed.
To form the seal of the Great Wrathful King’s Threatening Gaze, stand the hands in the shape of a "T" (the *ding* character).
With both thumbs, press against the side of the base joints of the ring fingers.
Each [hand] should form a fist by tightly gripping the thumb with the middle, ring, and little fingers,
while extending each index finger straight.
Press the left hand against the upper side of the waist;
extend the index finger forward.
Place the right hand directly over the chest, holding it upright.
With the index fingers facing outward toward the sides,
form the gesture of making a pact.
This mudrā and samādhi subjugate all evil nāgas, devas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, asura kings, and vināyakas.
All spirits and ghosts who create obstacles shall be utterly dispersed and destroyed;
it can also annihilate all grave offenses, including the ten evil deeds and the five heinous crimes.
All [obstacles] are completely eliminated.
For the Seal of the Crown of the Great Furen Wang (Mahā-krodharāja), insert the right thumb into the mouth of the left hand's tiger-claw,
together with the index, middle, ring, and little fingers.
Quickly grasp the left thumb;
form a fist with the index, middle, ring, and little fingers,
leaving the left thumb exposed.
Insert [the thumb] into the tiger’s mouth of the right hand, and with the index, middle, ring,
and little fingers, grasp the right thumb.
Form a fist with the index, middle, ring, and little fingers.
This seal, when bound as a samādhi, establishes a boundary and bestows protection upon the body;
it serves as the means for realizing and integrating all dharmas.
The Amoghapāśakalparāja Sūtra, Scroll Twenty-two;
The Amoghapāśakalparāja Sūtra, Scroll Twenty-three.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Bodhiruci of Central India during the Great Tang Dynasty.
Chapter Forty-Eight, Part Two: The Mandalas and Mudrās of All Families. Regarding the Mandala and Mudrā of the Great Furenu (Mahā-pratāpa) King: it follows the twelfth mudrā as previously described.
Only change the right index finger,
extending it straight outward.
This mudrā is used for all ritual applications within the maṇḍala.
Regarding the mudrā for summoning the Great Wrathful King: with both hands, interlace the index, middle, ring, and little fingers such that the right hand presses down upon the left;
hook them together and grasp firmly.
Extend the two thumbs, moving them up and down;
by this mudrā and samādhi, one invites all mantra-deities, vidyā-deities, and deities of the altar to assemble at the ritual site and remain there.
The Seal of the Great Wrathful King Seeing Reality (Mahā-krodharāja-dṛṣṭa-tattva-mudrā) follows the fourteenth seal mentioned previously;
however, one modifies it by interlocking the joints of the ten fingers so that the tips of all the joints protrude.
Place both thumbs with the right pressing upon the left, bend them into a fist,
and join the wrists so they touch.
By this mudrā, one will swiftly perceive the true nature of all dharmas through samādhi and behold all devas and humans.
The mudrā for making offerings to the Great Wrathful King (*Mahākrodharāja*) is as follows: join both palms together with the hollows of the hands left empty;
extend both thumbs and press them against the upper side-textures of the middle joints of the middle fingers.
Bend both index fingers and press them upon the backs of the two thumbs;
the backs of the two index fingers should be joined together.

This seal-samādhi can rain down all kinds of the seven treasures, garments, palaces, towers, pavilions, banners, pennants, jeweled canopies, and various flowers from both water and land throughout all lands of the ten directions and the three periods of time.
With clouds of oceans of all kinds of wondrous fragrances,
they extensively perform offerings to all those Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Mahāsattvas in each and every Buddha-assembly.
The Great Furen-wang (Great Wrathful King) seals the various devas with his right hand; all five fingers are extended together,
the elbow is bent so that it is level with the shoulder,
and the palm faces outward.
Press the tip of the index finger against the tip of the thumb;
extend all five fingers of the left hand downward and hang them loosely.
This mudrā pacifies all the celestial deities of the samādhi assembly.
Causing all to rejoice, they shall beg for all their wishes.
For the consecration mudrā of the Great Furenu King (Mahā-pratyaṅgira), join the palms and extend the index, middle, ring, and little fingers of each hand.
Bend both middle joints of the index fingers so that their tips touch each other;
extend both thumbs straight and place them side by side.
Placed alongside the side of the index finger:
if one is consecrated by this seal-samādhi,
one will receive the praise of all Tathāgatas.
The mudrā for dispatching the Great Furen Wang (Mahā-krodharāja) is as follows: the right hand is placed against the chest with the palm facing upward;
the middle finger is bent into a hook, and the thumb is likewise bent toward the palm.
The distance between the middle finger and the index finger is half an inch.
The index, ring, and little fingers are each slightly spread and bent.
Move the thumbs back and forth.
With the left hand, palm facing upward, place it upon the left knee.
This mudrā is the samādhi for dispatching all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, mantras, vidyās, and deities.
By practicing these ten seals,
one will swiftly attain all siddhis before them;
all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Mahāsattvas will be entirely delighted.
The Great Moisture Seal (Mahā-ārdrā-mudrā): Join the wrists and open the palms of many Bodhisattvas.
The five fingers of the right hand are spread and slightly bent like lotus petals;
the distance between each of the five fingers is one cun.
With the left hand, press the thumb against the base of the ring finger;
then, with the middle, ring, and little fingers,
clench the thumb to form a fist.
The index finger is extended straight and slightly bent.
This seal assists in the accomplishment of all dharmas through samādhi.
For the hook seal of the Bodhisattva Mahāśvetā, join the wrists and open the palms.
Bend the two middle fingers like hooks.
With the thumbs, index fingers, ring fingers, and little fingers of each hand,
hold them together in a loose, open spread, slightly bending them.
The distance between each of his ten fingers was one cun.
The tips of his two thumbs, his two middle fingers,
and his two little fingers were each one cun apart.
This seal brings about mastery and accomplishment among all dharmas through samādhi.
Furthermore, for the Great Śvetaketu Bodhisattva’s Seal According to the Mind, join the wrists;
extend both thumbs side by side and flatly.
Slightly bend the tips of both index fingers and both middle fingers;
the tips should be one inch apart.
Straighten and extend both ring fingers upward.
The two little fingers are each slightly bent,
their tips separated by half an inch.
The space between the tips of the index and middle fingers is one inch.
By practicing this seal-samādhi according to one's mind,
all dharmas will be accomplished.
The Bodhisattva Mahāśvetā performs the fundamental contemplation seal while sitting in the full lotus posture.
The head is slightly lowered toward the right shoulder, gazing downward.
The right hand is bent upward with the palm facing up;
the tips of the index and middle fingers are bent.
Supporting the right ear-opening,
the thumb, ring finger, and little finger are spread apart and slightly bent.
Extend the left hand upward and place it upon the right knee,
forming the gesture of contemplation (*cintā-mudrā*). This seal is the samādhi for all seals and samayas.
This is the most supreme.
For the Bodhisattva Mahāśvetā, the hook mudrā of the mind-seal of all dharmas is formed with the right hand positioned at the front of the heart;
the thumb presses against the base of the ring finger.
With the middle, ring, and little fingers,
grasp the thumb to form a fist with the fingers bent like hooks;
with the left hand, the thumb presses upon the joint at the base of the ring finger.
Clench the fist by grasping the thumb with the four fingers and place it upon the left knee.
These five mudrās are exceedingly rare.
If one constantly maintains this bond,
the ten non-virtuous actions and the five heinous crimes, along with all karmic obstructions, will swiftly be entirely extinguished,
and one will achieve a mass of all meritorious virtues.
One shall achieve all success through the mantra, vidyā, and mudrā methods of the Avalokiteśvara family.
As for the fundamental mudrā of Bodhisattva Tārā: with both hands, join the middle, ring, and little fingers.
Each forms a fist with the backs of the fists joined together;
the two index fingers are each slightly bent.
The heads [of the hands] touch one another;
the two thumbs are extended straight and parallel,
pressing down upon the sides of the middle fingers.
This seal and samādhi assist in accomplishing all mantra-maṇḍala seals and samayas of the King of Non-Emptiness.
The heart seal of Bodhisattva Tārā follows the fundamental seal.
Bend the two index fingers to form a fist;
slightly bend the two little fingers so that their tips touch one another.
Extend both thumbs side by side and press them against the upper sides of the index fingers;
the remaining fingers are positioned as before.
This mudrā-samādhi is the foremost among the auxiliary rites for the Amogharāja method.
For the consecration offering mudrā of Bodhisattva Tārā, join the wrists and extend the two middle fingers straight upward.
Bend the first phalanges of both hands so that their tips touch one another.
Bend the two index fingers so that each presses against the side of the middle phalanx of the middle finger, forming a hook-like shape.
Form fists with both ring fingers;
extend both thumbs side by side,
pressing down upon the sides of the ring fingers.
With the two little fingers extended upward and their tips joined,
this mudrā-samādhi can produce an ocean-like cloud of immeasurable and various colored objects for offering,
making offerings to all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and the assembly of Mahāsattvas.
Furthermore, one should protect the body by means of the seal of consecration (*abhiṣeka*).
For the Bodhisattva Tārā’s seal for subduing Māra, the left hand is placed at the heart,
grasping the wrist of the right hand.
The middle, ring, and little fingers of the right hand are placed side by side and held upright, pointing forward;
the index finger and thumb are bent tightly toward the palm like a hook.
This seal-samādhi subdues all evil yakṣas, rākṣasas, and vināyakas;
they all flee in terror, none daring to oppose it.
Thus, these four seals assist in accomplishing the samaya of the seals of the Mañjuśrī Amoghapāśa King’s maṇḍala.
All karmic obstructions shall be completely extinguished;
all practices and vows shall swiftly and fully be perfected.
Regarding the Great Body Seal (Mahāmudrā) of the Lotus Sunārī deity: the ten fingers of both hands enter into the palms.
With the right hand pressing down on the left fingers,
the palms face each other in a hook-like shape.
Forming fists from the joined palms, the right thumb presses upon the back of the left thumb.
This seal is the samaya-seal of the Amogharāja-maṇḍala for the assembly of the Samādhi;
it accomplishes all dharmas.
The seal of the Bodhisattva Mahāpāṇḍaravāsinī is according to the Sūnārī seal.
Change the two index fingers so they stand straight up,
slightly bending their tips until they touch one another.
The two thumbs are bent sharply inward like hooks.
Open the palms three inches apart;
the remaining fingers are as described before.
This seal is the samaya-seal of the King of Amogha that assists and protects the maṇḍala; it accomplishes all dharmas according to one's practice.
The mudrā of the one-tufted rākṣasī goddess is performed according to the pāśinī mudrā,
with the modification that the two thumbs press down upon the sides of the two middle fingers.
Join the palms together so they touch;
the remaining fingers are to be adjusted as before.
This mudrā is for the Samādhi of King Amoghasiddhi in this maṇḍala assembly.
It subdues all vināyakas who create obstacles and assists in the attainment of siddhi.
For the Frightful Eye Mudrā, follow the Rākṣasa Mudrā, but open the palms.
Insert both thumbs into the palms,
each pressing against the top of the side of the little finger;
extend both index fingers straight upward.
Joining the tips together,
the two middle fingers and the two ring fingers are hooked together as before.
Place the two thumbs against each other at the upper side of the back of the fingernails.
This mudrā is the samaya of all the terrifying deities of the Amogharāja Maṇḍala, which assists the assembly of samādhi.
For the Kīlikila mudrā, join the palms; hook the middle fingers, the two ring fingers,
and the two little fingers of the right hand over those of the left to form fists facing each other,
with the two thumbs extended side by side.
Press the sides of the middle fingers of both hands together;

extend the two index fingers straight upward so that they support one another. This mudrā is the Samādhi-Assembly for the simultaneous accomplishment of all Kīlikās; it is used for the purpose of Samādhi.
The Vajraśekhara mudrā is identical to the Cakravartin mudrā,
with the exception that the two index fingers are bent at their upper joints like hooks.
This mudrā is the samaya of the Samādhi Assembly, the mudrā of the Amogharāja Maṇḍala, and the samaya of all the Vajra families.
The mudrā for the Tārās is modeled after the Kīlikīla mudrā;
it is formed by interlocking the tips of the two little fingers and holding them upright.
This mudrā is the samaya for all the mudrās of the Tārās within the ritual methods of the Samayoga-Abhyudgata-rāja-maṇḍala.
The mudrā for the boundary-binding of the Great Wrathful King is modeled after that of the Messenger;
however, one changes it by inserting the two little fingers into the palms and interlacing them to form fists.
With the two index fingers extended straight upward and their tips joined,
this mudrā of samādhi binds the realms of the ten directions and restrains all vināyakas.
The mudrā for the invitation and authorization of the Great Wrathful King is the boundary-binding (sīmābandha) mudrā.
Modify it by interlocking the tips of the two middle fingers;
then, with the tips of the two index fingers, press against the joints on the backs of the two middle fingers.
Press the two thumbs against the sides of the two ring fingers.
With the two index fingers, count back and forth; this mudrā is used for the samādhi of summoning, dispatching, and invoking all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Vajras, mantras, vidyās, and deities.
The mudrā for making offerings to the Great Furenwang (Mahākrodharāja) is the same as the mudrā for invocation;
however, the two index fingers are modified so that each presses against the side of the middle joint of the respective middle finger.
This seal, empowered by samādhi, consecrates all articles of offering.
One arranges them within the maṇḍala and makes offerings with it.
For the empowerment and bathing seal of the Great Furenu King (Mahācaṇḍarāja), join the palms; extend the two little fingers and the two ring fingers together and upright.
Slightly bend the heads [of the fingers] so they touch one another.
The two middle fingers and the two index fingers are held straight upright;
slightly curve their heads, each being about one cun apart.
Insert both thumbs into the palms and bend them double like hooks.
Place this seal of samādhi upon the crown of the head.
Have a person pour scented water over the seal and bathe the body with it for consecration.
For the Great Furenu (Mahā-krūra) King, the seal for removing garments corresponds to the seal for consecration.
Bend the two index fingers into hooks.
When wearing or removing clothing during this mudrā-samādhi,
empower the garments with this seal before putting them on, and release it upon taking them off.

The Great Furenno King (Mahā-krodharāja) recollects the mantra and mudrā: join the palms, press the two little fingers against the backs of the two thumbs, and extend the two ring fingers straight upward.
Slightly bend the two index fingers so that their tips touch;
keep the two middle fingers straight and erect,
slightly curved at the tips, with a space of one inch between them.
Bend both index fingers inward like hooks.
By means of this mudrā, one will be remembered by all bodhisattvas, mantras, vidyās, and deities,
who will protect and never forsake one.
The Great Wrathful King Purifies: With the right hand, touch the thumb and the little finger together;
extend the middle and ring fingers straight and parallel.
Bend the index finger like a hook.
With this seal of samādhi, take water and sprinkle it upon the eyes, nose, throat, mouth, ears,
and forehead to purify the karma of body and speech.
For the mudrā of the Great Wrathful King with Incense and Flowers:
the index finger of the right hand is joined to the tip of the thumb;
the middle finger is held upright and slightly curved.
The ring finger and little finger are placed side by side and held upright.
This mudrā is used for the consecration of incense and flowers during samādhi; it is the proper offering mudrā.
For the lamp mudrā of the Great Wrathful King, follow the incense and flower mudrā, with the modification that the middle finger is extended straight.
With this seal, empowered by samādhi, one performs homa over the lamps and the sacrificial food.
For the Great Furenuwa (Mahā-krodharāja) Mahācakra Seal: the right hand’s thumb, index finger, middle finger, ring finger, and little finger are each extended upward and spread apart.
Insert the thumb, index finger, middle finger, ring finger,
and little finger of the left hand between the spaces of the index finger, middle finger, ring finger, and little finger of the right hand.
Quickly grasp the back of the right hand with the left.
Press the first phalanx of the back of the right thumb with the left thumb.
With this mudrā of samādhi, rotate it three times clockwise around the body.
Cast [the hand] three times each upon the upper body and the lower body.
Thereupon, the Great Wrathful King Avalokiteśvara manifests various great supernormal transformations and the *samaya* signs.
As for the seal of the Great Wrathful King for subduing the *vināyakas*, both hands have the four fingers [extended].
Form fists by grasping the upper joints of the thumbs.
Bring the faces of the two fists together tightly.
This mudrā of samādhi subdues all vināyakas so that they may not cause harm or disturbance.
The mudrā of the Great Wrathful King for subduing all gods and ghosts is modeled after the mudrā for subduing Vināyakas:
clasp the hands with the palms touching,
then extend both thumbs side by side.
Press the upper sides of the middle joints of both index fingers.
With this seal of samādhi, one subdues all yakṣas, rākṣasas, and various spirits and ghosts, preventing them from causing further harassment or harm.
The body mudrā of Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva is modeled after the mudrā for subduing spirits and ghosts;
however, one modifies it by straightening the two index fingers,
slightly bending them so that their tips are one inch apart.
Extend both thumbs side by side and press them against the middle joints of the sides of the two middle fingers.
This mudrā is the samaya-seal for the Samādhi-Assistance Avalokiteśvara King Mañjuśrī Maṇḍala.
The heart-seal of Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva is performed according to the previous Vajra-body seal;
with the fists joined face-to-face,
change the left index finger by extending it upright.
The right index finger is tightly bent like a hook.
This mudrā is the samaya-seal of the Samādhi that Assists and Protects the King of Amogha Maṇḍala;
it may be employed for all ritual activities.
Join the palms of the three realms' heavenly mudrā; spread and separate each of the ten fingers,
bending the tips so they touch one another,
with each space between the joints of the ten fingers measuring half an inch.
This seal-samādhi is the samaya-seal of Maheśvara, Nārāyaṇa, and Mahābrahmā;
it is able to assemble all the celestial hosts of the triple world.
Abiding in the samaya of the mudrā of the Maṇḍala of the King of Non-Emptiness,
the mudrā of Yama-rāja is modeled after the mudrās of the deities of the Three Realms,
with the modification that the right index finger and thumb are bent inward.
Each [finger] is bent like a hook;
the left index finger and thumb are each slightly bent.
This mudrā is the samaya-seal of the Amogharāja Maṇḍala for the Samādhi Assembly.
The mudrā of Varuṇa is modeled on that of Yama-rāja;
however, one should bend the left index finger and thumb into a hook shape,
ensuring that their tips do not touch those of the right index finger and thumb.
This seal-samādhi is named the Heart Seal of All Dragon Kings.
It accords with the Samaya Seal of the Amoghapāśa King Maṇḍala Assembly.
The seal of the god Kumāra follows the seal of Varuṇa.
Modify the two index fingers by bending them over the upper joints of the two middle fingers.
This mudrā is the Samaya-seal of the Amogharāja-maṇḍala for the benefit of the Samādhi-assembly.
The seals of all Tathāgatas of the three periods are formed by joining the wrists, with the five fingers of the right hand extended upward, slightly bent.
The intervals between the five fingers are each one inch apart.

The tips of the left thumb and little finger touch one another, while the index, middle, and ring fingers are held together, pointing straight upward. This mudrā is to be bound within the Samādhi Maṇḍala.
Then one attains the supernormal powers (*abhijñā*) of all Tathāgatas and is comforted by them.
For the Sealing Gesture of the Great Wrathful King (*Mahākrodharāja*), join the palms sideways;
extend the two ring fingers and the two little fingers straight upward with their tips joined.
The middle fingers of both hands are bent so that they rest against the upper joints of the sides of the two ring fingers;
the tips [of the middle fingers] are half an inch apart.
The two index fingers are bent like hooks.
One inch to the side of the second fingers;
the two thumbs each rest upon the second fingers, slightly bent.
This is the Samādhi Maṇḍala Assembly of this Seal.
One should prostrate and entreat all Tathāgatas to make offerings to it.
As for the seal of the gate to the maṇḍala of the Great Wrathful King: join the wrists and open the palms.
The two thumbs and the two little fingers are held upright,
slightly bent, with their tips joined.
The two middle fingers and the two ring fingers are each bent into the shape of a hook.
The tips of the two index fingers are four finger-widths apart; they are held upright and extended, slightly bent,
with their tips four finger-widths apart.
The distance between the eight fingers at their junctions is half an inch.
This mudrā is the samādhi that empowers all maṇḍala gates;
it is the samaya-mudrā of the fifty-three seals within the maṇḍala of the family of Avalokiteśvara, the Great Unfailing Wrathful King.
The power is able to accomplish the siddhi-samaya.
Thus, for all who employ these mudrās,
they shall all attain accomplishment.
These mudrās are taught through the empowerment of the great supernormal powers of all Buddhas of the three times.
If there is anyone who practices these mudrās, [they shall attain success].
That location shall be a stūpa containing the relics of all Buddhas and a ground as firm and solid as vajra. Furthermore,
if there be any person who constantly practices these mudrās, [they shall likewise attain such a place].
It should be known that such a person has already attained the stage of non-retrogression.

Chapter Forty-nine: The Samaya of the Mantra-Syllable Wheel Mandala of the Great Furanu-rāja. O Bhagavat, this is the Samaya of the Mantra-Syllables and Mudrās for the Maṇḍala of the Great Furanu-rāja Amogha.
It can accomplish all methods for attaining *siddhi*;
it can eliminate all dark karmic obstacles;
and it can block all karma leading to the three evil realms.
If there are those who, relying upon this secret dharma-gate of the Vajra Wisdom Seal of all Tathāgatas, practice this maṇḍala seal samaya,
they will certainly attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
Having fulfilled all the various practices and vows for the enlightenment of all Buddhas,
one should purify and smear the ground over an area of five cubits square,
delineating the boundaries of the courtyard and opening four wide gates.
Upon a blue ground within the inner courtyard,
there is a thousand-petaled, fully blossomed lotus;
upon its pedestal, the two hands are joined with the wrists touching.
Looking upward, open the fingers and palms;
the central pāśa-mudrā has the left and right hands entwined,
with the two ends of the cord fashioned in the shape of dragon heads.
Surrounding the upper flames,
one should sequentially paint the seals and mantras of the fifty-eight weapons upon the lotus petals,
encircling them with radiant light.
In the four directions and four corners, lotus flowers are in full bloom.
Upon the pedestals in the four directions are the vajra-flower-garland-vajra seal and the jewel-lotus-garland seal,
surrounded above by flames.
Upon the four-cornered pedestal is the seal of the *vajra-maṇi* jewel, encircled by upward-flaming fire.
The next court is filled everywhere with the waters of the great ocean,
and there are lotus flowers on all four sides.
On each of the platforms, one should sequentially paint fifty-eight hand-seals (mudrās) and mantras,
surrounded by the radiance of their syllables.
On the platforms of the four gates, there are the seals of the vajra-maṇi jewel.
Above is a flame. On the four-cornered pedestal, there is a seal of a crossed vajra (viśvavajra) surrounded by upward-flaming fire.
In the next court, on a blue ground, are lotus and Sumeru thrones at each of the four sides.
There are seals of jeweled banners, canopies, and various precious flowers and fruit trees;
at the four gates and four corners, upon pedestals, are wish-fulfilling jars from whose mouths emerge lotus stalks and leaves.
The waters of the four gates are bounded internally by the diamond-marked boundary of the two inner courtyards;
externally, the precious ground boundary is encircled above by various colored maṇi-jewels emitting upward-flaming light.
Various banners and flowers, *argha* water, scented water, ghee lamps, oil lamps, all kinds of food and drink were arranged as offerings;
various famous incenses were burned, along with diverse flowers, rice blossoms, white mustard seeds, and various powdered incenses.
One should scatter [offerings] upon the mandala as an act of worship.
The mantra practitioner, having purified their body and clothing according to the ritual rules,
shall cause the upāsakas to pay respectful homage and receive the empowerment (abhiṣeka).
Those who enter this maṇḍala shall enter the samaya of the mudrās of the maṇḍala of the lineage of all Buddhas.
They shall extinguish all defilements, burdens, and karmic obstructions from billions of kalpas in the past,
and all their vows and practices shall swiftly be fulfilled.

The Honored One’s mantra-samaya is as follows:
within all the maṇḍala-mudrā-samayas of Avalokiteśvara,
one should perform the rite of consecration three or five times according to the specific nature of each object.
Then, one will swiftly achieve accomplishment without any obstacles.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara again addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One..."
Because the Tathāgata has heard, spoken, recited,
and studied the *Sarvāśūnya-tathāgata-guhyakula-samāja-sarvamandala-mudrā-samaya-guhya-dharmatā-niṣprapañca-mahāsukha-āśūnyavajra* [Sūtra], he has accomplished the reality of all things.
Through skillful means, he establishes supreme wisdom;
all his activities subdue the world,
pervading the three realms with sovereign supremacy.
This samaya has been selected and elucidated from among all the methods of mudrās and maṇḍalas for the true liberation of unsurpassed bodhi;
it is for the sake of the mantra-practitioner’s perfect accomplishment of all bodhi and the elimination of all veils and hindrances.
If bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, sons of good family,
or daughters of good family are able to rely upon the profound wisdom-seal of the Tathāgata Sarvārthasiddha and well establish the vajra-dharma-gate of the nature [of reality],...
With a mind of great compassion, one should reverently make offerings,
uphold, recite, transcribe, and explain it,
or likewise teach others to transcribe and uphold it.
Reflecting in accordance with the Dharma and practicing with purity,

one should never abandon or neglect [this practice], but always rely upon each of the maṇḍalas, mudrās, and samayas within the samaya of the Heart-King Dhāraṇī Mantra of the Unfailing Lasso (Amoghapāśa).
I shall follow each ritual action performed according to the mantra methods and provide protection for you,
in order to eliminate the heavy sins and defilements of beginningless time.
I pray that you grant the vow for the swift manifestation of the methods of accomplishment according to one's measure and for their non-emptiness.
O Bhagavān, I shall never forsake such a person;
I shall establish them in the stage of non-retrogression.
"Up until the turning of the wheel of Dharma at the stage of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*,
I shall always serve and cherish such a person,
just as Ānanda served the Tathāgata."
Without a moment's negligence,
he served [the Buddha] in this manner until his parinirvāṇa, whereupon he collected the śarīra relics and erected a stūpa for them made of the seven precious substances.
With various flowers, incense, banners, pennants, precious canopies, and robes,
they constantly make offerings without interruption.
World-Honored One, regarding such a person as this, I—
Thus, with love, joy, reverence, respect, and devoted service,
one makes offerings to the World-Honored One. Yet, if there is a *caṇḍāla* who upholds this Dharma,
though he does not recognize kindness or righteousness, outwardly appearing virtuous while inwardly practicing corruption.
They secretly steal all dharanis, mantras, mandalas, mudras, and samayas;
they are arrogant and conceited, lacking the bodhicitta;
they do not maintain pure precepts and do not abide in compassion.
Deceitful, crooked, jealous, and mutually disparaging, they slander all dhāraṇīs, mantras, maṇḍalas, mudrās, and samayas; furthermore,
they lack faith in these dhāraṇīs, mantras, maṇḍalas, mudrās, and samayas.
Such people as these are truly of an evil lineage, the *caṇḍāla* caste.
O World-Honored One, regarding such *caṇḍāla* persons,
I shall employ various skillful means and supernormal powers.
If one desires to deliver this person from even a small measure of calamity and is unable to provide relief,
it is due to these causes and conditions that the practice fails to achieve success; it is not my fault.
Furthermore, World-Honored One, there are bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, and sons of noble family whose bodies and minds are tranquil and who uphold the precepts of the Tathāgata;
with right view and right faith, they [practice] this Great Liberation Lotus Maṇḍala Seal Samaya of the Heart-King Dhāraṇī Mantra of the Amoghapāśa.
Fully relying on the various dharmas and being free from all envy,
they shall diligently apply themselves day and night to receiving, upholding, reading, and reciting them without ever ceasing.
Out of my love and affection for such persons, I shall carry them upon my shoulders and never abandon them.
All the dharmas sought by the mind shall be fulfilled.
At that time, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni praised the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, saying:
Excellent, excellent, O Great Compassionate One!
This vow you have made is the most supreme vow.
You should indeed fulfill such a vow.
He delivers all sentient beings in the world,
causing them all to dwell securely in the stage of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
At that time, the Vajradhara Lord of Secrets—
All the retinues of the maṇḍala deities, the deities of the four great kings,

"Excellent, excellent, O Greatly Compassionate One!
We, this great assembly, shall follow the Venerable One throughout the world."
One should reverently make offerings to this Great Liberation Lotus Maṇḍala Seal Samaya of the Amoghapāśahṛdaya-rāja-dhāraṇī-mantra.
This Dharma is truly the samaya that unifies the lineage of all Tathāgatas.
We shall all be able to constantly and diligently uphold, recite, copy, hear, revere, and make offerings to it according to the Dharma, seeking great accomplishment.

"We always protect, assist, and bring to fulfillment the rites of dharma.

"May you long protect and never abandon this Dharma.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara addressed the great assembly, saying, "Excellent, excellent!"
"You are able to give rise to this most supreme vow of diligence to protect and uphold this Dharma.
This Dharma is the true samaya that unifies the lineages of all Tathāgatas. At that time, the Vajradhara Lord of Secrets and his entire retinue [responded].

Within his own palace, surrounded before and behind by immeasurable great mantra-vidyādhara kings,
he sat upright and contemplated this dharma.
He addressed the sages, saying:
"That Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara has taught this Great Liberation Lotus Maṇḍala Seal Samaya of the Heart-King Dhāraṇī Mantra of Amoghapāśa."
This is the place where all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas together join their palms in reverence, pay homage with their heads bowed, and cultivate purification;
it is an exceedingly profound and secret treasury of the Dharma.
I, along with Brahmā, Śakra, all the devas, all the mantra-holders, sages,
all the hosts of māras, śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, humans, non-humans, and so forth, are entirely bewildered;
this is not within the scope of thought or deliberation, nor can it be fathomed by the intellect.
This Dharma is vast and exceedingly profound, difficult to understand and difficult to enter.
Thus, the mantra of the Heart-King Dhāraṇī of the Amoghapāśa, its vast liberation, the lotus maṇḍala, the images, and the samayas are immeasurable and innumerable.
Having already spoken before the Buddha in the great assembly as extensively as the great ocean,
how may one enter this gateway of the samādhi of the Great Dharma Ocean, and how may one cultivate,
study, receive, and uphold it?
It would be as if we were to strike Mount Sumeru with a mustard seed;
how could it ever be moved?
It would be like using all the atoms of the Buddha-fields throughout the ten directions.
Within the mustard seed,
how can one enter? Furthermore,
if there are those who desire to transcribe, uphold, recite, hear, or practice [this teaching], [how shall they do so?]

Previously, they did not serve, revere, or make offerings to all the Buddhas—numbering as many as the sands of hundreds of thousands of koṭi-nayuta Ganges Rivers—in all the buddha-fields of the ten directions throughout the past and present;
nor did they read, recite, or hear any of the profound teachings.
By what means can one obtain the understanding of this Great Liberation Lotus-Candana Seal Samaya of the Heart-King Dhāraṇī Mantra of Amoghapāśa?
This belongs to all Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas.
Together, with palms joined in reverence, they pay homage, offer praise, uphold, recite,
and cultivate this Great Secret Samaya,
the locus of liberation.
This is not a dharma practiced by me;
because of this delusion,
it is difficult to understand and difficult to enter— this great, profound, and secret samaya.
Furthermore, there are those who uphold all the Buddha's teachings on the Dharma,
who have realized the skillful wisdom of the most profound supramundane Dharma,
and who, within this Dharma, apply themselves with courageous diligence, faith, understanding, and upholding.
If even those who read, recite, and hear it do not yet fully comprehend it,
how much less so can this be achieved by bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās in the present life or in this world?
One should uphold, recite, hear, and practice this Great Liberation Lotus-Candana Seal Samaya of the Heart-King Dhāraṇī Mantra of Amoghapāśa, along with its various supernormal powers.
For those seeking accomplishment,
how should they achieve it?
We— the Bodhisattvas, Brahmās, Śakras, and all the devas— [shall assist].
All these assemblies have such doubts and perplexities that it is necessary to question the Buddha in order to resolve the uncertainties in their minds;
he shall cause sentient beings to cultivate and perfect them so that all their aspirations may be fulfilled.

Celestial exquisite garments, various flowers of land and water,

at that time the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, the Lord of Secrets, [spoke].
Together with the assembly of sages, they stood before the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara;
with bated breath, they adjusted their robes to one side,
joined their palms in reverence, and gazed up at him in silent devotion.
In an instant, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, Lord of Secrets,
brandished his vajra and strode toward the Buddha like a lion;
he then prostrated, circumambulated him three times to the right, and withdrew to one side.
Kneeling with palms joined, he addressed the Buddha,
saying: "World-Honored One, that Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara has spoken this Heart-King Dhāraṇī Mantra of the Unfailing Lasso, the Great Liberation Lotus Maṇḍala, and the Samaya Seals."
This is the place where all Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas join their palms in reverence, pay homage with their heads bowed, and cultivate purification;
it is exceedingly profound, difficult to understand, and difficult to enter.

it is immovable, exceptionally marvelous and rare, and difficult to uphold, recite, and practice.
Within this Dharma are immeasurable and boundless dharanis and mantras,
as well as the methods for accomplishing the vast liberation lotus mandala, mudras, samayas, and images.
The Dharma of manifesting supernatural powers by immeasurable Tathāgatas;
and all the methods for receiving, upholding, reciting, practicing, and accomplishing supernatural transformations possessed by the Immeasurable Amogharāja Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva.

How may this cause the bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās of the present and future [to attain them]?
Having faith, understanding, receiving, upholding, reciting, and practicing,
with a mind that does not scatter its focus and a mind that is not deluded—
by means of which dharma-gate is accomplishment attained?
"I only pray that the Tathāgata will explain this for me to sever all my doubts.

achieves great accomplishment,

what is called 'attaining the supreme accomplishment'?"

Place this sutra together with them,

uphold, read, recite, hear, and practice it.
