surpassing a hundred thousand varieties of worldly incense;
this fragrant mist covered the maṇḍala, extending over a vast circumference of a hundred thousand yojanas.
Resembling a parasol and the color of blue lapis lazuli,
there appears in the sky the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara with the Amoghapāśa.
Upon the lotus pedestal in its center, there further emerges a pure physical body endowed with the thirty-two major marks and eighty minor signs.
Like the Great Brahmā Heavenly King,
his body has four arms;
one hand holds a lotus flower, and another hand holds a lasso.
In one hand he holds a trident, and with the other he displays the gesture of fearlessness (*abhaya-mudrā*).
On his head he wears a jeweled crown upon which resides an emanation Buddha.
He is adorned with celestial garments, earrings, and bracelets.
Adorned with various precious necklaces,
his body emitted a radiance surpassing the light of hundreds of thousands of suns first rising;
his countenance was serene and joyful.
Vajrapāṇi ascended into the air and, observing the mantra-practitioner,
surveyed the ten directions and proclaimed in a loud voice:
"Excellent, excellent, O Great Mantra-Practitioner!"
Then, extending hundreds of thousands of koṭis of radiant hands, he stroked the crown of his head;
he immediately realized supernatural powers and followed the Bodhisattva as they ascended into the air to sit there.
He was granted the samādhi of the liberation through the miraculous manifestations and the great light-adornment of the Amoghapāśa Mahāvairocana King,
and the samādhi of the Amogha Contemplation.
The Samādhi of Praising the Vast and Great Treasure Treasury;
the Samādhi of Vimalakīrti;
and the Samādhi of the Heart Mantra of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, the Amoghapāśa Dhāraṇī King.
One receives and attains as many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of *samādhis* as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River.
If one realizes these *samādhis*,
then one attains all the qualities of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Together, they joined their palms in reverence and prostrated.
Then, the Great Liberation Lotus Maṇḍala, mudrās, transformed images, and samayas of the Sarva-amoghapāśahṛdayarāja-dhāraṇī-mantra all appeared before them.
Furthermore, they attain the samaya of the dharanis, mantras, mandalas, and mudras of the entire vast Lotus family.
Furthermore, they attain the samaya of the dharanis, mantras, mandalas, and mudras of the entire Tathagata family.
Furthermore, they attain the samaya of all the mantra-dhāraṇī maṇḍalas and mudrās of the Vajra family;
furthermore, they attain the samaya of all the mantra-dhāraṇī maṇḍalas and mudrās of the Maṇi family.
Furthermore, they attained the samaya of the dhāraṇī-mantra-maṇḍala-mudrās of all the lineages of fragrant elephants;
and they further attained the samaya of ninety-two hundred-thousand-ten-million-billion *gaṅgā-sikatā* vidyā-rishis and mahā-vidyā-rishis.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara spoke again, saying: "What else do you seek?
I shall now fulfill all your needs for you."
This is what is sought by the hearts of mantra practitioners;
all supramundane vows and practices for enlightenment should be requested therein.
Furthermore, it instructs and reveals the dharmas of the three times, both mundane and supramundane.
Causing all to attain awakening and understanding.

Chapter Fifty-Four: The Great Vidyārāja’s Threefold Samaya. Chapter Fifty-Four: The Great Vidyārāja’s Threefold Samaya. The World-Honored One [spoke] this Samaya of the Mantra of Amoghapāśa, the Great Vidyārāja.
Regarding the visualization for the śāntika samaya:
visualize the syllable VAṂ placed [there],
extending from beneath that ground down to the limit of the vajra-wind.
Above it is the syllable VA (pronounced with a retroflex *v*), its written form clearly delineated;
it manifests in the shape of a five-pronged vajra,
emitting great flames whose blaze is fiercely penetrating.
He burns his own body until it is consumed and reduced to white ash.
Using this white ash, he smears and coats the great white maṇḍala,
which becomes a vast ocean, its light pervading everywhere.
The water is white like milk, pure and limpid;
it is vast and boundless.
Within it dwell various kinds of soft-shelled turtles, crocodiles, tortoises, snapping turtles, makaras, whales, alligators, and porpoises.
All dragons, fish, wild ducks, geese, mandarin ducks, white cranes, peacocks, and all other birds and beasts became silent and motionless,
facing one another with hearts of compassion. Within the ocean-mind,
an immeasurable thousand-petaled pure white lotus appeared, its light spreading and its fragrance wafting.
Upon the trunk, the Nanda and Upananda Dragon Kings coil themselves to the left and right;
atop the platform, he beholds the Tathāgata Śākyamuni,
his body the color of white gold, sitting cross-legged upon a lion-jewel throne.
To the right, visualize the Great Radiant King Aṅkuśa, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva,
Prajñā Bodhisattva, Pratyekabuddhas, and Śrāvakas,
all seated in the half-lotus posture upon white lotus thrones.
To the left, one beholds the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, Lord of Secrets, and the Śrāvakas of the four fruits,
seated in the half-lotus posture upon white lotus thrones.
Beneath the Tathāgata’s seat, one beholds white lotuses and lion jewel-thrones.
Above, one contemplates the Dharani-mantra Treasury of the Three Families’ White Light, from which flow forth all the teachings of the Three Vehicles.
To the right, one contemplates the Vidyārāja of Vast Radiance, with a pure white body appearing like a noble being.
Sitting in the half-lotus posture while holding and turning a rosary, visualize the countenances of the noble assembly as serene and tranquil, their bodies pure white.
When the prescribed number of recitations for the ritual practice is completed, recite according to the dharma.
Having gathered the multitude of holy Avalokiteśvaras he had recited,
he addressed Avalokiteśvara, saying:
"Entrust them to the hidden white tuft of hair between your eyebrows."
Reciting the *oṃ* syllable, the mantra of protection, and performing the mudrā-consecration,
if a practitioner constantly practices this samādhi during the six periods of the day without interruption,
they will before long attain the vast accomplishment of meditative concentration (*dhyāna*) and liberation belonging to the Lotus family (*padmakula*) of the *amogha* kings.
If one contemplates the *bhusuku* samaya,
one visualizes the syllable *vaḥ*— pronounced with a reversed *u*— rising from beneath the earth down to the limit of the vajra-wind;
above it is the syllable *vaḥ*, likewise pronounced with a reversed *u*, its form and lines clearly delineated.
He manifests a five-pronged vajra,
from which great flames of fire issue forth, blazing and penetratingly radiant;
it incinerates his own body until it is consumed to white ashes.
The great maṇḍala, colored like gold and smeared with ointment,
becomes a vast ocean that shines through everywhere;
its waters are golden-yellow, pure and limpid, extending to boundless shores.
Within it were various kinds of soft-shelled turtles, crocodiles, tortoises, snapping turtles, makara sea-monsters, whales, porpoises, and sturgeons;
as well as all manner of dragons, fish, wild ducks, geese, mandarin ducks, white cranes, peacocks, and all other birds and beasts.
They all rejoiced and looked toward one another with hearts of loving-kindness.
Within the ocean-like mind, there appeared immeasurable thousand-petaled golden lotuses,
their radiance spreading and their fragrance wafting.
Upon the trunk, the dragon kings Nanda and Upananda coil themselves to the left and right.
Upon the pedestal, Śākyamuni Tathāgata appears,
his body the color of *candana* gold, sitting cross-legged upon a lion throne of jewels, preaching various teachings.
With his right hand raised in the gesture of the open palm and his left hand extended in the mudrā of fearlessness, he emits golden light from his right side.
To the right, one visualizes the Great Vidyārājñī Prabhāvatī and the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
The Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvarī Pāṇḍaravāsinī, the Bodhisattvas Bhṛkuṭī and Tārā,
Mahālakṣmī, the Pratyekabuddhas, and the Śrāvakas.
He sits in the half-lotus posture upon a golden lotus throne.
To his left are Vajrapāṇi Guhyapati Bodhisattva,
the Bodhisattvas of the ten pāramitās, and the śrāvakas of the four fruits.
Sitting in the half-lotus posture upon a golden lotus throne,
he beheld before the Tathāgata’s seat a golden lotus lion-jewel throne,
upon which was the treasury of the Dharma of the mantras of the three families.
From it flow forth all the teachings of the Three Vehicles.
To the right of the Great Vidyārāja is Avalokiteśvara,
with a pure white body appearing like a noble being.
Having spread out a seat and sat down, hold the prayer beads.
Visualize the countenances of the various sages as serene and joyful, their bodies golden in color.
When the recitation is performed according to the ritual and the prescribed number of counts is completed:
Having gathered the multitude of holy Avalokiteśvaras whom he had recited,
he addressed Avalokiteśvara, saying:
"Entrust them to the hidden white tuft of hair between your eyebrows."
Recite the *oṃ* syllable and the mantra of protection while forming mudrās and performing consecration.
If the practitioner constantly practices these three samādhis during the six periods of the day, they shall never be interrupted or abandoned.
Before long, one shall attain the vast accomplishment of the samaya of the mudrā and maṇḍala of the liberation of the lotus lineage of the Āmogha King.
This occurs if one contemplates and observes the samaya of the ābhicāruka [wrathful] rite.
The skin of the Great, Terrifying, and Wrathful Vidyārāja is a fierce blue;
his form is vast and fearsome, his face frowning,
his eyes roaring, and his canine teeth protruding upward as he crouches.
Crouching upon a wheel in the air, he wields a dark blue *ḍamaruka* drum;
emitting great flames and manifesting a sound of violent trembling,
he is most terrifying, his majestic power being matchless.
If one practices and cultivates in this manner, one will attain accomplishment.
Regarding the ritual procedures for the *śāntika* samaya, one should maintain mindfulness of the sound;
when the voice is pure, harmonious, even, and tranquil, one should know it for oneself.
If it is for the ritual procedure of recollecting the *bhaiṣajya-samaya*,
the sound should be neither too loud nor too soft, but rather clear, swift, and sharp, so that it may be heard by those outside.
If it is for the ritual procedure of recollecting the *kāyarakṣā-samaya*, [the sound should be likewise].
The swift, whirling, and sharp sound is heard externally as firm.
If it is the ritual procedure for the *āveśa-rudra-samaya* (the samaya of fierce subjugation),
the sounds of wrathful shouting, derision, crushing, and expulsion are heard far off with awe.
If it is a śāntika samaya, at the end of each recitation of the dhāraṇī mantra,
one should calmly and harmoniously pronounce the word svāhā.
If it is the *bhaiṣajya* samaya,
at the end of each phrase of the dhāraṇī mantra,
one should joyfully and firmly utter the syllable *hūṃ*.
If it is an ābhicāruka samaya,
at the end of each phrase when reciting the dhāraṇī mantra,
one should fiercely roar the syllables *hūṃ phaṭ*.
If it is the śāntika samaya,
one should contemplate the mind as tranquil, relying upon the vajra-dharmatā of all Tathāgatas,
and perform the yoga of the corresponding signs according to the noble ones.
With a solemn countenance, gaze fixedly while sitting in the full lotus posture (*paryaṅka*). If it is the *bhusuku* samaya,
the consciousness-mind becomes joyful, relying upon the vajra-dharma gateways of all Tathāgatas.
Regarding the yoga of the similar aspect (*tulyākāra-yoga*),
as the Noble One is depicted with a joyful countenance,
seated in the full-lotus posture (*paryaṅka*), it is the *ābhicāruka-samaya*.
The consciousness-mind is agitated and resentful;
relying upon the supreme, sovereign, and wrathful Vajra subjugation dharma-gate of all Tathāgatas,
one performs the yoga of the corresponding signs according to the venerable deity.
With a stern expression on his face, he knelt and crouched.
If one maintains the samaya of body protection,
the consciousness-mind upholds the vajra-wisdom dharmas of all Tathāgatas.
In the yoga of the similar aspect, one should not allow the mind to deviate from the samaya as it has been prescribed.
Blessed One, if one were to subdue and punish all malarial spirits, ghosts, and other malevolent beings, one should speak words of truth.
While reciting and contemplating,
one should visualize oneself as a wrathful being invincible to all enemies,
with flames issuing from the body, surging upward and abiding in the sky.
Forming the secret mudrās of the hook and the noose,
one should gaze upon the spirits of malaria, or other malevolent spirits, whether male or female,
along with their retinues; wherever they may be, one should cast these mudrās like a wheel.
They are brought bound to places where there are illnesses;
subjected to various forms of life-threatening bonds, beatings, punishments, reprimands, and verbal chastisements;
they themselves cry out, "I submit! I beg for my life! I beg to be released!"
Then, having bound [the deity] with the seal and mantra, one should immediately dispatch them.
If one wishes to discern all signs of good and evil,
one should empower the guggulu incense.
Perform one hundred and eight homa offerings before my image and then go to sleep;
you shall dream that Avalokiteśvara appears in the form of a king and stands before you.
For them, he expounds all dharmas of good and evil,
so that they may attain immeasurable great majesty and vigor,
causing all karmic obstructions and hindrances to be completely extinguished.
If one desires to manifest Mahābrahmā, one should bathe the body and don consecrated garments. Mixing one ten-thousand pills of Du-zhong wood juice and An-hsi incense,
one should perform homa before an image of Mahābrahmā day and night for ten thousand repetitions.
Then the Brahmā Heaven will manifest its form and come to fill the heads of the assembly;
or, if one begs for this body to become like that of a Brahmā,
it shall be exactly as wished.
It causes the people of the world to delight in constant reverence.
If one wishes for the celestial king Nārāyaṇa to appear, one should bathe the body and,
dressed in clean garments, stand before the image of the celestial king Nārāyaṇa.
Consecrate *sumana* wood and kindle a fire;
consecrate frankincense, white mustard seeds, ghee, and honey,
and perform *homa* offerings day and night for ten thousand repetitions.
Then the deity Nārāyaṇa will manifest before them and say:
"Excellent, excellent, O mantra-practitioner!
I shall now bestow upon you this Amoghapāśa-vidyārāja mantra."
"Since you have brought me here, what is it that I now beg of you?
Grant all my wishes;
whatever I seek in my heart, I shall now request."
They obtain their wishes as they have prayed.
Or, if they beg for a body like that of Nārāyaṇa to manifest in various forms,
they likewise obtain it according to their wish.
If one wishes for Maheśvara to appear, one should purify one's body and clothing,
and perform homa day and night before an image of Maheśvara for ten thousand times, using consecrated powder of dried lotus, agallochum, and cow’s ghee.
Then Mahādeva will manifest his body and appear to fulfill all the aspirations of the assembly.
If one wishes for Mahākāla to appear,
one should bathe the body and don clean garments on the eighth day of the dark fortnight.
At night, in a śmaśāna forest, one should prepare a fire by chopping and arranging wood from that śmaśāna forest.
Then, empower dried lotus powder, agallochum (guggulu), white mustard seeds, *mīrudhira*, and cow’s ghee.
Perform the homa ritual day and night until ten thousand recitations are completed.
On the fifteenth day, perform the rite while fasting.
Furthermore, make offerings of *mālatī* flowers, red lotuses, and white non-glutinous rice.
Then the deity Mahākāla, leading his retinue of servants, will appear before one all at once and praise, saying:
"Excellent, excellent, O Mantra-practitioner!
This rite is now the most supreme. What do you seek? I shall fulfill it for you."
When the practitioner of mantras beholds this,
they should again present offerings of incense, flowers, and scented water;
then, all their prayers shall be fulfilled according to their wishes.
They shall follow him everywhere to provide great protection.
If one wishes for various forms and appearances of devas to manifest,
one should purify and adorn one’s body and clothing on the eighth day of the dark fortnight.
Burn *agaru* wood as fuel.
Empower *turuṣka*, *tagara*, *śrīkhaṇḍa*, white mustard seeds, clarified butter, honey, and curdled milk.
Perform *homa* offerings day and night for ten thousand repetitions.
On the fifteenth day, one should observe a fast and perform the ritual.
Using camphor, white sandalwood, and scented water,
fill a new and clean jar to the brim and offer it in worship.
Furthermore, using three new and clean jars,
fill them with the three white foods and various miscellaneous flowers to perform an offering.
Burn aloeswood incense, white sandalwood incense, and frankincense as an offering.
Furthermore, by reciting the mantra one thousand and eight times,
the celestial deity will immediately appear before the practitioner, mounted upon a palace;
this is what the mantra-practitioner shall behold at that time.
Whatever one’s heart desires, one may beg for it all.
If one begs to become a mother, one shall obtain wealth and provisions sufficient for one's needs.
If one begs to become an elder sister or a younger sister, [the same shall be granted].
All desired articles of adornment and requisites shall be provided in full satisfaction.
If one requests to serve as an attendant,
they shall always be made to perform various tasks according to their wishes.
Messengers were sent from afar and near, within a range of a thousand yojanas, to fetch goods;
they returned in a mere instant, having traveled all around,
and brought back various kinds of hidden treasures and precious gems.
Furthermore, for the sake of future generations who may be employed in this task,
these practitioners of mantra should redouble their diligence;
they must never fall into arrogance, indolence, or negligence, nor commit any unrighteous acts.
If one commits even a slight transgression, one's body will immediately perish,
or one will be cast into the cave of a yakṣa to be devoured by them.
Those whom he wishes to send to the celestial palaces, dragon palaces, and subterranean realms of all yakṣas, rākṣasas,
and various spirits throughout the worlds of the ten directions shall go wherever they desire.
In binding, seizing, and taking objects, everything shall be accomplished as desired without fail.
One should daily perform offerings using various scented waters and assorted flowers, ensuring they are never interrupted.
Then one will obtain all joyful services;
everything will be entrusted to them, and there will be nothing they do not master.
If one wishes for a yakṣiṇī to appear, [one should perform the rite].
Take a clean board of cypress wood, one cubit and a half square,
and having fashioned and adorned it according to the rules, paint upon it the image of a yakṣiṇī,
embellishing her with various necklaces and ornaments.
Thoroughly prepare the ritual altar and place this image upon it.
The practitioner of mantras should bathe the body and don clean garments,
making offerings of the three white foods and red flowers.
Place a fire before an image made of *dhatura* wood and perform *homa* for three days and three nights,
offering one thousand and eighty oblations of consecrated *guggulu* incense, white mustard seeds, and cow’s ghee.
A yakṣiṇī appeared before him,
and when she asked the mantra-practitioner,
"What do you seek now?", he replied:
"You should follow me and perform various services for me;
take all manner of precious jewels and use them as I see fit.
Then the yakṣī replied, "I shall do as you command."
Having spoken these words, she immediately vanished.
If the messenger subsequently consecrates *guggulu* incense and white mustard seeds and burns them one hundred and eight times,
the yakṣiṇī will come before him.
One may take whatever precious jewels one's mind desires and employ them as one wishes according to the Dharma for the sake of the mantra-practitioner.
If one wishes to cause an asura maiden to appear:
Consecrate wax to fashion the form of an asura maiden and adorn it with various necklaces and ornaments;
construct a mandala according to the ritual rules and place this image within its center.
Having purified oneself by bathing and donning clean garments, one shall not eat or speak for three days and three nights.
Seated before the image, one shall burn agalloch incense and make offerings of the "three white foods."
Consecrate white mustard seeds once and strike the image one thousand and eighty times.
One will cause an asura maiden to appear before them according to the ritual;
when she appears, whatever matter one seeks in one's heart shall be accomplished through her.
Until their lifespan is exhausted, they shall always be subject to service and labor.
If one wishes for the daughters of the rākṣasas to appear,
one should empower agallochum (guggulu) and *gośīrṣa* sandalwood.
If one performs the ritual within a śītavana cremation ground during the night,
reciting the mantra one thousand and eighty times with constant, flickering incense smoke that does not cease,
then all the rākṣasī daughters will appear simultaneously.
They shall be employed as servants until their lifespans are exhausted.
Each day, ten *kan* of silver coins shall be provided;
the mantra-practitioner shall divide these coins into three parts.
One portion is to be offered to all the Three Jewels;
one portion is for personal use; and one portion is to be distributed widely to those who are poor and destitute.
This is how a practitioner of mantras should daily prepare flour, parched grain, and raw vegetables.
By making offerings in accordance with the Dharma, one ensures that the rākṣasī daughters do not cease their attendance;
the rākṣasī daughters and their retinues will all be filled with joy,
constantly serving as attendants and never departing from one's side.
If one wishes for the Viśvadeva spirits to appear,
one should empower cow dung, mung beans, the sap of *Eucommia ulmoides* (duzhong), and *guggulu* incense,
and perform the rite at night at a crossroads.
Roast and fry [the offerings] one thousand and eighty times, ensuring that the smoke does not cease;
simultaneously, offer cakes and rice as an oblation.
Then, the Viśvedeva spirits will manifest their forms to serve you.
It is employed as one pleases and never abandoned;
it travels back and forth across a thousand li at will to fetch various objects and the like.
One should always, outside the gate, at the three times each day,
offer cakes and rice— regardless of whether they are refined or coarse—
and thus one will constantly experience joy.
Every day, one should hold a hundred silver coins in hand and place them at the head of the bed where the practitioner of the mantra lies.
One must not allow the silver coins thus obtained to accumulate.
Every day, use all [the offerings] to perform various meritorious deeds;
once they are exhausted, send them back.
If you wish for Nalapati and his retinue to be joyful, [do this].
Having purified the body through bathing and donned consecrated garments, one should perform *homā* one thousand and eight times using dried lotuses, *saindhava* salt, white mustard seeds,
and black mustard seeds. Furthermore, one should consecrate white mustard seeds and *gorocanā*.
Carrying it to the gate where one intends to go, scatter it all about;
this will cause the people there to eliminate all calamities and obstacles, and to regard one with joy, treasure, and respect.
If one wishes for Brahmins to be joyful and respectful, [one should do the same].
If one consecrates non-glutinous rice, barley, black sesame, ghee, honey, and curd,
and performs the homa, those [deities] will be pleased and respectful.
If one wishes to cause the Kṣatriya caste to rejoice, [one should do so].
If one consecrates white sesame, human hair, non-glutinous rice, small beans, ghee, honey, and curd,
and performs homa with them, one will obtain joy and respect.
If one wishes to cause the śūdras to rejoice, [one should do so].
If one performs *homa* with consecrated rice, sugar, salt, mustard seeds, clarified butter, honey, and curd,
one will receive joy and respect.
If one wishes for all evil persons to become joyful, [one should perform this].
If one consecrates licorice, the seven kinds of grains, clarified butter, honey,
and curd with mantras and performs homa, those wicked people will become joyful and respectful toward him.
If one wishes to stop the armies and bandits of others, [one should do so].
If one consecrates thorny wood and kindles a fire,
and performs *homa* with consecrated rice grains, white mustard seeds, ghee, honey, and curd,
then it will stop other thieves; furthermore, if one goes to another army’s battle lines, one will be victorious.

Having consecrated black mustard seeds, agallochum incense, hemp seeds, ghee, honey, and curd, once the *homa* ritual is completed, one will achieve victory over all those with whom one engages in combat. 55.

The Fifth and Final Chapter on the Medicinal Preparations (*āgada*) of the Vastly Renowned Great King (*Vistīrṇa-mahāvidyārāja*). O Bhagavān, this medicinal preparation (*āgada*) of the Vastly Renowned Great King removes all obstacles and ailments of sentient beings. He spoke these verses regarding the medicine:
These are the three types of samaya-mantra medicinal herbs: 1.
*Gandhārāsa* (Euphorbia) and *mādhuka* (Bassia latifolia); 2.
*Sañjara-paśunaka* (a type of plant) and *kṣemurā* (Angelica sinensis); 3. *Mandārava* seeds and rice husks.
Bhāluka medicinal herb, *parijātaka*, *Suvarṇadaṃṣṭrā*, clove, *achyranthes aspera*,
*deodar*, *bassia latifolia*, *añjana*, and *agallochum*; *Guggulu*, *tilvaka*, powdered *mucukunda*,
*bilva*, and realgar— all these ingredients should be taken in equal measures.
To treat with the essence of mantra-consecrated refinement:
take a *mātṛvatsa* (mother-calf) [plant] and blend it with scented water to smear upon the ground;
then, combine it with the Great Radiant Vidyārāja Aṅkuśa, and consecrate the medicinal substances one thousand times with the mantra.
By burning and fumigating with these, afflictions such as high spirits and malarial fever are all eliminated.
This medicinal eye-salve for samādhi consists of small juniper (śrīparṇī), decoctions of *khadira*, yellow *kakubha*,
*pippalī*, white pepper, dried ginger, conch-shell, *harītakī*, *vibhītaka*, and *āmalakī*.
Blue utpala flowers, realgar, sāmudra salt, saffron, sea-foam,
silver ore, and spikenard— take equal quantities of these and refine them together;
then add camphor, musk, and so forth, such that each of the sixteen ingredients constitutes one part.
Repeatedly harmonize and refine the treatment; recite the Great Vidyārāja Aṅkuśa mantra over the medicine several thousand times.
By applying this medicine to the eyes, one attains fearlessness and shall not be harassed by any ghosts or spirits.
It also cures cataracts in the eyes and cold or hot tears.
The red-eyed crows and wind-diseases were all cured; their eyes became clear and sharp, and all sins were extinguished.

Wherever they went, they rejoiced according to their wishes. Furthermore, they were not afflicted by various calamities, such as imprisonment, legal punishments, or dangers from water and fire, nor by any evil beasts, snakes, poisons, or insects.
None shall bring about harm; this is the supreme medicinal verse of samādhi:
*turuṣka*, *agaru*, the bark of the *śīrṣa* tree, *utpala* flowers, *śamī* leaves, *harītakī* fruit, and the roots of *darbha* grass.
*Āmalaka* fruit, white *pippalī*, *pippalīmūla*, dried ginger, *viśvabheṣaja*, *elā*,
medicinal herbs, *devadāru*, *khadira*, *haridrā*, *sugandhikā*, *bhallātaka*,
*guggulu*, *agarū*, *kālāgaru*, *uragasāra-candana*, and *kuṅkuma*.

Prepare an equal number of stone-honey pills (*śarkarā-guḍikā*), purify them by anointing them upon the altar, and empower them with the mantra several thousand times. Allow them to dry in the shade and wear them;
wherever one goes, all will rejoice, and all calamities, obstacles, and fears of malevolent spirits will be eliminated.

Zithers, flutes, harps, lutes, drums, and the sounds of cymbals and percussion—when those who hear this music are made joyful, all evil dreams and calamitous obstacles are dispelled. When all ghosts and spirits hear it, they are struck with terror;
famine, scarcity, misfortune, and the ten non-virtuous actions are all utterly extinguished, resulting in auspicious purity.
When these people have cast off their bodies, they will be born either in a pure land or in the heavens;
wherever they go, they will wear robes of fragrant incense smoke, always being loved and respected by the people, free from all suffering of illness, and endowed with auspicious marks.
Their merit and diligence will increase manifold of their own accord.
The evil signs of malicious speech shall naturally be extinguished. Those who wear this medicine will be freed from all obstacles and shall not be harassed or disturbed by ghosts or spirits.
For all those suffering from sores, swellings, or diseases, the medicine should be mixed with water and ground into a paste; when applied, they shall be cured. As for all diseases within the abdomen:
If one grinds [the substance] with warm water and ingests it, it will cause the illness to be eliminated.

One will be respected and loved by all when conversing with others. Chapter Fifty-Six: The Chapter on the Maṇḍala of the Great Vidyārāja Aṅkuśa. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara...
Again he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, within this mantra of the Great Vidyārāja Amoghapāśa,
there is the samaya of the seal of the Amoghapāśa Maṇḍala of the Vast Lotus."
This maṇḍala seal samaya is that which is collectively empowered by all Tathāgatas;
it is the place for the accomplishment of the Great Samaya.
If there are those who see, hear, rejoice in, receive, uphold, read, or recite [this],
they shall attain the accomplishment of the Dharma of the Image of the Mantra-Dhāraṇī-Samaya-Mudrā of the Vast Lotus Maṇḍala, which renders all spiritual transformations non-empty.
Furthermore, I have attained entry into the samaya of the mudrās of the maṇḍala of the families of all Tathāgatas,
and am sustained and protected by the empowerment of all Tathāgatas.
Before the Buddhas, out of compassion for those who practice mantras, I shall now act.
It is taught for the sake of attaining the most supreme accomplishment;
it is taught for the sake of benefiting all sentient beings and enabling them to attain peace and happiness;
and it is taught for the sake of extinguishing the hindrances and obscurations of all śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, śūdras, boys, and girls.
At that time, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, saying:
"Excellent, excellent, O Pure One!"
Possessing great compassion, it brings success to all practitioners of mantras— whether śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, vaiśyas, śūdras, boys, or girls—
and enables them to obtain the treasury of the Dharma and abide securely in bodhi.
You should now proclaim the samaya of the mudrās of the vast Lotus Aṅkuśa Maṇḍala,
as well as the samaya for the accomplishment of all the equal families.
This maṇḍala and its mudrā rites have already been empowered by the supernatural power and majesty of all Tathāgatas; I,
too, have empowered them through my own supernatural power.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, within this mantra of the Amoghapāśa King of Vast Radiance..."
This is the samaya of the mudrā of the vast and unfailing lotus-yaṅkuśa maṇḍala, which is the supreme accomplishment of reality;
it is eight cubits in length and breadth, or alternatively, five cubits, being perfectly square and circular.
Remove the evil soil— tiles, stones, bones, and wood—
and fill it with pure, good earth mixed with fragrant water.
Firmly compact and level the ground, raising the foundation to a height of five finger-widths.
Smear fragrant mud upon the boundary lines of the enclosure and the inner court.
In the center of the inner court, paint a hundred-and-eight-petaled white lotus flower.
Upon each petal, depict a noose seal (*pāśamudrā*) and a vajra-hook seal (*vajrāṅkuśamudrā*), with flames of fire blazing above them.
On the pedestal, the two hands are joined with the palms touching;
one hand holds a vajra-hook, and the other grasps a noose of the seven jewels.
The head of the hook is fashioned in the likeness of a dragon’s head.
The head of the handle has the appearance of a jewel.
Both ends of the cord have the appearance of snake heads.
Around the hook and the cord, there are blazing flames of light.
On the four sides and four corners is a precious Sumeru throne.
On the southern side is the mudrā of Bodhisattva Tārā;
on the northern side is the mudrā of the Mother Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara with a white body.
The mudrā of Avalokiteśvara Hayagrīva is on the west;
the mudrā of Avalokiteśvara Bhṛkuṭī is on the east;
and the mudrā of the Lotus Family of all Avalokiteśvaras is in the northeast corner.
The seal of the Bodhisattva Bahuputrika is in the southeast corner;
the seal of Yaśodharā is in the southwest corner;
and the seal of the accomplishment of Ekacakrā Tripadī is in the northwest corner.
It is surrounded by flames of fire.
In the four directions of the next courtyard, lotus flowers are in full bloom,
with moon disks upon their pedestals.
Upon the moon discs at the four gates are the wish-fulfilling jewel mudrās;
upon the moon discs at the four corners are the vajra mudrās;
and there are moon discs at the four faces.
The upper pāśa mudrā, the vajrāṅkuśa mudrā, the vajra-mālā mudrā,
the vajrasamaya mudrā, and the mudrās of all the Vajra families.
The Vajra-fist mudrā and the All-Vajra-chain mudrā have great vajra seals encircling upward-flaming fire.
In the four directions of the next court, lotus flowers are in full bloom.
A lunar disc upon the altar;
upon this lunar disc are placed all the hand-seals (mudrā) belonging to this family,
as well as the seal of the wish-fulfilling jewel vase at the four gates.
At the four corners are vajra-hooks with their seals, surrounded by flames of light.
In the next court, on all four sides, are jewel Sumeru thrones;
upon these thrones are various weapon-seals, surrounded by flames of light.
At the eastern gate is the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, Lord of Secrets,
holding a vajra and seated in the half-lotus posture.
At the southern gate is the rākṣasī goddess Ekajaṭī.
Holding a weapon, he sits in the half-lotus posture.
At the western gate is the Vajra-chain deity (Vajrasphoṭa),
holding a vajra chain and sitting in the half-lotus posture.
At the northern gate stands the messenger Duḍi,
holding a weapon in his hand and sitting in the half-lotus posture; at the four corners are the Four Heavenly Kings.
Holding hooks and spears, they sit in the half-lotus posture;
these eight deities have bodies adorned with flaming light.
The ground of the inner and outer courtyards is made of blue-colored jewels, which demarcate the boundaries of those courtyards.
The ground of vajra-jewels is surrounded by flames of various colored *cintāmaṇi* gems;
on its outer four sides is the boundary,
marked by a white boundary-path with four open corridors and gates.
Adorn it with various banners and flowers.
At the four gates and four corners,
drive in stakes of khadira wood to bind and maintain the boundaries of the square area.
The outer perimeter of the five-colored corded lines forms a boundary;
upon this boundary, various golden flowers, silver flowers,
pearl flowers, and flowers of blue lapis lazuli beads are interspersed and arrayed.
White lapis lazuli pearl flowers and red lapis lazuli pearl flowers;
yellow lapis lazuli pearl flowers and variegated lapis lazuli pearl flowers;
as well as conch shells of various colors and flower garlands of various colors.
At the four gates and four corners are silver *argha* vases filled with scented water;
various flower branches and leaves are inserted into their mouths,
and five-colored silk ribbons are tied around their necks.
Using vessels of gold, silver, and ceramic,
he filled them with various foods and drinks, including milk, curd, and fruits,
and arranged them according to the prescribed ritual.
Scatter various flowers as an offering.
Outside, in the eight directions, place lamp-stands on pedestals and burn oil lamps;
at the gates, place incense burners.
Using agallochum, white sandalwood, storax, *billyaka*, and camphor,
prepare them according to the ritual rules and burn them at the four gates.
Outside, arrange one hundred and sixty-four lamps to form a great garland of light.
At the four outer corners, one should burn agallochum, frankincense, and sallakī incense.
The mantra-practitioner and his companions, having invited the practitioner of the rite,
shall bathe thoroughly, anoint their bodies with fragrance, and don clean garments.
Regarding the mantras:
at the eastern gate, one recites the mantra of the Greatly Terrifying Vidyārāja Aṅkuśa to perform the rite of protection.
Recite the extensive mantra of the Great Vidyārāja Aṅkuśa to make aspirations and offer praise.
Consecrate the cow’s ghee, milk, and curd,
and have the recipient of the Dharma consume them as a means of performing personal protection (*rakṣā*).
Furthermore, having bound the boundary and burned fragrant incense,
one should recite the mantra of the Great Vidyārāja Aṅkuśa and invoke Amitābha Buddha,
Śākyamuni Buddha, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, and the assembly of their kinsmen.
Furthermore, he invited all the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, and all Vajras of the ten directions to the sacrificial altar for offerings;
he also invited all the devas, nāgas, spirits, and the eight classes of beings from the ten directions.
At the primary position of the assembly altar,
he again re-establishes the boundary and addresses the various holy assemblies;
then, maintaining his majestic deportment, he takes his seat upon the throne.
Having scattered various incenses and flowers everywhere as an offering,
they performed prostrations, recitations, circumambulations, and various other rites.
At the western gate, they instructed those who had come to request the Dharma.
Scattering flowers and prostrating, he received the samaya vows.
Again, prostrating with renewed reverence, he made the Four Great Vows.
Exiting through the southern gate, he extensively established a homa fire to the east and performed a great offering.
If a mantra practitioner performs the rite for protecting the body, the rite for bathing,
the rite for the rosary, the rite for the noose,
the rite for security, or the rite for abundance.
The method for subduing all humans and non-humans; the method for summoning;
the method for dismissal; the method for binding the boundaries;
and the method for awakening all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Vajras, devas, nāgas, and spirits of the ten directions.
All ritual objects for purification, as well as all rites performed with white *kuśa* grass,
are accomplished through the practice of the mantra of the Great Vidyārāja Aṅkusā.
World-Honored One, this mantra of the Great Vidyārāja Aṅkusā—
All Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Vajras of the ten directions bestow their great supernatural powers upon it through their constant empowerment.
Ovalokiteśvara Bodhisattva Mahāsattva.
Furthermore, all the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of that lineage shall also constantly bestow their empowerment through all their supernatural powers and majestic might,
granting the accomplishment of the great and unfailing siddhi.
If any śramaṇas or laypeople assemble at this maṇḍala,
they shall eliminate the karmic obstacles of the ten non-virtuous actions and all illnesses and afflictions accumulated within their bodies throughout beginningless kalpas.
It should be known that such a person will attain a great mass of merit in both this life and future lives, and shall dwell securely in the Great Jewel.
At the time of death, their body and mind will be peaceful and blissful, free from all pain and affliction.
One shall go to the Pure Land and be born by transformation from a lotus flower.
There, one will realize the wisdom of recollecting past lives and attain the simultaneous opening of the gates to hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Buddha-fields.
Wandering through these Buddha-fields, one will hear all the most profound teachings and achieve full awakening and understanding.
Furthermore, they receive the consolation of the Tathāgatas of these various Buddha-fields touching their heads with their hands, and are granted the prediction of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
At that time, they are addressed in unison: "This body of yours is now your final body."
Until they sit at the site of enlightenment and turn the great wheel of Dharma, remaining forever non-regressive,
they shall be revered and made offerings by the people of that age.
All treasures and wealth increase spontaneously.
[Therein dwell] Mahābrahmā, Nārāyaṇa, Maheśvara, and Īśvara.
All the hosts of devas in the Heaven of the Thirty-three,
as well as King Yama and others, will constantly protect,
revere, and praise this person.
Furthermore, one shall serve and make offerings to ninety-two hundred thousand koṭi-nayuta Ganges-sand numbers of Buddhas,
whereby the roots of goodness planted will reach maturity.
If anyone should, even for a moment, offer a single flower, a single fruit, a single unguent,
or a single incense to this maṇḍala,
they shall [be honored] with the divine fragrances of gośīrṣa sandalwood and aloeswood.

By offering this burnt incense, one generates a vast mass of merit equal to that of making offerings to ninety-nine hundred-thousand-ten-million-billion *gaṅgā*-sands of Buddhas throughout all the lands of the ten directions.
Furthermore, all the Tathāgatas of the ten directions bestow this praise upon him:
"Excellent, excellent, son of good family!
In the past, all the Tathāgatas also made offerings to this maṇḍala and thereby attained the six pāramitās."
One becomes endowed with the accomplishment of a great mass of merit;
furthermore, one attains the accomplishment of all masses of dharmas pertaining to enlightenment;
and furthermore, one attains the accomplishment of all supreme dharmas of the mantra of Amoghapāśa, the King of Vidyārājas of Vast Radiance.
The words of this person are accepted with faith by all people.
One should know that this maṇḍala is protected by all the Tathāgatas, like a caitya.
If there are sentient beings who draw near to it and rejoice in it, [they shall obtain great merit].
Furthermore, by extinguishing calamities, diseases, and the like, one shall behold the profound Dharma of all Tathāgatas and attain transcendence from the world.
Worldly dharmas shall be perfected, and all manner of misfortunes, enmities, and hardships shall be utterly extinguished.
Upon relinquishing this body, one shall be reborn in the Western Pure Land to arise by transformation from a lotus flower.
Those who behold this altar shall be born in the heavens;
until they attain Bodhi, they shall never again fall into or receive a body within the three miserable realms.
Chapter Fifty-seven: The Chapter on the Iconography of the Vast and Great Vidyārāja. World-Honored One, this is the image of Avalokiteśvara as the Vast and Great Amoghapāśa Vidyārāja.
It can eliminate all sinful obstructions of sentient beings, as well as calamities, epidemics, misfortunes, and the terrors of venomous insects and poisons caused by malevolent spirits;
it bestows benefit upon living beings and fulfills the vow for fearlessness.
The necessities of life will be perfected;
all roots of goodness and merit will increase;
and all wealth and treasures will naturally become abundant.
All mantras and the various practices for awakening are in perfect correspondence with the fulfillment of the ten pāramitās.
Should anyone see, hear, or remember them,
they shall obtain a great mass of merit and their roots of goodness will increase.
They shall be liberated from all the bitter fruits of the hells;
through slight meritorious practice, they shall obtain great rewards;
they shall attain a perfect lineage, be endowed with its corresponding qualities, and possess right view.
All śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, and the common people shall respectfully honor and make offerings to it with fine white cotton wool or fine silk cloth,
measuring two cubits, three cubits, or four or five cubits square, according to one's means and ability.
Begin the painting on the fifteenth day of the waxing moon.
Use fresh, clean, and high-quality pigments and brushes;
do not use animal glue.
When the painter paints, he shall bathe once and don clean garments.

He shall depict the Great Vidyārāja Amoghapāśa Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva sitting in the full lotus posture (*paryaṅka*), with three faces and six arms, his body the color of pure gold; his central face is serene and smiling.
The right face is slightly wrathful with canine fangs protruding upward;
the left face is intensely wrathful.
He has three heads and a lunar crown, upon which resides an emanation Buddha.
The hair on his three heads is fiery red and bristling upward.
His first left hand holds a vajra hook together with a lotus flower;
his first right hand holds a trident together with a vajra staff.
The second left hand holds a noose together with a vajra-hook;
the second right hand holds a vajra together with a vajra-hook;
the third left hand is extended, raining down various jewels.
The right third hand is raised outward with the palm facing up in a gesture of consolation, touching the crown of the head.
He is adorned with jewel necklaces, earrings, bracelets, and armlets,
as well as various celestial garments and diverse ornaments.
He sits upon a lion throne of precious lotus flowers,
adorned with a flaming halo that possesses a hook-like mark.
To his left is the Bodhisattva Tārā, her countenance serene and joyful.
On his head he wears a jeweled crown upon which resides an emanation Buddha;
he sits in the half-lotus posture.
To his right is the Bodhisattva Śvetaketu, whose countenance is joyful and serene.
Wearing jeweled crowns upon their heads, they sit in the half-lotus posture;
each holds a precious flower and gazes up at the Bodhisattva,
adorned with pearl necklaces, bracelets, armlets, and various celestial garments.
Adorned in various ways, he sits upon a precious lotus throne,
wearing a garland of flaming light.
Behind each of the Bodhisattva’s back are precious trees of flowers and fruits.
Upon the trees were parrots, śārikas, white cranes, peacocks, kalaviṅkas, and saṃjīva birds;
the necks of these various birds were adorned with necklaces of many jewels.
Behind the Bodhisattva Tārā—
The rākṣasī goddess Ekajaṭā has a wrathful countenance,
holds weapons in her hands, and sits in the half-lotus posture behind the bodhisattva Śvetaketu.
The Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, Lord of Secrets, frowns with bared teeth and bites his lower lip so tightly that his canine fangs protrude.
He wears a jeweled crown upon his head; his hair, encircling the crown, is fiery red and stands erect.
The right palm holds a great vajra;
the left hand is extended upward across the thigh.
He is adorned with pearl necklaces, bracelets, armlets, and various celestial garments.
Adorned with various ornaments, she sits in the half-lotus posture,
gazing up at the Bodhisattva from beneath the seat of the single-tufted rākṣasī.
The King Yama, the Water Deity, the Wind Deity, and the Fire Deity;
the Heavenly King Dhṛtarāṣṭra and the Heavenly King Virūḍhaka—
holding their weapons, they sit in the half-lotus posture.
Before the feet of the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, Lord of Secrets,
[are] the Dragon Kings Nanda, Sāgara, and Upananda;
and the Heavenly Kings Virūpākṣa and Vaiśravaṇa.
Holding a spear and a lasso, he sits in the half-lotus posture.
To the left above the Bodhisattva’s head are Śakra-devendra and Īśvara-deva.
Maheśvara, the gods of the Śuddhāvāsa heavens, Kumāra, and Sūrya,
riding upon clouds of manifold colors, sit in the half-lotus posture.
Holding precious flowers, they gaze up in worshipful offering.
To the right of the Bodhisattva’s crown are the Great Brahmā and Nārāyaṇa.
Maheśvara, Cūḍālā, and Candradeva,
riding upon clouds of various colors, sit in the half-lotus posture,
holding precious flowers to gaze up in worshipful offering.
To the right of the Bodhisattva’s seat,
the mantra practitioner sits in a half-kneeling posture (pralambapādāsana),
holding a branch with precious flowers and fruit in one hand and a rosary and incense burner in the other.
Beyond the perimeter on all four sides are vast mountains and rivers;
upon the mountains are various flowering and fruit-bearing forests,
as well as all manner of birds, beasts, palaces, and pāṇḍakas.
Having painted various palaces and hosts of ascetics according to the ritual rules and placed them within the maṇḍala,
the mantra practitioner shall generate the bodhicitta.
They made offerings with agallochum, white sandalwood, frankincense, camphor, and blended incenses,
as well as various fragrant flowers and diverse kinds of food and drink.
If one contemplates the image daily and recites the mantra of the Great Vidyārāja Aṅkuśa one hundred and eight times,
the five sins of immediate retribution in the Avīci hell, the sin of slandering the True Dharma, and all other intense sufferings will be swiftly purified and eliminated.
They shall never again receive the bodies of the various evil realms;
they will constantly behold all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Mahāsattvas,
and others, and shall attain the mundane and supramundane siddhi of all mantras.
All defiled karma of greed, hatred, envy, and pride shall likewise be extinguished.
All celestial deities will protect and keep one in mind.
If there are those with faith who contemplate this image, [they shall attain these benefits].
If one sees my body and makes offerings of flowers and incense to it, one shall thereby make offerings to all the Tathāgatas,
Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas throughout the ninety-nine hundred-thousand koṭi-nayuta Ganges-sands of Buddha-fields in the ten directions and the three periods of time.
In accordance with this, one shall attain an immeasurable mass of great merit, which, through the accumulation and maturation of roots of goodness,
corresponds to the stage of non-retrogression of all Tathāgatas.
Furthermore, one shall encounter a pure and great spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra) with whom one attains resonance.
World-Honored One, such an image shall bring about the accomplishment of the vast samādhis and siddhis for all practitioners of mantras.
Benefiting sentient beings by eliminating all past karmic obstacles,
they attain purity and receive supreme peace and happiness.
*Amoghapāśakalparāja-sūtra*, Fascicle Twenty-Five.
The Amoghapāśakalparāja Sūtra, Scroll Twenty-Six,
translated by the Tripitaka Master Bodhiruci of India during the Great Tang Dynasty.
Chapter Fifty-Eight: The Greatly Fearful Vidyārāja. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara—
Again, he addressed the Venerable Bhagavat, saying:
"Within this Great Liberation Lotus Maṇḍala Seal Samaya of the Amoghapāśahṛdayarāja-dhāraṇī-mantra..."
The Great Mantra Maṇḍala Seal Samaya of Amoghapāśa, the Great and Terrifying Vidyārāja,
is able to bestow [attainments] upon all practitioners of mantras.
The most supreme dhāraṇī-verse of the mantra of the Greatly Terrifying Vidyārāja Aṅkuśa,
which can realize all the peerless dharmas of the various excellent vows and practices of the Āmoghapaśa Kings.
It is capable of subduing all evil devas, nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and so forth.
They shall all comply with, revere, and protect this Dharma;
they will be able to subdue all evil vināyakas and the Māra kings of the desire realm, along with all their retinues,
who vow to submit and provide assistance and protection.
He is able to crush all enemies, wicked persons, and evil-doers;
through various punishments, imprisonments, and subjugations, he inspires great faith and insight.
Now, before the Buddha, I wish to demonstrate this Greatly Terrifying Vidyārāja Aṅkuśa mantra.
One should then perform the samaya of the seal for protecting all maṇḍalas,
by means of the great majestic power of the mantra of Acalanātha, the Greatly Terrifying Vidyārāja.
In all places, whether through governance or punishment, cause all evil and jealous spirits to provide protection and support,
and direct them toward abiding in this samaya of the seal of the vast liberation lotus maṇḍala.
May they give rise to reverence, purity, respect, and protective guardianship;
may they honor and revere this Dharma, assisting and upholding it so that all Buddhas may swiftly attain accomplishment.
We pray only that the World-Honored One, with great supernormal power, will look upon us with compassion as if covering us with a robe.
For those who extensively cultivate wholesome dharmas for the benefit of all sentient beings,
they shall attain supreme peace and happiness.
At that time, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni—
He said to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara:
"Excellent, excellent, son of good family!
I have already empowered and sealed this dharma-gate of yours."
All Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the past and present have likewise empowered and sealed this Dharma gate of yours.
All Vajradhara Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas [have done the same].
The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, Lord of Secrets,
likewise, through his supernormal powers,
has empowered this mantra-samādhi chapter of the Greatly Terrifying King Aṅkuśa for you.
All devas, nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas followed with joy,
reverently honoring and thirsting for this sublime Dharma.
You should expound this so as to bring extensive benefit.
Now, for all those who cultivate virtue,
it shall establish the accomplishment of the most supreme, peerless *siddhi* of the Dharma.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara,
receiving the Buddha’s instruction and gazing up at the Tathāgata with reverence, smiled joyfully.
Before the World-Honored One, he gazed intently at the great assembly.

He manifested a terrifying form through his supernatural powers, emitting great flames of fire, knitting his brows, glaring with wide eyes, and baring fangs that protruded upward. Shouting with a roar, he uttered the mantra of the Greatly Terrifying Vidyārāja Amoghapāśa, Aṅkuśa: [Mantra follows]
Namaḥ samantabhadraya | Tathāgatāya pāramitāśritāya || Namaḥ sarvadhātave || 1 || 2 || 3 ||
Kakara-khara-ga-gha-ṅa-ca-cha-ja-jha-ña-ṭa-ṭha-ḍa-ḍha-ṇa-ta-tha-da-dha-na-pa-pha-ba-bha-ma-ya-ra-la-va-śa-ṣa-sa-ha-kṣa.

6. Oṃ mahāmaṇḍalādhipataye namaḥ sarvabuddhādhyeṣikāya. 7. Śrī-tantra... (the remainder of the mantra follows).
