Śakra Devendra, the Four Great Heavenly Kings, Sūrya (the Sun Deity), Candra (the Moon Deity), and all their retinues will provide complete protection and guardianship.
Additionally, there are large barley, small barley, white grains, black beans, mung beans, sesame seeds, rice, clarified butter, and honey.
If one performs the consecrated homa one hundred and eight times,
then people will see, hear, believe in, and turn toward [the teaching].
Furthermore, there are rice, sesame, white mustard seeds, agallochum, ghee, honey, and curd.
Perform the empowerment through homa one hundred and eight times;
all yakṣas and rākṣasas will be completely humbled and submit.
Furthermore, [use] white mustard seeds, nāgapuṣpa flowers, ghee, curd, and honey.
Perform one thousand and eight empowerments of homa.
The Dragon King will rejoice and send down great sweet rain to moisten all things.
If the rain is excessive:
Take the ashes from a fire burning in a brazier;
while reciting the *vidyā-mantra* one hundred and eight times while facing the clouds, scatter them into the air. The rain will immediately clear and cease.
Furthermore, [take] black mustard seeds, clarified butter, and honey.
If one performs the empowerment-homa one thousand and eight times,
then no other thieves will come to invade the territory;
if they have already arrived, they will be made to retreat and disperse.
Furthermore, by consecrating soybeans, ghee, honey,
and curd with one hundred and eight recitations of the mantra and performing homa,
all pestilential diseases within the household will be immediately eliminated.
Furthermore, by consecrating rice, sesame, white mustard seeds, lotus stalks and leaves, clarified butter, honey, and curd,
and performing one thousand and eight rounds of homa,
one shall eliminate the ten evil deeds, the five heinous crimes, and all other grave offenses.
If one wishes to achieve the great accomplishment of the Greatly Terrifying Vidyārāja Aṅkuśa,
one should kindle a fire with a piece of purple *khadira* wood one span (*vitasti*) in length,
using white mustard seeds, agallochum incense, and clarified butter.
Perform the empowerment *homa* one thousand and eight times;
this is the most supreme accomplishment among all mantra-samayas,
and it is also capable of gathering together the mantras of all the great wrathful kings (*mahākrodharāja*).
Abiding within this mantra,
if at the end of each recitation one loudly utters the syllable *hūṃ* seven times after the word *svāhā*,
[one invokes] all the deities of the mantras of the Great Wrathful Kings.
All shall abide before [the deity] so that various matters and dharmas may be perfected.
If one wishes for the manifestation of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva as the Great Furenwu King (Mahā-krodharāja),
one should bathe thoroughly and don fresh, clean garments.

Light a fire with *deodar* wood and *mukūlaka* wood, and perform *homa* offerings ten thousand times using rice grains, lotus flowers, *utpala* flowers, white mustard seeds, white sandalwood incense, clarified butter, honey, and curd.
Perform the consecration (*adhiṣṭhāna*) throughout this process.
Immediately, the Great Wrathful King Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva appeared before them and placed his hand upon their heads, saying: "Excellent, excellent!
I shall fulfill the aspirations you have sought."
As for this mantra, if one has heavy karmic offenses from past lives or long-standing obstacles,
it will manifest its form in dreams and touch one’s head;
thus, all great vows shall be completely fulfilled.
That is to say, the mantras, the maṇḍala rites,
the mudrā rites, the image rites, and the great samayas are all fully accomplished.
[One should offer] śūrasa rice, non-glutinous rice, ghee, curd, and honey.
Perform one thousand and eight empowerments of homa;
one will swiftly obtain wealth and silk.
If a person takes grass three inches long and cuts it [into that length], [the rite is accomplished].
Perform one hundred and eight times of *homa* consecrated with clarified butter, curd, and honey;
you will be respectfully honored by all people whom you encounter.
[If one uses] sesame seeds, human fat, clarified butter, curd, and honey...
Perform the consecrated homa ten thousand times;
the Honored Buddhas have given this prediction.
If one seeks advancement in office, use asparagus, ghee, and honey.
If one performs the homa ten thousand times, it will be fulfilled according to one's wishes.
For those who possess the secret unimpeded samaya,
[the substances are] black mustard seeds, ghee, and salt.
If one performs this homa in such a manner, it will be fulfilled according to one's wishes.
If one performs this homa with sesame seeds and salt,
all wicked people will naturally respect one another.
If one performs homa with fennel flowers, ghee, and honey,
one shall obtain divine efficacy, mastery, and unimpeded power. If one uses clove,
white sandalwood, aloeswood, ghee, blended incense, and sesame oil;
If one performs the consecrated homa ten thousand times,
one will dream of all the Buddhas placing their hands upon one's head in blessing and praising one,
thereby attaining great siddhi.
Wherever they go, all people will offer them support.
When their lives come to an end, they will go directly to the Western Land of Peace and Bliss (*Sukhāvatī*).
There, they will be reborn within a lotus flower and attain the wisdom of recollecting past lives.
If one performs homa with rice husks in this manner,
one will see hidden treasures;
likewise with white mustard seeds and snake skin.
Perform one thousand and eight empowerments of homa;
the person who is the object of resentment will then feel shame and repent, and offer an apology.
If one cuts the bark of a plantain tree into inch-long pieces, [the same result follows].
If one performs homa in this manner with natural garments,
or with ghee mixed with white mustard seeds,
one will thereby attain an increase in longevity.
If one performs homa with fresh butter and black mustard seeds,
one will thereby eliminate the calamities of all accidental diseases.
If one performs homa with karañja seeds in this manner, [the same result is achieved].
Then, the fetters and shackles are released and one attains liberation.
Chapter Sixty-Two: The Accomplishment of the *Cakṣuḥ-añjana* (Eye-Ointment). Vajrapāṇi, Lord of Secrets, Bodhisattva Mahāsattva.
This is the mantra of the Great Terrifying Vidyārāja Aṅkuśa,
the samaya of the kṣāragada medicine;
all that is undertaken is swiftly accomplished.
All their various evils and grave offenses shall likewise be extinguished;
they shall not be harmed by any worldly illnesses or afflictions.
Their faculty of sight will be pure, and all whom they encounter will love and respect them.
He enters all mountains, forests, hermitages, and mountain caves alone without fear.
He enters all rivers, dragon pools, and great oceans without fear or obstruction.
He enters the palaces of all devas, nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, asuras, gandharvas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, and so forth, entering them all without hindrance.
He is joyfully honored by all monasteries, deva temples, kṣatriyas, brāhmaṇas, and various households;
he attains the secret samaya of great compassion.
They enter among all flocks of birds and herds of beasts without mutual fear or alarm;
thus they travel and move about with complete mastery,
never being subjected to the ridicule or criticism of others.
All undertakings will swiftly attain accomplishment; thus it is said in verse:
Realgar, bezoar, and *bhadrala*; Sea-foam, black pepper, saffron, and the filaments of the red lotus; Green *utpala* flowers and long pepper.
White sandalwood incense, conch-shell powder, the root medicine of *karañja*, and a decoction of *śiṃśapā*—these medicinal substances should be taken in equal proportions.
An equal amount of *śrīkhaṇḍa* juice should also be added, along with rock honey, musk, and camphor;
these should be divided into three portions relative to the quantity of the aforementioned drugs.
On the painted maṇḍala, place [the substances] separately;
empower them from beginning to end with the mantra of the Greatly Fearsome Vidyārāja without interruption.
Thoroughly purify and blend them together, then place them in a vessel of Persian glass or lapis lazuli, and set it before the image within the maṇḍala.
Performed on an auspicious lunar day during the waxing moon, under a favorable constellation, and on a Sunday.
Having bathed and purified oneself, wearing clean garments and eating the three white foods, one should practice this rite.
Offering various incenses, flowers, and food, facing west toward the image while sitting in the full-lotus posture, [recite] the mantra of the Greatly Terrifying Vidyārāja.

By consecrating the *kṣāra* herb with the mantra *tāt-tāt*, when the three signs of warmth, smoke, and light appear, one will be able to accomplish all mundane and supramundane dharmas; this is the secret master’s secret efficacy.
If one constantly applies it to the eyes, the faculty of sight becomes pure.
One shall obtain the supreme, incomparable divine eye,
and thereby receive the vajra empowerment and protection of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the three periods of time.

Furthermore, one shall obtain the protection of all devas, nāgas, the eight classes of beings, wind spirits, water spirits, deities of crops, deities of flowers and fruits, and deities of vital essence.
They shall eternally abide within this person’s six sense organs and limbs,
collectively providing protection and extinguishing all karmic obstacles and hindrances.
Upon the end of their life, they shall be reborn in the Western Pure Land of wondrous excellence.
Having attained the purity of the five eyes and the knowledge of recollecting past abodes,
they shall behold hundreds of thousands of koṭis of Ganges-sand-like Buddhas, Tathāgatas,
seated upon the bodhi-seat and attaining perfect enlightenment.
One will never perceive any evil signs;
one's vision gradually becomes clear and unobstructed.
Should there be people suffering from various eye diseases, [they shall be healed].
If one applies this medicine to the eyes for seven days and nights,
all eye ailments— regardless of whether they are distant or near—
will be cured, and the eyes will become clear and bright.
If one performs the consecration for twenty-one days and nights,
even those with congenital blindness or night-blindness will be cured;
they will be loved and respected by others, and their karmic obstacles will be extinguished.
63. Chapter Sixty-Three: The Medicinal Elixirs of Supernatural Transformation. The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, Lord of Secrets.
This is the samaya of the mantra-emanation of the Greatly Fearful Vidyārāja Aṅkuśa,
an āgada medicine capable of shaking all the great earth, mountains, and rivers.
It is capable of causing all people, gods, and spirits to be completely humbled and submissive. He then spoke a verse, saying:
"Take cow bezoar and white mustard seeds, Place them in a clean vessel and seal it securely;
Erect a maṇḍala and set it before the image— This is the mantra of the Greatly Terrifying Vidyārāja."

Through day and night empowerment, the three signs appear; having realized these signs, one achieves the application of empowerment through purification and bathing, donning clean garments, and holding this medicine to perform all rites.
O Lord of Secrets, if one wishes to bind a person:
First, one should bathe oneself and put on clean garments. Then,
having applied [fragrance] to the maṇḍala and laid out the colored powders for the boundary lines,
one should place there a vase of incense, food and drink, flowers, and incense.
Burn agalloch incense as an offering.
With powdered incense rubbed upon the hands, form the mudrā and recite the mantra.
Bind the person [to be consecrated], bathe them thoroughly, and have them don clean garments.
Adorning the crown of his head with a flower garland, he causes him to sit beside the altar.
Holding a bowl filled to the brim with food, he scatters medicinal powder over his body and says, "Bind! Bind! and they are immediately bound.
All matters concerning the three periods of time that were asked about were explained in their entirety.
If one binds the head of a person afflicted by illness, saying "Bind!
while binding them, then even if they inquire about illnesses caused by ghosts, all such things will be revealed.
To restore it to its original state, sprinkle water upon it.
If the bowl has been turned over, place it in a clean location or within the altar area;
scatter medicinal substances over the bowl, recite mantras, and snap your fingers.
Regarding the term "turning," it means that one may also turn a water jar or a large vat.
Alternatively, one may scatter [the substances] upon a knife, a sword, a vajra, a trident, a wheel, a lasso, a battle-axe, or a staff.
If one recites the mantra and snaps one's fingers, it will immediately move;
if consecrated water is sprinkled upon it, it returns to its original state.
If scattered over a lotus pond, the flowers will stir and flourish.
If one scatters [it] among a crowd or upon one's own body, one will immediately be bound.
If one scatters it within a city gate and walks over it, all calamities and hardships will be removed.
If one scatters it upon flowering or fruit-bearing trees...
The flowers and fruits will flourish and grow excellent, or they may all fall off on their own.
If one recites the mantra with a great roar of wrath while scattering the medicinal powder upon a mountain peak, that mountain will crumble and split apart.
If one scatters it at the gates of a village or town, [the same effect occurs].
Furthermore, if one empowers their hand and knocks on the gates of a village three, five, or seven times,
those villagers who see this will have their obstacles removed.
If [the empowered substance] is scattered at the base of a temple gate, the same occurs.
Those who have transgressed by treading upon a precept-breaking śramaṇa will immediately run about madly and naked,
or else they will be bound.
If one wishes to release [the affliction], by mixing milk with scented water and consecrating it for bathing the body,
it will return to its former state as before. If it is scattered upon a river or a pond, [the same result follows].
All fish, snakes, turtles, and tortoises emerge onto the shore;
they scatter among the horses, yet the horses suffer no disease or panic and flee together.
Furthermore, if one consecrates white mustard seeds and scatters them along with *yong-san* (eternal powder), they will not panic and run away.
If one scatters [the mantra] over a wine shop or over a wine jar,
at that time the wine jar shall also move;
if it remains as before, one should scatter empowered earth over it.
If scattered among a flock of sheep, the sheep will neither suffer from disease nor run away in panic;
furthermore, if cow urine is scattered, they will not run away in panic.
If scattered among a herd of cattle, the cattle will neither suffer from disease nor run away in panic.
Furthermore, if one consecrates saffron-scented water and scatters it, [the creatures] will no longer flee in terror.
If one scatters it into a granary or storehouse, the grain and wheat within shall spontaneously surge upward.
If they remain as before, one should scatter honey-water over them.
Scatter it over the various foods and drinks within the kitchen;
the obstacles of those who eat will be extinguished.
Scatter it within the celestial temples and monasteries.
Furthermore, hold the medicine and place it within the mouth of the celestial image,
causing all the celestial images to simultaneously reel and utter loud cries.
If it is placed within the mouth of the image of Mahākāla, [the same occurs].
He caused the image to roar;
as it let out that roar, the great earth, mountains, and forests shook all at once,
and the gods and ghosts within the mountain caves were made to cry out in unison.
If, at the hour of the Dog (the ninth watch), one recites the mantra with wrath amidst a crossroads while scattering medicinal powders in the four directions,
all yakṣas, rākṣasas, and spirits will gather like clouds.
They shall be employed as servants and constantly act as attendants.
If one scatters [the seeds] toward the Nākṣatra deities,
it will cause all the Nākṣatras to provide protection for oneself.
If one has apprehended a thief, one should smear the altar with a mixture of cow dung and clay.
Having strewn powdered earth along the boundary paths, one should write the name of the person suspected of stealing the object at the center of the altar.
Scatter various flowers and offer perfumed water as an offering.
Burn agalloch incense and recite this mantra one hundred and eight times over the medicinal powder while empowering it upon the name of the person [in question].
This causes the thief, regardless of distance,
to be seized and brought before him, where he must confess the stolen goods;
once the items have been recovered, the thief is released by scattering water over him.
If one goes to dwell or stay overnight in mountain wilds,
by scattering medicinal herbs in the four directions, all tigers, wolves, venomous snakes, and bandits will not plunder or harm them.
One should scatter medicinal herbs in the four directions at the site of the altar where the recitation is performed.
One will not be subjected to any disturbances caused by any *vināyakas*.
Furthermore, if one places medicinal powders or decoctions into water and gives it to someone to drink, that person will be bound immediately.
If they disperse, gaze at them with eyes wide open.
Chapter Sixty-Four: Invoking the Secret Protectors of the Gods. Vajrapāṇi, Lord of Secrets, Bodhisattva Mahāsattva.
This is the samaya-mantra of the Great Terrifying Vidyārāja Aṅkuśa;
it is also able to guide and gather all devas, nāgas, the eight classes of beings, śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, and all other people.
If one consecrates all incense, fruits, food and drink,
and clothing, and then offers, eats, or wears them, they will spontaneously become objects of reverence.
If one consecrates lotuses and all manner of fragrant flowers to make offerings to the devas, [the same result follows].
At that time, the various devas shall always joyfully and reverently protect [the practitioner].
If one empowers white mustard seeds from the *nāga-flower* tree and scatters them into a dragon pool,
one shall summon the Dragon King and all his retinue to come and protect the life-force of the messenger.
If one consecrates *guggulu* incense with mustard-seed oil and offers it by burning before an image of any yakṣa, that true yakṣa will be summoned;
filled with joy and reverence, he will submit to being commanded as an attendant.
If one empowers saffron, white sandalwood, rice flowers, and water at the riverbank,
one makes an offering to the gandharvas, kinnaras, and mahoragas.
Recite the name and invoke it while offering incense, flowers, and water into the river;
they will all be delighted and come to respectfully protect and uphold you, serving as your messengers for life.
If one consecrates various scented waters, non-glutinous rice, sugar, and various mixed flowers [with this mantra], [the same result shall follow].
Make offerings to an image of an asura, reciting mantras and invoking its name;
with reverence and respect, one shall thereby protect oneself.
If one offers consecrated milk-rice to an image of Nīlada, reciting mantras and invoking its name.
I respectfully entreat you to honor me and place yourself at my disposal as my servant.
If one empowers food and offers it to the piśāca spirits,
they will joyfully accept the instruction and protect the practitioner with reverence.
If one consecrates *śāli* rice, flowers, and *kruñca* grass,
and scatters them as offerings for the hungry ghosts (*preta*),
they will receive the instruction with joy and reverence.
If one consecrates various foods and drinks— such as clarified butter, oil, honey, milk, curd, fruits,
and melons— and gives them to śramaṇas, brahmins, and all people, who then consume them.
Through the profound power of the mantra, they will develop deep mutual respect and affection.
If one consecrates incense and flowers and offers them to a member of the Kṣatriya caste,
that person, guided by the mantra, will come to provide offerings.
If one consecrates *sumana* flowers with mantras and offers them to the image of the Goddess of Merit (*Śrī-devī*),
she will joyfully accept the invitation and provide protection.
If one consecrates scented water with mantras and bathes the image of Vaiśravaṇa with it...
I respectfully invoke you to come with joy and grant your protective guardianship.
If one consecrates black pepper and scatters it toward the sun,
one invites the Sun Deity to look upon and protect with joy.
If one consecrates cow’s milk and scatters it toward the moon deity,
the moon deity will be summoned and joyfully provide protection.
If one consecrates agarwood or cypress wood...
Light a fire and perform homa.
Summon the Fire God (Agni) to grant joy and protection. If he is of a wrathful mind, empower white mustard seeds and scatter them upon the tree;
the tree will immediately bend.
Furthermore, by empowering white mustard seeds with a mind of wrathful anger, one scatters them upon the tree; its roots will then emerge.
By scattering water over them, it immediately returns to its former state.
If one performs other rites, all shall be conducted according to this principle.
Chapter Sixty-Five: The Image of the Greatly Fearful Vidyārāja. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara—
Again, he addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One,
as for the image of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, the Great Terrifying King of Light—
if there are sentient beings who behold it..."
By joining the palms in prostration and making offerings,
all karmic obstacles of darkness from the past and present will be extinguished. If one makes these offerings constantly, [the same result shall follow].
Then one shall obtain the various liberations, merits, and accumulations of fortune of the samaya of the mantra of the Most Victorious and Greatly Terrifying Vidyārāja;
one shall also penetrate all mantra-samayas, and this should be done daily.
The mass of merit and roots of virtue from reverently making offerings to and serving ninety-nine hundred-thousand-ten-million-billion *koṭi-nayuta* Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas.
Furthermore, one will be constantly remembered by all the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, devas, and benevolent deities of the ten directions.
For the image, one should use white cotton cloth or silk;
do not cut both ends.
The dimensions shall be three cubits.
When the painter executes the work, he must constantly bathe and purify himself,
wear fresh clean garments, and observe the eightfold precepts of the fast.
Do not mix pigments with leather glue.
In the center, paint the great Mount Sumeru, a mountain of jewels;
atop its summit, a lotus flower made of the seven precious substances.
Upon the flower pedestal sits the Great Terrifying Vidyārāja Amoghasiddhi and the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara,
seated in the full lotus posture (*paryaṅka*), with three faces and six arms, his body the color of sandalwood gold.
The central face is serene and smiling, adorned with a jeweled garland;
the left face is wrathful, biting its lower lip with its fangs;
and the right face is terrifying, with canine teeth protruding upward.
He wears a three-peaked jewel crown upon which resides an emanated Buddha.
His flaming hair rises up in a fiery red blaze,
and from the center of his head emerges the upper half of the Greatly Terrifying Vidyārāja.
He has one face and two arms; his countenance is blue in color, with a laughing expression and canine fangs protruding upward.
On his head he wears a jeweled crown, upon which resides an emanation Buddha.
His topknot is red in color, and his sideburns are red and bristle upward with flames.
One hand holds a sword and the other grasps a mallet;
from above the sword and mallet, tongues of fire and flames issue forth.
Adorned with celestial garments, pearls, necklaces, and bracelets,
his body is fully embellished and enveloped in flames;
in his first right hand, he holds an opened lotus flower with its filaments curved like a hook.
The second right hand is extended, bestowing fearlessness and raining down various jewels;
the third right hand holds a trident;
the first left hand holds a hook.
The second left hand holds a lasso;
the third left hand holds a golden wheel.
From these six hands, various kinds of light are emitted.
Adorned with various exquisite flowers, colored silks, fine gauze, and celestial robes,
and fully embellished with pearl necklaces, earrings, and bracelets,
his body radiated a great light.
Furthermore, to the right of the Vidyārāja is the Bodhisattva Tārā,
her body yellowish-white in color, with a face and countenance full of joy.
Holding a blue utpala lotus in her hand,
with her head slightly bowed, she sits in the half-lotus posture;
behind her is the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvarī-mātṛkā.
Their bodies are naturally white in color, their faces are serene and joyful,
and they hold lotus flowers while slightly bowing their heads as they sit in the half-lotus posture.
These are the two bodhisattvas.
She was adorned with various gauze cloths, celestial garments, pearls, necklaces,
earrings, and bracelets, and sat upon a lotus throne;
next followed a one-tufted rākṣasī.
His countenance is fearsome, and he wears a human skull upon his head.
His body is truly blue in color and possesses six arms;
one hand holds a lotus flower, while another grasps a curved knife.
In one hand he holds a trident, in another a battle-axe;
in one hand he holds a noose, and with another he raises his palm.
His body is fully adorned with garments and jeweled necklaces.
Sitting in the half-lotus posture, they gazed up with reverence at the Noble One.
Behind them, the Heavenly King Virūpākṣa, the Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa,
and King Yama sat in the half-lotus posture, holding various precious flowers.
Furthermore, to the left of the Vidyārāja is the Yakṣa King Mahānala,
whose face is extremely wrathful and whose body is purple-black in color.
His hair is red and stands erect; he bows his body and kneels long on both knees.
With both hands at his chest, he grasps a curved knife, a halberd, and an axe.
He gazes up with reverence as flames blaze from his entire body.
Afterward, the yakṣa king Mahāraṇa, together with his retinue and servants,
knelt with palms joined while flames blazed from his entire body.
Following him were the celestial kings Dhṛtarāṣṭra and Virūḍhaka.
Sitting in the half-lotus posture and holding various precious flowers,
to the left of the head of the Vidyārāja are the Great Brahmā, Nārāyaṇa, Varuṇa, Agni, and Sūrya.
Sitting in the half-lotus posture, he holds various precious flowers.
To the right of the crown of the Vidyārāja are Śakra, Maheśvara, the Śuddhāvāsa deities, Vāyu, and Candra.
Sitting in the half-lotus posture, he holds various precious flowers.
Behind the Vidyārāja, on both sides, are flowering trees made of the seven treasures.
To the left of the Vidyārāja’s seat...
The mantra-practitioner kneels with both legs on the ground;
holding various branches, leaves, flowers, and fruits in one hand and a rosary in the other,
they gaze upward at the Noble One.
The Vidyārāja sits to the right;
the celestial maidens and messengers have faces that are fearsome.
They stand with bodies slightly bowed, their two hands held in formal *añjali* at the chest while grasping swords.
The celestial hosts, their bodies adorned with exquisite garments, pearls, necklaces, bracelets,
and armlets, gazed upward at the Noble One from the midpoint of that mountain.
The Nanda Dragon King and Upananda Dragon King entwined each other from left and right around Mount Sumeru,
at the base of which lies the great ocean.
There were various kinds of fish, beasts, ducks, geese, lotus-herons, white cranes, and peacocks,
as well as various kinds of lotuses and *utpala* flowers;
once these had been fully painted and decorated.
In a secluded and quiet place, having bathed for purification and donned clean garments,
one should construct a maṇḍala according to the capacity of one’s mind,
and place this image in its center.
One should serve and make offerings with various flowers, incense, and fresh, pure food and drink.
Facing east toward the image, one sits in the full lotus posture (*paryaṅka*) and contemplates the Great Terrifying Vidyārāja Amoghapāśa and the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
Recite the mantra of the Greatly Terrifying Vidyārāja Aṅkuśa,
completing ten thousand recitations with perfect correspondence of syllables and phrases.
On the eighth day of each month, abstain from food and speech.
Having made offerings of various flowers, incense, food, and drink,
one should recite the mantra of the Greatly Terrifying Vidyārāja Aṅkuśa one hundred and eight times.
By doing so constantly, all worldly affairs will be accomplished according to one's thoughts.
One will immediately obtain the most supreme worldly accomplishments.
If there are sentient beings whose faith is pure who,
day after day, join their palms, gaze upon it, and pay homage, [they shall likewise attain success].
All the four grave offenses, the five heinous crimes, and the ten evil deeds committed by such a person, as well as calamities, portents, pestilence, and various bodily ailments,
shall all be completely extinguished. Should there be bhikṣus,
bhikṣuṇīs, laymen, or laywomen— [who recite this...]— their [sins and afflictions] shall likewise be eradicated.
On the eighth day of every waxing moon, one should be able to purify and smear the altar;
or, at the very least, sweep it clean, offer seasonal flowers and fruits, and burn various famous incenses.
Then, with palms joined and gazing upon the image, one should recite this mantra.
Thus, they equally served ninety-nine hundred-thousand-ten-million-billion *gaṅgā-saṃkhyeya* Buddhas,
honoring and making offerings through various assemblies of gifts,
thereby maturing a mass of merit.
