shall also constantly observe, empower, and protect [them].
At that time, when the Tathāgata Śākyamuni bestowed this prophecy upon the Vidyārāja,
the great earth in the ten directions shook in six ways, and from the midst of the sky there fell a dense, continuous rain of pure moonlight flowers.
Rucira flowers and mahārucira flowers;
māndārava flowers and mahāmāndārava flowers; padma flowers and kumuda flowers.
Puṇḍarīka flowers, blue utpala flowers, red utpala flowers, aśoka flowers,
pāṭala flowers, and punnāga flowers.
Gandhapuṣpaka flowers, kuṇḍalī flowers, atimuktaka flowers, pāruṣaka flowers,
and all kinds of golden and silver flowers.
Cloud-seas of various jewel-flowers and diverse blossoms;
cloud-seas of rains of various jewels and precious rains;
cloud-seas of rains of the fragrances of gośīrṣa-candana, aloeswood, camphor, and saffron, and all manner of scents.
They rain down clouds of oceans of various kinds of fine perfumed waters;
they rain down clouds of oceans of various wondrous sounds that resonate spontaneously without being struck;
and they rain down clouds of oceans of garments, jeweled crowns, pearl necklaces, earrings, bracelets, armlets, flower garlands, and precious ornaments.
It rained upon the Heaven of the Thirty-three, the Great Brahmā,
Śakra Devendra, Maheśvara, Kumāra, the Four Heavenly Kings, and the Water Deities.
From the god Īśvara and the god Maheśvara,
down to all the ninety-nine billion hundred-thousand sons of gods,
including their palaces, robes, crowns, and necklaces.
Jeweled bracelets and armlets, powdered incense and ointments,
and canopies made of the seven precious gems— like clouds of the ocean—
filled the ten directions, spreading vast and dense as a great offering.
Śākyamuni Buddha, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva,
the Pure Lotus Radiant King, the various great bodhisattvas,
the Vajradhara Lord of Secrets Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, and the entire assembly from all the buddha-fields throughout the ten directions.
All the Tathāgatas, all the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas,
and the entire great assembly all manifested various signs of the accomplishment of great supernormal powers within the sky.
All the secret heart-dhāraṇīs, mantras, maṇḍalas, mudrās, and samayas of these Tathāgatas manifested simultaneously;
likewise, all the celestial palaces of the gods throughout the ten directions also appeared.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi,
Lord of Secrets, rose from his seat, joined his palms in reverence,
circumambulated the Buddha three times, and prostrated with his head at the Buddha’s feet.
Standing to one side, he smiled radiantly and, brandishing his vajra, addressed the Buddha once more:
"World-Honored One, behold this supernatural power; its manifestation of ultimate emptiness is exceedingly vast."
Such supernatural powers are likewise all-pervasive.
The practitioner of mantras attains the gateway of great accomplishment and the samaya.
Furthermore, there are all the devas, nāgas, and the eight classes of beings.
Due to the manifestation of the supernatural powers of the King of Pure Lotus Radiance of this lineage,
they all assembled together.
They beheld the supernatural power, majesty, and virtue of that Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the King of Pure Lotus Radiance.
Transcending the ten directions and manifesting throughout the entirety of space—
by what spiritual power can such a transformed appearance suddenly be made to appear in this way throughout the ten directions?
"We only pray that the Tathāgata will take pity on us and explain [this matter] for us, thereby severing our doubts.
At that time, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni...
He addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, Lord of Secrets, saying:
"Listen attentively, listen attentively! I shall explain for you the causes, conditions, and manifested signs of this great supernormal power."
This is the gate of the Great Illusory Transformation Samādhi of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara;
it is the gate of the Samādhi of the Vajra Dhāraṇī, the Samādhi of Equanimity, and the Samādhi of the Branch of Courageous Prowess.
By means of these ninety-nine hundred-thousand-koṭi-nayuta samādhi doors,
he constantly manifests supernatural transformations following his body,
filling the realms of the ten directions.
These samādhis are also the manifestation of the power of the samādhi, mudrās, and great maṇḍalas of the heart-king mantra of Amoghapāśa, the Pure Lotus Vidyārāja Añkuśa.
Manifesting such supernatural powers and majestic virtue, and displaying the power of the samādhi of vast manifestation,
one should extensively and universally benefit all sentient beings by practicing this Dharma-gate of the name-mantra of the Pure Lotus King Aṅkuśa.
If one merely believes, understands, accepts, maintains, reads, and recites it,
one shall behold ninety-two hundred thousand koṭi-nayuta-gaṅgā-vāluka-saṃkhyeya Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas.
Having cultivated various roots of goodness through service and offerings,
one should equally recollect the names of these Tathāgatas and equally enter this assembly of the secret-heart *dhāraṇī*, mantra, great maṇḍala, and samaya of the lineage of these Tathāgatas.
They likewise equally uphold this chapter on the Secret Heart Dhāraṇī Mantra Great Maṇḍala Seals and Samaya of the families of all Tathāgatas;
they equally enter the gateway to the accomplishment of the Secret Heart Dhāraṇī Mantra Great Maṇḍala Seals and Samaya of all Tathāgatas of the three times.
Vajradhara Guhyapati Bodhisattva Mahāsattva,
for what cause and condition do you now proclaim this Pure Lotus Vidyārāja, who possesses great majestic power,
along with all the chapters on the secret heart-dhāraṇī mantras, maṇḍalas, mudrās, and ritual methods of all the Tathāgatas of the three periods of time?
All enter into this vidyārāja-dharma together,
becoming of one identical essence like water and milk, with no further distinction between them.
For this reason, it is called the name of the Pure Lotus Vidyārāja.
This Secret Heart Dharani Mantra of the Samaya of the Mandalas and Mudras of the Lineage of All Tathagatas possesses great majestic power.
Whether they be bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, laymen, or laywomen, [who enter it...]

Those who believe, understand, receive, and uphold this Vidyārāja Aṅkuśa mantra of the Pure Lotus shall equally receive and uphold the secret heart-dhāraṇī mantras, maṇḍalas, mudrās, and samayas of the lineage of all Tathāgatas of the three periods of time.
One shall attain the aggregates of morality, concentration, wisdom, and liberation of all Tathāgatas, the Buddhas of the three periods of time, thereby maturing one's roots of goodness;
and for the sake of all Tathāgatas, the Buddhas of the three periods of time, one shall constantly offer praise.
It is associated with the samaya-siddhi of the greatest accomplishment of Amoghasiddhi;
it is associated with the samaya-siddhi of the secret equality of all Tathāgata families.
One attains the correspondence with the sphere of miraculous transformations of the Great Samādhi of the Mind of Mantras and Vidyās, which is the supernatural power of all Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas;
one attains the correspondence with the adornment of the six pāramitās of the Great Bodhicitta.
One attains conformity with the samaya of the mudrās of the Great Maṇḍala of all Mantra-Vidyārājas.
This is the supernatural power and majestic virtue of the pure Lotus Vidyārāja Aṅkuśa mantra.
Furthermore, they constantly receive the empowerment of the supernormal powers and samādhis of all Tathāgatas,
as well as the empowerment of the supernormal powers and samādhis of all Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas.
For this reason, he spoke this mantra of the Pure Lotus King Aṅkuśa.
It possesses great majesty and great supernatural power.
If one should even for a moment [offer] flowers, fruits, ointments, or music, [the result shall be as follows].

One who makes offerings at the place of recitation and chanting shall serve and make offerings to the secret heart-dhāraṇī mantras, great maṇḍalas, and samayas of all the Tathāgatas of the three times and of all their lineages.
For those who uphold, recite, and chant this mantra of the Pure Lotus King Aṅkuśa,
all yakṣas, rākṣasas, and vināyakas who create obstacles and difficulties shall be utterly dispersed and flee.
All disputes, calamities, portents, epidemics, hatred, slander, flattery, the ten evil deeds, and the five heinous crimes—
all karmic obstructions without exception shall be completely extinguished.
All Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Mahāsattvas shall provide consolation, protection, and mindfulness.
The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, Lord of Secrets;
the ten great Vajra-yakṣa generals, and the Great Sovereign Vajra-yakṣa general.
All the celestial deities, the gods of the Four Great Kings,
together with their retinues, shall respectfully protect [the practitioner].
One shall attain the most supreme accomplishment of the secret heart-dhāraṇī mantra, maṇḍala, mudrā, and samaya of the family of all Tathāgatas.
One attains the supreme accomplishment of the Samaya, the Seal, and the Great Maṇḍala of the Lotus of Vast Liberation, which is the mantra of the Amogha-vimokṣa-guhyahṛdaya-dhāraṇī.
One shall attain the supreme accomplishment of the unerring reality,
and all devas, nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, gandharvas, asuras, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas shall come to guard and protect them.
Furthermore, one shall receive great offerings within the world;
all vows and practices will increase and reach fulfillment;
and all curses, sorcery, poisonous drugs, and venomous insects [shall be neutralized].
Various evil spirits and ghosts shall not inflict calamities or afflictions upon them;
furthermore, they shall suffer no ailments caused by wind or phlegm,
nor any fevers, chills, malarial fevers, sores, carbuncles, scabs, or itch.
Regarding all illnesses such as headaches, abscesses, hemorrhoids, and dysentery—
except for those that are the ripening of past karma and must be experienced lightly in the present life—
the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, Lord of Secrets, [will provide protection].
This Amoghapāśahṛdayarāja Viśuddhapadmavijayāñkuśa-mantra is named the Secret Heart Dhāraṇī-mantra of All Tathāgatas of the Three Times, the Dhāraṇī of Samādhi, and the Samaya.
It is also named the Samaya of the Universal Dhāraṇī and Samādhi of the Secret Mind-Superknowledge of All Vajradharas.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, the Lord of Secrets, [spoke].
Having heard the Buddha’s praise of the miraculous power and merit of this mantra of the Secret Pure Lotus Vidyārāja Añkuśa, Mañjuśrī,
he leaped for joy and came forward to address the Buddha, saying:
World-Honored One, this is the mantra of the Pure Lotus Radiance King Aṅkuśa.
It is marvelous and rare, endowed with all the merits of enlightenment;
it can fulfill all aspirations and bring to maturity all roots of goodness for enlightenment.
This completes all mandalas, mudrās, and samayas;
it is the supreme accomplishment of immeasurable merit.
O Bhagavān, this is the mantra of the Pure Lotus Radiance King Aṅkuśa.
It is especially rare and difficult to encounter,
just as when the Tathāgata appears in a certain place,
sits beneath the Bodhi tree, and turns the Great Wheel of Dharma.
This is the mantra of the Pure Lotus Radiance King Aṅkuśa;
does it not appear from the white tuft of hair between the eyebrows of that Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara?
This shall be for the benefit of those who uphold mantras;
it is a dharma-gate for attaining true liberation and accomplishment that cannot be encountered or heard by those with meager roots of virtue.
Having accumulated roots of goodness in the presence of all Buddhas throughout immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas,
one is finally able to see, hear, revere, make offerings to, believe and understand, copy, receive and uphold, recite, and fully cultivate this [teaching].
If a mantra practitioner momentarily forgets their mindfulness,
one should know that they lose immeasurable and boundless roots of goodness and all merits of enlightenment;
how much more so for a single day and night, a month, or a year?
Even after hundreds of thousands of days, they will completely forget [the teachings];
one should know that such a person has forever lost all the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Mahāsattvas of the ten directions and the three periods of time.
This is the Great Samaya of all the roots of virtue, the provisions, and the mass of merit of the qualities of enlightenment.
At that time, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni again addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, the Lord of Secrets, saying:
It is so, it is so, just as you have said.

These sentient beings must, over many kalpas, have made offerings to and served ninety-nine hundred-thousand-nayuta-koti Ganges-sand Buddhas, Tathāgatas, and accumulated roots of virtue through the great maṇḍala mudrās and samayas.
If these sentient beings have not accumulated merit in the past, they will neither see nor hear this vidyārāja mantra-samaya, nor will they receive, uphold, read, or recite it;
nor shall they see or hear this great maṇḍala, mudrā, and samaya of the vidyārāja mantra.
Furthermore, there are sentient beings who,
throughout immeasurable asaṃkhyeya kalpas,
have made offerings to and served all the Tathāgatas of the ten directions— past and present— as well as the profound dharmas of the great maṇḍala, mudrās, and samayas of their families.
Furthermore, by receiving instruction, hearing the teachings, practicing, and accumulating roots of goodness,
one shall attain the full realization of this Great Maṇḍala of the Family of Mantra-kings, including its mudrās and samayas.
By upholding, reciting, and clearly understanding all [the teachings],
and by accomplishing various feats based on the practice of the Vinaya,
one shall become a Great Ācārya.
Among all mantra-practitioners, one shall be the foremost;
one shall become a great Dharma-son within the samaya of the mudrās and maṇḍalas of all Tathāgatas of the three periods of time.
All Tathāgatas of the three periods of time shall bestow upon this person a prophecy of enlightenment (*vyākaraṇa*).
It should be known that such a person attains great firmness, a matured mass of merit, and the provisions of the roots of goodness.
One should know that they have attained the perfection of the cultivation, recitation, and mastery of the mantra, great maṇḍala, mudrā, and samaya of this Vidyārāja.
All the roots of goodness that perfect the merits of enlightenment in all Buddha-fields—
O Vajrapāṇi, Lord of Secrets, Bodhisattva Mahāsattva,
you should further contemplate the power of the samādhi of the vast and great spiritual transformations of that Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara.
The power of the dhāraṇī, the maṇḍala, and the mudrā;
the power of the manifestation of the majesty of the siddhi-samādhi of the mantra of Amoghapāśahṛdayarāja-viśuddhapadma-vidyārāja-Añkuśa.
This is the great supernormal power of the mind of all Tathāgatas;
it fulfills all bodhi-vows and practices.
This is the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara.
This vidyārāja mantra, which is the place where all aspirations are fulfilled,
[is for] those sentient beings in the world who possess defilements, obstacles, and meager merit.
Performing great Buddha-work, they illuminate and shatter all darkness;
acting as great ferries and bridges, they crush the abodes of Māra.
Winds and rains come in their proper seasons, and the crops flourish in abundance.
There shall be no famines, nor calamitous portents from malevolent stars;
it shall cause the lifespan of those who uphold it to be long and far-reaching,
free from disasters, untimely death, or illness, and abundant in wealth and treasures.
If there are sentient beings who constantly purify their bodies and attire,
and with a mind of great compassion,
recite and maintain according to the Dharma the mantra of the Pure Lotus Vidyārāja Aṅkuśa through the yoga of the Dharma-contemplation;
If one practices constantly without interruption or cessation,
one shall immediately accomplish all roots of goodness by abiding in this place of the pure Lotus-Vidyārāja Aṅkuśa mantra.
All the deities of the maṇḍala gathered together at once to protect it;
all the mantra-deities, maṇḍalas, mudrās, and divine palaces of every lineage assembled simultaneously.
One should offer worship with the mantra of the Pure Lotus King Aṅkuśa to all the Tathāgata family, the Avalokiteśvara family,
the Vajra family, the Maṇi family, and so forth.
The mantra-deities, mudrās, palaces,
and deities of the maṇḍala shall all simultaneously come to pay homage, make offerings, and purify [the practitioner]. By means of the mantra of the Vidyārāja Padmaśuddhi-Aṅkuśa,
the reciter of the mantra shall obtain seven auspicious dreams.
First, he dreamed that he entered the assembly hall of the maṇḍala palace and partook of the samaya.
Second, he dreamed that he entered the samaya assembly of the maṇḍala palaces belonging to the families of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
He attained the accomplishment of the mantra, mudrā, and samaya for the conferral of empowerment by all the Tathāgatas.
Third, he dreamed of entering the assembly of the mudrā and samaya of the Empowerment Maṇḍala of All Vajras.
He attained the accomplishment of the samaya of all vajra-kings through the bestowal of the mantras and mudrās for the consecration of all vajras.
Fourth, he dreamed that he entered the assembly of the samaya of the mudrās of the consecration maṇḍala of the entire maṇi family.
He obtained various kingly maṇi jewels and was granted the great empowerment mantra, mudrā, and samaya for the accomplishment of all maṇi jewels.
Fifth, he dreamed that he entered the seven-jeweled palace of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara on Mount Potalaka, the Great Amoghapāśa Vast Liberation Lotus Maṇḍala Mudrā Samaya Assembly.
One beholds all the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, the Great Vidyārāja, all the celestial deities, and the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara,
who take one by the hand and lead one into the consecration mandala.
He was then consecrated.
He received various instructions on the chapters concerning the mantras, maṇḍalas, mudrās, and samayas, and their accomplishments.
In the sixth dream, he saw himself entering the maṇḍala, mudrā, and samaya assembly of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara with a Thousand Hands and Thousand Eyes.
He attained the realization of the Thousand-Handed and Thousand-Eyed Avalokiteśvara,
receiving the empowerment, maṇḍala, mudrā, and samaya of accomplishment.
In his seventh dream, he saw the Tathāgata seated upon the vajra-throne beneath the Bodhi tree.
He turned the Great Dharma Wheel and subdued the armies of Māra.
He beheld Vairocana Tathāgata extending his hand to touch his head,
conferring upon him the empowerment of the Maṇḍala Seal Samaya Chapter.
And they shall behold all the Tathāgatas in all the Buddha-fields of the ten directions,
who bestow upon them the mantras, maṇḍalas, mudrās, and the accomplishments of the mundane and supramundane samayas of their respective lineages.
If, at the time of death, one does not lose mindfulness,
one will go directly to the West to be born by transformation within a lotus flower;
for this reason, one becomes a great mantra-vidyādhara of the Unfailing [Amoghapāśa].
He constantly beholds ninety-nine billion *koṭi-nayuta* hundreds of thousands of Buddhas, the Tathāgatas;
these Buddhas manifest for him all the various Buddha-fields as the single essence of the three bodies (*trikāya*) of all Tathāgatas.
They all possessed the physical marks and signs of the body of Vairocana Buddha.
Having attained the knowledge of past lives,
they were able to know the births and deaths they had undergone throughout hundreds of thousands of great kalpas in the past.
All the samādhi-gates of the empowerment mantras and mudrās of the supernatural powers and majestic virtue of all Tathāgatas appeared before him.
He also beheld the accumulation of merit from his past births, the purity of his roots of goodness, and the perfection of his karmic deeds.
If one merely constantly recites and maintains this mantra of the Vidyārāja day and night without fail,
one will certainly obtain such great merits as these,
as well as the Dharma-gate of being revered by the inclinations and minds of all sentient beings.
Having bathed thoroughly and donned clean garments,
one should purify the interior of the room with incense and flowers as offerings,
and recite the mantra of the Pure Lotus King Aṅkuśa.
It continues without interruption until,
during the final watch of the night, all transgressions— the ten evil deeds, the five heinous crimes, the four grave offenses, and all karmic obstructions— manifest simultaneously before one.
He addressed the one who recites the mantra, saying:
"The retributions for past sins should have caused you to undergo various intense sufferings within the five destinies;
yet, by the power of the mantra, they have been utterly incinerated and extinguished."
All roots of goodness are now perfected.
If one suffers from malaria,
one should empower a white thread with twenty-one knots.
If a patient wears this as an amulet, they will immediately be cured.
In cases of illness caused by ghosts or spirits,
one may empower a sword or empower a peacock feather.
Alternatively, one may empower an arrow by reciting the mantra seventeen times;
by waving it over the patient’s body while maintaining the empowerment, the illness will be cured.
Or, one may empower a five-colored thread with one hundred and eight knots.
Tie it around his neck.
Consecrate agallochum incense and burn it before the patient;
one should then consecrate the patient.
One may become a disease-demon, manifesting one's form to come and explain whatever is asked;
by being employed as a servant, illnesses will be cured.
If one wishes to go to a place of debate and discussion, they will cause those there to rejoice.
Consecrate one's hands seventeen times and rub them upon the face;
those who go to see such a person will be filled with joy and reach a reconciliation.
If one has been affected by poison, [the same applies].
Consecrate cow’s milk and honey together;
or, by consecrating pure water seven times, have [the victim] drink it and the poison will be removed.
If one is stung by a venomous insect:
Consecrate a peacock feather seventeen times and brush [the patient] with it;
likewise, consecrate yellow clay or realgar and apply it thickly and repeatedly.
Alternatively, one may empower cooked beans along with their broth;
by dipping [the afflicted part] into the beans, all [afflictions] shall be eliminated.
This applies even to those who have been subjected to malevolent sorcery, curses, or the poison of *gūḍha* (venomous charms).
For five days, every day fill a new, clean jar with scented water and empower it one hundred and eight times.
When you bathe your body with this, you will immediately be cured.
If the deceased is a child with little physical strength,
one should perform the ritual three times, five times, or seven times; at each performance,
a mandala should be drawn on the bank of a flowing river according to the season.
Take white grains, rice, barley, wheat, large beans, small beans, white mustard seeds, cumin seeds, and *tianshen* (asparagus);
grind them into equal parts and empower water with them.
The paste is like dough; first,
empower fresh butter and smear it thickly over the entire body,
then apply the medicinal paste generously over the whole body.
Having purified and wiped [the object], mold it into the shape of a human figure.
Empower an iron blade with mantras and cut it into eight pieces.
Place clean basins at each of the four corners and four sides of the mandala.
Place a portion of medicine in each basin.
Position a jar of scented water at the center of the altar and place consecrated white mustard seeds inside the jar.
Insert various flower branches and leaves into the mouth of the jar.
Kneeling and facing east, perform one hundred and eight recitations of empowerment over the water jar,
and likewise perform one hundred and eight recitations of empowerment over the medicinal basin.
Divide the medicinal ingredients from the eight basins into small pieces and scatter them,
each into its corresponding direction.
Warm the perfumed water within the altar and give it to the patient.
Having bathed in purity and put on fresh, clean garments,
one should make offerings of various flowers, incense,
food, and drink to the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
Furthermore, when the assembly of monks establishes a great assembly for giving,
the sufferings of the sick shall be immediately relieved and cured,
and no malevolent spirits or ghosts shall be able to cause them harm.
It shall also cause their karmic obstructions to be extinguished.
After the end of their lives, they will be reborn in the pure and wondrous land of the West and realize the wisdom of recollecting past lives;
until they attain enlightenment, they shall never again fall back into the various evil realms.
If one suffers from eye ailments, one should empower licorice juice,
or empower the residual water from offerings seven or ten times;
by using it to wash the eyes, the ailment will be cured.
If one suffers from a headache,
empower fresh ghee, sesame oil, and cumin seeds by reciting the mantra seventeen times;
apply them while slightly warm to the head, and the ailment will be immediately cured.
If one suffers from toothache, empower a pomegranate branch seventeen times;
use it to brush the teeth, and it will quickly bring about recovery.
If one suffers from earache, empower cumin seeds and sesame oil [seventeen times].
Boil [the ingredients] together for twenty to thirty boils,
then filter out the dregs.
Afterwards, when it has become lukewarm, drip it into the ear.
The ailment shall be immediately eliminated.
If one suffers from mouth sores,
empower *bīja* beans and mung beans.
Boil the decoction with ghee and empower it seventeen times.
By holding it in the mouth for a day, one will immediately recover.
This is for those suffering from abdominal pain.
Consecrate *saindhava* salt and take it with warm water; it shall bring about recovery.
Alternatively, consecrate *ūṣara* salt, *añjana*, and *tagara*.
Mix equal parts [of the ingredients] with two *dō* (large sheng) of water;
boil until nine *he* (hectoliters) remain, empower it twenty-one times, and drink it.
All ailments such as abdominal pain, heartache, abdominal tumors, hemorrhoids, and leprosy shall be eliminated and cured.
If one consecrates white mustard seeds twenty-one times and scatters them at the base of all government offices, [the effects will follow].
All subordinates and associates who see this will be filled with joy.
If one empowers white pepper by reciting [the mantra] one hundred and eight times and holds it in the mouth while conversing with others, all who hear it will believe and accept it.
If there are frequent occurrences of fierce winds, hail, or rain, empower a pomegranate branch one hundred and eight times.
Go to a high vantage point and direct it toward the four quarters; immediately all [the disturbances] will be dispersed.
If one constructs a fire altar beside a dragon pool,
using straight-grained timber or *agallochum* wood to kindle the fire,
and offers ghee, honey, curdled milk, and white mustard seeds;
Perform one consecration and one burning for one thousand and eight times.
Continue in this manner until the seven days are complete,
and then the entire world will receive a widespread descent of sweet rain.
If one empowers rice blossoms, white mustard seeds, and ghee,
and burns them one thousand and eight times for seven full days, one shall obtain wealth and treasures.
If one wishes to cause a *ṛddhika* (sorcerer) to develop faith and submit,
one should empower rice husks, salt, and black mustard oil,
and burn them while reciting the person's name one thousand and eight times; then they will obtain their wish.
If one consecrates these burnt husks, salt, and ashes twenty-one times and scatters them at the entrance of a *naṣṭa*,
they will not remain settled there.
If one consecrates white mustard seeds one hundred and eight times and scatters them upon a battlefield where troops are fighting,
the soldiers and the wicked men will both be reconciled.
If one consecrates realgar so that signs of warmth and smoke appear,
and then applies it to the heart and the forehead,
one immediately attains the secret samaya.
No yakṣas or rākṣasas will look upon this person with their eyes.
If one empowers gorocanā until it manifests signs of warmth and smoke,
one should apply it to the forehead and the heart.
He enters all mountains, forests, caves, and marshes without obstruction;
he is venerated and provided with offerings by the people;
and he is invited by kings and high officials.
Apply it to the palms of both hands and empower them seven times;
then go to the gate of a king or high official, knock, and enter.
All the people whom one encounters will be filled with joy, love, and respect, and will offer worship.
Thus, through this vidyārāja mantra,
all dharmas that are practiced shall be accomplished.
Chapter Sixty-Eight: The Chapter on the Accomplishment of the Initiation Mantra. At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara...
He saw this King of Pure Lotus Radiance upon the lotus pedestal emitting great light;
before the Tathāgata, he requested the initiation into the secret heart-dhāraṇī mantra, maṇḍala, mudrā, and samaya of all the Tathāgata families.
One should perform offerings for all Tathāgatas, namely Vairocana Tathāgata and Śākyamuni Tathāgata.
Then, he spoke the mantra of the Jewel Light of Non-empty Contemplation, saying:
Oṃ hūṃ āryāvalokiteśvara vajrapāṇi jvala jvalana bhoṃ svāhā. This is the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara.
Having spoken this mantra and made offerings to the Buddha,
he called to mind the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, praying:
"May you graciously bestow upon me the samaya of the empowerment of the Pure Lotus Vidyārāja."
While reciting this mantra,
the Pure Lotus Vidyārāja bowed his body,
joined his palms, and paid homage with profound respect once again.
Gazing upon the Tathāgata, they did not for a moment turn their eyes away.
At that time, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni extended his right hand and stroked the crown of the head of the Pure Lotus Radiance King.
At that time, throughout the ten directions, in all the trichiliocosm Buddha-worlds,
the great earth, mountains, and forests shook in six ways;
the great oceans and rivers surged and boiled all at once.
He measured all the lands of the ten directions throughout the entirety of space,
including all Tathāgatas of the past, present, and future,
and Vairocana Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha.
At that time, they all appeared together and praised Śākyamuni Tathāgata with one voice, saying:
"Excellent, excellent!
Such an empowerment is truly rare."
We [offer] to all the Tathāgatas of the three periods of time in all the lands of the ten directions,
and to Vairocana Tathāgata.
He likewise conferred upon them the samaya of the empowerment of the Pure Lotus Vidyārāja.
At that time, all Tathāgatas of the three times throughout all buddha-fields in the ten directions— namely, the Tathāgata Vairocana— [bestowed it].
At that time, they all extended their right hands in the gesture of fearlessness and touched the crowns of the heads of the Vidyārāja Pure Lotus,
together reciting the mantra of the Light of the Great Empowerment of Amoghasiddhi, which says:
Oṃ hūṃ āmu-kha-vairocana mahā-mudrā-rāja prathama-jvala parākrama hūṃ. At that time, throughout all the lands of the ten directions...
The Tathāgatas of the three periods of time, including the Tathāgata Vairocana,
spoke this mantra and sprinkled it upon the crown of the King of Illumination.
At that time, he again praised the Tathāgata Śākyamuni:
"How wonderful is the Honored Muni, who has skillfully bestowed the great majestic power of the vidyārāja-mantra and the empowerment dharma of the King of Light!"
At that time, all the Tathāgatas of the three periods throughout all the lands of the ten directions— namely, the Tathāgata Vairocana—
simultaneously spoke this consecration mantra.
And they became the Pure Lotus Vidyārāja;
each was consecrated with the various lineages, all supernatural powers, the great wish-fulfilling jewel, the great empowerment of the secret maṇḍala, and the samaya empowerment.
The empowerment of the Great Wish-Fulfilling Jewel of All Lineages, the secret maṇḍala mudrā-samaya empowerment, and the accomplishment [are bestowed].
At that time, all Tathāgatas of the three times in all lands throughout the ten directions—namely, the Tathāgata Vairocana—[bestowed them].
He addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, the Lord of Secrets, saying:
"This mantra of the light of empowerment is for those who have purified their physical vessel in accordance with the Dharma."
Constantly exerting diligent effort and generating the mind of great compassion,
one should perform the yoga-contemplation of the Buddha and offer various flowers and incense at all appropriate times.
By receiving, upholding, reading, and reciting [this] without interruption for one hundred thousand times,
one shall also achieve this consecration samaya.

First, he dreamed that he entered the Great Secret Maṇḍala of the Mudrā-Samaya Assembly of the Great Wish-Fulfilling Jewel and the Great Empowerment of all Tathāgatas of the three times throughout all the buddha-fields of the ten directions, namely, Vairocana Tathāgata.
We, all the Tathāgatas, shall bestow the empowerment of the Maṇḍala Seal Samaya Chapter.
We, the Tathāgatas, shall simultaneously praise [you] with one voice, saying:
Excellent, excellent, son of good family!
You have attained the gate of the simultaneous opening of all Buddha-fields in the ten directions;
you may travel at will.
In each of those buddha-fields, there were ninety-nine billion *gaṅgā-nadī-vāluka* *koṭi-nayuta-śata-sahasra* Tathāgatas who, mindful of him, bestowed their empowerment.

In his second dream, he saw himself entering the palace assembly of the samaya-mudrā maṇḍala of the great *maṇi-ratna* within the Great Lotus Family of all Tathāgatas of the three times throughout all the buddha-fields of the ten directions.
I, the Tathāgatas, shall bestow upon you the chapter on the Great Maṇi-jewel Empowerment Maṇḍala Seal Samaya of the Great Lotus Family,
and the chapter on the Great Maṇi Seal Empowerment Maṇḍala Seal Samaya of all Tathāgatas shall manifest before you.
All the Tathāgatas spoke with one voice, praising him:
"Excellent, excellent, son of good family!
You have attained the Samaya Chapter of the Seal of the Empowerment Maṇḍala of the Great Lotus Family."
This is the samaya of the Great Maṇi Seal, which is embraced and empowered by all Tathāgatas.

Third, he dreamed that he entered the samaya of the Great Maṇi Jewel Maṇḍala Seal of the Great Vajra Family of all Tathāgatas throughout the three times and in all buddha-fields of the ten directions.
We, the Tathāgatas, have conferred upon you the chapter on the Samaya of the Great Maṇi-ratna Consecration Mandala Seal of the Vajra Family,
as well as the chapter on the Samaya of the Dhāraṇī Mother of the Vajra Family of all Tathāgatas for us.
All the Vajras raised their voices in unison and praised him, saying:
"Excellent, excellent, son of good family!
You have attained the Samaya Chapter of the Great Maṇi-ratna Mandala Seal of the Vajra Family of all Tathāgatas."
One attains the samaya of the Great Maṇi-ratna Vajra-mudrā, which is the empowerment and protection of all Vajras.
Fourth, one dreams of entering the seal-samaya of the Great Consecration Mandala of the Maṇi-ratna Family of all Tathāgatas throughout the three times and all lands in the ten directions.
I, all the Tathāgatas, bestow upon you this chapter on the Samaya of the Great Maṇi Jewel Family’s Great Initiation Maṇḍala Mudrās.
Behold this secret accomplishment samaya of the Great Maṇi Jewel Initiation Maṇḍala Mudrās of all the Tathāgatas of the Great Maṇi Jewel Family.
Then all the Tathāgatas praised him with one voice, saying:
"Excellent, excellent, son of noble family!

You have now received this empowerment ritual, which is the empowerment of the mandala and mudrās of the Great Maṇi Jewel lineage of all the Tathāgatas, and is empowered by the presence of this Secret Heart Chapter."
This is the Chapter on the Samaya of the Secret Heart-Mantra of the Great Wish-Fulfilling Jewel Family of all Tathāgatas.
Fifth: Dreaming of Entering the Secret Maṇḍala of Seals and Samaya of the Non-Retrogressive Great Empowerment of all Tathāgatas of the Three Times in all Buddha-fields of the Ten Directions.
We Tathāgatas bestow upon you the chapter on the secret maṇḍala mudrā samaya for the great empowerment of non-retrogression.
We Tathāgatas, with one voice, proclaim:
Excellent, excellent, son of good family!

You have now obtained this "Chapter on the Samaya of the Secret Mandala Seals" for the Great Empowerment of Non-retrogression of all Tathāgatas throughout the three times in all buddha-fields of the ten directions.
The sixth dream was that we saw all the Tathāgatas of the three periods of time in all the buddha-fields of the ten directions proceeding to the site of enlightenment, sitting upon the vajra-throne,
manifesting equal and perfect awakening, and performing the dharma of the consecration ground for the Great Dharma Kings.
He beheld all the buddha-fields of the ten directions and all the Tathāgatas of the three periods of time seated upon lion thrones,
conferring upon him the dharma of the stage of empowerment as a non-regressing Dharma King of all Tathāgatas.
Then all the Tathāgatas praised him with one voice, saying:
"Excellent, excellent, O steadfast one!
You have now attained the empowerment of the Dharma-kingship of non-retrogression of all Tathāgatas; we shall protect and mind you, so that you may firmly uphold it without ever abandoning it."
Seventh, he dreamed that the Tathāgata Śākyamuni sat beneath the Bodhi tree upon the vajrāsana,
emitting great radiance, turning the Great Wheel of Dharma,
kindling the great torch of the Dharma, and raining down the great rain of the Dharma.
They raise the great Dharma banner and blow the great Dharma conch;
they beat the great Dharma drum and crush the armies of Māra.
Simultaneously, they behold all the buddha-fields of the ten directions and all the Tathāgatas of the three periods of time.
Seated beneath the Bodhi tree upon the Vajra-throne,
he turned the Great Wheel of Dharma and crushed the great armies of Māra.
This is the Chapter on the Samaya of the Mudrās of the Secret Maṇḍala of the Supreme Great Empowerment.
Having attained the Chapter on the Samaya of the Secret Mandala Seals for the Great Empowerment of Turning the Wheel of Dharma conferred by all the Tathāgatas,
at that time all the Tathāgatas praised him with one voice, saying:
Excellent, excellent, son of noble family!
You have obtained the samaya of the seal of the secret maṇḍala for the great empowerment of turning the wheel of Dharma, which is true and firm liberation.
In this manner, one should always diligently and earnestly practice the Buddha-yoga meditation according to the Dharma,
upholding, receiving, reading, and reciting it without ever ceasing or neglecting it.
Then one shall obtain these seven great auspicious dreams,
and realize the dharma of the mantra-emanations of the Great Radiant Seal of all the Tathāgatas of Non-emptiness and the Tathāgata Vairocana of Non-emptiness.
One should enter the Great Maṇḍala Seal Samaya Assembly of the Non-empty Tathāgatas of the Three Times in all lands throughout the ten directions, and of the Non-empty Vairocana Tathāgata.
Entering the gateway of the Samaya of All Places,

one is able to behold the subtle and wondrous form bodies of all the Tathāgatas of the three periods of time throughout all lands in the ten directions— the non-empty Tathāgatas and the non-empty Vairocana Tathāgatas— and reverently make offerings to them.
One should uphold all the names of the Tathāgatas Amogha and Amoghasvabhāva-Vairocana throughout all the lands of the ten directions and all three periods of time;
thereby one shall attain the state of the Tathāgatas Amogha and Amoghasvabhāva-Vairocana throughout all the lands of the ten directions and all three periods of time.
It is the foremost among the chapters on the methods of supernatural power for the Samaya of the Mother Dhāraṇī Seal.
Should there be any past transgressions—whether the ten evil deeds, the five heinous crimes, or the four grave offenses—[this shall purify them].
It will be completely extinguished like a burnt wick.
If there are sentient beings who, wherever they may be, hear this Great Consecration Light Mantra two, three, or seven times,
such that it passes through their faculty of hearing;
One shall immediately attain the eradication of all karmic obstacles;
even if sentient beings have committed the ten evil deeds, the five heinous crimes, and the four grave offenses,
such that they fill this world like fine dust, [they shall be purified].
Upon the dissolution of the body at the end of life, one falls into the various evil realms.
By consecrating earth and sand one hundred and eight times with this mantra and scattering it over the remains of the deceased in a śītavana (cemetery), [one shall deliver them].
Or they scatter [the offerings] upon the tomb or the stupa;
wherever they encounter them, they scatter them all.
As for those who have passed away there—
Whether among the denizens of hell, the hungry ghosts, the asuras, or the animals,
by the power of the empowerment of sand and earth through the mantra of the Great Consecration Light of the True Original Vow of the Tathāgata Sarvākāśa-Vairocana, which is entirely non-empty.
At that moment, they immediately attained radiance and new bodies;
having eliminated all retributions for their sins and cast off their suffering bodies,
they departed for the Land of Ultimate Bliss in the western direction.
Born by transformation within lotus flowers, they shall not fall back again until they attain bodhi.
Furthermore, there are sentient beings who, for years on end and months on end,
are afflicted by the wasting disease of jaundice, suffering from myriad forms of torment.
This illness is the karmic retribution of the patient's past lives.
Therefore, before the patient, recite this mantra aloud for one, two, or three days each day.
If one recites this mantra one thousand and eighty times,
one will obtain the eradication of the obstacles of illness resulting from past karma.
If one is afflicted by ghosts, [the same shall apply].
The spirit and consciousness become distressed and confused, losing their voice and remaining speechless.
The mantra-holder empowers their hand one hundred and eight times and then rubs and strokes the head and face.
Place the hand upon the heart and the forehead;
by performing the empowerment one thousand and eighty times,
one will attain recovery.
If the deity Mahākāla should cause illness or affliction,
he is likewise able to cure and dispel it;
as are the ailments caused by various ghosts, spirits, and malevolent demons.
Consecrate a cord of five-colored threads with one hundred and eight knots;
when tied around the waist, arms, or neck of the patient,
they will be cured.
If one has various types of malarial fevers,
empower a white cord with one hundred and eight knots and tie it around the head and neck.
Furthermore, by performing an empowerment (adhiṣṭhāna) upon clothing,
one will cause the illness to be immediately cured.
If one empowers stone chrysanthemum (śi-chang-pu) one hundred and eighty times, [the same result follows].
If one holds it while conversing with another,
one will surpass and subdue them.
If one uses black pepper and tagara incense...
Take *aguru*, *śiṃśapā*, *khadira*,
and *rocanā* (which in the Tang language means "the juice of small *khadira*"), and other such ingredients, and prepare medicinal pills the size of jujubes.
Recite the mantra over them one hundred thousand times, then dry them in the shade.
If one suffers from any kind of demonic illness, spirit possession,
various types of malaria, poisoning, or loss of voice,
one should always grind the medicine with water.
Perform the empowerment one hundred and eight times.
Dot [the mantra] on both eyes, the forehead, and the heart.
If one performs the empowerment while manifesting wrath, the affliction will be immediately eliminated.
If the spirits who cause illness do not relinquish [the victim],
their heads shall immediately split open like the branches of an *ari* tree.
As for those stung by various venomous insects, snakes, or scorpions:
By applying the medicine as an ointment or ingesting it, one will immediately be cured.
Furthermore, there is another method: using *taṇḍula* of new rice, one should bathe for purification and put on clean garments.
Grind the medicine with water and empower it one hundred and eight times.
Apply it to the eyes of the *mīḍha* (infant).
Then, manifesting wrath, empower it one thousand and eighty times.
Then he will immediately rise from his seat and answer all that is asked.
If one wishes to release him,
one should empower white mustard seeds and water twenty-one times.
If one scatters rice upon the *daṇḍara*, it will immediately become as it was before.
If one is invited by a person of high status,
one should apply the medicine to the eyes and go to see them.
Then they honored and respected one another. *Amoghapāśakalparāja-sūtra*,
Scroll Twenty-Eight (also titled *Amoghapāśakalparāja-sūtra*, Scroll Twenty).
Translated during the Great Tang Dynasty by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci.
Chapter Sixty-nine: The Consecration Maṇḍala. At that time, the King of Pure Lotus Radiance...
Having received the consecration from all the Tathāgatas,
he circumambulated the Buddha three times and then stood to one side before the Buddha with palms joined in reverence.
He bowed his head once more and reflected:
"Why does the Tathāgata not bestow upon me the samaya of the mudrās of the maṇḍala of the vajra family of all Buddhas?
At that time, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, knowing the thoughts in his mind, [responded].
Then he spoke the mantra for the empowerment of Amoghasiddhi, saying:
Oṃ hūṃ āḥ mukuṭamaṇḍala pradhāna-viśeṣa-maṇiratna sarvatathāgataviśeṣaka hūṃ. At that time, when the Tathāgata had uttered this mantra,
By means of great supernormal power, the great earth of the Buddha-worlds throughout the ten directions— the three thousandfold world-systems—
was simultaneously transformed into a vajra-maṇḍala ground,
square and circular, with brilliant radiance and successive layers of boundary markers.
The families of all Tathāgatas— the Lotus family, the Vajra family, and the Maṇi family— along with all the vast maṇḍalas of liberation, mudrās, samayas, and assemblies,

appeared simultaneously in their various forms. Furthermore, there manifested the individual bodies of all the devas according to their respective sizes, as well as the diverse physical characteristics, mantras, maṇḍalas, mudrās, samayas, and all manner of divine transformations resulting from the power of their roots of goodness.
He also manifested the inconceivable various supernatural transformations of the Samaya of the entire family of the Heart-King Amoghapāśa,
and simultaneously bestowed them all upon the Pure Lotus Vidyārāja.
All of this was fully manifested within the samaya of the mudrās of the Great Maṇḍala.
At that time, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, the Lord of Secrets, saying:
Now, if one applies oneself diligently to this mantra,
constantly giving rise to immeasurable great compassion and the yoga-visualization of the Buddha.

Whoever recites and maintains this Vajra Empowerment Mantra ten million times according to the Dharma shall enter the Great Lotus Empowerment Maṇḍala Assembly of all Tathāgatas of the three periods of time in all lands throughout the ten directions.
One should enter the great maṇi-jewel lotus empowerment maṇḍala assembly of all Tathāgatas of the three times in all lands of the ten directions.
[Therein dwell] all Tathāgatas of the three times in all lands of the ten directions.
Within that dream,

he manifested various miraculous transformations of the Great Maṇḍala Palace of the Sublime Form Body, as well as the miraculous manifestations of the maṇḍalas of all the devas of the Heaven of the Thirty-three and the Vidyārājas.
Furthermore, one dreams of the great maṇḍalas of the family of all Tathāgatas, the great maṇḍala of the Lotus family,
the great maṇḍala of the Vajra family, and the great maṇḍala of the Maṇi family.
The Samaya of the Mudrās of the Vast Liberation Lotus Maṇḍala of the Heart-King Amoghapāśa;
the Samaya of the Mudrās of the Maṇḍala of the Treasury Born of the Great Compassion of the Dharmakāya of the Tathāgata Vairocana.
The various classes of attendants, mandalas, mudrās, samayas, and all miraculous transformations;
furthermore, he dreams of all the bodhisattvas’ practices, vows, and transformative activities throughout their stages of the causal ground.
Until awakening, he turns the great wheel of Dharma and crushes all demonic armies.
Furthermore, he dreams of the great consecration maṇḍala assemblies of all Tathāgatas throughout the lands of the ten directions and across the three periods of time.
Having received from all the Tathāgatas the samaya of the maṇḍala for the supreme great empowerment of all,
the practitioner of mantras experiences a doubling of joy in body and mind within dreams, as well as an increase in vigor and courage.
When this Samādhi of the Empowerment of the Seal of the Lotus Maṇḍala of the Great Liberation, the King of Mantras of the Amoghapāśa, was attained,
all the Tathāgatas simultaneously uttered these words of praise:
Excellent, excellent, O mantra-practitioner!
You have now received from me the great empowerment samaya of the use of all Tathāgatas throughout the ten directions and the three times, across all buddha-fields.
One attains entry into the secret maṇḍala assembly of the great empowerment of all Tathāgatas throughout the three times and all lands in the ten directions,
becoming a great Dharma prince to all Tathāgatas.
The light of all dharmas simultaneously illuminates;
one suddenly awakens and attains great merit,
becoming foremost among all devas and humans as they praise one in various ways.
If sons or daughters of good family who seek a great mass of merit and the maturation of their roots of goodness,
should daily offer flower garlands, head-ornaments, or various exquisite and beautiful robes and monastic garments.
Perform the empowerment one thousand and eight times.
Thread it onto the Buddha and place it upon the head of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva,
performing a great offering through the power of the mantra.
Then, may all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the three periods of time in all lands throughout the ten directions each wear a celestial crown of the seven jewels and robes of the kāṣāya.
Those various flower crowns, monastic robes,
and garments each emitted immeasurable hundreds of thousands of rays of light,
which successively made offerings to all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Mahāsattvas throughout the lands of the ten directions and across the three periods of time.
All were adorned with radiance as they made this offering,
presenting various rare treasures and foods of a hundred flavors.
One should make offerings to all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, and all celestial deities throughout the lands of the ten directions and across the three periods of time;
one should also make offerings to all the great consecrated maṇḍala assemblies.
Furthermore, one attains the dissolution of all karmic obstacles of body, speech, and mind;
one achieves a great mass of merit and the perfection of roots of goodness;
and wherever one goes, there is always no obstruction.
The words spoken by one who is thus honored will be like the fragrance of sandalwood, which all people love and revere.
If one constantly applies oneself with diligence to reciting and upholding the mantra, never allowing for interruption or neglect.
One's breath will be fragrant and pure like the scent of the *utpala* flower;
all aspirations shall be fulfilled, one’s life shall not be cut short prematurely, and one shall be free from all afflictions and diseases.
One shall subdue and conquer all *vināyakas*.
Yakṣas and rākṣasas will have faith and turn toward it, providing protection and support.
Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, the Vidyārāja, will observe and guard it.
One shall become a master (ācārya) capable of performing all great maṇḍalas.
Furthermore, one attains the accomplishment of the Samaya of the Unfailing Supreme Mandala.
Chapter Seventy: The Mantra for the Offering of the Unfailing Jewel (Amoghamani). At that time, the Pure Lotus Radiance King (Viśuddhapadma-prabhā-rāja)...
Having been granted these seals of the great samaya of the vast and great supernatural powers of all the great maṇḍalas,
they joined their palms in reverence, circumambulated the Buddha three times,
prostrated at his feet, and returned to their original seats.
With palms joined in reverence, he gazed up at Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva Mahāsattva and thought:

At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara beheld this vast and great supernormal power,
the miraculous manifestation of the seal-samaya of the universal great maṇḍala, and its majestic virtue.
Appearing simultaneously throughout the lands of the ten directions,
having bestowed the Pure Lotus Vidyārāja,
he then spoke this mantra for the Amogha-maṇi offering:
Oṃ hūṃ āḥ mukuṭa-bhūṣita-maṇi padma-abja-śrī tathāgata milokite sāmba-prabha-svara hūṃ. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara...
When this mantra was recited,
immeasurable, boundless,
and manifold supernatural powers and vast majesty simultaneously manifested in the void.
All the articles of offering for all the devas;
the Samaya of the majestic array of the miraculous transformations of the Great Maṇḍala of the Mantra-Vidyārājas and the various extensive great supernatural powers of the Sarvatathāgata-Amogha.

Equal in extent to all Buddha-fields of the ten directions,

and *puṇḍarīka* flowers, as well as palaces,
towers, and various kinds of terraces and pavilions.

as well as palaces, towers, and various pavilions.
A sea-cloud of flower crowns, necklaces,
and all manner of ornaments rained down unspeakable numbers of *sāla* jewel-flowers and *campaka* jewel-flowers.
Atimuktaka jewel-flowers, udumbara jewel-flowers,
and sumana jewel-flowers; palaces,
towers, and various terraces and pavilions.
A sea of clouds of flower crowns, necklaces, and all manner of ornaments rained down unspeakable numbers of every kind of flower from the waters, lands, mountains, and forests,
as well as various palaces, towers, pavilions, and terraces.
An ocean-cloud of flower crowns, necklaces, and all manner of ornaments;
raining down unspeakable oceans of clouds of various precious decorations, garments, and forms from all lands.

various crowns, necklaces, hairpins, earrings, bracelets, and bangles—

ocean-clouds of various palaces, towers, terraces, and pavilions.

All the various unguents and powdered incenses of the devas,
as well as immeasurable billions of kinds of clouds of oceans of incense,
rained down as unspeakable clouds of oceans of precious banners, streamers, canopies, pearl nets, and clusters of various jeweled bells.

Oceans of clouds of *atimuktaka* oil-lamp trees, aloeswood oil-lamp trees,
white sandalwood oil-lamp trees,

They rain down unspeakable oceans of clouds of ambrosia and food of a hundred flavors for all the devas;

A vast offering to all Buddhas, the assembly of all Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas,

Manifesting through empowerment,

We awaken all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Mahāsattvas throughout the ten directions.
He comforted all the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the ten directions,

Those who do not practice the holy life dwell together with those who practice the holy life;

To those who are not at peace, he provides equal peace;
to those who do not practice the True Dharma, he provides the practice of the True Dharma;
to those who lack tranquility, he provides the attainment of tranquility.
He gave treasures to the poor,
clothing to the naked,
and food to the hungry.
To those who thirst, give drink;
to those who have lost their way, give the path; to those with short lives, grant them a full lifespan;
and to those whose eyes are not yet pure, grant them the purity of vision.
To those who are deaf, he grants hearing;
to those afflicted by distress, he grants the removal of distress;
to those who have lost mindfulness, he grants right mindfulness.
To those who delight in unwholesome dharmas, he gives wholesome dharmas;
to those who do not practice generosity, he gives the attainment of generosity;
to those who do not practice pure ethical discipline, he gives the attainment of pure ethical discipline.
Not cultivating patience and yet attaining patience;
not cultivating diligence and yet attaining diligence;
not cultivating meditative concentration and yet attaining meditative concentration.
Not practicing prajñā and attaining prajñā;
not having been granted the samaya and having been granted the samaya;
not having been granted the mudrā and having been granted the mudrā.
Those who have not yet attained the mantras and vidyās shall attain them;
those dwelling on wrong paths shall dwell on the right path;
and those lacking the roots of merit for awakening shall possess them.
Those who have not yet crossed the great ocean of birth and death and those who have crossed it;
those who dwell in the obscuration of darkness and those who have shattered that obscuration;
those bound by the fetters of defilements and obscurations and those who have liberated themselves from them.
There are those with immediate karma and those who have destroyed immediate karma;
those who have not yet attained nirvana and those who have attained great nirvana;
those who have not yet received a prediction of enlightenment and those who have received such a prediction.

those with leprosy shall be cleansed, and the sick shall be healed;
those who are not pliant shall become pliant.
To those whose clans have not yet assembled, he provides equal assembly;
to those without light, he provides equal light;
and to those who have lost their royal status, he provides equal royal status.
To those who harbor resentment, he causes them to give rise to a mind of loving-kindness;
to those with excessive lust, he provides the means to eliminate lust;
to those with excessive anger, he provides the means to eliminate anger.
Being despised by others versus receiving respect;
not encountering Buddhas and Bodhisattvas versus encountering Buddhas and Bodhisattvas;
and not hearing the True Dharma versus hearing the True Dharma.
Those who do not delight in receiving honor and offerings come to receive honor and offerings;
those who lack the six sense faculties come to possess the six sense faculties;

Bodhisattvas, and Mahāsattvas, as well as the various families of maṇḍalas and samaya assemblies, throughout all the buddha-fields of the ten directions.

Chapter Seventy-one: The Ritual for Invoking Rain. Again, he addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, the Lord of Secrets, saying:
When there is a drought,
the mantra-holder should bathe cleanly, put on pure garments,
remain in quiet silence, and generate a heart of great compassion toward all sentient beings.
Before a śarīra-stūpa, or within a Buddha-hall,
or atop a high tower, or upon a lofty mountain,
or in a great forest, or within a garden grove.
Whether by the side of a lotus pond, or by the edge of a dragon pool,
or within a royal palace, or in a celestial temple,
or in a shrine to the gods— one should select an excellent location.
Construct a mandala measuring four cubits.
Adorn the surface of the mandala by smearing it with a paste of cow dung and yellow earth;
further adorn the surface of the mandala by smearing it with white sandalwood incense paste.
Demarcate the boundaries of the enclosure and open wide the four gates;
paint the ocean waters all around.
In the center of the inner court, empower yellow sandalwood paste.
Paint the figure of the Great Dragon King resembling a celestial deity;
his countenance is serene and joyful,
and he faces west.
He sits in the full lotus posture according to the Dharma;
with one hand he holds a precious jewel-palms, and with the other he makes the seal of the dragon-rope.
From the head of this deity emerge nine dragon heads.
On the four sides and four corners, depict various small nāgas as attendants;
their heads all face inward, gazing upon and supporting the Nāgarāja.
On the four corners of the outer enclosure, draw the mudrā of Amoghapāśa.
On all four sides, various mudrās should be depicted surrounding a blaze of fire;
these should all be drawn according to the ritual rules upon lotus pedestals.
One should provide various foods and drinks, including milk, curd, ghee, honey, rice-gruel, and stone-honey syrup.
Various kinds of flowers and incense were arranged as offerings.
At the four outer corners, jars of fragrant water were placed,
with branches and leaves of various flowers inserted into their mouths.
At the four gates, burn this dragon incense in the incense burners as an offering to all.
Perform the rites for protection and invocation at the four gates.
At each session, first recite the Mother Dhāraṇī mantra and the Secret Heart mantra seven times;
next, the mantra of Caṇḍamahāroṣaṇa;
and next, the mantra of the Great Vidyārāja Aṅkuśa.
Next, recite the mantra of the Greatly Terrifying Vidyārāja Aṅkuśa three times,
followed by the mantra of the Pure Lotus Vidyārāja Aṅkuśa three times.
Recite the Maṇi-offering mantra one thousand and eight times to summon the dragon kings along with their retinues.
Empower the ritual implements to cause sweet rain to fall, and then speak this verse:
One hundred and eight *liang* each of *nāga-puṣpa* and *āgasti-agarū*;
three *liang* each of *tagara* and the root of *kuśa* grass;
four *liang* of the finest white *candana*; and two *liang* of white mustard seeds.
Empower the incense with the mantra one hundred and eight times; grind and refine the stone honey and blend it together.
Place the vessel upon the navel of the Nāga King and burn this incense as an offering.
After each recitation of the offering mantra, invoke the name of the Nāga King Sāgara.
Some call him by the name of the Nanda Dragon King; some call him by the name of the Utpalagandha Dragon King;
some call him by the name of the Vāsuki Dragon King; some call him by the name of the Takṣaka Dragon King;
some call him by the name of the Kalmāṣapāda Dragon King; or some call him by the name of the Varuṇa Dragon King.
Or the name of the Nāga King Manasvin, the Nāga King Elāpattra, Saṃmardakāra, and the Nāga King Candra—
these names of the various nāgas are what the mantra practitioner should first recite.
He spoke aloud, saying: "For the sake of the sentient beings within the realm of Jambudvīpa, I now universally entreat you to send down a great rain of sweet nectar.
May all the Dragon Kings, together with their retinues, descend upon Jambudvīpa and let fall a great rain of sweet nectar.
At each session, he burned incense and made this request according to the ritual.
Grasp white mustard seeds.
Recite the mantra once over each seed while calling the name of the Dragon King, and strike the Dragon King’s heart with one.
If you strike him for one day, it will rain on the second day.
If it thunders for two days, it will rain on the third day;
if it thunders for three days, it will rain for seven days.
For three or seven days, a great sweet rain will certainly fall over an area extending a thousand yojanas in circumference.
Furthermore, upon a white cotton cloth or silk,
one should paint the blue-bodied Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, one cubit in length and breadth,
with a wrathful facial expression and four arms.
On his head he wears a jeweled crown, upon which resides an emanation Buddha.
One hand holds a curved battle-axe, one hand grasps a trident,
one hand holds a lasso, and one hand holds a lotus flower.
He was adorned with various garments, precious pearls,
necklaces, earrings, bracelets, and armlets;
his body was surrounded by a halo of blazing light as he sat cross-legged upon a precious lotus throne.
Below the lotus, paint a large pool of water.
Within the water, paint lotuses of various colors.
On both sides of the Bodhisattva, paint great nāga kings.
The figures resemble devas, kneeling with palms joined in reverence and gazing up at the Bodhisattva.
Each has nine dragon heads upon its head.
The image is placed within the altar, facing west.
Every day, perform the visualization of the yoga of the *sādhya-dharma*.
Recite the mantra over white mustard seeds one by one and strike the various dragon kings approximately one thousand and eight times each.
Whether for three days or seven days,
even if there has been a drought for a thousand years, one who performs this rite shall command the Dragon King to surely send down heavy rain.
If calamities such as fierce winds, hail, and excessive rain arise repeatedly, [this rite shall likewise be applied].
On the summit of a high mountain or atop a multi-storied pavilion,
place the image facing the direction from which one has set out.
Before the image, recite the Maṇi-pūjā-mantra one thousand and eight times.
Even if one dispatches fierce winds, hail, rain, great mountains, or the ocean below,
[the rite succeeds]. Furthermore, according to the ritual method, one constructs a four-cubit altar at a dragon pool or stream,
coats it with mud as prescribed, and places the image within the altar.
Before the image, empower seven *modaka* (joy-balls) one thousand and eight times,
then cast them into the pool while reciting the name of the Dragon King as before.
If one recites the mantra one thousand and eight times,
the Dragon King will manifest as a youth; his upper body will appear,
and he will join his palms in homage before the image.
The mantra-reciter asked, "What are you doing now?
The mantra-reciter replied, "Nāga, you should survey this Jambudvīpa.
Thereupon, he surveyed it everywhere.
When the youth observed the time, he replied once more, saying,
"Tell me all the auspicious and inauspicious matters of the world.
He spoke again, saying:
For my sake, let a great rain of sweet nectar fall throughout the entire continent of Jambudvīpa,
so that all the crops may be thoroughly nourished and all sentient beings may attain great peace and happiness.
At that time, the youth said to the mantra-practitioner,

At that time, the youth turned toward the mantra-practitioner,
joined his palms and gazed upon him,
speaking again: "Listen attentively, listen attentively!"
I shall now explain for you the supreme medicine of ambrosia:
the Dharma of the twelve links of dependent origination, the Dharma of the four noble truths,
the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and the Dharma of the eightfold noble path.
Regarding the Dharma of the *Ṣaṭpāramitā-dharmāśūnyapaśavārāsa-vikurvaṇa-mantra-sūtra*:
at the time of preaching this Dharma, great clouds and mist arose from the body of the youth,
pervading Jambudvīpa and bringing down a widespread, sweet rain.
It rained only upon the pool and not below it.
The youth joyfully made offerings to the image.
The youth then spoke again to the mantra-practitioner.
"Enter my palace; for my palace is the palace of the mantra-practitioner.
Then the mantra-practitioner said to her, "You shall receive from me the ten precepts of the Buddha."
I shall then enter your palace. If you,
young man, receive the ten precepts of good conduct,
this body will transform back into its original form as a dragon.
He adorns his body with various necklaces and crowns made of the seven precious gems;
if he is unwilling to accept [the offering], he immediately sinks into the water and does not appear again.
If one wishes to see the Great Dragon King:
On a leaf of red copper, one should engrave the mantra for the offering of the maṇi according to the ritual rules using golden letters; then,
empower white honey by reciting it one hundred and eight times.
Thickly smear [the mantra] over the characters.
Empower white mustard seeds one hundred and eight times and scatter them over the honey.
Again, empower it one thousand and eight times.
Cast the *karpūra* incense into the eyes of the pool and,
while making offerings, recite the mantra according to the ritual rules.
When this incense is burned, the Naga King Sāgara will manifest in the form of a pure-conduct Brahmin.
Standing on the bank of the pool,
he bowed respectfully and asked the mantra-practitioner, "Have you attained peace and security?
The mantra-practitioner replied.
Now, by upholding this mantra of the Heart-King Dhāraṇī of Amoghapāśa and its miraculous verses, one’s body shall be exceedingly peaceful and happy, long-lived, and free from illness.
He spoke again, saying: "O Naga, listen now with close attention."
"The Dragon shall protect and uphold all the Buddha-dharma so that it remains eternally in the world.
At that time, the Brahmin was greatly rejoiced.
Then, the mantra-practitioner...
He spoke the names of the seven Buddhas, the eight great Bodhisattvas,
and the four great Śrāvakas.
When the Brahmin heard these names, he was moved.
With redoubled joy, they praised the mantra-reciter:
"Excellent, excellent! These names of the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Śrāvakas which you have now spoken are most auspicious and are well-expounded."
These names and so forth are difficult to encounter and difficult to hear;
they meet with the practitioner of mantras only most rarely.
To have seen and heard this *Amoghapāśahṛdayarāja-dhāraṇī-mantra*, these miraculous words and phrases, is [a rare occurrence].
Furthermore, it is the most difficult among difficulties.
What is now being received and upheld is likewise extremely difficult;
to explain it to others is yet again the most difficult of all.
When the brahmin had finished speaking these words,
he transformed his appearance and manifested the body of the nāga king Sāgara,
asking the mantra-practitioner, "What boon do you now seek?"
"Please explain to me the fulfillment of the signs.
At that time, the practitioner then clearly set forth the aspirations of his mind.
Upon hearing this, the dragon was satisfied;
he caused all the nāga kings and their attendants to pay respectful homage and carry out his commands.
These practitioners, training according to the Dharma with diligence,
should not harbor doubts or suspicions regarding the teachings I have spoken;
they should practice without slackening day and night.
By upholding, reciting, and chanting this true dharma, one attains great accomplishment. Furthermore,
there is a method wherein one places an image upon the tip of a staff,
and while holding it with reverence, chants the mantra.
When traveling through gardens, groves, fields, or wilderness,
he performs rites such that wherever he goes, all calamities, obstacles, locusts, venomous insects, wild beasts, and other hardships are eliminated;

Chapter Seventy-Two: The Chapter on the Accomplishment of the Vidyārāja Pure Lotus. Again, he addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, the Lord of Secrets, saying:
Furthermore, upon white cotton cloth or silk,
according to its size— whether square or circular—

On the first day of the bright fortnight of the first month.

The samādhi of the Lord of Dhāraṇīs;

The torch samādhi, the samādhi endowed with full radiance,
