and the two little fingers are each extended side by side and placed upon the backs of the wrists.
Place the mudrā at the heart; the mantra is:
Oṃ hūṃ āḥ mukha-akuśala-jvala hūṃ. As for the formation of this mudrā:
One should then bind the mudrās of all the hundred thousand koṭis of the Tathāgata family,
the mudrās of all the Padma family,
and the mudrās of all the Vajra family.
The seals of all the great maṇi families and so forth—
each consisting of hundreds of thousands of koṭis of seals—
these seals are the gateway to the mass of merit accumulated from all wish-fulfilling jewels.
Because it fulfills all the aspirations of the mantra-practitioner,
this mudrā is also the gateway to the assembly of the most supreme secret heart-dharma of all Tathāgatas of the ten directions and the three periods of time.
It is also the secret seal of all families and the samaya of all seals;
it is also the non-empty heart-seal of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara,
which never passes through any dharma-gate in vain.
If one constantly binds this mudrā,
all siddhis will be swiftly accomplished.
For the mudrā of the wrathful Aṅkuśa, follow the previous mudrā but modify it by changing the two index fingers.
Extend the backs of both hands;
insert each of the two thumbs into the palms and bend them crosswise like hooks.
Bend the middle fingers of both hands toward the palms like hooks.
Place the mudrā at the heart; the mantra is: Oṃ amogha-kuru-dṛṣṭi hūṃ. When forming this mudrā:
With furrowed brows and angry eyes,
one should utter the sound "HŪṂ" three or five times in a wrathful voice;
this constitutes the binding of the Wrathful Family Seal of all the Tathāgatas, numbering in the hundreds of thousands of koṭis.
The wrathful mudrā of the Lotus family;
the wrathful mudrā of the Vajra family;
the wrathful mudrā of the Great Maṇi family.
It utterly destroys all yakṣas, rākṣasas, asura kings, vināyakas, and Yama kings,
causing all gods and ghosts to scatter and flee in every direction.
This mudrā is the foremost among all mudrās;
it can destroy hundreds of thousands of Mount Sumerus and dry up hundreds of thousands of oceans until they are parched.
It can subdue all evil devas, nāgas, spirits, ghosts, and wicked people,
who will then rejoice and pay respectful homage;
it also causes all maṇḍalas, mudrās, and samayas to be fully accomplished.
For the mudrā of the Vidyārāja mantra, follow the previous mudrā but bend the two index fingers like hooks;
bend the joints of the two middle fingers;
and bend the tips of the two thumbs and the two ring fingers so they are level and pressed against one another.
Extend both little fingers straight upward.
Place the mudrā at the heart and recite the mantra:
Oṃ [as above] Bhiḥ-ṭiṅ-ja-ra-ja-pa-thu-mi-jva-la-hūṃ. This mudrā is the samaya-seal that universally unites all Tathāgata families.
Regarding the mudrās of all Tathāgata families, Padma families, and Vajra families.
The Maṇi-kula mudrā is the foremost of all;
it is also the preeminent leader among the mudrās of the Vimala-padma-vijaya-rāja maṇḍala.
Regarding the binding of these mudrās:
one should bind hundreds of thousands of koṭis of mudrās belonging to such families to eliminate all karmic obstructions.
One shall receive from all Tathāgatas the prophecy of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
One shall plant hundreds of thousands of accumulations of merit and roots of goodness.
All Tathāgatas shall mindfully observe and praise one.
All Bodhisattvas joyfully grant their vows,
and all devas constantly provide protection.
For the Maṇi-abhiṣeka-mudrā, extend the right hand upward toward the heart.
Bend the head [of the index finger] to point toward the palm;
the middle finger is slightly bent,
with a distance of one cun between it and the head [of the index finger].
The thumb is held askew;
the ring finger is extended upward and bent so that its tip aligns with the first joint-mark of the thumb.
The distance between them is about one and a half inches.
Bend the tip of the little finger toward the palm so that it passes about one inch beyond the tip of the ring finger.
Cover the left hand and bend the tip of the ring finger so that it touches the tip of the right middle finger;
extend the left middle finger straight and slightly askew.
At a distance of approximately two and a half inches from the tip of the right thumb,
[place the tips of] the left thumb, index finger, and little finger.
The mantra for the mudrā of Dispelling All Evil is as follows:
Oṃ (as above) mi-mi-ta ā-mogha-vidyā-maṇi pā-ra-vāriṣaya hūṃ. This mudrā should be formed every time during the ritual cycle.
Recite the Maṇi-offering mantra twenty-one times.

With each recitation, visualize placing [the offering] within all the Buddha-lands and all the assemblies of Buddhas throughout the ten directions and the three periods of time, as numerous as all atoms.
There shall rain down upon them oceans of clouds of various celestial unguents, powdered incenses, and burning incenses;
oceans of clouds of various celestial garments;
and oceans of clouds of various celestial crowns, necklaces, hairpins, earrings, rings, and bracelets.
Ocean-clouds of various kinds of celestial ambrosial food and drink and all manner of fruits;
ocean-clouds of various kinds of celestial palaces made of the seven treasures;
and ocean-clouds of various kinds of celestial jeweled banners, pennants, and canopies.

Various clouds of oceans of celestial flowers, fruits, and trees made of diverse precious jewels from all the devas make offerings to all Buddhas and the assembly of Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas in all Buddha-lands as numerous as atoms throughout the ten directions and the three periods of time.
By the power of the mudrās and mantras,
throughout the Buddha-assemblies in all the Buddha-fields as numerous as atoms in the ten directions and the three periods of time,
there fell such oceans of clouds of various offerings.
Making extensive offerings, this is the most supreme.
Therefore, the mantra practitioner should always form this mudrā when reciting the Maṇi-offering mantra.
May they swiftly bring the six pāramitās to full perfection.

May they constantly cause various wish-fulfilling jewel trees to rain down within all the assemblies of Buddhas in the Buddha-fields as numerous as atoms throughout the ten directions and the three periods of time.
It produces all manner of jewels and makes offerings to all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and the assembly of Mahāsattvas through the power of mantras and mudrās.
Then one obtains immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of clouds of oceans of accumulations of the seven treasures,

as numerous as the Sumeru Kings of the three-thousandfold great thousandfold world-systems within the Buddha-fields as many as the atoms of the Buddhas of the ten directions and the three periods of time.
He made vast offerings of heaps of the seven precious gems to all the Buddhas and the assembly of Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas;
through these various offerings, he generated a supreme mass of merit and a field of virtue.

All such various and vast offerings are due to the power of the Samaya-mantra and the Seal of Offerings, sustained by the inconceivable and immeasurable supernormal powers of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.
The mudrā for accomplishing vows is modeled after the fourth mudrā mentioned previously;
however, change the left ring finger so that it extends straight,
and bend the left index finger to join with the right middle finger.
The thumbs are joined together;
the remaining four fingers are extended and spread as before.
The mantra for this mudrā is:
Oṃ ā-mukā-sarvatatvārā-śrādaya hūṃ. [This is used for summoning, establishing the boundary, receiving the dharma, and conferring empowerment.]
Burn incense, apply ointments, and scatter flowers upon the ritual platform;
offer food and drink, perform ablutions and wash the hands,
cleanse the face and rinse the mouth, and put on or take off one's garments.
When binding the hair into a topknot to protect oneself and others;
when sitting, practicing the Way, preparing fire, or offering food;
and when requesting other sections of mantras.
At all times and in all places when dissolving the boundary,
one should bind this seal for all activities; thus,
they will be swiftly accomplished.
Within all phenomena, one attains the accomplishment of the dharma of non-empty merit;
furthermore, one attains the samaya of the seal of all lineages, which is the non-empty fruition of the gathered assembly.
These five seals have not been taught previously;
they are now being taught.
Each one is capable of truly manifesting various supernatural powers and immeasurable merits.
If there are those who see or hear these five mudrās,
they too shall obtain all non-empty merits.
Furthermore, these five mudrās are the locus where all accumulated merits are made non-empty.
It is also the non-void place where immeasurable afflictions are destroyed;
it is also the non-void place where all Buddha-fields of the ten directions and the three periods of time are manifested;
it is also the non-void place where karma is transformed.
It is also the locus of the true great compassionate mind of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva;
it is also the locus where all sentient beings attain peace and happiness;
and it is also the locus where practitioners of mantras achieve accomplishment.
It is also the place where all calamities and faults are extinguished;
it is also the most supreme place of liberation;
it is also the immeasurable place of great nirvana.
This is also the place for accomplishing the various true dharmas that are not in vain.
Therefore, the mantra practitioner should bind these five mudrās during the six periods of day and night.
The Dharma Gate for Manifesting the Swift Attainment of Such a Supreme Accumulation of Merit.

Chapter Seventy-Seven: The Secret Rituals and Mantras. Chapter Seventy-Seven: The Secret Rituals and Mantras. Furthermore, the World-Honored One possesses mantras of majestic deportment that accomplish all matters.
Protecting all, one enters all places and attains great peace and happiness.
The mantra for binding the boundary is: Oṃ amogha-maṇḍale hūṃ. (The first *oṃ* is as above; the second is pronounced with a long *ā*; the third is *hūṃ*.)
The Mantra for Purifying the Ground: Oṃ samantamukhe vili hūṃ phaṭ.
The Mantra for Sweeping and Preparing the Altar: Oṃ āgaccha puruṣottama hūṃ jaḥ.
The Mantra of Māyājāla: Oṃ (as above) bṛttivī rāja-saṃkṣepa hūṃ. The Mantra for Purifying Water: Oṃ āmukhara-prasaravāni.
3. *Hūṃ* 4. The mantra for sprinkling water: *Oṃ āmukha-mūrdhni vaśī svāhā*. 3.
The mantra for purifying the cord and the boundary: *Oṃ āmukha-mi-pu-ṣkara-paṅkaja-hūṃ*. 4. *Hūṃ*.
The Mantra for Purifying Colors: Oṃ jñānaraśme hūṃ. The Mantra for Purifying Bath Water: Oṃ jvalāmīṃ āmukha-sudhite hūṃ.
The Mantra for Washing Hands, Face, and Mouth: [Omitted in source].
The mantra for calling out is as follows: Oṃ bhuje re āmukha-buddha hūṃ.
The mantra for taking up and putting on the robes is: Oṃ āmukhāvasitthire cīvara-prāvāraṇāya hūṃ.
The mantra for arranging the hair and topknot is: Oṃ ā... (as above).
The *mudrā* for protecting the body: Oṃ amogha hūṃ. The *mantra* for protecting one’s companions: Oṃ sarvasattvavajra amoghani amogha hūṃ.
*Urdhva-ḍaṃṣṭrāri hūṃ* (The mantra for entering the maṇḍala: *Oṃ āmukha-bhara-miśe pavanī hūṃ*).
*Vandana-mantra*: *Oṃ āmukha-vati hūṃ*. *Caṅkramaṇa-mantra*.
Recite *Oṃ* as before (1). *Āmukha-karake* (2). *Hūṃ* (3). This is the mantra for receiving the Dharma.
Recite *Oṃ* as before (1). *Svayaṃ-sthe* (2). *Āmukha-vati* (3). *Hūṃ* (4).
This is the mantra for purifying flowers, unguents, and incense. Recite *Oṃ* as before (1). *Āmukha* (2).
1. *Puṣpabhadra* (補澁豍哺) 2. *Bhara-bhara* (跛同上囉嚩囉) 3. *Jaya-jaya* (健地儞三惹野惹野) 4.
*Svāhā* (娑去嚩訶五) The mantra for food, drink, and fruit:
*Oṃ amoghasiddhe pravarṇi rasarasāgre svāhā*. (唵同上呼一 阿暮伽上縒囉二 去布囉抳二 囉縒囉縒三 䞘囉嚩底四)
HŪṂ. The mantra for the oil of the five lamps: OṂ (as above) ĀMUKA (vocative) TUṄ SVĀHĀ.
These various mantras each follow their respective root rituals.
Recite this three times or five times.
By purifying all objects and making offerings,
one attains the auspicious accomplishment of all dharmas.
It shall not be invaded, pursued, or destroyed by any māras, spirits, ghosts, or vināyakas who obstruct the Dharma.
This is the mantra of the Vidyārāja: Oṃ (as above) āmukhāpate (1) trāmi trāmi (2) saṃtrāmi (3) svāhā (5). This is the mantra of the Vidyārāja.
Whether walking, standing, sitting, or reclining, or when eating food or drinking water,
one should recite [the mantra] three or seven times while dispatching the assembly of noble ones and subduing spirits and ghosts.
One attains the auspicious accomplishment of all dharmas.
Chapter Seventy-Eight: Entrustment. Furthermore, he addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, the Lord of Secrets, saying:
This is the Amoghapāśa-mantra of the Great Vidyārāja Amoghasiddhi;
the Amoghapāśa-mantra of the Great Terrible Vidyārāja Amoghasiddhi;
and the Amoghapāśa-mantra of the Pure Lotus Vidyārāja Amoghasiddhi.
Because each acts as all dharmas for one another,
do not cause them to assist each other by means of other mantras.
Those who uphold this dharma must not harbor thoughts of false speech.
One should not engage in frivolous play, idle chatter, or divisive speech; nor should one harbor stinginess, envy, malice, anger, or resentment.
One must never speak of the faults or transgressions of others, nor discuss the Three Vehicles or the Triple Gem in a manner that leads to mutual contention or dispute.
All such actions are improper and should be entirely avoided.
Simply practice this method at all times;
according to your capacity, constantly make offerings of incense, flowers, and pure water.
This will enable you to swiftly and unfailingly fulfill the perfection of generosity.
Constantly, with respect to all feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness,
by upholding all pure prohibitive precepts, one is able to cause the perfection of pure ethical discipline (*śīla-pāramitā*) to be swiftly and fully accomplished, not in vain.
By practicing patience in all matters,
one is able to swiftly and fruitfully fulfill the perfection of patience.
At all times, one practices diligence.
It enables one to swiftly and fruitfully fulfill the perfection of diligence;
it cultivates meditative concentration regarding all objects,
enabling one to swiftly and fruitfully fulfill the perfection of meditative concentration.
Contemplate all phenomena and cultivate correct wisdom through reflection;
this will cause the Prajñāpāramitā not to be in vain and will swiftly bring it to fulfillment.
At all times, venerate the Triple Gem with devotion.
With a mind that practices the right path, one’s speech shall not be flattery or deceit.
One shall reverently uphold all gateways of dhāraṇīs and mantras,
and take delight in honoring all images of Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Vajra deities.
Having generated great compassion for all sentient beings and delighting in the practice of the six perfections for their sake,
they shall receive, uphold, read, recite, revere, and make offerings to this *Amoghapāśa-kalparāja-sūtra-samaya*.
With the phrases and clauses clearly distinguished,
one should personally transcribe it or instruct others to transcribe it,
having oneself thoroughly understood the principles of the teachings and the meaning of the text.
Furthermore, you should also instruct others to explain the meaning of the text,
so that this great, true, and non-empty heart-king of the *Amoghapāśa*, the vast liberation, the lotus maṇḍala, the mudrās, and the samaya may never be interrupted.
This Dharma is always held in reverence by all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas,
who join their palms, pay homage with their heads bowed, and uphold it.
This Dharma is also the samaya locus of the secret great maṇḍala seal-treasury, common to the lineage of all Tathāgatas.
It is also the place where all beings of the realms of existence attain great bodhi and transcend birth and death;
it is also the locus of the most profound and secret Dharma-treasury of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.
At that time, after the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara had spoken this sutra, Śākyamuni Tathāgata [spoke].
And all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the ten directions, as numerous as ninety-nine hundred thousand koṭi-nayuta Ganges sands,
praised the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, saying:
Excellent, excellent, O Great Compassionate One!
You have been able to skillfully expound this Heart-King Dhāraṇī Mantra of the Amoghapāśa,
with its profound and wondrous verses and various teachings.
I shall act as a great light for sentient beings to shatter all veils of darkness;
I shall become a most unfailing collection of wish-fulfilling jewels,
bringing about great benefit and happiness, and awakening them to bodhicitta.
We Buddhas also constantly praise, proclaim, and disseminate it.
At that time, there were an assembly of nine hundred and ninety billion nayutas of koṭis of hundreds of thousands of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas within the gathering.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, Lord of Secrets, acting as the leader,
rose from his seat together with the others, circumambulated the Buddha three times, withdrew to sit at one side, and joined his palms toward the Buddha.
They likewise praised the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara with these verses:
"Your body of great compassion is pure and wondrous; Its light manifests universally in all colors, Pure as a lotus flower, Adorned with perfected supernormal powers."
Adorned with the power of charity, The marks and signs are all perfectly complete;
His radiance is peerless, And his brilliance exceeds the multitude of lunar disks.
With a Brahma-voice most pure and penetrating, He roars forth the gateway of great compassion.
Fully manifesting all manner of spiritual transformations,
Surpassing the various modes of guidance of the kalaviṅka and others; Possessing equal, pure,
and stainless great wisdom that exceeds the multitude of suns, With merit equal to the expanse of space.
Emitting light that fills the ten directions, the entire assembly of Buddhas makes offerings;
with the fuel of passion consumed without remainder,
the wheel of the Dharma-torch delivers all sentient beings from the three realms— those of the present and the future.
He taught the Dharma of non-emptiness through various gateways of mantra;
furthermore, this Honored One of Sages, Vairocana Buddha— the Buddha of all the Ganges-sands— upholds the power of seals and supernormal faculties.
Not being empty or quiescent, you are able to manifest the path of the meaning of ambrosia and transform it into the City of Ambrosia;
you cause [beings] to receive the bliss of Bodhi and liberate them from all the sufferings of existence within the great ocean of suffering.
All have attained fearlessness and joy, ascending to dwell within the ocean of virtue and the Way, which is eternally deep and vast; no analogy can know it.
Great compassion arises for the three realms, with sincere devotion that never ceases.
The ocean of non-empty merit and compassion for the boundless—
the merit of copying and upholding this [sūtra] cannot be known even in its slightest portion, even if a Buddha were to expound it with his Buddha-power and wisdom throughout many eons.
We praise thus, like drops of water in the ocean; we,
the multitude of bodhisattvas, collectively revere the unfailing Dharma and always dwell in peace,
following the gateway of liberation through mantras.
Together with those of great compassion, within the non-empty dharmas of mind,
wherever they arise and flow according to direction, they all assist in upholding and proclaiming them;
at that time, the deities of the maṇḍala of all lineages.
And there were immeasurable hundreds of thousands of mantra-siddhas and deities,
including Mahābrahmā, Śakra Devendra, Nārāyaṇa, and Īśvara.
Maheśvara-deva, immeasurable hundreds of thousands of Śuddhāvāsa-devas, Yama-rāja, Varuṇa-deva,
Sūrya-deva, Candra-deva, Tāraka-deva, Vāyu-deva, Agni-deva, and the Cāturmahārājika-devas.
Even unto the mantra-vidyādharīs of the Trāyastriṃśa heaven,
and the immeasurable hundreds of thousands of nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, asuras, gandharvas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and so forth.
Having heard this Dharma, they were filled with joy and leaped for gladness;
rising all at once, they joined their palms, prostrated themselves,
circumambulated the Buddha three times, and then withdrew to stand to one side.
Bowing with bodies bent, they stood gazing up at the Tathāgata without averting their eyes for even a moment.
At that time, they praised the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara with these verses:
"O Greatly Wise Muni, Honored One! Ganges-like tens of millions of Buddhas..."
Vairocana Buddha, together with the Dharma-seal of great supernormal powers and supreme wisdom, empowers the Great Compassionate Honored One,
the Mahāsattva of Great Compassion, and the Dharma of Great Bliss and Amogha.
The supreme dhāraṇī, the various divine transformations,
maṇḍalas, mudrās, and samādhis; furthermore, these are the various practices of the true Dharma of the Great Compassionate Honored One, rooted in the power of kindness and charity.
The Great Amogha Torch, constantly turning the wheel [of Dharma] to rescue all sentient beings from the three realms of existence; the True Ground of Amoghasiddhi,
the True City of Amoghasiddhi— may they establish [beings] in the Unsurpassed Path.
We vow to protect and uphold [the teachings]. With great compassion as our armor,
O Greatly Compassionate Avalokiteśvara, we vow to protect and uphold [the teachings] as we cycle through the ocean of desires and the maṇḍala of the Amogha-mantra.
The provisions for enlightenment are fulfilled; may we vow to protect that which eternally abides and fills the world.
The King of Amoghasiddhi’s Wrath subdues the māras of the three realms; this is the Discourse on Subduing All Māras.
We vow to protect and uphold all the mantras and so forth of the Amoghapāśa Sūtra,
and to cause this supreme and wondrous gateway of samādhi to spread throughout the world, never allowing it to disappear even for a moment.
We vow to protect and uphold those bhikṣus and bhikṣuṇīs,
and men and women of noble family, who in the future, wherever they may be in the lands and towns of Jambudvīpa, receive and maintain this sutra.
Not following the activities of Māra, Subduing and severing all afflictions,
And upholding according to the Dharma and the True Dharma—
We vow to protect and maintain All the Buddha-dhāraṇīs and the various methods of supernormal powers.
The Samādhi of the Vehicle of Liberation and the immeasurable gates of dhāraṇī are all revealed within this sutra; therefore, we vow to transcribe this inconceivable teaching,
to receive and uphold it, and to expound it for the sake of the multitude.
At that time, Śākyamuni Tathāgata,
seeing the great assembly of bodhisattvas, humans, and devas,

all leaping for joy, simultaneously praised the *Amoghapāśa-kalparāja-sūtra* (The Sutra of the Divine Transformation Mantra of the Unfailing Lasso) of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara with these verses.
To ensure the circulation and protection [of this scripture], I encourage you to personally transcribe, uphold, and recite it. I declare:
"Excellent, excellent! You are all able to preserve this *Ārya-avalokiteśvara-mahāsatpuruṣa-amoghapāśa-vikurvaṇa-mantra-sūtra*."
May it remain long in the world and be reverently propagated;

throughout Jambudvīpa, in every direction and location, let it not be scattered, destroyed, or hidden away in the earth. By thus honoring and protecting it, one shall obtain the gateway to immeasurable merit and a mass of blessings.
It cannot be fully described.
If bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, sons of noble family, or daughters of noble family should receive,
uphold, recite, copy, and circulate it.
The merit derived from explaining this to others is likewise the same.
For this reason, you great assembly should diligently practice it and provide protection according to the circumstances.
At that time, the great assembly, having received the Buddha’s instruction, rejoiced with faith and acceptance, and they took it upon their heads to practice accordingly.
*Amoghapāśakalparāja Sūtra*, Fascicle Thirty.
